items.title: Ireland Raises Trafficking Concerns Over 22 Unaccompanied Somali Children
items.description: Irish authorities have alerted police to concerns that 22 Somali children who arrived in Ireland without accompanying adults may have been trafficked, according to a report published by the Irish Examiner on Tuesday. DUBLIN (WDN) — Irish authorities have raised concerns about the possible trafficking of 22 Somali children who arrived in Ireland unaccompanied, highlighting growing scrutiny of the risks facing vulnerable young migrants entering the country. The Irish Examiner , reporting on October 20 , cited figures from Tusla, Ireland’s Child and Family Agency, which notified An Garda Síochána, the national police service, of concerns about the potential trafficking of 35 children during the year. Somalis accounted for 22 of those cases, the largest national group identified in the notifications. The figures indicate concerns about possible trafficking, not confirmation that every child was trafficked. The report places the Somali children at the center of a wider investigation into the vulnerability of unaccompanied minors arriving in Ireland and the possibility that criminal networks may be exploiting them. Vulnerable children at risk Tusla said it works with other state agencies to protect unaccompanied children seeking international protection. Referrals can come from the International Protection Office, border authorities, police and Ireland’s national out-of-hours service. Social workers then assess the needs of young people believed to be under 18 and arriving without an accompanying adult. The agency emphasized that many unaccompanied minors arrive after fleeing conflict or humanitarian crises. The majority of separated children currently in Tusla’s care are from Ukraine, Afghanistan and Somalia, according to the report. The same figures recorded concerns about possible trafficking involving five Afghan children, two Vietnamese children, two Eritrean children, two children from The Gambia, one from Guinea and one from Pakistan. The distinction between a referral and a proven trafficking case is important. The published figures do not establish who transported the Somali children, how they travelled, whether they were recruited or coerced by traffickers, or whether anyone has been arrested or charged in connection with their cases. Questions for Somali authorities and international partners The report raises important questions about the networks and circumstances that may expose Somali children to exploitation during migration. Children travelling without parents or trusted guardians can be especially vulnerable to deception, coercion, abuse and disappearance. The findings also underline the need for cooperation between Irish authorities, Somali institutions and international organizations to identify children at risk, establish their circumstances and protect them from further exploitation. Any response must prioritize the children’s safety and welfare rather than treating them as offenders because of their migration status. Authorities must also establish the facts of individual cases before attributing responsibility to particular people or networks. For Somali families, the report is a reminder of the dangers that vulnerable children may face when travelling abroad without reliable protection. For Ireland, it presents a safeguarding challenge: ensuring that children who arrive alone receive appropriate care while investigating credible concerns that traffickers may be targeting them. The central issue is not simply how 22 Somali children reached Ireland, but whether criminal networks exploited their vulnerability—and whether authorities can identify those responsible while ensuring that the children receive the protection they need. items.title: Deadly Roadside Bombings Highlight Al-Shabaab’s Grip on Somalia’s Rural Areas
items.description: Civilian vehicles struck in Lower Shabelle as militants sustain attacks on major highways; Puntland reports killing two suspected bomb-makers ahead of a new offensive in the Calmadow Mountains. MOGADISHU, Somalia (WDN) — A pair of roadside bombings targeting civilian transport in southern Somalia has left multiple people dead and others wounded, underscoring the dangers facing travelers on highways that pass-through areas where Al-Shabaab maintains a persistent presence beyond major urban centers. The first explosion struck a passenger vehicle travelling from Mogadishu towards Baidoa, the capital of Bay region, between Waraaboole and Doonka in Lower Shabelle. The vehicle was reportedly devastated by the blast. A local resident quoted by Shabelle TV said only the driver and a woman survived, while the other passengers were killed or injured. The precise death toll was not immediately established. A second explosion hit a Fekon motorcycle travelling towards Afgooye. The motorcycle carried two passengers and a driver, all three of whom reportedly died at the scene, according to local sources. Security forces and civilians arrived to assist the victims. The area has previously seen operations by Somali government troops and attacks attributed to Al-Shabaab, which has continued targeting government forces and African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) personnel moving along major roads in the region. The bombings illustrate a wider security challenge: although government forces and international partners maintain a presence in key towns and conduct operations across the country, Al-Shabaab continues to operate in rural areas, threaten transport routes and impose risks on communities beyond the main urban centres. Rural influence and the limits of government control Al-Shabaab’s reach extends beyond direct territorial control. Its ability to plant roadside explosives, stage ambushes and threaten movement along important routes allows the group to disrupt commerce and civilian travel even where government forces are present. Across parts of Somalia, the contrast between control of urban centres and security in surrounding rural areas remains significant. The government’s presence in a town does not necessarily mean that nearby villages, roads and countryside are secure. Al-Shabaab has exploited these gaps to sustain pressure on security forces and undermine public confidence. The latest incidents do not, by themselves, establish the group’s precise territorial control in Lower Shabelle. They nevertheless demonstrate how the threat persists along roads linking Mogadishu with other major population centers. Puntland prepares a new offensive In Northeastern Somalia, Puntland authorities said their forces killed two suspected Al-Shabaab members near Galgala in the Calmadow Mountains of Bari region. According to a statement issued by the Puntland government, the men were allegedly planting landmines along roads and in surrounding areas. The operation followed a separate mine explosion near Galgala the previous day that struck a vehicle carrying Puntland security personnel, killing one person and injuring two others, according to the authorities. Puntland said it was preparing Operation Onkod, a campaign targeting Al-Shabaab fighters operating in the Calmadow Mountains. The announcement signals an effort to prevent the group from using the rugged terrain as a base for planting explosives and threatening nearby communities and security forces. The results of the planned offensive remain to be seen. Experience across Somalia has shown that killing individual fighters or clearing particular locations may not be enough to secure an area permanently unless military operations are followed by sustained security, functioning local administration and protection for civilians. The latest bombings in Lower Shabelle and the reported operation in Puntland highlight the geographically dispersed nature of Somalia’s security challenge. Al-Shabaab faces pressure from government and regional forces, yet it continues to exploit rural terrain and vulnerable transport routes. For civilians travelling between towns, the immediate consequence is a continuing risk of death and injury. For Somali authorities, the challenge is broader: translating military operations into lasting control of roads and rural communities, so that security in major towns is no longer surrounded by insecurity in the countryside. items.title: Yemen’s War Sends Refugees Across the Gulf of Aden to Puntland’s Bossaso
items.description: Renewed fighting in Yemen is driving families towards Somalia’s northeastern coast, placing fresh demands on Puntland’s authorities and humanitarian agencies to provide protection and assistance. BOSSASO, Puntland (WDN) — The renewed conflict in Yemen is creating a new humanitarian challenge across the Gulf of Aden, with people fleeing the violence arriving in Puntland, including through the coastal port city of Bossaso. The arrivals include Yemeni refugees seeking safety from escalating hostilities and Somali nationals returning after years of living in Yemen. Their journeys reflect the increasingly interconnected humanitarian crises affecting the two sides of the Gulf of Aden, where conflict can turn people who once found refuge abroad into refugees or returnees themselves. A report published by Puntland Signal on September 19 said authorities in Puntland and Somaliland had reported increased arrivals, numbering in the hundreds across the two regions. The report did not provide a separate figure for Puntland or a detailed breakdown of Yemeni refugees and Somali returnees. The developments follow renewed fighting in Yemen that has displaced tens of thousands of people inside the country and prompted others to seek safety across the sea. Reuters reported on September 18 that at least 112,000 people had been displaced within Yemen, while nearly 3,000 had fled by sea to Djibouti. Some refugees and returnees were also reported in Puntland and Somaliland. Bossaso’s humanitarian responsibility Bossaso has a long history as a gateway for people moving between Somalia and the Arabian Peninsula. During earlier phases of Yemen’s conflict, the city received both Yemeni refugees and Somali families returning after years abroad. The United Nations refugee agency documented this pattern in 2015, when families fleeing Yemen arrived in Bossaso and received temporary accommodation and assistance while arranging onward travel to relatives elsewhere in Somalia. The current situation presents different needs for different groups. Yemeni families escaping conflict may require temporary shelter, food, healthcare, documentation and protection while considering their next steps. Somali returnees may need help reconnecting with relatives, finding accommodation and rebuilding livelihoods after returning to a country that may have changed considerably during their absence. The scale of these needs in Bossaso remains unclear. However, any sustained increase in arrivals could place additional pressure on local services and humanitarian organisations, particularly if international assistance does not keep pace with demand. A call for coordinated action Puntland’s authorities, the Federal Government of Somalia, the United Nations and humanitarian organizations face the task of ensuring that new arrivals are identified, registered where appropriate and assessed according to their individual circumstances. Yemeni refugees should have access to protection, while Somali returnees need practical support to reintegrate into their communities. Women, children and people with urgent medical needs may require particular attention. The response must also recognize the contribution of local communities, which often provide the first assistance to displaced people. Without adequate resources, however, the responsibility can become difficult to sustain. The renewed arrivals are a reminder that the consequences of Yemen’s war extend beyond its borders. For Puntland, Bossaso is once again a place of refuge for people crossing the Gulf of Aden in search of safety. The immediate challenge is to ensure that those arriving are not left without shelter, protection or basic services. As the conflict continues, timely humanitarian assistance and coordination will be essential to prevent a regional emergency from becoming a deeper crisis for vulnerable families and the communities receiving them. items.title: SNA’s Bid to Retake Buurhakaba Fails After Al-Shabaab Ambush
items.description: Federal special forces reportedly lose two armoured vehicles in an ambush near Jamaada as government troops retreat to their bases, dealing a setback to Mogadishu’s effort to recover territory in Bay region. BUURHAKABA, Bay Region (WDN) — An attempt by Somali federal forces to recapture Buurhakaba district from forces aligned with former South West State president Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed (Laftagareen) has reportedly failed after government troops were ambushed by Al-Shabaab fighters near the settlement of Jamaada. Local sources told WardheerNews (WDN) that the fighting inflicted casualties on both sides, with federal forces reportedly suffering the heavier losses. Two armoured vehicles were said to have been destroyed in the clash. According to information provided by residents familiar with the incident, the government troops were advancing towards Buurhakaba when Al-Shabaab fighters struck them from positions along the route. The federal forces reportedly had not anticipated the militants’ presence, leaving them vulnerable to the ambush. The sources said government troops subsequently withdrew to their bases rather than continuing towards Buurhakaba. Their retreat indicates that the operation failed to achieve its immediate objective of retaking the district. The reported casualties and destruction of the vehicles could not be independently verified, and no official casualty figures were immediately available. Setback for Mogadishu’s Military Campaign The operation involved members of the Somali National Army’s Danab special forces and the Gorgor commandos. Their reported setback comes after federal authorities had projected confidence that government troops could advance on Buurhakaba and reverse recent territorial losses in Bay region. The planned offensive was expected to mark the first major attempt by federal forces to recover territory following the capture of several districts in the region during the previous week. The loss of Buurhakaba and other locations has intensified the political and security crisis in South West State, where rival forces are contesting control of territory and the authority to govern. The federal administration has supported the authorities in Baidoa, while forces aligned with Laftagareen have made territorial gains. The latest ambush demonstrates the difficulties facing Mogadishu as it seeks to regain ground. Even units trained and equipped for specialised operations can face serious setbacks when advancing through areas where armed opponents retain the ability to conduct ambushes and plant explosives. Al-Shabaab Exploits the Security Vacuum The reported encounter also highlights the wider threat posed by Al-Shabaab in Bay and neighbouring regions. While federal forces and their allies are preoccupied with the struggle over South West State’s political leadership and territorial control, the militant group continues to operate along rural routes and in areas where security remains fragile. The presence of Al-Shabaab near the route to Buurhakaba raises questions about the intelligence available to government commanders and their ability to secure roads before launching an offensive. The reported destruction of two armoured vehicles, if confirmed, would underline the operational risks facing forces advancing without adequate information about enemy positions. The incident also illustrates how political and military confrontation between Somali actors can complicate efforts to contain the insurgency. Disputes over regional authority have created an additional layer of instability in an area where civilians already face insecurity and disruption to travel and commerce. For now, the reported withdrawal of federal troops means Buurhakaba remains beyond the reach of the operation’s immediate objective . Mogadishu’s ability to retake the district will depend not only on deploying more forces, but also on reliable intelligence, effective planning and a broader strategy for securing territory after military advances. The failed push is a reminder that public declarations of confidence cannot substitute for results on the ground. Until federal forces can advance without being ambushed and establish lasting security in recovered areas, the struggle for Bay region will remain uncertain—and Al-Shabaab will continue to exploit the gaps left by Somalia’s competing security priorities. items.title: Dhirbaaxo culus oo ku dhacday Giriiga iyo Israa’iil kadib markii Turkiga uu…
items.description: Tripoli (Caasimada Online) – Baarlamaanka Liibiya ayaa aqlabiyad ku ansixiyey heshiiskii xuduudaha badda ee Turkiga iyo Liibiya ay kala saxiixdeen sannadkii 2019-kii, tallaabadaas oo loo arko mid xoojinaysa mowqifka istaraatiijiga ah ee Ankara, isla markaana caqabad ku noqon karta danaha Giriiga iyo Israa’iil ee Bariga Mediterranean-ka. Heshiiskan ayaa dib u soo cusboonaysiinaya muranka muddada dheer ka taagnaa xuduudaha badda, khayraadka tamarta iyo saamaynta juqraafiyeed ee gobolka. Turkiga ayaa heshiiska u arka mid xoojinaya sheegashadiisa ku aaddan aagagga badda ee uu danaynayo, halka Giriiga iyo dalal kale ay ka horyimaadeen qodobbadiisa. Heshiiska ayaa la saxiixay sannadkii 2019-kii, xilli ciidamada uu hoggaaminayey Janaraal Khaliifa Xaftar ay guluf milatari ku hayeen caasimadda Tripoli, halkaas oo ay fadhiday Dowladda Midnimada Qaran ee Liibiya oo Qaramada Midoobay aqoonsanayd. Turkiga ayaa xilligaas taageero milatari siiyey dowladda, taas oo qayb ka ahayd iskaashiga amni iyo siyaasadeed ee labada dhinac. Giriiga ayaa si adag uga soo horjeestay heshiiska, isaga oo ku doodaya inaan si caddaalad ah loo tixgelin xuquuqda badeed ee jasiiradihiisa. Turkiga iyo Giriiga ayaa muddo dheer isku hayey xuduudaha badda, hawada iyo xuquuqda ka dhalata jasiiradaha ku yaalla Badda Aegean-ka iyo Bariga Mediterranean-ka. Masar ayaa iyaduna iskaashi siyaasadeed iyo mid badeed la samaysay Giriiga, taas oo qayb ka ah loollanka gobolka. Dhanka Israa’iil, heshiiska ayaa saamayn ku yeelan kara qorshayaasha tamarta ee Bariga Mediterranean-ka, halkaas oo ay ku yaallaan goobo gaas dabiici ah oo muhiim u ah dhoofinta tamarta. Israa’iil, Giriiga iyo Qubrus ayaa hore u taageeray qorshayaal lagu gaarsiinayo gaaska gobolka suuqyada Yurub, oo uu ka mid yahay mashruuca dhuumaha EastMed, kaas oo la kulmay caqabado siyaasadeed, farsamo iyo dhaqaale. Turkiga ayaa doonaya inuu noqdo marin muhiim ah oo isku xira ilaha tamarta ee Bariga Dhexe iyo suuqyada Yurub. Ankara waxay heshiiska Liibiya u aragtaa mid xoojinaya booskeeda juqraafiyeed iyo saamaynteeda ku aaddan qorshayaasha tamarta, gaar ahaan haddii la tixgeliyo mashaariicda dhuumaha gaaska ee mari kara aagagga badda ee muranku ka taagan yahay. Ansixinta heshiiska ayaa sidoo kale imanaysa xilli uu soo dhowaanayo xiriirka Turkiga iyo dhinacyada kala duwan ee siyaasadda Liibiya, oo uu ku jiro maamulka Khaliifa Xaftar. Turkiga ayaa soo dhaweeyey go’aanka baarlamaanka, kaas oo siinaya heshiiska taageero siyaasadeed oo dheeraad ah, inkasta oo muranka sharci iyo kan siyaasadeed ee ku xeeran aanu dhammaan. Heshiiska Turkiga iyo Liibiya ayaa sidaas ku sii noqonaya arrin miisaan ku leh loollanka Bariga Mediterranean-ka, kaas oo ku saabsan xuduudaha badda, sahminta shidaalka iyo gaaska, amniga iyo marin-biyoodka. Si kastaba, ansixinta heshiiskan ayaa dib u soo noolaynaysa khilaafaadka gobolka, iyadoo Turkigu doonayo inuu xoojiyo saamayntiisa, halka Giriiga iyo Israa’iil ay danaynayaan ilaalinta danahooda badeed iyo qorshayaashooda tamareed. items.fullContent: Tripoli (Caasimada Online) – Baarlamaanka Liibiya ayaa aqlabiyad ku ansixiyey heshiiskii xuduudaha badda ee Turkiga iyo Liibiya ay kala saxiixdeen sannadkii 2019-kii, tallaabadaas oo loo arko mid xoojinaysa mowqifka istaraatiijiga ah ee Ankara, isla markaana caqabad ku noqon karta danaha Giriiga iyo Israa’iil ee Bariga Mediterranean-ka. Heshiiskan ayaa dib u soo cusboonaysiinaya muranka muddada dheer ka taagnaa xuduudaha badda, khayraadka tamarta iyo saamaynta juqraafiyeed ee gobolka. Turkiga ayaa heshiiska u arka mid xoojinaya sheegashadiisa ku aaddan aagagga badda ee uu danaynayo, halka Giriiga iyo dalal kale ay ka horyimaadeen qodobbadiisa. Heshiiska ayaa la saxiixay sannadkii 2019-kii, xilli ciidamada uu hoggaaminayey Janaraal Khaliifa Xaftar ay guluf milatari ku hayeen caasimadda Tripoli, halkaas oo ay fadhiday Dowladda Midnimada Qaran ee Liibiya oo Qaramada Midoobay aqoonsanayd. Turkiga ayaa xilligaas taageero milatari siiyey dowladda, taas oo qayb ka ahayd iskaashiga amni iyo siyaasadeed ee labada dhinac. Giriiga ayaa si adag uga soo horjeestay heshiiska, isaga oo ku doodaya inaan si caddaalad ah loo tixgelin xuquuqda badeed ee jasiiradihiisa. Turkiga iyo Giriiga ayaa muddo dheer isku hayey xuduudaha badda, hawada iyo xuquuqda ka dhalata jasiiradaha ku yaalla Badda Aegean-ka iyo Bariga Mediterranean-ka. Masar ayaa iyaduna iskaashi siyaasadeed iyo mid badeed la samaysay Giriiga, taas oo qayb ka ah loollanka gobolka. Dhanka Israa’iil, heshiiska ayaa saamayn ku yeelan kara qorshayaasha tamarta ee Bariga Mediterranean-ka, halkaas oo ay ku yaallaan goobo gaas dabiici ah oo muhiim u ah dhoofinta tamarta. Israa’iil, Giriiga iyo Qubrus ayaa hore u taageeray qorshayaal lagu gaarsiinayo gaaska gobolka suuqyada Yurub, oo uu ka mid yahay mashruuca dhuumaha EastMed, kaas oo la kulmay caqabado siyaasadeed, farsamo iyo dhaqaale. Turkiga ayaa doonaya inuu noqdo marin muhiim ah oo isku xira ilaha tamarta ee Bariga Dhexe iyo suuqyada Yurub. Ankara waxay heshiiska Liibiya u aragtaa mid xoojinaya booskeeda juqraafiyeed iyo saamaynteeda ku aaddan qorshayaasha tamarta, gaar ahaan haddii la tixgeliyo mashaariicda dhuumaha gaaska ee mari kara aagagga badda ee muranku ka taagan yahay. Ansixinta heshiiska ayaa sidoo kale imanaysa xilli uu soo dhowaanayo xiriirka Turkiga iyo dhinacyada kala duwan ee siyaasadda Liibiya, oo uu ku jiro maamulka Khaliifa Xaftar. Turkiga ayaa soo dhaweeyey go’aanka baarlamaanka, kaas oo siinaya heshiiska taageero siyaasadeed oo dheeraad ah, inkasta oo muranka sharci iyo kan siyaasadeed ee ku xeeran aanu dhammaan. Heshiiska Turkiga iyo Liibiya ayaa sidaas ku sii noqonaya arrin miisaan ku leh loollanka Bariga Mediterranean-ka, kaas oo ku saabsan xuduudaha badda, sahminta shidaalka iyo gaaska, amniga iyo marin-biyoodka. Si kastaba, ansixinta heshiiskan ayaa dib u soo noolaynaysa khilaafaadka gobolka, iyadoo Turkigu doonayo inuu xoojiyo saamayntiisa, halka Giriiga iyo Israa’iil ay danaynayaan ilaalinta danahooda badeed iyo qorshayaashooda tamareed. items.title: DF Soomaaliya oo shaacisay heshiis ay la gaartay Somaliland
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa sheegtay in is-afgarad laga gaaray khilaafkii ka dhashay nidaamka fiisaha elektaroonigga ah (eVisa), iyadoo tilmaantay in Somaliland ay hadda ku qanacsan tahay habka loo maamulayo nidaamkaas. Maareeyaha Hay’adda Duulista Rayidka Soomaaliya, Axmed Macallin Xasan oo la hadlay BBC ayaa sheegay in aanay hadda jirin caqabado la xiriira eVisa-ha, isla markaana nidaamku u furan yahay ganacsatada Soomaaliyeed, oo ay ku jiraan kuwa ka hawl-gala magaalada Hargeysa ee maamulka Somaliland. Wuxuu meesha ka saaray walaaca laga qabay in nidaamku caqabad ku noqdo ganacsatada Somaliland, isagoo caddeeyay in wakaaladaha socdaalka ee Hargeysa iyo kuwa ka hawlgala deegaannada kale ee dalka ay adeegsan karaan nidaamkaas. Maareeyaha ayaa sheegay in khilaafkii dhawaan ka dhashay eVisa-ha aanu hadda taagnayn, isla markaana is-afgarad laga gaaray adeegsiga nidaamka. Inkastoo uu tilmaamay in arrimaha la xiriira shuruucda dalka iyo qaybsiga kheyraadka lagu maareeyo habraacyada u degsan dalka. Khilaafka eVisa-ha ayaa hore walaac uga abuuray dadka u kala safra Soomaaliya iyo Somaliland, gaar ahaan maamulka socdaalka iyo lacagaha laga qaado dadka soo galaya deegaannada kala duwan. Axmed Macallin Xasan wuxuu si cad u sheegay in nidaamku u furan yahay ganacsatada Soomaaliyeed meel kasta oo ay joogaan, isla markaana uu gacan ka geysan karo horumarinta ganacsiga duulista iyo adeegyada socdaalka. Mar la weydiiyay canshuuraha laga qaado tigidhada diyaaradaha iyo wada-shaqaynta nidaamyada socdaalka Soomaaliya iyo Somaliland ayuu sidoo kale heegay in nidaamku yahay mid mideysan oo laga isticmaali karo guud ahaan dalka. Si kastaba, hadalkan ayaa imanaya xilli ay jireen walaacyo la xiriira hirgelinta nidaamka eVisa-ha iyo saamaynta uu ku yeelan karo dadka u safraya Somaliland, iyadoo Dowladda Federaalku ay hadda ku adkeysaneyso in khilaafkii arrintaas ka dhashay la xalliyay, isla markaana nidaamku u furan yahay dhammaan dadka iyo ganacsatada Soomaaliyeed. items.title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Remarks to the Press
items.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Remarks to the Press Marco Rubio, Secretary of State Taj Mahal Palace Hotel Mumbai, India October 21, 2026 SECRETARY RUBIO: What’s up? All right, let’s go. QUESTION: Sir, The Wall Street Journal reported that Elon Musk is the one who made the decision to throttle Starshield and catch Ukraine off-guard. Is this something you were aware of? Can you — SECRETARY RUBIO: Starlink. QUESTION: Starlink and Starshield. SECRETARY RUBIO: Okay, again, there’s this – all this confusion. These are two separate programs, okay? Starlink is a commercial – Starlink is the receivers you put on the roof of your house and you use for – it’s used for commercial purposes. It’s not a military system, although it could be used in order to guide drones and things of this nature and so forth. And then Starshield is different. It’s a unique defense product that is sold and operated through the Department of War, as an example. It’s two different items and it’s important to distinguish one from the other. I have not seen The Wall Street Journal reporting because I have not read it. I know that what – so I’m not familiar with the story that you’re referring to. But Starlink is a private company. They have a contract. They have contractual terms upon how that technology can be used. The important point is we cannot direct a private company as to the decisions they make or not make. What I can tell you with certainty is the President of the United States nor anyone in our system ever requested that any changes to that system be made, and that’s what we said repeatedly. I don’t know what the story reflects, but that is the case. QUESTION: Isn’t – even if it’s a private company, I mean, this obviously is vital national security infrastructure for Ukraine. Isn’t this something that the U.S. – you as National Security Advisor – should have been given a heads-up on before? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, again, I’m not going to comment on what we knew that they might or might not do. Suffice it to say that the reporting out there was that somehow the United States Government was denying them something they needed in order to defend their country. That’s not true. That’s not accurate. And for leaders in Ukraine to continue to represent that is also not accurate. I would also say – and again, I hark back on this statement that was made a few days ago. I don’t know who this official was in the Ukrainian Government that went around saying that a bunch of people had died as a result of what America was denying them. Not only are we not denying them and it’s not true, how many millions of people have been saved because of what America has already provided? No country in the world has done more to help Ukraine over the last four and a half years than the United States, including under the Trump Administration, and that continues to be the case. But ultimately, what the President wants here is an end to this war. That’s what he’s focused on. QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, regarding the system in question, you said it’s inaccurate to say that the administration told SpaceX to throttle this service, but you’re not ruling out that the U.S. Government, if I understand correctly, knew about this decision. SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, we’ve seen the public reporting on it. We’ve seen the Ukrainians reporting that they were no longer able to use basically the internet. QUESTION: Knew about this decision beforehand. SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, I’m not aware that we knew about this decision beforehand. I certainly – but it’s irrelevant. The bottom line is that that is – that is governed by a private commercial contract as to the – how their stuff can be used and what speeds they allow it to be used at. And so we’ll continue to engage on the matter, but the reporting initially was that somehow this was part of a directive from the United States Government, and I’m just here to tell you, as I’ve said repeatedly from the very beginning and the President has made clear, at no point did he say deny them the use of this system because I’m trying to punish them or teach them a lesson. That’s just not accurate, and that’s what I’ve been addressing repeatedly. QUESTION: But it doesn’t mean there was no foreknowledge. SECRETARY RUBIO: What do you mean, it doesn’t mean there’s no foreknowledge? I don’t understand your question. QUESTION: Well, just because – just because the President – you’re not – just because the President doesn’t tell Musk do this doesn’t mean it wasn’t discussed. SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I – again, I don’t – the President has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr. Musk. That’s a private company. The President doesn’t run that company and can’t direct that company to do anything. I’m not aware of any foreknowledge, nor anyone – but again, the reporting was not about foreknowledge. I’m telling you there was no foreknowledge, but beyond it, even if there was, we don’t control what a private company – how they decide their product can be used. Now, if they’re in a contract with the United States military, like Starshield, that’s a different matter, because that’s something we are purchasing and using for our use. But in the case of Starlink – we’re arguing something that’s just – it just makes no sense, the argument that people continue to make that somehow we had foreknowledge or directed it. It’s not accurate that we somehow knew about this ahead of time or directed it in any way. QUESTION: Sir, do you expect Foreign — SECRETARY RUBIO: And by the way, I’m – by the way, we’re no longer going to be defensive about this topic, okay, because what the United States – if it were not for the assistance of the United States, including under the Trump Administration, there would be no Ukraine right now. Ukraine as a sovereign state would not exist. That doesn’t mean the bravery of the Ukrainian fighters should not be highlighted, because they have absolutely very bravely and – fought for their country and done extraordinary things with the aid that’s been provided to them, standing up to a large – much larger country. But let’s be very clear: There would be no Ukraine today were it not for the assistance the United States has supplied Ukraine in the billions of dollars going back to the Biden administration and going – and through this administration as well. QUESTION: Do you expect Foreign Minister Lavrov to come to the G20 Summit – or foreign ministers’ summit in Atlanta, and (inaudible)? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, the Russians are invited to be a part of the G20. The President made that decision. So obviously they’re going to be represented at each of these summits. I don’t know if he himself is coming. I expect he might. I think he told us he was in the last time we engaged with him, so they’re part of the G20 and so they’ll be at that meeting. And I know obviously there’s the potential that Putin might come to the one in Miami as well, although we don’t have confirmation on that. QUESTION: Mr. Secretary — QUESTION: Secretary, just thinking about the – your – your final remaining meeting here in India with Reliance. Are you looking for anything specific from them in terms of an investment commitment or number or something about them changing what they do in terms of business regarding taking on more Venezuelan crude or making a greater investment in the U.S.? Anything specific along those lines? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, perhaps. I mean, we’ll see how the meetings go. Obviously that’s something that – on the energy field the Department of Energy would be very involved on the details of any specific ask. I think for us it’s more an opportunity to see their operations and have a broader discussion about their presence globally at a time in which energy is featuring prominently in many of the geopolitical decisions that are being made. This is a very large and prominent energy company. They also have a pretty large investment already in the United States. They have extensive refining capacity. As I highlighted to you yesterday, this is a company, for example, that has the capability to refine the heavy crude that’s produced in the Western Hemisphere, including from Venezuela, so I’m sure that’s a topic we’ll discuss. It’s – and I think through our conversations we’ll hopefully identify other opportunities to partner and work together. QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, staying on India but on a different subject, there are many protests from the opposition and students here in India, and UN experts have criticized the crackdown — SECRETARY RUBIO: Oh, the UN experts, yeah, my favorite. The UN experts are the oxymoron. QUESTION: Do you have a comment on those protests and — SECRETARY RUBIO: No. It’s a domestic political matter. I mean, I’m not going to get involved in their politics. I mean, they have – this is a democracy. They have elections here, so I’m not going to opine on their domestic political matters. We have protests every day in the United States because we’re – I mean, people view protests – I mean, obviously I’m not talking about the riots, like what you’re seeing in Europe, where they’re vandalizing and breaking into things and burning down buildings. I’m not talking about that. But in many ways, the fact that people are out there expressing themselves – I’m not talking about India; in any country in the world – is the sign that this is a country where there’s political discourse and so forth and differences of opinion. So the fact that you – you just said a moment ago as part of your question “the opposition.” Well, that – there’s no – for example, like there – in Cuba there is no opposition, like – that can actually go out and do anything without going to jail and being oppressed or – and exiled. So – but we’re not going to comment on internal political matters. That’s for the Indian people to decide and navigate. QUESTION: Sir, there were reports in Qatari media that Qatar and Pakistan have put forth a new proposal to Iran for the U.S. and Iran to come back to the negotiating table. Are those reports accurate? Is this something you’re — SECRETARY RUBIO: I think there’s a number of countries that have been engaging over a period of time with Iran, floating proposals. Ultimately any proposal that’s offered by any country in the world – look, we welcome mediation efforts. Obviously these are countries that we have strong alliances and partnerships with. In the case of Qatar in specific, they’ve been involved on this topic for a very long time. I understand that Field Marshal Munir was actually in Tehran yesterday. But in the end, any decision on what would be acceptable is on – is in the hands of the President of the United States, and I think he’s been abundantly clear at the core of all of this is something very simple to understand, is the United States will not support any deal that creates a pathway for Iran to ever have a nuclear weapon. As long as President Trump is in office, they will never have a nuclear weapon. QUESTION: There are reports that Witkoff is presenting Putin with an updated proposal from the U.S. side for a peace deal to end the war in Ukraine. Can you share any information on the details of that? SECRETARY RUBIO: No. I’m not going to. I mean – so Steve was in – I believe he just left Norway, but he met with Zelenskyy, and – so I think they floated some ideas. He wanted to go there first. He’s on his way to St. Petersburg – my understanding, he might even be underway as we speak – and I think he’ll share some ideas. This is how – this is how this works, right? You have to sort of see what the other side would be open to, and then you bring it to the other side and see if they’d be open to it and start to sort of narrow the gaps and the differences between the two sides. This is a very difficult negotiation. I don’t need to tell you that. And at its core, ultimately, has been the differences over Donbas. I mean, I don’t try to oversimplify this, because this is a complex war for a lot of different reasons, but at the core of all this has been that part of Donbas that Russia demands but has not been able to take on the battlefield and that Ukraine currently holds and has done so very bravely and against all odds and against many predictions. Remember, people predicted this war would be over in five days, and we’re going on five years, and a lot of that is credit to the fighters in Ukraine and their bravery and how hard they have fought. That said, the fight now is really concentrated on what happens to the remainder of Donbas, and so I think there’s some – been some creative ideas that have been put out there about how to resolve that difference, but obviously it has to be one in which both sides will have to agree to give up on something, and that’s always very difficult conversations to have. I think for Ukraine the predominant desire is to ensure their long-term security and safety so that they’re never re-invaded or re-attacked in the future. And so Steve is conditioning those ideas. He met with Zelenskyy a few hours ago. My understanding from the – what information he provided to me and the readout I got from it is that it was positive. Nothing unexpected, nothing surprising, and he’ll now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St. Petersburg and share them with the Russian side and let’s if we can make some progress. But as I said, these things are complex, and this a – if this was an easy war to solve, it would’ve been solved a long time ago. QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, could you tell us if – are you hopeful that the Russians will release Stephen Hubbard? SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, I don’t comment on that, other than to say that we think Mr. Hubbard should be released as soon as possible. QUESTION: Yeah. SECRETARY RUBIO: We’ve made that ask of the Russian system on a consistent basis, and we remain hopeful that that will happen. But that’s – beyond that, I’m not going to comment on that right now. STAFF: Thanks, guys. SECRETARY RUBIO: No, let me just give them one last one. This poor guy. STAFF: All right, all right. (Laughter.) QUESTION: Wanted to ask — SECRETARY RUBIO: He never gets questions. (Laughter.) Go ahead. QUESTION: Last week, the President pushed out Ambassador Guilfoyle from Greece after the reports alleging unethical behavior. The next day, you sent a message to remind State Department employees globally about the standards that you hold them to in terms of obeying rules regarding ethics, gifts, all of the rules, the structure of the State Department in posts globally. Are you concerned that the kind of issues that we saw with Ambassador Guilfoyle go beyond her personally or there could be other — SECRETARY RUBIO: No. First of all, let me say that message that went out just happened to go out the next day, but it had been something that we had – I had ordered to go out like weeks in advance. For whatever reason, the – somebody who works for me couldn’t get it out on time, because we asked them to do that weeks and weeks and weeks ahead of time. So – but this is a message we’ve sent out multiple times. It’s just a constant reminder of people, of who they work for. They work for the Government of the United States, they work for the people of the United States, and we expect everyone in our department to do so not just in accordance with the law but with the higher standards possible. Our ability to diplomatically represent this country is undermined and is sabotaged if there’s any implications that what you are doing – and I’m not talking about Kimberly in specific; anybody – you are undermined when – anytime there’s the notion that somehow what you are doing is somehow in your interest but not in the interest of the country. So we – it’s not the first time we’ve sent that message. That is something we repeatedly do because to me it’s a very important principle of how we do our work. It just happened to go out the day after, but that is something that, frankly, had been drafted and that I had ordered sent weeks in advance and unfortunately did not go out when I wanted it to go out for whatever reason. But – and won’t – it probably won’t be the last time that a message like that is sent. It’s something we just constantly remind people of just to set the right culture and standards. STAFF: All right, thanks guys. SECRETARY RUBIO: Okay, thank you guys.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, we’ve seen the public reporting on it. We’ve seen the Ukrainians reporting that they were no longer able to use basically the internet. QUESTION: Knew about this decision beforehand. SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, I’m not aware that we knew about this decision beforehand. I certainly – but it’s irrelevant. The bottom line is that that is – that is governed by a private commercial contract as to the – how their stuff can be used and what speeds they allow it to be used at. And so we’ll continue to engage on the matter, but the reporting initially was that somehow this was part of a directive from the United States Government, and I’m just here to tell you, as I’ve said repeatedly from the very beginning and the President has made clear, at no point did he say deny them the use of this system because I’m trying to punish them or teach them a lesson. That’s just not accurate, and that’s what I’ve been addressing repeatedly. QUESTION: But it doesn’t mean there was no foreknowledge. SECRETARY RUBIO: What do you mean, it doesn’t mean there’s no foreknowledge? I don’t understand your question. QUESTION: Well, just because – just because the President – you’re not – just because the President doesn’t tell Musk do this doesn’t mean it wasn’t discussed. SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I – again, I don’t – the President has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr. Musk. That’s a private company. The President doesn’t run that company and can’t direct that company to do anything. I’m not aware of any foreknowledge, nor anyone – but again, the reporting was not about foreknowledge. I’m telling you there was no foreknowledge, but beyond it, even if there was, we don’t control what a private company – how they decide their product can be used. Now, if they’re in a contract with the United States military, like Starshield, that’s a different matter, because that’s something we are purchasing and using for our use. But in the case of Starlink – we’re arguing something that’s just – it just makes no sense, the argument that people continue to make that somehow we had foreknowledge or directed it. It’s not accurate that we somehow knew about this ahead of time or directed it in any way. QUESTION: Sir, do you expect Foreign — SECRETARY RUBIO: And by the way, I’m – by the way, we’re no longer going to be defensive about this topic, okay, because what the United States – if it were not for the assistance of the United States, including under the Trump Administration, there would be no Ukraine right now. Ukraine as a sovereign state would not exist. That doesn’t mean the bravery of the Ukrainian fighters should not be highlighted, because they have absolutely very bravely and – fought for their country and done extraordinary things with the aid that’s been provided to them, standing up to a large – much larger country. But let’s be very clear: There would be no Ukraine today were it not for the assistance the United States has supplied Ukraine in the billions of dollars going back to the Biden administration and going – and through this administration as well. QUESTION: Do you expect Foreign Minister Lavrov to come to the G20 Summit – or foreign ministers’ summit in Atlanta, and (inaudible)? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, the Russians are invited to be a part of the G20. The President made that decision. So obviously they’re going to be represented at each of these summits. I don’t know if he himself is coming. I expect he might. I think he told us he was in the last time we engaged with him, so they’re part of the G20 and so they’ll be at that meeting. And I know obviously there’s the potential that Putin might come to the one in Miami as well, although we don’t have confirmation on that. QUESTION: Mr. Secretary — QUESTION: Secretary, just thinking about the – your – your final remaining meeting here in India with Reliance. Are you looking for anything specific from them in terms of an investment commitment or number or something about them changing what they do in terms of business regarding taking on more Venezuelan crude or making a greater investment in the U.S.? Anything specific along those lines? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, perhaps. I mean, we’ll see how the meetings go. Obviously that’s something that – on the energy field the Department of Energy would be very involved on the details of any specific ask. I think for us it’s more an opportunity to see their operations and have a broader discussion about their presence globally at a time in which energy is featuring prominently in many of the geopolitical decisions that are being made. This is a very large and prominent energy company. They also have a pretty large investment already in the United States. They have extensive refining capacity. As I highlighted to you yesterday, this is a company, for example, that has the capability to refine the heavy crude that’s produced in the Western Hemisphere, including from Venezuela, so I’m sure that’s a topic we’ll discuss. It’s – and I think through our conversations we’ll hopefully identify other opportunities to partner and work together. QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, staying on India but on a different subject, there are many protests from the opposition and students here in India, and UN experts have criticized the crackdown — SECRETARY RUBIO: Oh, the UN experts, yeah, my favorite. The UN experts are the oxymoron. QUESTION: Do you have a comment on those protests and — SECRETARY RUBIO: No. It’s a domestic political matter. I mean, I’m not going to get involved in their politics. I mean, they have – this is a democracy. They have elections here, so I’m not going to opine on their domestic political matters. We have protests every day in the United States because we’re – I mean, people view protests – I mean, obviously I’m not talking about the riots, like what you’re seeing in Europe, where they’re vandalizing and breaking into things and burning down buildings. I’m not talking about that. But in many ways, the fact that people are out there expressing themselves – I’m not talking about India; in any country in the world – is the sign that this is a country where there’s political discourse and so forth and differences of opinion. So the fact that you – you just said a moment ago as part of your question “the opposition.” Well, that – there’s no – for example, like there – in Cuba there is no opposition, like – that can actually go out and do anything without going to jail and being oppressed or – and exiled. So – but we’re not going to comment on internal political matters. That’s for the Indian people to decide and navigate. QUESTION: Sir, there were reports in Qatari media that Qatar and Pakistan have put forth a new proposal to Iran for the U.S. and Iran to come back to the negotiating table. Are those reports accurate? Is this something you’re — SECRETARY RUBIO: I think there’s a number of countries that have been engaging over a period of time with Iran, floating proposals. Ultimately any proposal that’s offered by any country in the world – look, we welcome mediation efforts. Obviously these are countries that we have strong alliances and partnerships with. In the case of Qatar in specific, they’ve been involved on this topic for a very long time. I understand that Field Marshal Munir was actually in Tehran yesterday. But in the end, any decision on what would be acceptable is on – is in the hands of the President of the United States, and I think he’s been abundantly clear at the core of all of this is something very simple to understand, is the United States will not support any deal that creates a pathway for Iran to ever have a nuclear weapon. As long as President Trump is in office, they will never have a nuclear weapon. QUESTION: There are reports that Witkoff is presenting Putin with an updated proposal from the U.S. side for a peace deal to end the war in Ukraine. Can you share any information on the details of that? SECRETARY RUBIO: No. I’m not going to. I mean – so Steve was in – I believe he just left Norway, but he met with Zelenskyy, and – so I think they floated some ideas. He wanted to go there first. He’s on his way to St. Petersburg – my understanding, he might even be underway as we speak – and I think he’ll share some ideas. This is how – this is how this works, right? You have to sort of see what the other side would be open to, and then you bring it to the other side and see if they’d be open to it and start to sort of narrow the gaps and the differences between the two sides. This is a very difficult negotiation. I don’t need to tell you that. And at its core, ultimately, has been the differences over Donbas. I mean, I don’t try to oversimplify this, because this is a complex war for a lot of different reasons, but at the core of all this has been that part of Donbas that Russia demands but has not been able to take on the battlefield and that Ukraine currently holds and has done so very bravely and against all odds and against many predictions. Remember, people predicted this war would be over in five days, and we’re going on five years, and a lot of that is credit to the fighters in Ukraine and their bravery and how hard they have fought. That said, the fight now is really concentrated on what happens to the remainder of Donbas, and so I think there’s some – been some creative ideas that have been put out there about how to resolve that difference, but obviously it has to be one in which both sides will have to agree to give up on something, and that’s always very difficult conversations to have. I think for Ukraine the predominant desire is to ensure their long-term security and safety so that they’re never re-invaded or re-attacked in the future. And so Steve is conditioning those ideas. He met with Zelenskyy a few hours ago. My understanding from the – what information he provided to me and the readout I got from it is that it was positive. Nothing unexpected, nothing surprising, and he’ll now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St. Petersburg and share them with the Russian side and let’s if we can make some progress. But as I said, these things are complex, and this a – if this was an easy war to solve, it would’ve been solved a long time ago. QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, could you tell us if – are you hopeful that the Russians will release Stephen Hubbard? SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, I don’t comment on that, other than to say that we think Mr. Hubbard should be released as soon as possible. QUESTION: Yeah. SECRETARY RUBIO: We’ve made that ask of the Russian system on a consistent basis, and we remain hopeful that that will happen. But that’s – beyond that, I’m not going to comment on that right now. STAFF: Thanks, guys. SECRETARY RUBIO: No, let me just give them one last one. This poor guy. STAFF: All right, all right. (Laughter.) QUESTION: Wanted to ask — SECRETARY RUBIO: He never gets questions. (Laughter.) Go ahead. QUESTION: Last week, the President pushed out Ambassador Guilfoyle from Greece after the reports alleging unethical behavior. The next day, you sent a message to remind State Department employees globally about the standards that you hold them to in terms of obeying rules regarding ethics, gifts, all of the rules, the structure of the State Department in posts globally. Are you concerned that the kind of issues that we saw with Ambassador Guilfoyle go beyond her personally or there could be other — SECRETARY RUBIO: No. First of all, let me say that message that went out just happened to go out the next day, but it had been something that we had – I had ordered to go out like weeks in advance. For whatever reason, the – somebody who works for me couldn’t get it out on time, because we asked them to do that weeks and weeks and weeks ahead of time. So – but this is a message we’ve sent out multiple times. It’s just a constant reminder of people, of who they work for. They work for the Government of the United States, they work for the people of the United States, and we expect everyone in our department to do so not just in accordance with the law but with the higher standards possible. Our ability to diplomatically represent this country is undermined and is sabotaged if there’s any implications that what you are doing – and I’m not talking about Kimberly in specific; anybody – you are undermined when – anytime there’s the notion that somehow what you are doing is somehow in your interest but not in the interest of the country. So we – it’s not the first time we’ve sent that message. That is something we repeatedly do because to me it’s a very important principle of how we do our work. It just happened to go out the day after, but that is something that, frankly, had been drafted and that I had ordered sent weeks in advance and unfortunately did not go out when I wanted it to go out for whatever reason. But – and won’t – it probably won’t be the last time that a message like that is sent. It’s something we just constantly remind people of just to set the right culture and standards. STAFF: All right, thanks guys. SECRETARY RUBIO: Okay, thank you guys.

items.title: Xogta duqeyn culus oo lagu beegsaday ciidanka Lafta-gareen
items.description: Waajid (Caasimada Online) – Wararka naga soo gaaraya gobolka Bakool ayaa sheegaya in maanta duqeymo diyaaradeed lala beegsaday maleeshiyaad ka tirsan kooxda Al-Shabaab iyo ciidamo taabacsan Lafta-gareen oo ku sugnaa duleedka degmada Waajid ee gobolkaasi. Duqeynta oo ahayd bartilmaameed ayaa lala eegtay goobo ay isku uruursanayeen maleeshiyaadka, iyadoo khasaare culus lagu gaarsiisay halkaasi. Saraakiil ka tirsan milatariga Soomaaliya ayaa sheegay in howlgalka uu u dhacay sidii loo qorsheeyay, isla markaana ay sii wadi doonaan gulufka ay ka wadaan deegaannadaasi. Ma shaacin saraakiishu khasaaraha rasmiga ah ee ka dhashay weerarka duqeynta ah, waxaase la filayaa in dowladdu ay faah-faahin ka bixiso dhacdadaasi. Xaaladda ayaa weli kacsan, waxaana dhaq-dhaqaaqyo iska soo horjeedo laga dareemayaa qaybo badan oo kamid ah gobollada Baay iyo Bakool ee koonfurta Soomaaliya. Howlgalkan ayaa kusoo aaday, xilli maalmihii u dambeeyay ciidamada daacadda u ah madaxweynihii hore ee Koonfur Galbeed ay weerarro ka wadeen deegaannada maamulkaasi, iyaga oo degmooyin dhowr ah kala wareegay maamulka uu hoggaamiyo Aadan Madoobe. Si kastaba, ha’ahaatee, Koonfur Galbeed Soomaaliya ayaa haatan qorseyneysa inay qaado guluf ka dhan ah ciidanka taabacsan Cabdicasiis Lafta-gareen ee qabsaday degmooyinka Qansaxdeere, Bardaale, Buurhakaba iyo Diinsoor oo ka wada tirsn gobolka Baay. Tallaabooyinkan ayaa kusoo aaday xi lli ay haatan sii xoogeysanayaan khilaafka siyaasadeed iyo iska horimaadyada u dhexeeya ciidamada taabacsan Cabdicasiis Lafta-gareen iyo kuwa taageersan maamulka hadda ka jira Baydhaba, oo garab ka helaya Dowladda Federaalka The post Xogta duqeyn culus oo lagu beegsaday ciidanka Lafta-gareen appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Falcelin aan caadi ahayn oo ka dhalatay tallaabo uu qaaday guddoomiye Jaamac
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Falcelin xooggan iyo hadal-heyn ayaa ka dhalatay tallaabo uu xalay guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac), kaas oo bogga Facebook ee Golaha ku baahiyay kulan fogaan-arag ah oo uu la yeeshay xubno ka tirsan Golaha Arlaadi Council, oo kala ah Prof. Cabdi Maxamed Kuusow, Prof. Sarmaan Ibraahim Gorodaase iyo Dr. Cali Sheegow. Kulanka ayaa diiradda lagu saaray muhiimadda ay leedahay xoojinta la-tashiyada ku saabsan arrimaha Koonfur Galbeed, maadaama ay kasii darayaan dhaq-dhaqaaqyada hubeysan ee ka jira maamulkaasi. Sidoo kale, waxaa kulanka lagu soo qaaday doorka muhiimka ah ee ay aqoonyahannada Koonfur Galbeed ku leeyihiin dib-u-heshiisiinta bulshada, nabadda, xasilloonida iyo dowlad-dhiska Koonfur Galbeed, iyadoo laga faa’iidaysanayo aqoontooda iyo waayo-aragnimadooda si loo helo talooyin wax-ku-ool ah oo horseeda nabad waarta, xasillooni iyo sidoo kale horumar. Arrintan ayaa dhalisay falcelin xooggan, iyadoo dad badan ay su’aallo ka keeneen in Page-ka rasmiga ah ee Golaha Shacabka diiradda lagu saaro xiisadda ka taagan Koonur Galbeed. Yuusuf Bashiir: “Page-kan miyuusan ahayn boggii Baarlamaanka Soomaaliya ee ka koobnaa 275 Xildhibaan ee Soomaali oo dhan ay ka koobneyd. Dhinac kasta miyaa la suurad xumeynayaa nidaamkii iyo haykalkii dawladnimo!! Madaxaa nafuran waxaaga iska Walaaqo”. Cabdixakiin Cabdullahi: “Bismillaahi Raxmaani Raxiimi, page-kii dhammaay ee Baarlamaanka miyaa isku badalay Page koonfur Galbeed logu arrimiyo?”. Siyaasiga Cali Yare Cali ayaa isna yiri “Boggaan soow kii Golaha Shacabka maaha, mise sidii xalay bogga JSP looga adeegtay ayaa isagana laga howlgalay?”. Maxamed Tahliil Cabdi: “Golohu ma waanu ahayn Golohii Shacabka ismaan dhaafku xaggee buu ka jiraa?. Shaafici Cumar Shooli: “Golihii Shacabka miyaa isku rogay pagekii Southwest State of Somalia iyo kii madaxaa nafuran waa maxey amuurtan?!”. The post Falcelin aan caadi ahayn oo ka dhalatay tallaabo uu qaaday guddoomiye Jaamac appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Somaliland denies entering into an air traffic management agreement with the Government of Somalia
items.description: Somaliland’s Minister of Civil Aviation, Fu’aad Ahmed Nuh, has denied that Somaliland has entered into an air traffic management agreement with the government of Somalia. He refuted a statement made by the Director of the Somali Civil Aviation Authority, who claimed that an agreement regarding air traffic management had been reached. In an exclusive interview with BBC Somali, the Minister stated that no new agreement has been reached between the two sides concerning aviation matters. He noted that if such an agreement existed, Somalia’s electronic visa system would be operational within Somaliland. “There is no truth to it; if an agreement had been reached, their visa would be valid in Somaliland—but it is not. If a traveler arrives at Hargeisa Airport with such a visa, it is cancelled, and they are issued a Somaliland visa instead,” the Minister said. He explained that while some individuals arrive in Hargeisa holding visas issued by Somalia, these visas do not grant them entry into Somaliland. He described this situation as detrimental to international standards, reiterating that the Somali government’s systems do not function within Somaliland. The Minister stated that the Somali government is relying on an agreement reached between the two sides in 2013, which stipulated that the management of airspace should be transferred to Somali hands. However, he accused the Somali government of subsequently taking sole control of the airspace management, thereby violating the terms of the agreement. He mentioned that a delegation from Somaliland is currently in Canada, where they intend to seek a review of that agreement and examine its impact on matters such as Somalia’s visa system. He noted that the headquarters of United Nations agencies responsible for aviation are located in Canada, and that they have filed a formal complaint regarding this issue, expressing hope for a successful outcome. The Minister also expressed concern regarding the security of Somalia’s electronic visa system, stating that the system has previously been hacked on several occasions—a situation that could jeopardize the personal data of the people of Somaliland. Somaliland standard

items.title: Itoobiya ma ixtiraamin Soomaaliya ee waa cabsatay
items.description: Markii la weydiiyay sababta ay Addis Ababa ugu dhiiran weyday inay tallaabadii Israa’iil oo kale qaaddo oo ay si rasmi ah u aqoonsato Somaliland, safiirka Itoobiya u fadhiya Tel Aviv, Tesfaye Yetayeh Anteneh, ma uusan daliishan shuruucda caalamiga ah ama xushmeynta deris-wanaagga. Taa beddelkeeda, wuxuu si toos ah farta ugu fiiqay khasaaraha baaxadda leh ee dalkiisa ka soo gaari kara tallaabadaas. “Tusaale ahaan, isla markii ay Itoobiya aqoonsato Somaliland, dowladda Soomaaliya waxay dalban doontaa in ciidamada Itoobiya laga saaro dalkeeda,” ayuu Anteneh u sheegay taleefishinka Israa’iil ee i24NEWS. Wuxuu intaas ku daray: “Al-Shabaab-na waxay heli doontaa waddo furan oo ay ku weerarto labada dhinacba — Soomaaliya iyo Somaliland,” isaga oo ka digay in xasilooni-darrada ka dhalata ay u soo tallaabi karto gudaha Itoobiya, sidaas darteedna aysan habboonayn in Addis Ababa “ku degdegto” aqoonsi. Hadalka safiirku ma ahayn mid ku doodaya in aqoonsiga Somaliland uu mabda’ ahaan khaldan yahay ama uu xadgudub ku yahay qarannimada Soomaaliya; wuxuu si cad u sharraxay sababta ay tallaabadani ficil ahaan ugu noqon karto mid qaali ah oo halis ku ah amniga Itoobiya. Farqiga u dhexeeya labadaas arrimoodna waa mid aad u weyn oo ay tahay in dowladda federaalka ee Muqdisho si qoto-dheer u dhuuxdo: Xushmeynta madax-bannaanida qaran waa inay noqotaa mabda’ joogto ah oo aan isbeddelin marka duruufuhu wareegaan. Balse haddii xakameynta gardarrada derisku ay ku xiran tahay oo keliya cabsida khasaaraha ka dhalan kara, micnaheedu waxa weeye in nabaddu ay ku xiran tahay inta uu khasaarahaasi sarreeyo oo keliya. Heshiiskii Ankara iyo xisaabta Addis Ababa Bishii Janaayo 2024, xukuumadda Ra’iisul Wasaare Abiy Axmed waxay Somaliland la saxiixatay is-afgarad muran dhaliyay oo ay ku doonaysay marin badeed ciidan iyo mid ganacsi oo ku yaal xeebaha Gacanka Cadmeed. Heshiiskaas oo hareer maray dowladda federaalka Soomaaliya, ayaa dhaliyay xiisad diblamaasiyadeed oo halis gelisay iskaashigii milateri ee labada dal iyo mustaqbalka ciidamada Itoobiya ee ku sugan gudaha Soomaaliya. Dhexdhexaadintii dowladda Turkiga ayaa keentay “Baaqii Ankara” ee 11-kii Diseembar 2024, halkaas oo Abiy Axmed iyo Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ay dib ugu xaqiijiyeen ballan-qaadkooda ku aaddan ixtiraamka madax-bannaanida, midnimada iyo wadajirka dhuleed ee labada dal. Heshiiskaas wuxuu dhidibbada u taagay qaab-dhismeed ay Itoobiya ku heli karto marin badeed ganacsi iyada oo la raacayo shuruucda iyo qarannimada dowladda Soomaaliya. Marka la barbardhigo ballanqaadyadaas sharciyeed, sharraxaadda uu safiir Anteneh ka bixiyay Tel Aviv waxay muujinaysaa xaqiiqo kale. Safiirku wuxuu si faahfaahsan uga hadlay khatarta amni ee ka dhalan karta aqoonsiga, balse ma uusan carabaabin meesha ay kaga jirto xushmeynta heshiiskii Ankara iyo madax-bannaanida dhuleed ee Soomaaliya. Tani waxay daliil u tahay in rabitaankii Itoobiya ee aqoonsiga uusan meesha ka bixin, balse waxa hadda hortaagan ay tahay xisaab amni iyo mid danaysi gaar ah. Kaarka awoodda Muqdisho iyo danta Itoobiya Itoobiya waxay ciidamo ku haysaa gudaha Soomaaliya iyada oo ku joogta dalladda Midowga Afrika iyo heshiisyo laba geesood ah. In kasta oo ciidamadaasi ay gacan ka geystaan la-dagaallanka Al-Shabaab, haddana waxa ugu weyn ee ay u joogaan Soomaaliya waa inay xakameeyaan khataraha ku soo fool leh xuduudaha Itoobiya lafteeda. Haddii Addis Ababa ay aqoonsato Somaliland, Muqdisho waxay haysataa awood sharci oo ay kaga dalban karto in ciidamadaasi ay dalka faarujiyaan. Digniinta safiirka Itoobiya waxay si dadban u qireysaa in dowladda Soomaaliya — inkasta oo ay ku tiirsan tahay taageero milateri oo dibadda ah — ay weli gacanta ku hayso kaar gorgortan oo awood leh (diplomatic and security leverage) kaas oo qasbi kara in Itoobiya ay xisaabtanto. Wakiilka Somaliland ee Israa’iil, Maxamed Xaaji, ayaa gaaashaanka ku dhuftay cabsida uu muujiyay safiirka Itoobiya, isagoo ku dooday in aqoonsigu “uusan wadan wax khatar amni ah”, ciidamada ajnabiga ahna aysan weligood sii joogi karin Soomaaliya. Balse doodda Hargeysa ma tirtiri karto xaqiiqada dhabta ah ee miiska saaran: Ka bixitaan degdeg ah oo ay ciidamada Itoobiya uga baxaan Soomaaliya burbur diblamaasiyadeed dartiis wuxuu abuurayaa faaruq amni oo khalkhal gelin kara gobolka oo dhan, waana taa waxa Addis Ababa xilligan ka hor taagan go’aankaas. Loolanka badda: Berbera mise dekedda Casab? Xayiraadaha iyo culeyska amni ee ku xeeran arrinta Somaliland waxay sidoo kale iftiiminayaan hamiga ballaaran ee Itoobiya u qabto badda, iyo haddii cabsida ka dhalatay tallaabada Berbera ay soo noolayn karto damaceedii ku wajahnayd dekedda Casab ee dalka Ereteriya. Itoobiya ma laha bad tan iyo markii ay Eritrea ay xornimadeeda qaadatay sannadkii 1993-kii, Abiy Axmed-na wuxuu helitaanka bad ku tilmaamay qaddiyad jiritaanka dalkiisa ku xiran. Xilli uu xiriirka Asmara iyo Addis Ababa meel xun marayo, warbixinno dhawaan soo baxay ayaa sheegaya in ciidamada Itoobiya ay u ruqaansadeen xadka Eritrea gaar ahaan aagga Zalambessa, iyadoo ay jiraan warar kale oo sheegaya dhaqdhaqaaqyo milateri oo ku wajahan dhanka wadada Cafarta ee aadda Casab. Khatar kasta iyo waddo kasta oo ay Itoobiya u marto helitaanka marin badeed, baahida dhaqaale ee ay u qabto badda marnaba uma siinayso xaq sharci ah inay ku tumato xuduudaha iyo madax-bannaanida dal deris ah. Su’aasha hortaalla xukuumadda Muqdisho Itoobiya waxay sheegtaa in ay xaq u leedahay inay hesho marin badeed ganacsi oo la awoodi karo laguna kalsoonaan karo, qaab-dhismeedka Ankara-na wuxuu siiyay waddo sharci ah oo lagu gaari karo danahaas iyadoo aan la dhaawicin midnimada Soomaaliya. Balse kalsoonida heshiiskaas waxay ku xiran tahay haddii ay Addis Ababa heshiiska u aragto mid joogto ah, iyo haddii ay u aragto xeelad ku-meel-gaar ah oo ay ku dhaafto culeysyada hadda taagan. Su’aasha ugu weyn ee ay tahay in dowladda Soomaaliya ay is-weydiiso ayaa ah: Maxay Itoobiya sameyn doontaa haddii berri ay yaraadaan ama meesha ka baxaan khasaarihii iyo halistii amni ee uu safiirkeedu ka digay? Qarannimada Soomaaliya ma noqon karto mid lagu badbaadiyo oo keliya in khasaaraha derisku uu markasta ka cabsanayo; dowladda federaalka waxaa la gudboon inay dhisato cududdeeda amni ee gudaha, adkeysana isbahaysiyadeeda dibadda, si aysan go’aamada masiiriga ah ee dalka ugu tiirsanaan cabsida iyo xisaab-xirka siyaasadeed ee Addis Ababa. items.title: Rag qoysaskooda oo barakac ah ka saaray nolol xumo markii ay abuurteen fursado ganacsi
items.description: (ERGO) – Cunno xumo, hoy la’aan iyo daruufo kale oo nololeed ayay qoysaskooda ka saareen tan iyo bishii May ee sanadkaan rag barakac ah oo ku nool xeryaha magaalada Diinsoor ee gobolka Bay. Waxaa u suuraagaliyay lacago ay ka amaahdeen bankiga Salaam oo ay ku furteen ganacsiyo kala duwan. Midkasta wuxuu qaatay $500 oo sanad uu ku bixinayo, maaddaama ay isku deegaan yihiin waxay wada u diyaarsadeen shuruudihii laga rabay oo damiin iyo waraaqahooda aqoonsigu ugu horeeyaan. Arintaas ayaa u sahashay in ay hal maalin lacagta wada qaataan. Waxaa damiintay dad hanti leh iyo qaar deegaanka laga yaqaano. Qaarkood waxay magaalada ka kiraystaan guryo leh biyo iyo koronto oo aysan horay u awoodin, taas oo isbeddel u noqotay. Axmed Liibaan Cali oo dadkaan ka mid ah wuxuu 7 May furtay dukaan uu ku iibiyo raashin tafaariikh ah iyo bagaash. Wuxuu u noqday il dhaqaale oo qoyskiisa ku hogaamisay nolol wanaagsan. Waxay joogto u helaan baahiyaha aas-aasiga ah oo cunnada ugu horayso, kuwaas oo horraan ku adkaa. “Maalgashi ayaan sameeyey oo kala duwaansho oo dhanka nolosha ah ayaan ku jirnaa. Xaaladii aadka u liidatay waa soo wanaagsanaatay. Qof wax awooda ayaa noqday.” Axmed wuxuu ka mid yahay 89 nin oo qorshaha daynta ka faa’iidaystay. Wuxuu sheegay in celcelis ahaan uu maalinkii ganacsigiisa ka helo $5 illaa $7. Lacagtaan oo uu u kala qaybiyo biilka reerkiisa oo 11 ah, waxbarashada carruurta, dukaanka iyo in uu ku yar yareeyo amaahda aya ka fududaysay culaysyo dhaqaale oo haystay. Axmed horay uma lahayn qibrad ganacsi, balse dadaalka iyo ka go’aanaanta shaqadiisa ayaa u miro dhalay. Ninkaan oo 47 jir ah ayaa sheegay in uu nolosha qoyskiisa ka maarayn jiray shaqooyin xamaal ah oo helitaankoodu adkaa. Mar ama labo ayuu toddobaadkii heli jiray waxaana ka soo gali jiray $3 illaa $4 oo aan wax badan u goyn jirin. Marka uu soo waayo wuxuu ku qasbanaa in uu dadka wax waydiisto. “Culaysyada iga fududaaday waxa kamid ah wagii hore maalin waa la qadi jiray ama hal wakhti ayaa dabka la shidan jiray, laakiin hadda waxaa la karsadaa saddex waqti. Dhibkaas waa ka baxay waxkasta waa u awoodaa.” Axmed iyo 11 kale oo kale waxaa damiintay nin ay isaga qaraabo yihiin, ragga kalena uu ku soo xiray oo bankiga dhigay shatiga ganacsigiisa iyo sabraloogada dhulalkiisa. Amaahda wuxuu saddexdii bil ee u danbaysay bixiyay min $25. Inta dhiman wuxuu qorshaynayaa in uu iska dhameeyo bilaha harsan. Ninkaan ayaa sheegay in qoyskiisa uu bishii September ka saaray xero barakac oo ay deganaayeen tan iyo 2024. Wuxuu xaafada Waabari ee Diinsoor uga kireeyay 2 qol iyo musqul oo bishii ah $50. Waxay ka baxeen hoy xumo haysay ku dhawaad 3 sano oo ay ku noolaayeen buush yar oo aan deeqin. Ganacsigaan wuxuu u suuragliyay in markii ugu horaysay uu iskuul hoose iyo dugsi Qur’aan ku daro shan carruurtiisa ah. wuxuu tilmaamay in ay murugo ku haysay daruus la’aantooda, balse uusan xal u hayn, maaddaama uu faro marnaa si dhib ahna uu ku heli jiray cunnadooda. “Waxaan awooday in aan ilmahayga ka bixiyo $25 bil kasta. Waxaan dhigtay kaydkii ugu horeeyay oo $50 ah, si aan ugu baxsado, marka ay culaysyo yimaadaan ama aan ganacsigayga ugu sii kabo oo ugu hormariyo.” Axmed ayaa sheegay in korontada iyo biyaha guriga ugu jira uu isku darkooda bishii iska dhiibo $14. Alaabta dukaanka u taalla iyo kaydka uu dhigtay wuxuu ku qiyaasay in ay gaarayaan illaa $1,000, taas oo rajo weyn u abuurtay. Qoyskiisu waxay ka soo barakaceen horraantii 2024 miyiga degmada Qansax-dheere ee gobolka Bay. Abaaro xilligiis jiray ayay ku waayeen intii u danbaysay 100 ari ah iyo 19 lo’ ah oo noloshoodu ku tiirsanayd. Wuxuu sheegay in daruuftii barakaca ay ka baxeen. Raggaan oo ah beeraley iyo xoolo dhaqato ay hore abaaruhu u saameeyeen waxay furteen ganacsiyo iskugu jira raashin, bagaash, khudaar iyo dhar. Guddi ay samaysteen oo caawin ka helaya ganacsato iyo waxgaradka deegaanka ayaa qorshahooda bankiga hor dhigay, iyadoo damiin laga yahay. Daa’uud Nuur Cali oo ka mid ah dadka ka faa’iidaystay amaahda bankiga Salaam. Wuxuu $15 ku kiraystay dukaan. Wuxuu billowgii u soo adeegay Khudaar iyo bagaash ay ugu baxday $300. Maalinle ayuu hadda uga helaa ugu yaraan $6 oo u noqotay il dhaqaale oo ay uga soo kabsadeen nolol xumo. “Ganacsigaan sidaan u dhexgalay waa ka ku faa’iiday. Qof ayaa gacan igu siiyay {I damiintay}. Culaysyadii waa ka soo gudbay carruurtayda si wanaagsan ayaan u maareeyaa.” Daa’uud ayaa markii hore qoyskiisa oo 8 ah ka maarayn jiray shaqooyin dhisme oo maalinka uu helo ay ka oo gali jirtay $4. Mararka qaar wuxuu sheegay in toddobaadka dhan uu waayi jiray ama uu hal maalin helayay. Bilihii Luulyo, Agoosto iyo September wuxuu sheegay in uu iska bixiyay sagaashan dollar oo dayntii bankiga ka mid ah. Waxaa ku harsan $410 oo uu sii bixin doono. Wuxuu tilmaamay in ay wax weyn uga dhigan tahay baahiyaha reerkiisa ee uu xalliyay. Sanado uu barakaca ku noolaa fursadaan oo kale ma soo marin. Dadkaan qofkasta waxaa la waydiiyay bishii inta uu bixin karo amaahda. Daa’uud wuxuu xusay in uu doortay in bil walba uu iska dhiibo $30, halka bilaha lacago dheeraad ah uu helo uu kordhin karo. “Shaqadaan ayaa ii suuragalisay dayn $50 ah oo magaalada la iiga lahaa in iska dhiibay. Guri 2 qol oo min $25 ah ayaan kiraystay. Hoy la’aanta, markii hore dhibaato ayay nagu ahayd. Buush aan roobka iyo kulaylka midna celinayn ayaan ku jirnay, Faa’iido ayaan dareemayaa hadda.” Ninkaan waxay qoyskiisa oo beeraley iyo xoolo dhaqato isku ahaa ay ka yimaadeen sanadkii 2023 deegaanka Oflow oo gobolka Bay ka tirsan. Roob yari xilligaas jirtay ayay kaga nacfi beeshay beer 3 hektar ah, waxaana uga dhamaaday 70 ari ah oo ay dhaqanayeen, taas oo barakaca ku qasabtay. Aweys Xasan Mayow oo ka mid ah dadka damiintay raggaan ayaa Raadiyow Ergo u sheegay in talaabadaan ay qoysas badan fursad u noqotay. Wuxuu tilmaamay in iyagoo reerahooda ka biilaya, dayntii yar yaraynaya, haddana uu kobac sameeyay ganacsigoodu. Ninkaan ayaa tilmaamay in illaa iyo hadda aysan soo gaarin cabasho weyn oo ku saabsan caqabado ay la kulmeen ganacsatadaan billowga ah, taas oo wax weyn uga dhigan. “Waxay gaareen isbeddel aad u wanaagsan. Qaarkood lacagta wax badan ayaa ku dhiman, balse guusha ay gaareen darteed dhawaan waa iska bixin karaan.” Aweys waa qofka damiintay Axmed iyo ragga kale ee saaxiibadiis ah. Wuxuu magaalada Diinsoor ku leeyahay bakhaar lagu iibiyo qalabka dhismaha iyo guryaha. Wuxuu xusay in talaabadaan uu u qaaday si ay nolol u helaan dadka barakacay ee waayay ilihii ay ku tiirsanaayeen. Ninkaan ayaa sheegay in ay kormeer ku sameeyaan dadkaan si ay ula socdaan qaabka ay shaqadu u tahay. Lacagaha ay billaha u bixiyaan iyo haddii ay caqabado la kulmaan in ay la xalliyaan. Wuxuu sheegay in ay u soo jeediyeen in ay samaystaan kayd dhigasho ay ku midaysan yihiin. Si haddii ay caqabad ku timaado qof ka mid ah loogu taageero. Bishii sagaallaad ayay billaabeen in ay akoon ku aruuriyaan min hal dollar oo ka dhexeeya, ayna markale u baxsan karaaan. Aweys ayaa sheegay in ay qorshaynayaan in marka ay kuwaan dhameeyaan amaahda ay dadkale damiintaan, si noloshooda ay ugu filaadaan oo barakaca ay uga baxaan qoysas badan.
