items.title: Somalia on the brink: A constitutional crisis with no clear exit
items.description: By Abdullahi A. Nor Disputed constitutional changes, rival electoral positions and deepening federal divisions raise a critical question: can Somalia reach a political settlement before the crisis escalates? Somalia is approaching a defining moment in its fragile state-building process. What began as a disagreement over constitutional amendments and the timing of national elections has developed into a wider confrontation over political legitimacy, federal authority and the rules governing the transfer of power. The central question is no longer simply when Somalia will hold its next elections. It is whether the country’s principal political actors can agree on the constitutional and electoral framework under which those elections will take place—and whether all sides will accept the outcome. The Federal Government has announced parliamentary elections for 15 April 2027 and a presidential election for 15 May 2027. Opposition leaders have challenged the constitutional changes underpinning that timetable, arguing that fundamental decisions about the country’s political future cannot be settled unilaterally. The announcement establishes dates, but it does not resolve the dispute over their legitimacy. Somalia’s central problem is that an electoral timetable cannot, by itself, settle a constitutional disagreement about who has the authority to establish the rules. The danger is that the country could approach 2027 with an official election schedule but without the political agreement needed to make the process broadly credible. A constitution without a common interpretation At the heart of the crisis is the contested revision of Somalia’s Provisional Constitution, adopted in 2012 as part of the settlement that accompanied the re-establishment of federal institutions. On 4 March 2026, parliament approved constitutional amendments that extended presidential and parliamentary terms from four to five years, shifting the expected national electoral timetable into 2027. Opposition leaders challenged the process, questioning its legitimacy and arguing that the changes lacked sufficient agreement among the country’s principal political stakeholders. The Federal Government has defended constitutional reform as part of the transition towards a more democratic system, including direct elections. Its supporters argue that Somalia cannot indefinitely retain an indirect electoral arrangement in which political elites and clan representatives exercise decisive influence over the selection of national leaders. That argument raises an important question: how long can Somalia postpone giving citizens a direct role in choosing their representatives? But the opposition raises an equally consequential question: can fundamental constitutional changes be considered legitimate when major political stakeholders dispute the process through which they were adopted? These questions are not mutually exclusive. Somalia needs electoral reform, but reform must also command sufficient political and public confidence to be implemented peacefully. Direct elections and political consensus should not be treated as opposing objectives. The controversy is particularly serious because the changes affect the duration of the mandates held by the institutions involved in making them. Constitutional amendments that alter the rules governing an incumbent administration require transparency, legal clarity and confidence that the process serves the public interest rather than the political advantage of those in power. Opponents argue that the amendments cannot legitimately extend mandates established under the previous constitutional arrangements. The government maintains that the revised framework provides the basis for its approach. The constitutional challenge therefore matters. An independent judicial determination could help clarify the legal issues, provided the court is regarded as impartial, its authority is respected and its ruling is implemented. Yet even a legal judgment may not settle the political crisis if significant stakeholders reject the process or consider the judiciary incapable of resolving the dispute fairly. Somalia needs both legal clarity and political agreement. Neither can sustainably substitute for the other. The federal compact is under strain The electoral dispute is also exposing unresolved tensions at the heart of Somalia’s federal system. The 2012 constitutional settlement established a federal structure intended to accommodate regional political authority within a unified state. However, the division of powers between Mogadishu and the Federal Member States remains contested, including the respective roles of federal and state institutions in determining national electoral arrangements. Puntland and Jubaland have emerged as prominent opponents of the Federal Government’s constitutional and electoral approach. Their objections concern not only the proposed voting system but also whether federal member states have a meaningful role in decisions that affect the entire country. For the Federal Government, direct elections represent a step towards strengthening national institutions and expanding citizens’ participation. For its opponents, the central concern is whether such a system can be introduced fairly without an agreed legal framework, credible electoral administration, adequate security and clear rules governing federal-state relations. The disagreement becomes dangerous when each side treats its own interpretation of the constitution as the only legitimate one. A federal government cannot secure a durable national settlement merely by asserting authority over the states. Equally, federal member states cannot resolve a national constitutional dispute simply by rejecting decisions taken in Mogadishu. Both levels of government must operate within a common framework that defines their powers and provides credible mechanisms for resolving disagreements. If that framework remains contested, political authority risks becoming increasingly dependent on unilateral decisions, rival claims of legitimacy and the ability of competing institutions to enforce their positions. The result could be a federal system that continues to exist formally while becoming less effective in practice. The consequences of Somalia’s political divisions are not confined to constitutional arguments. In 2026, political tensions have coincided with clashes in Mogadishu and South West State. In August, federal forces retook Baidoa following fighting involving opposition-aligned forces linked to former South West president Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen. Reports of casualties among fighters and civilians underscored the human cost of political confrontation. These events do not mean that every electoral disagreement will lead to violence. They do, however, demonstrate the risks when political factions lose confidence in negotiations and begin relying on armed mobilisation to defend their positions. Somalia is already fighting Al-Shabaab, which retains the capacity to conduct attacks and control territory. Every serious confrontation between Somali political and security actors risks diverting resources, weakening cooperation and creating opportunities for the insurgency to exploit divisions. The economic consequences could also be significant. Businesses need predictable rules, functioning institutions and confidence that political disputes will not repeatedly disrupt markets and transport. Citizens displaced by conflict and families struggling with poverty cannot afford another prolonged period of instability. Somalia’s strategic location near the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea also attracts regional and international interest. External partners can support security, dialogue and institution-building, but foreign competition may complicate domestic politics if Somali factions increasingly seek outside backing to strengthen their positions against one another. International involvement is most constructive when it supports a Somali-led settlement and reinforces common institutions. It becomes less helpful when external relationships deepen mistrust between domestic political actors. Ultimately, the responsibility for resolving Somalia’s political crisis rests with Somali leaders. What happens if the election timetable is rejected? The announced dates create a deadline, but they do not guarantee agreement on the process. Important questions remain unresolved: which constitutional provisions will govern the transition; how elections will be administered; what role federal member states will play; how political organisations will compete; and how disputes over voter registration, candidate eligibility and electoral results will be handled. If these questions remain unanswered, Somalia could enter 2027 with an official timetable but without a political settlement capable of commanding broad confidence. Three broad scenarios illustrate the risks. 1. A negotiated settlement The Federal Government, opposition leaders and federal member states could return to negotiations and agree on the constitutional provisions governing the transition, the electoral system, the respective roles of federal and state institutions, and a credible timetable. Such an agreement would not require every party to abandon its preferred political model. It would require the parties to accept that the rules of competition must be established through a process in which all major stakeholders have a meaningful opportunity to participate. The agreement could include transparent electoral administration, credible mechanisms for resolving constitutional disputes and safeguards against the use of force to settle political disagreements. This would offer the clearest route towards elections whose results have a reasonable prospect of being accepted across the political spectrum. It would also allow the government and federal member states to concentrate more resources on security, economic recovery and public services. The obstacle is that negotiations have already struggled to bridge disagreements over constitutional authority and the electoral system. A settlement would therefore require genuine compromise, not simply a renewed meeting followed by competing claims of victory. 2. Competing electoral processes and rival claims of legitimacy If negotiations fail, the Federal Government could proceed with its announced timetable while opponents refuse to recognise the process or pursue alternative political arrangements. This could deepen divisions between Mogadishu and federal member states, generate competing claims of electoral legitimacy and weaken the authority of national institutions. An election can be formally organised yet still face a serious legitimacy problem if significant political constituencies reject the rules under which it was conducted. Conversely, rejecting the federal timetable would not automatically make an alternative process lawful or nationally representative. Any competing arrangement would face its own questions about constitutional authority, participation and public acceptance. The danger is a cycle in which each side cites the other’s actions to justify unilateral decisions. As trust declines, compromise becomes politically more difficult, and institutions become instruments of competing factions rather than mechanisms for resolving disputes. 3. A deeper constitutional and security crisis The most damaging scenario would be a further breakdown in dialogue accompanied by armed confrontation between forces aligned with rival political authorities. The clashes witnessed in 2026 show that political disputes can become violent. They do not establish that wider conflict is inevitable, but they underline the potential consequences of failing to reach an agreement. A prolonged confrontation could weaken cooperation against Al-Shabaab, increase displacement, disrupt commerce and intensify regional rivalries. It could also make future negotiations more difficult as casualties, destruction and political grievances accumulate. This would not necessarily mean the formal dissolution of the Somali state. A more immediate danger would be the gradual erosion of effective national authority: institutions continuing to exist on paper while their decisions are rejected or implemented unevenly across the country. Such fragmentation could persist for years without any formal declaration of separation. Who can break the deadlock? The presidency has a central responsibility because the dispute concerns constitutional amendments, the duration of national mandates and the electoral process being advanced by the incumbent administration. But responsibility for preventing escalation does not rest with one institution alone. Opposition leaders and federal member states must also clarify what compromises they would accept and how their proposals would operate within a common constitutional order. A durable settlement cannot be built solely around preventing one faction from exercising power. It must establish rules that political competitors can accept even when they lose. Parliament must ensure that constitutional changes follow legitimate procedures. Electoral institutions must demonstrate independence, transparency and the capacity to administer a credible process. The judiciary must be able to consider constitutional disputes impartially. Security forces must remain subject to lawful authority and must not become instruments for deciding political disagreements. International partners should support inclusive dialogue and constitutional procedures rather than encourage competing factions to rely on external patrons. Their engagement is most effective when it reinforces a Somali-owned settlement rather than substitutes for one. The immediate priority should be an inclusive political process that addresses constitutional authority, the electoral model and transition arrangements together. Treating the election timetable as a technical matter separate from the question of political legitimacy is unlikely to resolve the underlying dispute. Where will Somalia’s crisis end? There is no reliable basis for declaring that Somalia will inevitably reach a negotiated settlement, descend into wider conflict or break apart. The outcome will depend on decisions that political leaders have yet to make. Somalia could still reach an agreement before the announced elections. It could also enter a period of competing electoral claims and institutional paralysis. If political confrontation increasingly intersects with armed mobilisation, the risks will become more serious. The crucial distinction is between the survival of formal institutions and the survival of a workable political compact. A government may continue to operate, a parliament may pass laws and an electoral commission may announce dates, yet the wider system can lose legitimacy if major stakeholders no longer accept the rules. Somalia’s experience since the collapse of the central state in 1991 demonstrates the enormous costs of political fragmentation. The federal settlement was intended to provide a framework for rebuilding national institutions while accommodating regional authority. Its durability depends on political actors recognising the need for both effective national institutions and meaningful federal participation. The country therefore faces a choice that extends beyond the next presidential election: will constitutional rules be established through a sufficiently inclusive process to secure political acceptance, or will each side continue pursuing its preferred outcome while disputing the authority of its rivals? The decisive test is not whether Somalia can announce an election date. It is whether the country can establish a process in which political competitors have confidence, institutions can resolve disputes and those who lose accept the result. Somalia’s crisis has no predetermined ending. But without a negotiated constitutional and electoral settlement, the country risks another cycle of disputed mandates, rival claims of authority, political paralysis and potentially renewed violence. The opportunity for compromise remains. The longer the principal actors delay, the more difficult—and costly—it may become to seize it. Abdullahi A. The controversy is particularly serious because the changes affect the duration of the mandates held by the institutions involved in making them. Constitutional amendments that alter the rules governing an incumbent administration require transparency, legal clarity and confidence that the process serves the public interest rather than the political advantage of those in power. Opponents argue that the amendments cannot legitimately extend mandates established under the previous constitutional arrangements. The government maintains that the revised framework provides the basis for its approach. The constitutional challenge therefore matters. An independent judicial determination could help clarify the legal issues, provided the court is regarded as impartial, its authority is respected and its ruling is implemented. Yet even a legal judgment may not settle the political crisis if significant stakeholders reject the process or consider the judiciary incapable of resolving the dispute fairly. Somalia needs both legal clarity and political agreement. Neither can sustainably substitute for the other. The federal compact is under strain The electoral dispute is also exposing unresolved tensions at the heart of Somalia’s federal system. The 2012 constitutional settlement established a federal structure intended to accommodate regional political authority within a unified state. However, the division of powers between Mogadishu and the Federal Member States remains contested, including the respective roles of federal and state institutions in determining national electoral arrangements. Puntland and Jubaland have emerged as prominent opponents of the Federal Government’s constitutional and electoral approach. Their objections concern not only the proposed voting system but also whether federal member states have a meaningful role in decisions that affect the entire country. For the Federal Government, direct elections represent a step towards strengthening national institutions and expanding citizens’ participation. For its opponents, the central concern is whether such a system can be introduced fairly without an agreed legal framework, credible electoral administration, adequate security and clear rules governing federal-state relations. The disagreement becomes dangerous when each side treats its own interpretation of the constitution as the only legitimate one. A federal government cannot secure a durable national settlement merely by asserting authority over the states. Equally, federal member states cannot resolve a national constitutional dispute simply by rejecting decisions taken in Mogadishu. Both levels of government must operate within a common framework that defines their powers and provides credible mechanisms for resolving disagreements. If that framework remains contested, political authority risks becoming increasingly dependent on unilateral decisions, rival claims of legitimacy and the ability of competing institutions to enforce their positions. The result could be a federal system that continues to exist formally while becoming less effective in practice. The consequences of Somalia’s political divisions are not confined to constitutional arguments. In 2026, political tensions have coincided with clashes in Mogadishu and South West State. In August, federal forces retook Baidoa following fighting involving opposition-aligned forces linked to former South West president Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen. Reports of casualties among fighters and civilians underscored the human cost of political confrontation. These events do not mean that every electoral disagreement will lead to violence. They do, however, demonstrate the risks when political factions lose confidence in negotiations and begin relying on armed mobilisation to defend their positions. Somalia is already fighting Al-Shabaab, which retains the capacity to conduct attacks and control territory. Every serious confrontation between Somali political and security actors risks diverting resources, weakening cooperation and creating opportunities for the insurgency to exploit divisions. The economic consequences could also be significant. Businesses need predictable rules, functioning institutions and confidence that political disputes will not repeatedly disrupt markets and transport. Citizens displaced by conflict and families struggling with poverty cannot afford another prolonged period of instability. Somalia’s strategic location near the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea also attracts regional and international interest. External partners can support security, dialogue and institution-building, but foreign competition may complicate domestic politics if Somali factions increasingly seek outside backing to strengthen their positions against one another. International involvement is most constructive when it supports a Somali-led settlement and reinforces common institutions. It becomes less helpful when external relationships deepen mistrust between domestic political actors. Ultimately, the responsibility for resolving Somalia’s political crisis rests with Somali leaders. What happens if the election timetable is rejected? The announced dates create a deadline, but they do not guarantee agreement on the process. Important questions remain unresolved: which constitutional provisions will govern the transition; how elections will be administered; what role federal member states will play; how political organisations will compete; and how disputes over voter registration, candidate eligibility and electoral results will be handled. If these questions remain unanswered, Somalia could enter 2027 with an official timetable but without a political settlement capable of commanding broad confidence. Three broad scenarios illustrate the risks. 1. A negotiated settlement The Federal Government, opposition leaders and federal member states could return to negotiations and agree on the constitutional provisions governing the transition, the electoral system, the respective roles of federal and state institutions, and a credible timetable. Such an agreement would not require every party to abandon its preferred political model. It would require the parties to accept that the rules of competition must be established through a process in which all major stakeholders have a meaningful opportunity to participate. The agreement could include transparent electoral administration, credible mechanisms for resolving constitutional disputes and safeguards against the use of force to settle political disagreements. This would offer the clearest route towards elections whose results have a reasonable prospect of being accepted across the political spectrum. It would also allow the government and federal member states to concentrate more resources on security, economic recovery and public services. The obstacle is that negotiations have already struggled to bridge disagreements over constitutional authority and the electoral system. A settlement would therefore require genuine compromise, not simply a renewed meeting followed by competing claims of victory. 2. Competing electoral processes and rival claims of legitimacy If negotiations fail, the Federal Government could proceed with its announced timetable while opponents refuse to recognise the process or pursue alternative political arrangements. This could deepen divisions between Mogadishu and federal member states, generate competing claims of electoral legitimacy and weaken the authority of national institutions. An election can be formally organised yet still face a serious legitimacy problem if significant political constituencies reject the rules under which it was conducted. Conversely, rejecting the federal timetable would not automatically make an alternative process lawful or nationally representative. Any competing arrangement would face its own questions about constitutional authority, participation and public acceptance. The danger is a cycle in which each side cites the other’s actions to justify unilateral decisions. As trust declines, compromise becomes politically more difficult, and institutions become instruments of competing factions rather than mechanisms for resolving disputes. 3. A deeper constitutional and security crisis The most damaging scenario would be a further breakdown in dialogue accompanied by armed confrontation between forces aligned with rival political authorities. The clashes witnessed in 2026 show that political disputes can become violent. They do not establish that wider conflict is inevitable, but they underline the potential consequences of failing to reach an agreement. A prolonged confrontation could weaken cooperation against Al-Shabaab, increase displacement, disrupt commerce and intensify regional rivalries. It could also make future negotiations more difficult as casualties, destruction and political grievances accumulate. This would not necessarily mean the formal dissolution of the Somali state. A more immediate danger would be the gradual erosion of effective national authority: institutions continuing to exist on paper while their decisions are rejected or implemented unevenly across the country. Such fragmentation could persist for years without any formal declaration of separation. Who can break the deadlock? The presidency has a central responsibility because the dispute concerns constitutional amendments, the duration of national mandates and the electoral process being advanced by the incumbent administration. But responsibility for preventing escalation does not rest with one institution alone. Opposition leaders and federal member states must also clarify what compromises they would accept and how their proposals would operate within a common constitutional order. A durable settlement cannot be built solely around preventing one faction from exercising power. It must establish rules that political competitors can accept even when they lose. Parliament must ensure that constitutional changes follow legitimate procedures. Electoral institutions must demonstrate independence, transparency and the capacity to administer a credible process. The judiciary must be able to consider constitutional disputes impartially. Security forces must remain subject to lawful authority and must not become instruments for deciding political disagreements. International partners should support inclusive dialogue and constitutional procedures rather than encourage competing factions to rely on external patrons. Their engagement is most effective when it reinforces a Somali-owned settlement rather than substitutes for one. The immediate priority should be an inclusive political process that addresses constitutional authority, the electoral model and transition arrangements together. Treating the election timetable as a technical matter separate from the question of political legitimacy is unlikely to resolve the underlying dispute. Where will Somalia’s crisis end? There is no reliable basis for declaring that Somalia will inevitably reach a negotiated settlement, descend into wider conflict or break apart. The outcome will depend on decisions that political leaders have yet to make. Somalia could still reach an agreement before the announced elections. It could also enter a period of competing electoral claims and institutional paralysis. If political confrontation increasingly intersects with armed mobilisation, the risks will become more serious. The crucial distinction is between the survival of formal institutions and the survival of a workable political compact. A government may continue to operate, a parliament may pass laws and an electoral commission may announce dates, yet the wider system can lose legitimacy if major stakeholders no longer accept the rules. Somalia’s experience since the collapse of the central state in 1991 demonstrates the enormous costs of political fragmentation. The federal settlement was intended to provide a framework for rebuilding national institutions while accommodating regional authority. Its durability depends on political actors recognising the need for both effective national institutions and meaningful federal participation. The country therefore faces a choice that extends beyond the next presidential election: will constitutional rules be established through a sufficiently inclusive process to secure political acceptance, or will each side continue pursuing its preferred outcome while disputing the authority of its rivals? The decisive test is not whether Somalia can announce an election date. It is whether the country can establish a process in which political competitors have confidence, institutions can resolve disputes and those who lose accept the result. Somalia’s crisis has no predetermined ending. But without a negotiated constitutional and electoral settlement, the country risks another cycle of disputed mandates, rival claims of authority, political paralysis and potentially renewed violence. The opportunity for compromise remains. The longer the principal actors delay, the more difficult—and costly—it may become to seize it. Abdullahi A. items.title: K/Galbeed oo shaacisay degmada u horreysa ee laga saarayo ciidanka Lafta-gareen
items.description: Baydhaba (Caasimada Online) – Dowlad-goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed ayaa maanta ku dhawaaqday inay qaadeyso guluf ka dhan ah ciidamada taabacsan madaxweynihii hor ee maamulkaas, Cabdicasiis Lafta-gareen oo todobaadkii hore qabsaday 4 degmo oo ka tirsan gobolka Baay. Wasiirka Warfaafinta Koonfur Galbeed, Nuur Siidow Baaba ayaa sheegay in gulufkooda uu ka bilaaban doono degmada Buurhakaba, ayna ka xoreyn doonaan ciidanka Lafta-gareen. Sidoo kale, wuxuu weerar afka ah ku qaaday mas’uuliyiinta la safan Lafta-gareen ee haatan ku sugan degmooyinka Qansaxdheere, Bardaale, Buurhakaba iyo Diinsoor ee gobolka Baay. “Laba saf lee loo kala bixi doonaa saf sadexaaad ma jiri doono wixii aad sheegi lahaydeen waa soo hormarsateen hadda waa xiligii laydin cirib tiri lahaaa Khalaas (1) BuurHakaba,” ayuu yiri Wasiirku. Nuur Siidow Baaba ayaa horay u ballan u qaaday in shacabka Koonfur Galbeed ay maqli doonaan war ay ku farxaan, isla markaana ay degmooyinka la qabsaday ay kusoo celin doonaan gacantooda, sida uu hadalka u dhigay. “Maalmaha soo socda shacabka reer Koonfur Galbeed waxay dhagahooda maqli doonaan wax ay aad ugu farxaan, waxaana lasoo celin doonaan neecaawdii dowladnimada. Degmooyinka ay hadda ku sugan Khawaarijta waxaa dib loogu soo celin doonaan gacanta dowladda,” ayuu raaciyay. Tallaabooyinka ayaa imaanaya xi lli ay sii xoogeysanayaan khilaafka siyaasadeed iyo iska horimaadyada u dhexeeya ciidamada Lafta-gareen iyo kuwa taageersan maamulka hadda ka jira Baydhaba, oo garab ka helaya dowladda federaalka. Si kastaba, ha’ahaatee, Hadalkan ayaa kusoo aadaya xilli ay isbeddello waaweyn ka dhacayaan gobolka Baay, halkaas oo ciidamada taabacsan Lafta-gareen ay maalmihii ugu dambeeyay si isdaba joog ah ula wareegayeen magaalooyin muhiim ah. items.title: Somalia police enter Hormuud headquarters in Mogadishu amid Southwest state tensions
items.description: MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – Somalia’s police entered two Hormuud company premises in Mogadishu on Sunday, including its headquarters in Bakara Market and its main management headquarters on the road leading to the airport, with investigations under way under a court warrant, Somali Stream reported. Initial reports suggest the investigation is linked to recent developments in Southwest state, where forces loyal to former regional president Abdiasis Laftagaren have retaken all major towns in Bay region except Baidoa. The latest advances reverse gains made by Somalia’s federal government during a March offensive that ousted Mr Laftagaren and his administration. The federal government imposed economic sanctions on Mr Laftagaren’s administration and anyone who co-operates with it. Contact us: info@somaliguardian.com

items.title: Taliyeyaasha xoogga iyo NISA oo arrin xasaasi ah la wadaagay BF + Sawirro
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Guddiga Difaaca ee Golaha Shacabka Soomaaliya ayaa maanta xarunta Guddoonka iyo Guddiyada ee Villa Hargeysa kulan gaar ah kula yeeshay Taliyaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed, Sarreeye Gaas Ibraahim Maxamed Maxamuud, iyo Taliyaha Hay’adda Nabad Sugidda iyo Sirdoonka Qaranka (NISA), Mahad Maxamed Salaad, kuwaas oo guddiga la wadaagay arrimo xasaasi ah. Kulankan ayaa qeyb ka ahaa dadaallada la xiriira diyaarinta iyo dib-u-eegista Hindise-sharciyeedka difaaca qaranka, kaas oo muhiim u ah qaabeynta siyaasadda difaaca dalka iyo xoojinta awoodda hay’adaha amniga ee mas’uulka ka ah ilaalinta madax-bannaanida iyo wadajirka dhuleed ee Soomaaliya. Sidoo kale, Kulanka oo uu shir guddoominayay Guddoomiyaha Guddiga Difaaca ee Golaha Shacabka, Xildhibaan Yuusuf Geele Ugaas, ayaa waxaa diiradda lagu saaray talooyinka iyo aragtiyada ay Taliyeyaashu ka qabaan Hindise-sharciyeedka Difaaca Qaranka, iyada oo la dhageystay soo jeedintooda la xiriirta qodobada ay muhiimka u arkaan in lagu daro sharciga. Taliyeyaasha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka iyo NISA ayaa kulanka ka jeediyay talooyin ku saabsan hindise-sharciyeedka, kuwaas oo la xiriira muhiimadda ay leedahay in la helo sharci si waafaqsan baahiyaha difaaca qaranka iyo waajibaadka hay’adaha amniga u hagaya howlaha la xiriira difaaca dalka. Dhankooda xubnaha guddiga difaaca ee Golaha Shacabka ayaa dhageystay aragtiyada ay soo bandhigeen taliyeyaasha, iyaga oo ka wada-hadlay muhiimadda ay leedahay in hindise-sharciyeedka laga tixgeliyo talooyinka iyo khibradaha saraakiisha hoggaamisa hay’adaha ugu muhiimsan ee amniga iyo difaaca dalka. Ugu dambeyn, waxaa la’isku af-gartay in talooyinka iyo aragtiyada ay Taliyeyaashu soo jeediyeen lagu daro hindise-sharciyeedka difaaca qaranka, maadaama uu muhiim u yahay dhismaha nidaam sharciyeed oo hagaya difaaca qaranka iyo howlaha la xiriira sugidda amniga dalka. Kulankan ayaa muujinaya wada-shaqeynta u dhexeysa Golaha Shacabka iyo hoggaanka sare ee hay’adaha amniga, gaar ahaan doorka ay wada leeyihiin marka laga hadlayo diyaarinta sharciyada saameynta ku leh difaaca iyo amniga gudaha Soomaaliya. items.title: Somaliland’s retired civil servants left struggling: a lifetime of service, a retirement without dignity
items.description: Pensioners say meagre monthly payments cannot cover food, rent, education and essential medicines, raising questions about the implementation of Somaliland’s pension system. HARGEISA (WDN) — After spending decades serving Somaliland’s government, many retired civil servants face a troubling question: how can they survive retirement when their pensions are insufficient to cover even their most basic needs? For former government employees, retirement can mean losing a meager, regular salary without gaining the financial security that should accompany a lifetime of public service. Some pensioners reportedly receive around $50 a month, leaving them struggling to pay for food, rent, school fees and essential medicines. The exact payment levels, number of affected retirees and extent of any outstanding arrears require official clarification. Yet the underlying concern is clear: retirement should not condemn people who served the public for decades to poverty and dependence. Many retirees spent their working lives in ministries, public agencies and other government institutions, contributing their skills and experience to the state. They now expect the government to honour its obligations and provide the pension benefits to which they are entitled. A government that demands years of service from its employees must also take responsibility for their lives after that service ends. Retirement Should Not Mean Poverty For an elderly pensioner, monthly income determines whether there is food on the table, rent can be paid and essential medicines can be purchased. When pension payments fall far below living costs, retirees are forced to depend on relatives, friends and community assistance. Those without reliable family support may face even greater hardship. The consequences extend beyond pensioners themselves. Many continue to support spouses, grandchildren and other dependants, even as their own incomes decline. For people who spent decades in public service, often without the opportunity to build substantial savings, this can be particularly painful. Retirement should bring relief from the pressures of employment, not the fear of being unable to afford food or medicine. Pensions must therefore be treated as an essential part of public-sector employment, not as discretionary assistance that retirees should accept regardless of its adequacy. A Pension Law Raises Questions About Implementation Somaliland, has established a legal framework for civil-service pensions. In January 2025, President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdillahi Cirro enacted the Pension and Compensation Agency Law, Law No. 108/2024, following its approval by the House of Representatives in December 2024. The legislation provides a framework for retirement and compensation benefits for government employees. The existence of legislation, however, does not guarantee adequate, timely or reliable payments. Key questions remain: Is the scheme being fully implemented? Are pension entitlements calculated and paid transparently? Are all eligible retirees covered? And are the benefits sufficient to meet basic living costs? The government should publish clear information on the number of registered pensioners, payment schedules, benefit calculations, funds allocated to the scheme and procedures for resolving complaints. It should also explain how years of service completed before the pension system became operational are recognised. Retirees should not have to navigate an opaque bureaucracy while waiting for benefits earned through years of public service. In August 2026, the government announced the recruitment of 1,393 employees to fill positions vacated by retiring public servants. President Cirro reportedly stressed that retirement should not end a worker’s dignity and urged government institutions to cooperate with the Pension and Compensation Authority. Those commitments establish a standard against which implementation should be judged. The key question is not simply whether a pension agency exists or younger employees are being recruited. It is whether retirees receive the benefits and security to which they are entitled. Transparency Is Essential to Public Confidence President Cirro, himself a former civil servant, faces the responsibility of ensuring that the retirement system protects the dignity of those who have served the government. Critics question the fairness of requiring employees to retire when their pensions may not provide a reasonable living. Some also suspect that replacing experienced officials could create opportunities for political patronage. These allegations have not been independently substantiated and should not be treated as established fact. Nevertheless, they underline the need for transparent, merit-based retirement and recruitment procedures. The government should explain the criteria for selecting replacement employees, how vacancies are allocated and what safeguards prevent political loyalty from taking precedence over competence. Retirement can create legitimate opportunities for younger people to enter public service. But renewal of the civil service should not come at the expense of those leaving it. Nor should retirement become a means of removing experienced officials without ensuring their financial security. Replacing a civil servant may fill a vacancy. It does not settle the government’s obligation to the person who spent a working lifetime creating that vacancy. A Warning to the Next Generation The treatment of retirees has implications for Somaliland’s wider public administration. Younger civil servants are watching how their predecessors are treated. If they believe that decades of service will end in financial insecurity, confidence in a long-term public-sector career may weaken. Inadequate retirement protection can damage morale, institutional loyalty and the incentive to develop professional expertise. Employees who lack confidence in their future pensions may feel compelled to prioritise immediate financial survival over long-term career development. This is not an accusation against civil servants. It is a warning about the institutional consequences of an unreliable retirement system. A professional civil service requires more than recruitment and salaries. It depends on predictable career structures, fair promotion, protection from arbitrary political interference and confidence that employees will be treated fairly when their working lives end. Pension reform is therefore not merely an issue for older workers. It is an investment in the confidence and stability of the entire civil service. Civil Servants Need an Effective Voice The difficulties facing pensioners raise a broader question: how can public employees collectively defend their interests when decisions about employment and retirement rest with political authorities? Serving civil servants could explore lawful ways to organise through an independent professional association or trade union, subject to applicable Somaliland law. Such a body could advocate for adequate pensions, transparent calculations, timely payments, fair recruitment and protection against political interference. It could document retirees’ experiences, engage the government in formal discussions, propose reforms and seek parliamentary scrutiny of the pension system. Where legally permitted, petitions, peaceful demonstrations and other forms of collective action could help draw attention to unresolved problems. Any industrial action should comply with applicable law and take account of the public’s dependence on essential services. The objective should be constructive pressure for a sustainable pension settlement, not disruption for its own sake. An independent assessment could also establish the cost of providing a reasonable minimum pension, examine the government’s available resources and recommend a financing model that is affordable and sustainable. The Government Must Turn Commitments into Results Somaliland’s government should now move beyond declarations of support and demonstrate that its pension system works for those it was designed to protect. First, publish the facts. Second, assess pension adequacy. Benefits should be measured against the actual cost of basic necessities, including food, housing, utilities and essential medicines. A government’s responsibility to its civil servants does not end when they retire. That is when the promise of a pension is tested most directly. HARGEISA (WDN) — After spending decades serving Somaliland’s government, many retired civil servants face a troubling question: how can they survive retirement when their pensions are insufficient to cover even their most basic needs? For former government employees, retirement can mean losing a meager, regular salary without gaining the financial security that should accompany a lifetime of public service. Some pensioners reportedly receive around $50 a month, leaving them struggling to pay for food, rent, school fees and essential medicines. The exact payment levels, number of affected retirees and extent of any outstanding arrears require official clarification. Yet the underlying concern is clear: retirement should not condemn people who served the public for decades to poverty and dependence. Many retirees spent their working lives in ministries, public agencies and other government institutions, contributing their skills and experience to the state. They now expect the government to honour its obligations and provide the pension benefits to which they are entitled. A government that demands years of service from its employees must also take responsibility for their lives after that service ends. Retirement Should Not Mean Poverty For an elderly pensioner, monthly income determines whether there is food on the table, rent can be paid and essential medicines can be purchased. When pension payments fall far below living costs, retirees are forced to depend on relatives, friends and community assistance. Those without reliable family support may face even greater hardship. The consequences extend beyond pensioners themselves. Many continue to support spouses, grandchildren and other dependants, even as their own incomes decline. For people who spent decades in public service, often without the opportunity to build substantial savings, this can be particularly painful. Retirement should bring relief from the pressures of employment, not the fear of being unable to afford food or medicine. Pensions must therefore be treated as an essential part of public-sector employment, not as discretionary assistance that retirees should accept regardless of its adequacy. A Pension Law Raises Questions About Implementation Somaliland, has established a legal framework for civil-service pensions. In January 2025, President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdillahi Cirro enacted the Pension and Compensation Agency Law, Law No. 108/2024, following its approval by the House of Representatives in December 2024. The legislation provides a framework for retirement and compensation benefits for government employees. The existence of legislation, however, does not guarantee adequate, timely or reliable payments. Key questions remain: Is the scheme being fully implemented? Are pension entitlements calculated and paid transparently? Are all eligible retirees covered? And are the benefits sufficient to meet basic living costs? The government should publish clear information on the number of registered pensioners, payment schedules, benefit calculations, funds allocated to the scheme and procedures for resolving complaints. It should also explain how years of service completed before the pension system became operational are recognised. Retirees should not have to navigate an opaque bureaucracy while waiting for benefits earned through years of public service. In August 2026, the government announced the recruitment of 1,393 employees to fill positions vacated by retiring public servants. President Cirro reportedly stressed that retirement should not end a worker’s dignity and urged government institutions to cooperate with the Pension and Compensation Authority. Those commitments establish a standard against which implementation should be judged. The key question is not simply whether a pension agency exists or younger employees are being recruited. It is whether retirees receive the benefits and security to which they are entitled. Some also suspect that replacing experienced officials could create opportunities for political patronage. These allegations have not been independently substantiated and should not be treated as established fact. Nevertheless, they underline the need for transparent, merit-based retirement and recruitment procedures. The government should explain the criteria for selecting replacement employees, how vacancies are allocated and what safeguards prevent political loyalty from taking precedence over competence. Nor should retirement become a means of removing experienced officials without ensuring their financial security. Replacing a civil servant may fill a vacancy. It does not settle the government’s obligation to the person who spent a working lifetime creating that vacancy. items.title: Barack Obama oo kashifay qorshaha Trump ka leeyahay baaritaanka Ilhaan Cumar
items.description: Washington (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynihii hore ee Mareykanka Barack Obama ayaa Axaddii ku eedeeyey maamulka Donald Trump inuu baaritaanka muwaadinnimada xildhibaanad Ilhaan Cumar u adeegsanayo cabsi-gelin siyaasadeed. Hadalka Obama ayaa yimid lix maalmood kaddib markii saraakiisha waaxda Baarista Amniga Gudaha Mareykanka (HSI) ay baareen guriga Ilhaan ee Washington. Ilhaan, oo gobolka Minnesota ku matasha Aqalka Wakiillada, ayaa beenisay inay wax sharci-darro ah sameysay. Weli wax dacwad ciqaabeed ah laguma soo oogin, waxayna bisha November u tartameysaa dib-u-doorasho. “Awoodda dowladda federaalka oo dhan ayaa lagu beegsanayaa mas’uul la soo doortay oo sharciga dhowra, sababtoo ah waxay ku dhiirratay inay dhaliisho madaxweynaha,” ayuu Obama ku qoray barta X. Obama ayaa sheegay in dowladdu aysan dad u beegsan karin aragtidooda siyaasadeed ama hadalladooda, taas oo uu ku tilmaamay mabda’ aasaasi u ah dimoqraadiyadda Mareykanka. Wuxuu dadka Mareykanka ugu baaqay inay arrintaas ka soo horjeestaan, iyadoon loo eegin mowqifkooda ku aaddan Ilhaan. Wasaaradda Caddaaladda ayaa sheegtay in garsoore uu oggolaaday baaritaanka guriga, uuna qeyb ka yahay dambi-baaris federaal ah oo weli socota. “Waxaan u arkaa qof aad u xun, laakiin arrintaas waxay u taallaa Wasaaradda Caddaaladda. Anigu wax lug ah kuma lihi,” ayuu Trump u sheegay wariyeyaasha kaddib baaritaanka. Muranka dhalashada Obama ayaa sheegay in Ilhaan ay Mareykanka timid iyadoo 12 jir ah, ayna shan sano kaddib si toos ah u heshay jinsiyadda markii aabbaheed la siiyey, iyadoo iyadu 17 jir ah. Waxa uu sheegay in baarayaashu ay daba socdaan sheegasho aan caddeyn loo hayn oo ah inay 18 jir ahayd markii aabbaheed uu jinsiyadda qaatay sanadkii 2000, sidaas darteedna ay ahayd inay si gaar ah u dalbato. Sharcigii xilligaas jiray wuxuu shardi ka dhigayey in ilmuhu ka yar yahay 18 sano si uu jinsiyadda ugu helo waalidkiis. Waxaa ku jiray qodob khuseeya carruurta uu mid ka mid ah waalidkood geeriyooday, waalidka noolna uu helo jinsiyadda, iyadoo sidoo kale ay jireen shuruudo deggenaansho. Wakaaladda Reuters ayaa Jimcihii soo werisay, iyadoo soo xiganeysa dad xog-ogaal u ah baaritaanka, in hay’adaha Mareykanka ay baarayaan in Ilhaan ama xubno qoyskeeda ka mid ahi ay xog been ah ku bixiyeen codsiyadii socdaalka ama jinsiyadda. Mid ka mid ah ilahaas ayaa Reuters u sheegay in ujeeddooyinka suuragalka ah ee baaritaanka ay ka mid tahay in Ilhaan lagala noqdo jinsiyadda, lana masaafuriyo. Wakaaladdu waxay sheegtay in amarka baaritaanka, oo aan dadweynaha loo bandhigin, lagu xusay dambiyada la baarayo ee shirqoolka, bixinta xog been ah oo la xiriirta socdaalka iyo wax isdaba marin la xiriirta socdaalka. Dhanka kale, wargeyska The Washington Post ayaa Khamiistii sheegay in saraakiisha socdaalku ay sanadkii 2019, intii uu jiray maamulkii koowaad ee Trump, eegeen diiwaannada Ilhaan, balse aysan helin caddeyn ku filan oo lagu furo baaritaan buuxa. Qiimeyntaas hore waxay taabatay su’aalo ku saabsan taariikhda dhalashadeeda iyo adeeggii ciidan ee aabbaheed oo geeriyooday uu ka soo qabtay Soomaaliya, sida uu wargeysku ka soo xigtay saraakiil hore oo socdaalka ka tirsanaa. Muranka baaritaanka guriga Qareennada Ilhaan ayaa Jimcihii dalbaday in loo soo celiyo hantidii laga qaaday gurigeeda, lana ilaaliyo duubisyadii laga sameeyey howlgalkii baaritaanka, sida ku cad warqad ay soo xigatay wakaaladda Associated Press (AP). Waxay ku doodeen in baarayaashu ay ku xadgudbeen xuquuqdeeda dastuuriga ah, ayna raaci waayeen shuruudihii uu dejiyey garsoorihii oggolaaday baaritaanka. The Washington Post ayaa sheegay in waxyaabaha lagu eedeynayo baarayaasha ay ka mid tahay inaysan marka hore la xiriirin Xafiiska La-taliyaha Guud ee Sharciga ee Aqalka Wakiillada. Tallaabadaas waxay suurtagelin lahayd la-tashi ku saabsan dokumiintiyada shaqadeeda sharci-dejinta ee laga yaabo in aan sharci ahaan lala wareegi karin. “Qareennadeenna iyo hay’adaha fulinta sharciga ee nala shaqeeya waxay u hoggaansameen dhammaan amarrada maxkamadda iyo waajibaadka sharciga, sida ay mar walba sameeyaan,” ayay tiri afhayeenka Wasaaradda Caddaaladda, Emily Covington. Baaritaanka guriga ayaa ku soo beegmay toddobaadyada ugu dambeeya ka hor doorashooyinka xilliga dhexe ee Mareykanka, xilli Wasaaradda Caddaaladdu dhaqan ahaan si gaar ah uga taxaddarto tallaabooyinka baaritaan ee si furan looga qaado musharraxiinta. Habraaca qoran ee wasaaradda ayaa mamnuucaya in xeer-ilaaliyeyaasha iyo baarayaashu ay waqtiga tallaabo ay qaadayaan u doortaan si ay saameyn ugu yeeshaan doorasho. Wuxuu sidoo kale waajibinayaa inay la tashadaan qeybta wasaaradda u qaabilsan hufnaanta hay’adaha dowladda (Public Integrity Section) marka tallaabadu dhalin karto walaac ku saabsan faragelin doorasho. “Ma aha in madaxweyne uu awoodda dowladda federaalka u adeegsado cabsi-gelinta kuwa siyaasad ahaan ka soo horjeeda,” ayaa lagu yiri qoraal ka soo baxay xafiiska Ilhaan kaddib baaritaanka. Obama ayaa sidoo kale ka digay in baaritaannadu ay dadka u keeni karaan kharash iyo dhaawac sumcadeed, xitaa haddii aan ugu dambeyn wax dambi ah lagu helin. Wuxuu arrinta Ilhaan la xiriiriyey tallaabooyin federaal ah oo khuseeya dad loo arko inay maamulka ka soo horjeedaan, oo ay ka mid yihiin xeer-ilaaliyaha guud ee gobolka New York, agaasime hore oo FBI-da ah iyo mas’uuliyiin ka tirsan bangiga dhexe ee Mareykanka. Ilhaan ayaa iyadoo yar qoyskeeda kala soo qaxday dagaalkii sokeeye ee Soomaaliya. Waxay afar sano ku qaadatay xero qaxooti oo ku taalla Kenya ka hor intaysan Mareykanka gaarin sanadkii 1995. Sanadkii 2018 ayaa markii ugu horreysay loo doortay Congress-ka, waxayna noqotay qofkii ugu horreeyey ee Soomaali-Mareykan ah ee ka mid noqda hay’addaas sharci-dejinta. items.title: Galmudug parliamentary election under fire: Opposition critics say key winners were known before voting
items.description: Dhusamareb (WDN) — What is being presented as an election for the leadership of Galmudug’s parliament has drawn criticism from opponents who argue that the outcome was largely settled before voting began, with the process resembling a formal confirmation of political arrangements already established behind the scenes. The election for speaker and two deputy speakers of the Galmudug House of Representatives is scheduled to take place today in Dhusamareb, the regional capital. Four candidates have been registered for the three positions, according to the National Independent Electoral Commission. Two candidates are contesting the speakership, representing the Justice and Solidarity Party (JSP) and the SINCAD political organisation. The two deputy-speaker positions, however, each have only one registered candidate, both from JSP. With no rival candidates registered for those posts, the deputy speakers are effectively uncontested. The composition of the parliament has added to questions about the competitiveness of the process. Critics say JSP secured 69 of the assembly’s 85 seats in earlier local elections conducted under an electoral process they allege was controlled by the president’s party and its associated electoral commission. That claim is confirmed through independent scrutiny, and if substantiated, it would help explain why the ruling party enters the parliamentary leadership contest with such a substantial advantage. Election or formal confirmation? Opponents argue that the real contest was decided before the parliamentary vote, when the assembly’s composition and party balance were established. They contend that the current proceedings are unlikely to produce a meaningful change in the distribution of power. The uncontested deputy-speaker positions reinforce that criticism. Although the speakership has two candidates, the absence of competition for the other posts raises questions about how much genuine political choice the process offers. Some critics maintain that the leading candidates and likely winners were widely anticipated at least a week before the vote. That assertion has not been independently verified, and the official results will determine who is formally elected. Nevertheless, the limited number of candidates and JSP’s reported parliamentary majority have fuelled doubts about the level of competition. The wider issue is whether the electoral arrangements have provided a fair opportunity for political alternatives to emerge—or whether earlier decisions have effectively predetermined the outcome. The next stage: choosing Galmudug’s president Once the parliamentary leadership election concludes, attention is expected to turn to preparations for the election of Galmudug’s president and vice-president. The speaker’s election is therefore more than a contest for parliamentary offices. The leadership of the assembly could influence the political environment in which the region’s next executive leadership is selected. For critics, the central concern is that an electoral process cannot be considered genuinely competitive merely because ballots are cast. Its credibility also depends on how candidates are selected, how the assembly is constituted, whether opponents can compete on fair terms and whether the outcome reflects a meaningful choice. Galmudug’s parliamentary vote may formally determine who occupies the assembly’s top positions, but the deeper test is whether the process commands public confidence. Four candidates have been registered for the three positions, according to the National Independent Electoral Commission. Two candidates are contesting the speakership, representing the Justice and Solidarity Party (JSP) and the SINCAD political organisation. The two deputy-speaker positions, however, each have only one registered candidate, both from JSP. With no rival candidates registered for those posts, the deputy speakers are effectively uncontested. The composition of the parliament has added to questions about the competitiveness of the process. Critics say JSP secured 69 of the assembly’s 85 seats in earlier local elections conducted under an electoral process they allege was controlled by the president’s party and its associated electoral commission. items.title: Awaamiir lagu adkeynayo amniga oo lagu soo rogay Baraawe iyo Waajid
items.description: Dowlad Goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed ayaa adkeysay ammaanka Degmooyinka Baraawe iyo Waajid ee Gobolada Shabellaha Hoose iyo Bakool, xilli ay jirto cabsi laga qabo inay la wareegaan ciidamada taabacsan Madaxweynihii hore ee Koonfur Galbeed, Cabdicasiis Xasan Maxamed (Laftagareen). Ka dib markii ciidamadan ay maalmihii la soo dhaafay la wareegeen Degmooyinka Gobolka Baay, marka laga soo tago Baydhabo ayaa waxay dhaqdhaqaaqyadooda is ballaarinta ay dareen ka abuureen degmooyinka kale ee ka tirsan Koonfur Galbeed, gaar ahaan kuwa Gobolka Bakool. Wararka ayaa sheegaya in Dowlad Goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed ay maanta Degmada Waajid gaysay ciidamo, ka dib markii diyaarad looga qaaday Magaalada Baydhabo. Gudoomiyaha Degmada Waajid, Xasan Cabdi Isaaq iyo Taliyaha Saldhigga Booliska, Iftiin Aadan Cali oo Axaddan si wadajir ah Warbaahinta ula hadlay ayaa ku dhawaaqay amar lagu mamnuucayo gaadiidka imanaya degmadaasi. Gudoomiyaha Degmada Waajid ayaa carabka ku adkeeyay in baabuur iyo mooto oo dhan oo imaan karaa degmadaasi aanay jiri karin, illaa 30-ka bishan October, haddii kalena loo tixgelin doono gaadiid ay leeyihiin maleeshiyada Al Shabaab. Taliyaha Saldhigga Booliska Degmada Waajid ayaa dhankiisa ka digay in la gubi doono gaadiidkii isku dayaa in uu soo galo magaalada, isagoo intaasi ku daray in muddada ay xayiraadda socoto aan la ogoleyn in sidoo kale ay gaadiidka ka baxaan magaaladaasi. Dhanka kale Maamulka Degmada Baraawe ayaa degmadaasi ku soo rogay bandow xilliga habeenkii ah, taas oo lagu ilaalinayo nabadgelyada degmadaasi. Gudoomiye Kuxigeenka Dhinaca Amniga & Siyaasadda ee Degmada Baraawe, Axmed Cabdi Yuusuf iyo Taliyaha Saldhigga Booliska, Maxamuud Sheequnaa ayaa Warbaahinta la wadaagay awaamiirta cusub ee lagu soo rogay Baraawe oo ka bilaabaneysa 8-da fiidnimo, isla-markaana soconeysa illaa waaberiga. “Magaalada waxaa lagu soo rogay bandow, kaasoo ka bilaaban doona haddii Alle idmo 8-da habeenimo. Wixii 8-da habeenimo ka bilowdo gaadiid ama qof socdo la arko, waxaa la waafajin doonnaa sharciga.” Ayuu yiri Taliyaha Saldhigga Booliska Degmada Baraawe. Taliyaha ayaa dadka deegaanka faray inay jaraan Geed Yahuudka ama Cali Garoobka, sidoo kalena ay leyrar ku xiraan afaafka hore ee guryahooda, isagoo ka digay in gurigii aan leyrka shidin loo arki doono dad ka soo horjeeda awaamiirta maamulka, sida uu yiri. Baraawe ayaa ah Xarunta Dowlad Goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed, walow maamulku uu si ku-meel-gaar ah ugu shaqeeyo Magaalada Baydhabo.

items.title: Soomaaliya iyo Turkiga oo ka wada hadlay xoojinta iskaashiga kalluumaysiga
items.description: Muqdisho (Goobjoog News) — Wasiirka Wasaaradda Kalluumaysiga iyo Dhaqaalaha Buluugga ah ee Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Axmed Xasan Aadan, ayaa kulan la yeeshay Danjiraha cusub ee Turkiga u fadhiya Soomaaliya, Ferhat Alkan, kaas oo looga hadlay xoojinta iskaashiga labada dal ee dhinacyada kalluumaysiga iyo dhaqaalaha buluugga ah. Kulanka oo ka dhacay xarunta Wasaaradda Kalluumaysiga iyo Dhaqaalaha Buluugga ah ee Muqdisho ayaa diiradda lagu saaray sidii loo horumarin lahaa iskaashiga Soomaaliya iyo Turkiga ee ka faa’iidaysiga kheyraadka badda Soomaaliya. Wasiir Axmed Xasan Aadan ayaa kulanka ku soo bandhigay muhiimadda ay leedahay horumarinta kalluumaysiga iyo maalgashiga kheyraadka badda, si kor loogu qaado wax-soo-saarka dalka, loo abuuro fursado shaqo, loona kobciyo dhaqaalaha buluugga ah. Danjire Ferhat Alkan ayaa dhankiisa muujiyay muhiimadda ay leedahay sii xoojinta xiriirka iyo iskaashiga labada dal, gaar ahaan dhinacyada ka qayb qaadan kara horumarka Soomaaliya. Kulankan ayaa qayb ka ah dadaallada lagu xoojinayo xiriirka diblomaasiyadeed iyo iskaashiga horumarineed ee Soomaaliya iyo Turkiga, iyadoo horumarinta kalluumaysiga iyo ka faa’iidaysiga kheyraadka badda ay ka mid yihiin fursadaha muhiimka u ah kobaca dhaqaalaha Soomaaliya.

items.description: MOGADISHU, Somalia — Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre received the European Union’s newly appointed Ambassador to Somalia, László Eduárd Máthé, at his office, where the two discussed strengthening relations and strategic cooperation between Somalia and the European Union.

items.title: Soomaaliya oo dib u hanatay nidaamka caalamiga ah ee tigidhada diyaaradaha kaddib 35 sano
items.description: Muqdisho (Goobjoog) — Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Soomaaliya, Xamsa Cabdi Barre, ayaa si rasmi ah u daah-furay dib u soo celinta nidaamka caalamiga ah ee tigidhada diyaaradaha ee IATA-BSP, kaas oo Soomaaliya ay dib u hanatay kaddib 35 sano. Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ayaa sheegay in dib u soo celinta nidaamkan ay ka dambeysay dadaallo muddo dheer socday, dib-u-habeyn lagu sameeyay hay’adaha dowladda, diyaarinta xeerar iyo siyaasado, iyo tababarka shaqaale awood u leh inay maareeyaan adeegyada duulista rayidka. Xamsa Cabdi Barre ayaa xusay in Soomaaliya ay horumar ka sameysay dhinacyo kala duwan, oo ay ka mid yihiin kobaca dhaqaalaha, deyn-cafinta, ku biirista Bulshada Bariga Afrika iyo la wareegista mas’uuliyadda amniga qaranka. Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ayaa sidoo kale carrabka ku adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay dib u dhiska hay’adaha dowladda iyo isku-xirka shaqadooda, isaga oo sheegay in Soomaaliya ay leedahay fursado maalgashi oo waaweyn, gaar ahaan gaadiidka, beeraha iyo wax-soo-saarka kale, maadaama ay ku taallo goob istaraatiiji ah oo isku xirta qaaradaha dunida. “Waxaa naga go’an in la sii horumariyo oo la tayeeeyo hay’adaha qaranka. Waxaan hubaa inaan gaari doonno dunida horumartay ee aan dib uga harnay 30-kii sano,” ayuu yiri Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamsa Cabdi Barre. Dhanka kale, Ra’iisul Wasaaruhu wuxuu bogaadiyay dadaallada Wasaaradda Gaadiidka iyo Duulista Hawada iyo Hay’adda Duulista Rayidka Soomaaliyeed, isaga oo ku boorriyay inay dardargeliyaan horumarinta garoomada diyaaradaha, maamulka hawada dalka iyo adeegyada duulimaadyada. Wuxuu sheegay in horumarinta adeegyadaasi ay muhiim u tahay kor u qaadista tayada adeegyada ay helaan shacabka iyo shirkadaha diyaaradaha, iyo xoojinta isku-xirka Soomaaliya iyo dunida inteeda kale. Dib u soo celinta nidaamka IATA-BSP ayaa ah tallaabo la xiriirta dib u habeynta adeegyada duulista rayidka iyo fududeynta howlaha la xiriira iibinta iyo xisaabinta tigidhada diyaaradaha ee shirkadaha ka qaybqaata nidaamka.

items.title: Hoggaamiyaha Koonfur Galbeed oo la kulmay Wakiilka Hay’adda UNDP
items.description: Hoggaamiyaha Dowlad Goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed, Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Aadan Madoobe) ayaa maanta Magaalada Muqdisho kula kulmay Wakiilka Hay’adda Qaramada Midoobey U Qaabilsan Horumarinta (UNDP) ee Somaliya, Christophoros Politis. Labada dhinac ayaa kulanka diiradda ku saaray xoojinta xiriirka wada-shaqaynta ee u dhexeeya Dowlad Goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed iyo Hay’adda UNDP, dardargelinta barnaamijyada horumarineed, dib-u-heshiisinta iyo sidii loo xoojin lahaa taageerada hay’addu siiso maamulka, gaar ahaan dhinacyada dowlad-dhiska, horumarinta adeegyada bulshada iyo kobcinta dhaqaalaha, sida lagu sheegay war ka soo baxay Madaxtooyada Koonfur Galbeed. “Hoggaamiye Sheekh Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Madoobe) ayaa adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay iskaashiga Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed iyo Hay’adaha Qaramada Midoobey, isaga oo xusay in taageerada hay’adaha caalamiga ahi ay door muhiim ah ka qaadan karto hirgelinta qorsheyaasha horumarineed, xoojinta hay’adaha dowladda iyo kor u qaadista nolosha bulshada ku dhaqan deegaanada Koonfur Galbeed.” Ayaa lagu yiri warka. Warka ayaa intaasi ku daray “Sidoo kale Hoggaamiye Sheekh Aadan ayaa muujiyay, sida ay Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed uga go’an tahay xoojinta wada-shaqaynta hay’adaha caalamiga ah, si loo xaqiijiyo mashaariic horumarineed oo wax ku ool ah, loona horumariyo adeegyada aasaasiga ah ee bulshada. Wakiilka cusub ee UNDP ee Somaliya, Mudane Christophoros Politis ayaa kala hadlay Hoggaamiyaha fursadaha lagu sii xoojin karo iskaashiga iyo taageerada dhinacyada mudnaanta u leh Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed.” Aadan Madoobe ayaa Muqdisho ka wada kulamo uu taageero siyaasadeed iyo amni uu ugu raadinayo maamulkiisa, oo cadaadis militari kala kulmaya Madaxweynihii hore ee Koonfur Galbeed, Cabdcasiis Xasan Maxamed (Laftagareen). Aadan Madoobe oo tan iyo Isniintii ku sugan Caasimadda Muqdisho ayaa muddadaasi waxaa maamulkiisa laga qabsaday Degmooyinka Buurhakaba, Berdaale, Diinsoor iyo deegaano muhiim ah oo ku dhow dhow Magaalada Baydhabo.

items.title: Aadan Madoobe oo Muqdisho kula kulmay wakiilka cusub ee UNDP Soomaaliya
items.description: Muqdisho (Goobjoog) — Hoggaamiyaha Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed, Sheekh Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Madoobe), ayaa magaalada Muqdisho kulan kula yeeshay wakiilka cusub ee Hay’adda Qaramada Midoobay u qaabilsan Horumarinta (UNDP) ee Soomaaliya, Christophoros Politis. Kulanka ayaa looga hadlay xoojinta wada-shaqeynta labada dhinac, dardargelinta barnaamijyada horumarinta, dib-u-heshiisiinta iyo kordhinta taageerada ay UNDP siiso Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed. items.title: Guddiga Difaaca Golaha Shacabka oo la kulmay Taliyeyaasha Ciidamada Qalabka Sida
items.description: Muqdisho (Goobjoog) — Guddiga Difaaca ee Golaha Shacabka Baarlamaanka Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa kulan la yeeshay Taliyeyaasha Ciidamada Qalabka Sida, kaas oo looga hadlay Hindise-sharciyeedka Difaaca Qaranka. Kulanka oo ka dhacay xarunta Guddoonka iyo Guddiyada ee Villa Hargeysa, ayaa waxaa shir guddoomiyay Guddoomiyaha Guddiga Difaaca ee Golaha Shacabka, Xildhibaan Yuusuf Geelle Ugaas, waxaana hoggaaminayay wafdiga taliyeyaasha Taliyaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed, Sarreeye Gaas Ibraahim Maxamed Maxamuud. Intii uu kulanku socday, guddiga ayaa taliyeyaasha ka dhageystay talooyin iyo aragtiyo ku saabsan Hindise-sharciyeedka Difaaca Qaranka, kuwaas oo la xiriira muhiimadda ay leedahay in sharcigu si waafaqsan baahiyaha dalka uga jawaabo arrimaha difaaca qaranka. Ugu dambeyn, labada dhinac ayaa isku raacay in talooyinka iyo aragtiyada ay taliyeyaashu soo jeediyeen lagu daro Hindise-sharciyeedka Difaaca Qaranka, iyadoo la adkeeyay muhiimadda uu sharcigani u leeyahay difaaca iyo amniga dalka.

items.title: Dagaalka Itoobiya: Colaad ka Tirsan Loollan Weyn
items.description: By: Ishaan Tharoor / October 7, 2026 W/T: Bahda Tifaftirka ee Goobjoog Haddii aad moodaysaan sheekada “burburka nidaamkii caalamiga ahaa” inay tahay hadaltiro aan dhab ahayn, kaalaya Geeska Afrika, si aad u aragtaan xaqiiqadiisii oo dhulka taalla. Dalalka gobolkan oo koobsaday buuro raf ah, togag jeexjeexyo ah iyo ban-xeebeedyo omos ahi waxay tusaale walaac leh u noqdeen casri cusub oo siyaasadda caalamka ah. Waa casri uu kan awoodda lihi muquuninayo ka laciifka ah, casri ay si joogto ah u fashilmayaan haayadihii loo dhisay nabad-abuurista, casri ay danaha dhaqaale iyo kuwa dheefdoon ee kooxo awoodo dibadeed ahi ka kormareen rafaadka rayidka. Itoobiya, loollan karkarayay muddo dheer ayaa isu beddelay dagaal furan. Dhammaadkii toddobaadkan waxay ka hortageen ciidamada dawladda iyo xoogagga isbahaysiga la ahi guluf ay soo qaadeen kooxo isbahaystay oo ka fallaagoobay xukuumadda dhexe ee Ra’iisalwasaare Abiy Axmed. Isniintiina Jabhadda Xoraynta Shacabka Tigraay (TPLF) ayaa qabsatay caasimadda gobolka Tigraay ee Maqalle. Waa jabhad ka mid ah isbahaysiga doonaya inay xukunka ka tuuraan Abiy Axmed. Qalalaase toddobaadyo socday oo ku fidsan caasimadda Addis Ababa, waqooyiga iyo illaa bariga Itoobiya ayaa keenay tobannaan waxyeello oo la diiwaangeliyay, telefoonnada iyo interneedka oo go’ay, iyo cabsi laga qabo masiibo aadaminimo. Loollanka u dhexeeya jabhadan TPLF oo hore u xuurtaysatay siyaasadda Itoobiya iyo xukuumadda Abiy Axmed waxa ka dhashay dagaal sokeeye oo bilaabmay sannadkii 2020. Dagaalkaas dadka ku dhintay waxa lagu qiyaasay lix boqol oo kun oo qof, dhinacyadana waxa lagu eedeeyay inay gaysteen dambiyo dagaal. Loollanka awoodda ee dhinacyada badan ka dhexeeya awgii, heshiiskii nabadda ee ay beesha caalamku taageertay ee Biritooriya sannadkii 2022 lagu gaaray isna muu waarin; taas ayaa jidka u jeexday fajacan cusub. Xaalka Itoobiya wuxuu u madowyahay sida uu waaqaceedu u murugsanyahay, waayo waa dawladda labaad ee ugu dadka badan Afrika, waana hoyga tobannaan qowmiyadood. Iyada oo ay taasi jirto waxaa xaaladda uga sii daraya xiisadaha kale ee gobolka. Dagaalka sokeeye ee ka socda Suudaan oo deris la ah ayaa saamayn ku leh colaadda ka soo cusboonaatay Itoobiya. Warbixinno ayaa sheegay inay xukuumadda Abiy Axmed lug ku leedahay tababarka Xoogagga Gurmadka Degdegga (RSF), kuwaas oo ah ciidamo milatari-la-mood ah oo gacanta ku haya qaybo badan oo galbeedka Suudaan ah. Waxa lagu eedeeyay ciidamadan gaboodfallo iyo xasuuqyo fara badan oo ay u gaysteen rayidka intii uu socday dagaalka ay kula jiraan ciidanka qaranka Suudaan. Taas lidkeeda, sida ay warbixinnadu sheegayaan, dagaalyahanno Tigraay ah ayaa ka soo muuqday barbarka Ciidanka Qaranka Suudaan ee dagaalka kula jira RSF. (Dagaalkii hore ee 2020, ciidamada Ereteriya waxay caawinayeen ciidanka Itoobiya, balse hadda Ereteriya waxay taageeraysaa fallaagada Tigraayga). Arrinkaasi wuxuu keenay inay Itoobiya cayriso toban diblomaasi oo Ereteriyiin ah iyo inay xirto toddobaadkii tegay safaaraddeedii caasimadda Ereteriya ee Asmara. Ereteriya ayaa iyaduna dhankeeda jartay xiriirkii diblomaasiyadeed ee ay la lahayd Itoobiya. Toddobaadkii tegay taliyaha ciidanka Itoobiya ayaa ku eedeeyay dawladaha Masar, Ereteriya iyo Ciidanka Qaranka Suudaan inay sii kicinayaan fallaagadan cusub. Dhammaan xukuumadaha dalalkaasi waxay soo saareen baaqyo ay eeddaas ku beeninayaan. Toddobaadka dhammaadkiisii waxay madaxda dalalkaasi Masar kula kulmeen madaxweynaha Soomaaliya, kaas oo isaguna dhankiisa ku diiddan Abiy Axmed xiriirka furfuran ee uu la leeyahay Soomaaliland, oo ah jamhuuriyad ismaamul gaar ah leh oo ku dhawaaqday inay ka madaxbannaan tahay Soomaaliya inteeda kale, in kasta oo ay ku jirto xuduudda Soomaaliya caalamku u aqoonsan yahay. Waxay soo saareen afarta dal baaq ay ku sheegeen dulmiga ay ku qabaan himilooyinka ay Itoobiya ku doonayso inay ku gaarto Badda Cas iyo inay biyaxireen weyn ka dhistay webiga Niil iyo inay diiddan yihiin aqoonsi ama taageero kasta oo la siiyo Soomaalilaan. (Israa’iil ayaa ah dawladda qura ee ka tirsan Qaramada Midoobay ee xiriir rasmi ah leh maamulka Soomaalilaan). Abiy Axmed oo ka jawaabayay eedaymahaas ayaa isniintii sheegay inay Itoobiya raadsanayso marin badeed, taas oo ay doonayso inay hadda ku soo ceshato xiriir ay la yeelato Soomaalilaan oo deris la ah. Haddii aad moodaysaan xaaladda aan ka soo sheekeeyay inay murugsantahay, wax yar suga! Daaha gadaashiisa wadaa ka socda qorshayaal iyo dano ay riixayaan awoodo waaweyn. Awoodahaas waxaa ka mid ah boqortooyooyinka Khaliijka sida Imaaraadka, Sucuudiga iyo Gadar, oo lagu daray Turkiga iyo Masar. Dhammaantood waxay lugaha kula jiraan dheeshan danaha iyo dagaalka ah ee fidsan laga bilaabo Liibiyada ay dagaalladu qurbeen ee Badda Cad illaa Yamanta ay colaaddu qaybisay ee Badda Cas. Dagaalladan waxaa hurinaya tartanka loogu jiro qabsashada marinnada istaraatiijiga ah iyo khayraadka dheefta leh sida shidaalka, macdanta halbawlaha, biyaha, iyo loollan ballaaran oo loogu jiro saamaynta juquraafi-siyaasadeed ee gobolka. Tartanka dawladahan ka dhexeeyaa wuxuu ka muuqdaa dagaallada wakaaladeed. Suudaan tusaale ahaan, Imaaraadku wuxuu maal iyo hub ku taageeraa Ciidanka Gurmadka Degdegga ah (RSF), halka ay Sucuudiga, Masar iyo Gadar barbar joogaan Ciidanka Qaranka Suudaan (SAF). Sidoo kale Soomaaliya waxa joogis ciidan oo xooggan ku leh Turkiga, dhanka Soomaalilaan Imaaraadka iyo Israa’iil oo ah awoodo liddi ku ah isaga ayaa degaan ka samaystay. (Kulan lagu qabtay magaalada Niyuu Yook bishii hore wuxuu igu yiri madaxweynaha Soomaaliland, Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi, in kasta oo ay tuhunno iska jiraan, ciidan Israa’iil leedahay ma joogaan Soomaaliland xilligan). Wuxuu igu yiri Alex Rondos oo ahaa ergaygii gaarka ahaa ee Midowga Yurub u fadhiyi jiray gobolkani: “wuxuu noqday Geeska Afrika qayb qalqalsan oo ka mid ah siyaasadda qarriban ee Bariga Dhexe.” Wuxuu intaas ku daray inuu dagaalka Itoobiya ka dhigan yahay “isku milan iyo in loo sii dhawaanayo wax ballaaran oo halis ah.” Iyana Michelle Gavin oo ah diblomaasiyad Maraykan ah oo hore, isla markaana ahayd guddoomiyaha koowaad ee arrimaha Afrika ee Golaha Amniga Qaran ee maamulkii Obaama, waxay aragtaa taxane loolanno is hirdiyaya oo la moodo inay isugu biyashubanayaan hal loollan oo weyn. Waxay tiri Gavin: “waxa la moodaa inaan balaayo saadinayo, balse waxa jira xasarado meelo badan ka jira oo ku xirmaya xasarado kale, iyada oo ay dhici karto xiisad meel ka kacday inay isu rogi karto xiisad gobolka oo dhan ka oogan.” Waxaa socda dadaallo lagaga hortagayo inuu oogmo dab shaamil ahi, waxayse u muuqdaan kuwo aan mira dhalayn. Tusaale ahaan Suudaan, ururro kala duwan iyo awoodo shisheeye ayaa waxba ka qaban waayay dagaalka, sida kooxda “Afarleyda” oo kala ah Maraykanka, Imaaraadka, Masar iyo Sucuudiga, iyo kooxda “Shanleyda” oo ah shan urur oo caalami ah oo ay ku jiraan Midawga Afrika iyo Midawga Yurub. Dhammaantood way ku guuldarraysteen inay joojiyaan dagaalkan galay sannadkiisii afraad, ee barakiciyay saddex meelood meel dadweynaha Suudaan, isla markaana gargaar aadaminimo u baahiyay in ka badan 65% shacabka. Baaq wadajir ah oo ay soo saareen ururrada gargaarka aadaminimo oo la baahiyay Isniintii ayaa ka digay in yaraanta gargaarka aadaminimo iyo dagaalka socdaa ay halis gelinayaan waxsoosaarka beeraha Suudaan ee sannadkan. Arrinkan waxa ka dhalanaya inay sii korodho baahida Suudaan oo markii horaba ahayd masiibada gaajo ee ugu daran caalamka. Dawlado Bariga Dhexe ah oo dano ka leh ayaa weli sii hurinaya loollanka, iyada oo aysan muuqan dhinacyo kale oo dibadeed oo qabanqaabin kara saamayn loogu qanciyo dhinacyada dagaallamaya inay colaadda joojiyaan. Dhinacyada dibadeed ee aan sheegayo waxaa ka mid ah Maraykanka, gaar ahaanna maamulka Taraam oo sameeyay dhaqdhaqaaqyo “qawda maqashii, waxna ha u qaban” ah, oo uu ku sheegay inuu doonayo joojinta loollanka Suudaan. Waxaa la sameeyay wareegyo wadahadallo ah, balse gorfeeyayaal ayaa sheegay inay faragelinta Maraykanku ahayd mid korkaxaadis ah oo aan waxba ku filnayn. Maamulkii madaxweyne Baydhan wuxuu kaalin ka qaatay inuu dhammeeyo colaaddii Tigraay sannadkii 2022, balse maamulkii ka danbeeyay ee Taraam “wuxuu garabka saaray dhinaca Abiy”, sida uu ku qoray Cameron Hudson mareegta Semafor, kaas oo mar hayay xilka guddoomiyaha arrimaha Afrika ee Golaha Amniga Qaranka ee xilligii madaxweyne Buush. Wuxuu xusay inuu maamulka Taraam ahmiyadda siiyay heshiisyo ganacsi oo waaweyn, oo diyaarado Maraykan ah lagaga iibinayay Itoobiya, iyo inuu maamulka Taraam cunaqabatayn ku soo rogay qaar ka mid ah masuuliyiinta Tigraay xilli hore oo sannadkan ah. Alex Rondos wuxuu igu yiri, Maraykanka “waxa looga yaqaannay gobolkan askariga waddamarista ee ugu sarreeya”, balse imika “waaqic ahaan wuu ka maqan yahay meesha”; taasina waxay ku abuurtay xukuumadaha gobolka “shucuur ah ciqaabo ma jirto, ee waxaad doonto samee.” Nuxurkoob siyaasadeed oo uu xilli hore oo sannadkan ah qoray Alex Rondos wuxuu ku sheegay inay laba garab ka abuurmayaan Geeska Afrika. “Garab wuxuu sheeganayaa inuu difaacayo madaxbannaanida iyo midnimada dawladaha ee hore u jirtay”; taasna waxa laga fahmi karaa khudbadihii madaxda Masar, Ereteriya iyo Soomaaliya ee toddobaadkii tegay iyo khudbadaha dawladaha iyaga taageera ee Turkiga iyo Sucuudiga. Arrinkaasi wuxuu ka soo horjeedaa danaha xukuumadaha Itoobiya, Imaaraadka iyo xitaa Israa’iil. Waa dawlado doonaya “inay qabsadaan marinnada istaraatiijiga ah, khayraadka iyo silsiladaha sahayda, oo aan dan ka lahayn qeexitaankii soojireenka ahaa ee talisgoboleedyada.” Wuxuu u muuqdaa maamulka Taraam inuu siyaasad ahaan iyo abuur ahaanba u janjeero garabka danbe. Isaga oo fursaddan ka faa’iidaysanaya, Madaxweyne Cabdiraxmaan Cirro wuxuu Aqalka Cad ku cadaadiyay inay aqoonsadaan Soomaalilaan. Wuxuu soo bandhigay dalabyo ay ka mid yihiin inuu madaar weyn ugu magacdari doono madaxweyne Taraam, iyo inay Hargeysa ka dhisi doonaan “Sarta Taraam.” Waxay tiri Gavin oo imika ka shaqaysa Golaha Xiriirka Arrimaha Dibaddu: “heshiisyada danaysiga ah ee awoodaha shisheeye iyo colaadda sii baahaysa ee ay shidaalinayaan waa astaamaha juquraafi-siyaasadeedka cusub.” Waxay intaas ku dartay: “jidkan cusub ee la raacay ee ah (lacagta ayaa hadlaysa), fashilka ku yimi haayadihii qaramada ee diblomaasiyadda kaga hortagi jiray ismaandhafyada, iyo dagaallada wakaaladeed ee ay dhinacyada saamaynta ku tartamayaa ku daadinayaan dhiigga Afrikaanka, dhammaan arrimahaasi waa astaamo murugo leh oo ina tusaya heerka aynu gaarnay.”
