Abiy Axmed oo ka jawaabayay eedaymahaas ayaa isniintii sheegay inay Itoobiya raadsanayso marin badeed, taas oo ay doonayso inay hadda ku soo ceshato xiriir ay la yeelato Soomaalilaan oo deris la ah. Haddii aad moodaysaan xaaladda aan ka soo sheekeeyay inay murugsantahay, wax yar suga! Daaha gadaashiisa wadaa ka socda qorshayaal iyo dano ay riixayaan awoodo waaweyn. Awoodahaas waxaa ka mid ah boqortooyooyinka Khaliijka sida Imaaraadka, Sucuudiga iyo Gadar, oo lagu daray Turkiga iyo Masar. Dhammaantood waxay lugaha kula jiraan dheeshan danaha iyo dagaalka ah ee fidsan laga bilaabo Liibiyada ay dagaalladu qurbeen ee Badda Cad illaa Yamanta ay colaaddu qaybisay ee Badda Cas. Dagaalladan waxaa hurinaya tartanka loogu jiro qabsashada marinnada istaraatiijiga ah iyo khayraadka dheefta leh sida shidaalka, macdanta halbawlaha, biyaha, iyo loollan ballaaran oo loogu jiro saamaynta juquraafi-siyaasadeed ee gobolka. Tartanka dawladahan ka dhexeeyaa wuxuu ka muuqdaa dagaallada wakaaladeed. Suudaan tusaale ahaan, Imaaraadku wuxuu maal iyo hub ku taageeraa Ciidanka Gurmadka Degdegga ah (RSF), halka ay Sucuudiga, Masar iyo Gadar barbar joogaan Ciidanka Qaranka Suudaan (SAF). Sidoo kale Soomaaliya waxa joogis ciidan oo xooggan ku leh Turkiga, dhanka Soomaalilaan Imaaraadka iyo Israa’iil oo ah awoodo liddi ku ah isaga ayaa degaan ka samaystay. (Kulan lagu qabtay magaalada Niyuu Yook bishii hore wuxuu igu yiri madaxweynaha Soomaaliland, Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi, in kasta oo ay tuhunno iska jiraan, ciidan Israa’iil leedahay ma joogaan Soomaaliland xilligan). Wuxuu igu yiri Alex Rondos oo ahaa ergaygii gaarka ahaa ee Midowga Yurub u fadhiyi jiray gobolkani: “wuxuu noqday Geeska Afrika qayb qalqalsan oo ka mid ah siyaasadda qarriban ee Bariga Dhexe.” Wuxuu intaas ku daray inuu dagaalka Itoobiya ka dhigan yahay “isku milan iyo in loo sii dhawaanayo wax ballaaran oo halis ah.” Iyana Michelle Gavin oo ah diblomaasiyad Maraykan ah oo hore, isla markaana ahayd guddoomiyaha koowaad ee arrimaha Afrika ee Golaha Amniga Qaran ee maamulkii Obaama, waxay aragtaa taxane loolanno is hirdiyaya oo la moodo inay isugu biyashubanayaan hal loollan oo weyn. Waxay tiri Gavin: “waxa la moodaa inaan balaayo saadinayo, balse waxa jira xasarado meelo badan ka jira oo ku xirmaya xasarado kale, iyada oo ay dhici karto xiisad meel ka kacday inay isu rogi karto xiisad gobolka oo dhan ka oogan.” Waxaa socda dadaallo lagaga hortagayo inuu oogmo dab shaamil ahi, waxayse u muuqdaan kuwo aan mira dhalayn. Tusaale ahaan Suudaan, ururro kala duwan iyo awoodo shisheeye ayaa waxba ka qaban waayay dagaalka, sida kooxda “Afarleyda” oo kala ah Maraykanka, Imaaraadka, Masar iyo Sucuudiga, iyo kooxda “Shanleyda” oo ah shan urur oo caalami ah oo ay ku jiraan Midawga Afrika iyo Midawga Yurub. Dhammaantood way ku guuldarraysteen inay joojiyaan dagaalkan galay sannadkiisii afraad, ee barakiciyay saddex meelood meel dadweynaha Suudaan, isla markaana gargaar aadaminimo u baahiyay in ka badan 65% shacabka. Baaq wadajir ah oo ay soo saareen ururrada gargaarka aadaminimo oo la baahiyay Isniintii ayaa ka digay in yaraanta gargaarka aadaminimo iyo dagaalka socdaa ay halis gelinayaan waxsoosaarka beeraha Suudaan ee sannadkan. Arrinkan waxa ka dhalanaya inay sii korodho baahida Suudaan oo markii horaba ahayd masiibada gaajo ee ugu daran caalamka. Dawlado Bariga Dhexe ah oo dano ka leh ayaa weli sii hurinaya loollanka, iyada oo aysan muuqan dhinacyo kale oo dibadeed oo qabanqaabin kara saamayn loogu qanciyo dhinacyada dagaallamaya inay colaadda joojiyaan. Dhinacyada dibadeed ee aan sheegayo waxaa ka mid ah Maraykanka, gaar ahaanna maamulka Taraam oo sameeyay dhaqdhaqaaqyo “qawda maqashii, waxna ha u qaban” ah, oo uu ku sheegay inuu doonayo joojinta loollanka Suudaan. Waxaa la sameeyay wareegyo wadahadallo ah, balse gorfeeyayaal ayaa sheegay inay faragelinta Maraykanku ahayd mid korkaxaadis ah oo aan waxba ku filnayn. Maamulkii madaxweyne Baydhan wuxuu kaalin ka qaatay inuu dhammeeyo colaaddii Tigraay sannadkii 2022, balse maamulkii ka danbeeyay ee Taraam “wuxuu garabka saaray dhinaca Abiy”, sida uu ku qoray Cameron Hudson mareegta Semafor, kaas oo mar hayay xilka guddoomiyaha arrimaha Afrika ee Golaha Amniga Qaranka ee xilligii madaxweyne Buush. Wuxuu xusay inuu maamulka Taraam ahmiyadda siiyay heshiisyo ganacsi oo waaweyn, oo diyaarado Maraykan ah lagaga iibinayay Itoobiya, iyo inuu maamulka Taraam cunaqabatayn ku soo rogay qaar ka mid ah masuuliyiinta Tigraay xilli hore oo sannadkan ah. Alex Rondos wuxuu igu yiri, Maraykanka “waxa looga yaqaannay gobolkan askariga waddamarista ee ugu sarreeya”, balse imika “waaqic ahaan wuu ka maqan yahay meesha”; taasina waxay ku abuurtay xukuumadaha gobolka “shucuur ah ciqaabo ma jirto, ee waxaad doonto samee.” Nuxurkoob siyaasadeed oo uu xilli hore oo sannadkan ah qoray Alex Rondos wuxuu ku sheegay inay laba garab ka abuurmayaan Geeska Afrika. “Garab wuxuu sheeganayaa inuu difaacayo madaxbannaanida iyo midnimada dawladaha ee hore u jirtay”; taasna waxa laga fahmi karaa khudbadihii madaxda Masar, Ereteriya iyo Soomaaliya ee toddobaadkii tegay iyo khudbadaha dawladaha iyaga taageera ee Turkiga iyo Sucuudiga. Arrinkaasi wuxuu ka soo horjeedaa danaha xukuumadaha Itoobiya, Imaaraadka iyo xitaa Israa’iil. Waa dawlado doonaya “inay qabsadaan marinnada istaraatiijiga ah, khayraadka iyo silsiladaha sahayda, oo aan dan ka lahayn qeexitaankii soojireenka ahaa ee talisgoboleedyada.” Wuxuu u muuqdaa maamulka Taraam inuu siyaasad ahaan iyo abuur ahaanba u janjeero garabka danbe. Isaga oo fursaddan ka faa’iidaysanaya, Madaxweyne Cabdiraxmaan Cirro wuxuu Aqalka Cad ku cadaadiyay inay aqoonsadaan Soomaalilaan. Wuxuu soo bandhigay dalabyo ay ka mid yihiin inuu madaar weyn ugu magacdari doono madaxweyne Taraam, iyo inay Hargeysa ka dhisi doonaan “Sarta Taraam.” Waxay tiri Gavin oo imika ka shaqaysa Golaha Xiriirka Arrimaha Dibaddu: “heshiisyada danaysiga ah ee awoodaha shisheeye iyo colaadda sii baahaysa ee ay shidaalinayaan waa astaamaha juquraafi-siyaasadeedka cusub.” Waxay intaas ku dartay: “jidkan cusub ee la raacay ee ah (lacagta ayaa hadlaysa), fashilka ku yimi haayadihii qaramada ee diblomaasiyadda kaga hortagi jiray ismaandhafyada, iyo dagaallada wakaaladeed ee ay dhinacyada saamaynta ku tartamayaa ku daadinayaan dhiigga Afrikaanka, dhammaan arrimahaasi waa astaamo murugo leh oo ina tusaya heerka aynu gaarnay.”

items.title: Somaliland Geostrategy: Geography, Power and Regional Influence
items.description: Introduction: When Geography Becomes Strategy In international politics, geography is never merely about where a country is located. It is about access, influence, security, trade, and the ability to shape events beyond national borders. Some territories acquire strategic importance because of their natural resources; others because of their military capabilities, economic strength, or diplomatic networks. A few possess a geographical position that places them at the intersection of several major international interests. Somaliland belongs in this last category. Located in the Horn of Africa, along the southern approaches to the Gulf of Aden, Somaliland occupies a position overlooking one of the world’s most important maritime corridors. Its proximity to the Red Sea, the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, the Arabian Peninsula, and the wider Indian Ocean gives it strategic relevance that extends well beyond its territorial size. A major diplomatic development has added a new dimension to this strategic position. On 26 December 2025, Israel formally recognized the Republic of Somaliland as an independent and sovereign state, becoming the first country to do so since Somaliland restored its independence in 1991. The announcement marked an important development in Somaliland’s pursuit of international recognition and opened a new chapter in its bilateral relations. [1] Yet geography and diplomatic recognition alone do not guarantee power. The central question is whether Somaliland can transform its location and emerging international relationships into sustainable economic opportunities, credible security partnerships, stronger diplomatic engagement, and meaningful regional influence. Understanding Somaliland’s geostrategy therefore requires examining the relationship between geography, state capacity, maritime commerce, international recognition, regional competition, and the changing distribution of power across the Horn of Africa. The Geography of Strategic Opportunity The Horn of Africa connects Africa, the Middle East, and the wider Indo-Pacific trading system. The Gulf of Aden serves as a maritime gateway between the Indian Ocean and the Red Sea, through which ships travel toward the Suez Canal and Mediterranean markets. This corridor matters to global commerce, energy transportation, supply chains, and international security. Instability around the Bab al-Mandeb Strait can affect shipping costs, insurance premiums, delivery times, and the calculations of governments and commercial operators worldwide. Somaliland’s northern coastline, including the area around Berbera, places it close to these strategic routes. This creates opportunities for port development, logistics, maritime services, fisheries, and international commercial partnerships. However, proximity to a major shipping lane should not be confused with control over it. Somaliland does not control the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, and its strategic value depends on its ability to provide reliable infrastructure, effective governance, and a secure environment for legitimate commercial activity. The distinction is important: geography creates potential, but policy determines how much of that potential can be realised. Berbera: From Port Infrastructure to Geo-economic Influence Berbera is central to Somaliland’s economic and strategic outlook. Its port offers the possibility of connecting maritime trade with inland markets, particularly Ethiopia, one of Africa’s most populous countries and a major economy without direct access to the sea. For Ethiopia, diversified access to ports is a significant economic and strategic consideration. For Somaliland, Berbera provides an opportunity to position itself as a commercial gateway serving regional trade, transport, and logistics. The Berbera corridor could help strengthen connections between maritime infrastructure and inland economic activity. Its long-term value, however, will depend on road networks, customs efficiency, competitive costs, dependable services, and cooperation among the relevant authorities. A successful port strategy requires more than expanding physical capacity. It requires building an integrated economic ecosystem involving warehousing, freight services, transport operators, financial institutions, insurance providers, and businesses that create jobs. If developed effectively, Berbera could become more than a port. It could serve as an instrument of geoeconomic influence: a means through which Somaliland builds mutually beneficial relationships with neighbouring economies and international commercial partners. The strategic objective should not be to turn trade into a weapon of political pressure. It should be to make cooperation economically attractive, commercially reliable, and beneficial to all participating parties. Ethiopia and the Strategic Politics of Sea Access Ethiopia’s need for dependable maritime access is one of the defining geopolitical questions in the Horn of Africa. Its reliance on external ports exposes its economy to transportation costs, logistical bottlenecks, and political developments beyond its borders. Somaliland’s location and the Berbera corridor create a basis for practical cooperation on these challenges. Such cooperation could encompass port services, transit arrangements, transport infrastructure, trade facilitation, and long-term investment. Nevertheless, maritime access is a complex issue involving sovereignty, international law, regional diplomacy, and the interests of multiple states. Commercial arrangements and any proposals involving special access rights must be assessed through careful negotiations and clear legal frameworks. For Somaliland, the most sustainable strategy is to demonstrate that cooperation can produce measurable economic benefits while respecting regional stability and the legitimate interests of all parties. For Ethiopia, diversified and commercially viable access arrangements could support economic resilience and reduce dependence on any single route. For the wider region, transparent agreements and practical cooperation would be preferable to escalating rivalries over ports and maritime access. The question is not simply who gains access to the sea. It is whether regional actors can build a framework in which maritime connectivity becomes a source of shared prosperity rather than confrontation. The Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden, and Maritime Security The strategic importance of Somaliland is inseparable from the wider security environment surrounding the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Piracy, armed conflict, attacks on commercial shipping, illicit trafficking, and geopolitical competition have demonstrated how quickly insecurity in this region can affect global trade. The interests of regional and international powers increasingly intersect around maritime routes, port infrastructure, military facilities, and security partnerships. Somaliland can contribute to regional stability by strengthening maritime domain awareness, developing effective coastguard and law-enforcement capabilities, combating illicit trafficking, protecting legitimate commercial activity, and cooperating with appropriate regional and international partners. Such efforts require investment in training, communications, surveillance, institutional accountability, and clear legal procedures. Maritime security should also be understood in economic terms. Safer shipping routes, predictable port operations, and effective law enforcement can reduce commercial risk and make the region more attractive to investors. Somaliland’s strategic contribution would be strongest if it were based on practical capabilities and responsible cooperation rather than geopolitical rhetoric alone. Israel’s Recognition of Somaliland: A New Diplomatic Chapter On 26 December 2025, the State of Israel formally recognised the Republic of Somaliland as an independent and sovereign state. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced the decision following a joint declaration involving Israel’s leadership and Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, commonly known as Cirro. The announcement made Israel the first country to formally recognise Somaliland since its restoration of independence in 1991. This development represents an important milestone in Somaliland’s diplomatic history. For more than three decades, Somaliland had pursued international recognition while developing its own governing institutions, conducting elections, and maintaining a distinct political and administrative system. Israel’s recognition introduces a new dimension to Somaliland’s international engagement. It creates a formal basis for bilateral relations and the potential development of cooperation in areas including agriculture, healthcare, technology, economic development, and maritime security. The extent to which these opportunities produce lasting benefits will depend on the agreements, institutions, and practical initiatives developed by both governments. The decision also has a wider geopolitical context. Israel’s interest in Somaliland intersects with the strategic significance of the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, where maritime security, international trade, and regional competition are increasingly interconnected. For Somaliland, the recognition presents an opportunity to expand diplomatic engagement and demonstrate its capacity to build constructive international partnerships. It may also encourage further discussion among policymakers and analysts about Somaliland’s role in regional security, economic connectivity, and the evolving political landscape of the Horn of Africa. However, the diplomatic implications should be assessed realistically. Recognition by Israel does not automatically mean that other countries will follow, nor does it establish universal international recognition or membership in the United Nations. The decision also generated opposition from Somalia’s federal government and criticism from several regional actors, who raised concerns about Somalia’s territorial integrity and the potential implications for regional stability. These reactions underline the importance of continued diplomatic engagement and peaceful management of disagreements. For Somaliland, the strategic challenge is to build on the recognition through substantive cooperation, economic development, and further diplomatic outreach. Its international engagement will be more sustainable if it combines the pursuit of recognition with transparent institutions, practical economic achievements, and constructive relations with neighbouring states. The central question is no longer only whether Somaliland can attract international attention. It is how Somaliland can translate an important diplomatic development into lasting institutional, economic, and strategic benefits. Somaliland in a Multipolar World The Horn of Africa is increasingly shaped by overlapping interests involving Gulf states, Türkiye, China, the United States, European countries, and regional powers. These actors do not necessarily share the same priorities: some focus on trade and investment, others on maritime security, political partnerships, military access, or broader competition for influence. Israel’s recognition adds another dimension to this evolving environment, but it does not remove the need for Somaliland to maintain a broad and balanced approach to international relations. A wider range of potential partners could support infrastructure development, investment, technological exchange, and diplomatic engagement. However, competition among external powers can also place pressure on smaller political actors to align themselves with one side against another. Somaliland’s most effective approach would be a form of strategic pragmatism: engaging partners according to clearly defined national interests while avoiding unnecessary dependence on any single external power. Such an approach would require transparent investment agreements, sound financial management, careful assessment of security commitments, and a consistent diplomatic message. Partnerships should be judged by the value they deliver: employment, infrastructure, skills, trade, institutional capacity, and long-term economic resilience. In a multipolar world, influence does not always come from military strength or economic size. It can also emerge from the ability to provide reliable services, connect markets, maintain stability, and build trust among competing interests. The Foundations of a Sustainable Somaliland Geostrategy A serious geostrategy must move beyond identifying geographical advantages. It must establish priorities, allocate resources, and build institutions capable of turning long-term objectives into practical results. Five priorities deserve particular attention. First, develop a comprehensive maritime and port strategy. Berbera should be integrated into a broader framework covering transport, logistics, fisheries, coastal protection, environmental management, and commercial services. Second, strengthen economic diplomacy. Somaliland should pursue partnerships that generate investment, expand export opportunities, improve infrastructure, and create measurable benefits for local communities. Third, invest in institutional capacity. Predictable regulations, transparent public administration, effective customs systems, and reliable dispute-resolution mechanisms are essential for attracting long-term investment. Fourth, pursue balanced regional relations. Cooperation with Ethiopia and engagement with neighbouring states should be based on dialogue, mutual benefit, peaceful dispute management, and respect for applicable international law. Somaliland should also seek to develop its bilateral relationship with Israel in ways that deliver tangible benefits while contributing to regional stability. Fifth, develop a credible international narrative. Somaliland’s external engagement should combine its historical and political case with verifiable evidence of institutional performance, economic potential, diplomatic engagement, and contributions to regional stability. Israel’s recognition should form part of this narrative, while further diplomatic engagement remains an important objective. These priorities are interconnected. A strategically located port cannot generate lasting influence without effective institutions. Diplomatic recognition cannot deliver its full potential without economic credibility. And geographical importance cannot substitute for a coherent, realistic, and consistently implemented national strategy. Conclusion: Turning Location into Influence Somaliland’s strategic importance rests on a combination of geography, maritime access, proximity to Ethiopia, the commercial potential of Berbera, and the wider international significance of the Red Sea–Gulf of Aden corridor. Israel’s formal recognition on 26 December 2025 added a significant diplomatic dimension to this strategic position. It established a new bilateral relationship and created opportunities for further engagement, while also highlighting the continuing disagreements over Somaliland’s international status and the future political order of the Horn of Africa. But Somaliland’s future will not be determined by geography or diplomatic recognition alone. The decisive question is whether Somaliland can transform its location and international partnerships into productive economic relationships, resilient institutions, effective maritime security, and constructive regional diplomacy. This requires patience, strategic clarity, and an understanding that lasting influence is built through both capabilities and relationships. For international policymakers, investors, researchers, and regional leaders, Somaliland deserves to be examined through this wider strategic lens. Its position raises important questions about maritime connectivity, diplomatic recognition, state-building, economic interdependence, and the future balance of power in the Horn of Africa. Ultimately, the strongest geostrategy is not simply about possessing a valuable location or securing diplomatic recognition. It is about turning both into lasting benefits for society while contributing to regional stability and international cooperation. Geography may open the door to strategic opportunity. Diplomatic recognition can widen that opening. Institutions, economic vision, and responsible diplomacy determine whether the opportunity becomes lasting influence. About the Author Mohamed Abdi Idris is a Somaliland-based analyst specializing in international relations, geopolitics, and foreign policy. He holds a Master’s degree in International Relations and Diplomacy and is actively engaged in policy discussions on global security, regional geopolitics, and the evolving strategic dynamics of the Middle East and the Horn of Africa. He is also involved in initiatives promoting peacebuilding, climate awareness, and international cooperation through civil society platforms in A Moment for Strategic Leadership Throughout modern history, decisions on diplomatic recognition have helped reshape international relations and create new political realities. From Kosovo’s declaration of independence and its subsequent recognition by the United States under President George W. Bush to the emergence of South Sudan as an independent state during President Barack Obama’s administration, American foreign policy has played a significant role in shaping the international status of emerging states. Under President Joe Biden, the United States also recognized the Cook Islands and Niue as sovereign states in their own right, strengthening their international engagement. Today, President Donald Trump has an opportunity to make a consequential contribution to this diplomatic legacy by formally recognizing the Republic of Somaliland. Such a decision would not simply address a longstanding political question; it could also open a new chapter in American engagement with the Horn of Africa, a region of growing strategic importance. More Than Three Decades of Self-Governance Since restoring its independence in 1991, Somaliland has pursued a distinct political path, focusing on building its own governing institutions, maintaining internal stability, and developing a system of electoral politics. Over more than three decades, it has established functioning institutions, held multiple elections, and sought to strengthen the foundations of democratic governance despite significant economic and security challenges. These achievements deserve serious consideration in international diplomatic discussions. Somaliland’s experience demonstrates the importance of locally driven institution-building and the determination of a society to manage its political affairs through its own institutions. Although challenges remain, particularly in economic development, democratic consolidation, and the resolution of territorial disputes, Somaliland’s record provides a substantive basis for a constructive international dialogue on its status and future. Why Somaliland Matters to the United States The case for Somaliland’s recognition extends beyond questions of historical identity and political self-determination. It also intersects with important American interests in regional security, maritime stability, economic cooperation, and the protection of international trade routes. Situated along the Gulf of Aden, near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Red Sea corridor, Somaliland occupies a strategically significant position connecting the Indian Ocean with some of the world’s most important maritime routes. Developments in this region have direct implications for international commerce, freedom of navigation, and broader security dynamics. The Port of Berbera and its associated economic development initiatives offer opportunities for expanded trade, infrastructure investment, and regional connectivity. With a carefully developed framework for cooperation, Somaliland could become a more significant partner in efforts to strengthen maritime security, combat transnational threats, and promote economic resilience across the Horn of Africa. Formal recognition could provide a clearer framework for bilateral engagement, although its practical benefits would depend on subsequent diplomatic agreements, institutional cooperation, and investment. Recognition as a Diplomatic Opportunity Recognition is a sovereign political decision, and the circumstances surrounding Kosovo, South Sudan, the Cook Islands, and Niue differ from Somaliland’s situation. Nevertheless, these cases demonstrate that international status can evolve through sustained diplomacy, political engagement, and decisions by individual states. For Somaliland, recognition would represent an important step toward broader international participation. It could facilitate more formal diplomatic relations, encourage international investment, and create new opportunities for cooperation in education, technology, infrastructure, trade, and security. At the same time, a successful diplomatic approach would require careful engagement with regional partners, including the African Union and neighbouring countries. Addressing regional concerns through dialogue and confidence-building would be essential to ensuring that any progress contributes to stability rather than deepening existing tensions. The United States could help facilitate such engagement by encouraging constructive dialogue, assessing Somaliland’s institutional record, and examining the potential strategic benefits of a more formal relationship. An Opportunity for President Trump’s Foreign Policy Legacy President Donald Trump has repeatedly emphasized strategic partnerships, national interests, and a foreign policy focused on tangible outcomes. Somaliland presents an opportunity to apply these priorities in the Horn of Africa through a policy that recognizes local political realities while pursuing broader regional objectives. A decision to recognize Somaliland would require careful legal, diplomatic, and strategic assessment. It would also require consideration of the possible responses of regional governments and international institutions. However, these complexities need not prevent serious discussion of the options available to Washington. By initiating a substantive review of Somaliland’s case and engaging relevant regional stakeholders, President Trump could help move a longstanding issue onto a more constructive diplomatic path. If the United States ultimately decides to extend formal recognition, the decision could become a defining moment in its engagement with the Horn of Africa. It would signal a willingness to reassess established diplomatic positions in light of evolving political realities and strategic interests. A New Chapter for Somaliland and the Horn of Africa Ultimately, Somaliland’s pursuit of recognition is about more than diplomatic status. It concerns international participation, economic opportunity, political representation, and the aspirations of a society that has spent decades developing its own institutions. Recognition alone would not resolve every challenge facing Somaliland, nor would it automatically guarantee peace, prosperity, or regional cooperation. Those outcomes would depend on effective governance, sustained economic development, and constructive relations with neighbouring states. Nevertheless, a carefully considered recognition policy could create opportunities for a new framework of engagement between Somaliland, the United States, and the wider international community. President Trump has an opportunity to make a lasting contribution to American diplomacy by giving Somaliland’s case the serious consideration it deserves. Through strategic leadership, sustained dialogue, and a clear assessment of mutual interests, Washington could help shape a new chapter in the political and economic future of the Horn of Africa. The time has come for Somaliland’s aspirations to receive serious, constructive, and sustained international consideration. For President Trump, this could be an opportunity not only to make history, but also to advance a more strategic and forward-looking American partnership in one of the world’s most important regions. About the Author Mohamed Abdi Idris is a Somaliland-based analyst specializing in international relations, geopolitics, and foreign policy. He holds a Master’s degree in International Relations and Diplomacy and is actively engaged in policy discussions on global security, regional geopolitics, and the evolving strategic dynamics of the Middle East and the Horn of Africa. He is also involved in initiatives promoting peacebuilding, climate awareness, and international cooperation through civil society platforms in Somaliland.

Its long-term value, however, will depend on road networks, customs efficiency, competitive costs, dependable services, and cooperation among the relevant authorities. A successful port strategy requires more than expanding physical capacity. It requires building an integrated economic ecosystem involving warehousing, freight services, transport operators, financial institutions, insurance providers, and businesses that create jobs. If developed effectively, Berbera could become more than a port. It could serve as an instrument of geoeconomic influence: a means through which Somaliland builds mutually beneficial relationships with neighbouring economies and international commercial partners. The strategic objective should not be to turn trade into a weapon of political pressure. It should be to make cooperation economically attractive, commercially reliable, and beneficial to all participating parties. Ethiopia and the Strategic Politics of Sea Access Ethiopia’s need for dependable maritime access is one of the defining geopolitical questions in the Horn of Africa. Its reliance on external ports exposes its economy to transportation costs, logistical bottlenecks, and political developments beyond its borders. Somaliland’s location and the Berbera corridor create a basis for practical cooperation on these challenges. Such cooperation could encompass port services, transit arrangements, transport infrastructure, trade facilitation, and long-term investment. Nevertheless, maritime access is a complex issue involving sovereignty, international law, regional diplomacy, and the interests of multiple states. Commercial arrangements and any proposals involving special access rights must be assessed through careful negotiations and clear legal frameworks. For Somaliland, the most sustainable strategy is to demonstrate that cooperation can produce measurable economic benefits while respecting regional stability and the legitimate interests of all parties. For Ethiopia, diversified and commercially viable access arrangements could support economic resilience and reduce dependence on any single route. For the wider region, transparent agreements and practical cooperation would be preferable to escalating rivalries over ports and maritime access. The question is not simply who gains access to the sea. It is whether regional actors can build a framework in which maritime connectivity becomes a source of shared prosperity rather than confrontation. The Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden, and Maritime Security The strategic importance of Somaliland is inseparable from the wider security environment surrounding the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Piracy, armed conflict, attacks on commercial shipping, illicit trafficking, and geopolitical competition have demonstrated how quickly insecurity in this region can affect global trade. The interests of regional and international powers increasingly intersect around maritime routes, port infrastructure, military facilities, and security partnerships. Somaliland can contribute to regional stability by strengthening maritime domain awareness, developing effective coastguard and law-enforcement capabilities, combating illicit trafficking, protecting legitimate commercial activity, and cooperating with appropriate regional and international partners. Such efforts require investment in training, communications, surveillance, institutional accountability, and clear legal procedures. Maritime security should also be understood in economic terms. Safer shipping routes, predictable port operations, and effective law enforcement can reduce commercial risk and make the region more attractive to investors. Somaliland’s strategic contribution would be strongest if it were based on practical capabilities and responsible cooperation rather than geopolitical rhetoric alone. Israel’s Recognition of Somaliland: A New Diplomatic Chapter On 26 December 2025, the State of Israel formally recognised the Republic of Somaliland as an independent and sovereign state. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced the decision following a joint declaration involving Israel’s leadership and Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, commonly known as Cirro. The announcement made Israel the first country to formally recognise Somaliland since its restoration of independence in 1991. This development represents an important milestone in Somaliland’s diplomatic history. For more than three decades, Somaliland had pursued international recognition while developing its own governing institutions, conducting elections, and maintaining a distinct political and administrative system. Israel’s recognition introduces a new dimension to Somaliland’s international engagement. It creates a formal basis for bilateral relations and the potential development of cooperation in areas including agriculture, healthcare, technology, economic development, and maritime security. The extent to which these opportunities produce lasting benefits will depend on the agreements, institutions, and practical initiatives developed by both governments. The decision also has a wider geopolitical context. Israel’s interest in Somaliland intersects with the strategic significance of the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, where maritime security, international trade, and regional competition are increasingly interconnected. For Somaliland, the recognition presents an opportunity to expand diplomatic engagement and demonstrate its capacity to build constructive international partnerships. It may also encourage further discussion among policymakers and analysts about Somaliland’s role in regional security, economic connectivity, and the evolving political landscape of the Horn of Africa. However, the diplomatic implications should be assessed realistically. Recognition by Israel does not automatically mean that other countries will follow, nor does it establish universal international recognition or membership in the United Nations. The decision also generated opposition from Somalia’s federal government and criticism from several regional actors, who raised concerns about Somalia’s territorial integrity and the potential implications for regional stability. These reactions underline the importance of continued diplomatic engagement and peaceful management of disagreements. For Somaliland, the strategic challenge is to build on the recognition through substantive cooperation, economic development, and further diplomatic outreach. Its international engagement will be more sustainable if it combines the pursuit of recognition with transparent institutions, practical economic achievements, and constructive relations with neighbouring states. The central question is no longer only whether Somaliland can attract international attention. It is how Somaliland can translate an important diplomatic development into lasting institutional, economic, and strategic benefits. Somaliland in a Multipolar World The Horn of Africa is increasingly shaped by overlapping interests involving Gulf states, Türkiye, China, the United States, European countries, and regional powers. These actors do not necessarily share the same priorities: some focus on trade and investment, others on maritime security, political partnerships, military access, or broader competition for influence. Israel’s recognition adds another dimension to this evolving environment, but it does not remove the need for Somaliland to maintain a broad and balanced approach to international relations. A wider range of potential partners could support infrastructure development, investment, technological exchange, and diplomatic engagement. However, competition among external powers can also place pressure on smaller political actors to align themselves with one side against another. Somaliland’s most effective approach would be a form of strategic pragmatism: engaging partners according to clearly defined national interests while avoiding unnecessary dependence on any single external power. Such an approach would require transparent investment agreements, sound financial management, careful assessment of security commitments, and a consistent diplomatic message. Partnerships should be judged by the value they deliver: employment, infrastructure, skills, trade, institutional capacity, and long-term economic resilience. In a multipolar world, influence does not always come from military strength or economic size. It can also emerge from the ability to provide reliable services, connect markets, maintain stability, and build trust among competing interests. The Foundations of a Sustainable Somaliland Geostrategy A serious geostrategy must move beyond identifying geographical advantages. It must establish priorities, allocate resources, and build institutions capable of turning long-term objectives into practical results. Five priorities deserve particular attention. First, develop a comprehensive maritime and port strategy. Berbera should be integrated into a broader framework covering transport, logistics, fisheries, coastal protection, environmental management, and commercial services. Second, strengthen economic diplomacy. Somaliland should pursue partnerships that generate investment, expand export opportunities, improve infrastructure, and create measurable benefits for local communities. Third, invest in institutional capacity. Predictable regulations, transparent public administration, effective customs systems, and reliable dispute-resolution mechanisms are essential for attracting long-term investment. Fourth, pursue balanced regional relations. Cooperation with Ethiopia and engagement with neighbouring states should be based on dialogue, mutual benefit, peaceful dispute management, and respect for applicable international law. Somaliland should also seek to develop its bilateral relationship with Israel in ways that deliver tangible benefits while contributing to regional stability. Fifth, develop a credible international narrative. Somaliland’s external engagement should combine its historical and political case with verifiable evidence of institutional performance, economic potential, diplomatic engagement, and contributions to regional stability. Israel’s recognition should form part of this narrative, while further diplomatic engagement remains an important objective. These priorities are interconnected. A strategically located port cannot generate lasting influence without effective institutions. Diplomatic recognition cannot deliver its full potential without economic credibility. And geographical importance cannot substitute for a coherent, realistic, and consistently implemented national strategy. Conclusion: Turning Location into Influence Somaliland’s strategic importance rests on a combination of geography, maritime access, proximity to Ethiopia, the commercial potential of Berbera, and the wider international significance of the Red Sea–Gulf of Aden corridor. Israel’s formal recognition on 26 December 2025 added a significant diplomatic dimension to this strategic position. It established a new bilateral relationship and created opportunities for further engagement, while also highlighting the continuing disagreements over Somaliland’s international status and the future political order of the Horn of Africa. But Somaliland’s future will not be determined by geography or diplomatic recognition alone. The decisive question is whether Somaliland can transform its location and international partnerships into productive economic relationships, resilient institutions, effective maritime security, and constructive regional diplomacy. This requires patience, strategic clarity, and an understanding that lasting influence is built through both capabilities and relationships. For international policymakers, investors, researchers, and regional leaders, Somaliland deserves to be examined through this wider strategic lens. Its position raises important questions about maritime connectivity, diplomatic recognition, state-building, economic interdependence, and the future balance of power in the Horn of Africa. Ultimately, the strongest geostrategy is not simply about possessing a valuable location or securing diplomatic recognition. It is about turning both into lasting benefits for society while contributing to regional stability and international cooperation. Geography may open the door to strategic opportunity. Diplomatic recognition can widen that opening. Institutions, economic vision, and responsible diplomacy determine whether the opportunity becomes lasting influence. About the Author Mohamed Abdi Idris is a Somaliland-based analyst specializing in international relations, geopolitics, and foreign policy. He holds a Master’s degree in International Relations and Diplomacy and is actively engaged in policy discussions on global security, regional geopolitics, and the evolving strategic dynamics of the Middle East and the Horn of Africa. He is also involved in initiatives promoting peacebuilding, climate awareness, and international cooperation through civil society platforms in A Moment for Strategic Leadership Throughout modern history, decisions on diplomatic recognition have helped reshape international relations and create new political realities. From Kosovo’s declaration of independence and its subsequent recognition by the United States under President George W. Bush to the emergence of South Sudan as an independent state during President Barack Obama’s administration, American foreign policy has played a significant role in shaping the international status of emerging states. Under President Joe Biden, the United States also recognized the Cook Islands and Niue as sovereign states in their own right, strengthening their international engagement. Today, President Donald Trump has an opportunity to make a consequential contribution to this diplomatic legacy by formally recognizing the Republic of Somaliland. Such a decision would not simply address a longstanding political question; it could also open a new chapter in American engagement with the Horn of Africa, a region of growing strategic importance. More Than Three Decades of Self-Governance Since restoring its independence in 1991, Somaliland has pursued a distinct political path, focusing on building its own governing institutions, maintaining internal stability, and developing a system of electoral politics. Over more than three decades, it has established functioning institutions, held multiple elections, and sought to strengthen the foundations of democratic governance despite significant economic and security challenges. These achievements deserve serious consideration in international diplomatic discussions. Somaliland’s experience demonstrates the importance of locally driven institution-building and the determination of a society to manage its political affairs through its own institutions. Although challenges remain, particularly in economic development, democratic consolidation, and the resolution of territorial disputes, Somaliland’s record provides a substantive basis for a constructive international dialogue on its status and future. Why Somaliland Matters to the United States The case for Somaliland’s recognition extends beyond questions of historical identity and political self-determination. It also intersects with important American interests in regional security, maritime stability, economic cooperation, and the protection of international trade routes. Situated along the Gulf of Aden, near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Red Sea corridor, Somaliland occupies a strategically significant position connecting the Indian Ocean with some of the world’s most important maritime routes. Developments in this region have direct implications for international commerce, freedom of navigation, and broader security dynamics. The Port of Berbera and its associated economic development initiatives offer opportunities for expanded trade, infrastructure investment, and regional connectivity. With a carefully developed framework for cooperation, Somaliland could become a more significant partner in efforts to strengthen maritime security, combat transnational threats, and promote economic resilience across the Horn of Africa. Formal recognition could provide a clearer framework for bilateral engagement, although its practical benefits would depend on subsequent diplomatic agreements, institutional cooperation, and investment. Recognition as a Diplomatic Opportunity Recognition is a sovereign political decision, and the circumstances surrounding Kosovo, South Sudan, the Cook Islands, and Niue differ from Somaliland’s situation. Nevertheless, these cases demonstrate that international status can evolve through sustained diplomacy, political engagement, and decisions by individual states. For Somaliland, recognition would represent an important step toward broader international participation. It could facilitate more formal diplomatic relations, encourage international investment, and create new opportunities for cooperation in education, technology, infrastructure, trade, and security. At the same time, a successful diplomatic approach would require careful engagement with regional partners, including the African Union and neighbouring countries. Addressing regional concerns through dialogue and confidence-building would be essential to ensuring that any progress contributes to stability rather than deepening existing tensions. The United States could help facilitate such engagement by encouraging constructive dialogue, assessing Somaliland’s institutional record, and examining the potential strategic benefits of a more formal relationship. An Opportunity for President Trump’s Foreign Policy Legacy President Donald Trump has repeatedly emphasized strategic partnerships, national interests, and a foreign policy focused on tangible outcomes. Somaliland presents an opportunity to apply these priorities in the Horn of Africa through a policy that recognizes local political realities while pursuing broader regional objectives. A decision to recognize Somaliland would require careful legal, diplomatic, and strategic assessment. It would also require consideration of the possible responses of regional governments and international institutions. However, these complexities need not prevent serious discussion of the options available to Washington. By initiating a substantive review of Somaliland’s case and engaging relevant regional stakeholders, President Trump could help move a longstanding issue onto a more constructive diplomatic path. If the United States ultimately decides to extend formal recognition, the decision could become a defining moment in its engagement with the Horn of Africa. It would signal a willingness to reassess established diplomatic positions in light of evolving political realities and strategic interests. A New Chapter for Somaliland and the Horn of Africa Ultimately, Somaliland’s pursuit of recognition is about more than diplomatic status. It concerns international participation, economic opportunity, political representation, and the aspirations of a society that has spent decades developing its own institutions. Recognition alone would not resolve every challenge facing Somaliland, nor would it automatically guarantee peace, prosperity, or regional cooperation. Those outcomes would depend on effective governance, sustained economic development, and constructive relations with neighbouring states. Nevertheless, a carefully considered recognition policy could create opportunities for a new framework of engagement between Somaliland, the United States, and the wider international community. President Trump has an opportunity to make a lasting contribution to American diplomacy by giving Somaliland’s case the serious consideration it deserves. Through strategic leadership, sustained dialogue, and a clear assessment of mutual interests, Washington could help shape a new chapter in the political and economic future of the Horn of Africa. The time has come for Somaliland’s aspirations to receive serious, constructive, and sustained international consideration. For President Trump, this could be an opportunity not only to make history, but also to advance a more strategic and forward-looking American partnership in one of the world’s most important regions. About the Author Mohamed Abdi Idris is a Somaliland-based analyst specializing in international relations, geopolitics, and foreign policy. He holds a Master’s degree in International Relations and Diplomacy and is actively engaged in policy discussions on global security, regional geopolitics, and the evolving strategic dynamics of the Middle East and the Horn of Africa. He is also involved in initiatives promoting peacebuilding, climate awareness, and international cooperation through civil society platforms in Somaliland.

items.title: Xasan oo war kasoo saaray doorashada guddoonka Baarlamaanka Galmudug
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Xildhibaannada Golaha Wakiillada Dowlad Goboleedka Soomaaliyeed ee Galmudug ayaa maanta si rasmi ah u doortay Guddoonka cusub ee Golaha, kadib doorasho ka dhacday magaalada Dhuusamareeb ee xarunta gobolka Galgaduud ee bartamaha Soomaaliya. Xilka guddoomiyaha ayaa waxaa loo doortay Xildhibaan ‎Xuseen Maxamed Nuur oo ka tirsan hoggaanka sare ee Xisbiga Cadaaladda iyo Wadajirka ee JSP. Sidoo kale, Cabdulqaadir Axmed Cali ayaa loo doortay Gudoomiye Ku-xigeenka Koowaad, halka Guddoomiye ku xigeenka labaad loo doortay ‎‎Mursal Cabdi Aadan. ‎ ‎Doorashada kaddib, Gudoomiyaha cusub ee Golaha Wakiillada Galmudug, Xuseen Maxamed Nuur, ayaa soo xiray kalfadhiga. Dhinaca kale, Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya, Mudane Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ayaa war kasoo saaray doorashadan ayaa hambalyo u diray Guddoomiyaha cusub ee Golaha Wakiilada D. Galmudug, Mudane Xuseen Maxamed Nuur, Guddoomiye Ku-xigeenka Koowaad, Mudane Cabdulqaadir Axmed Cali Quuri, iyo Guddoomiye Ku-xigeenka Labaad, Mudane Mursal Cabdi Aadan oo kusoo baxay doorashadii maanta. Ugu horreyn Madaxweynaha ayaa u rajeeyay guddoonka cusub guul iyo in ay si hufan oo xilkasnimo leh u gutaan waajibaadka loo igmaday, iyagoo mudnaanta siinaya danta guud, wadajirka iyo horumarka, waxa uuna ku booriyay in ay xoogga saaraan gudashada masuuliyaddooda, kana shaqeeyaan xoojinta wada-shaqeynta hay’adaha Dowlad Goboleedka iyo horumarinta howlaha Golaha. Sidoo kale, wuxuu bogaadiyey doorashooyinka sida nabadda iyo dimuqraadiyadda leh uga dhacay deegaannada Galmudug, isaga oo xusay in ay tallaabo muhiim ah u yihiin horumarinta hannaanka dimuqraadiyadeed ee dalka iyo xaqiijinta xaqa muwaadiniinta ee doorashada hoggaankooda. Doorashadan waxaa xigi doonto midda Madaxweynaha iyo ku xigeenkiisa oo maalmaha soo socda ka dhici doonta magaalada Dhuusamareeb ee caasimada Dowlad Goboleedka Galmudug. The post Xasan oo war kasoo saaray doorashada guddoonka Baarlamaanka Galmudug appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Xamza oo buuxiyay booskii uu baneeyay Jaamac iyo xogta shaqsiga uu magacaabay
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Soomaaliya, Xamza Cabdi Barre ayaa Cabdulqaadir Cumar Macallin u magacaabay Wasiirka Dekedaha iyo Gaadiidka Badda. Cabdulqaadir Cumar ayaa ka tirsan Xildhibaannada Baarlamaanka 11-aad, waxaana magacaabistiisa loo arkaa mid la xiriirta rabitaanka Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka, Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Jaamac oo hore u maamuli jiray Wasaaradda Dekedaha. Xiriirka ka dhexeeya labada mas’uul ayaa soo shaac baxay markii wasiirka cusub uu noqday shaqsigii la galay hoolka baarlamaanka Guddoomiye Jaamac, taas oo sida muuqata haatan u gogol xaartay inuu qabto xilkii uu ka tagay Jaamac. Magacaabistan ayaa qayb ka ah tallaabooyinka uu Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamza ku ballaarinayo xubnaha xukuumaddiisa, uguna soo darayo xubno cusub, xilli dastuurka muranka dhaliyay uu dhigayo kala saarista xukuumadda iyo baarlamaanka. Go’aanka ayaa kusoo aadaya xilli ay weli taagan yihiin doodaha siyaasadeed ee la xiriira dastuurka cusub iyo saameynta uu ku yeelanayo nidaamka awood-qaybsiga hay’adaha dowladda. Dhawaan, Guddiga Madaxbannaan ee Dib-u-eegista iyo Hirgelinta Dastuurka ayaa Golaha Wasiirrada u diray ogeysiis ku saabsan waajibaadka ka dhalanaya isbeddelkan dastuuriga ah, iyaga oo ku wargeliyay inay kala doortaan labada xil. Tani waxay ka dhigan tahay in mas’uulka haya xil wasiirnimo uusan sii wadan karin xubinnimada Golaha Shacabka haddii uu doonayo inuu sii hayo xilka dowladda, halka xildhibaanka aqbala xil kale oo dowladeed uu luminayo xubinnimadiisa baarlamaanka. The post Xamza oo buuxiyay booskii uu baneeyay Jaamac iyo xogta shaqsiga uu magacaabay appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Wasiirka Waxbarashada Soomaaliya oo sheegay in adeegyada wasaaraddu bilaash yihiin
items.description: Muqdisho (Goobjoog News) — Wasiirka Wasaaradda Waxbarashada, Hiddaha iyo Tacliinta Sare ee Soomaaliya, Faarax Sheekh Cabdulqaadir, ayaa sheegay inaysan jirin adeeg ay wasaaraddu bixiso oo lacag laga qaado dadka. Wasiirka ayaa sidoo kale shaaciyay in Wasaaradda Waxbarashadu ay bilowday inay iskuullada sida gaarka ah loo leeyahay ee gobolka Banaadir siiso taageero lacageed oo dhan 300 oo doollar bishii. Faarax Sheekh Cabdulqaadir ayaa sheegay in taageeradan loo qoondeeyay iskuullada gaarka loo leeyahay, hase yeeshee ma uusan bixin faahfaahin dheeraad ah oo ku saabsan tirada iskuullada ka faa’iideysanaya barnaamijkan. Hadalkan ayaa ku soo aadaya xilli ay jiraan dadaallo lagu horumarinayo waxbarashada dalka, lana doonayo in la xoojiyo taageerada la siiyo xarumaha waxbarashada.

items.title: Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamsa oo Qaabilay Safiirka Cusub ee Midowga Yurub u Qaabilsan Soomaaliya
items.description: Muqdisho (Goobjoog News) – Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Xukuumadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Xamsa Cabdi Barre, ayaa maanta xafiiskiisa ku qaabilay safiirka cusub ee Midowga Yurub u qaabilsan Soomaaliya, László Eduárd Máthé, iyaga oo ka wada hadlay xoojinta xiriirka iyo iskaashiga labada dhinac. Kulanka oo ka dhacay magaalada Muqdisho ayaa diiradda lagu saaray iskaashiga dhinacyada amniga, horumarinta dhaqaalaha, dowlad-dhiska, taageerada hay’adaha dowladda iyo hirgelinta qorshayaasha horumarineed ee mudnaanta u leh Soomaaliya. items.title: Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh oo Hambalyo u Diray Guddoonka Cusub ee Baarlamaanka Galmudug
items.description: MUQDISHO (Goobjoog News) — Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, ayaa hambalyo u diray guddoonka cusub ee Golaha Wakiillada Dowlad Goboleedka Galmudug oo maanta lagu doortay magaalada Dhuusamareeb. Madaxweynaha ayaa hambalyada u diray Guddoomiyaha cusub ee Golaha, Xuseen Maxamed Nuur, Guddoomiye Ku-xigeenka Koowaad, Cabdulqaadir Axmed Cali Quuri, iyo Guddoomiye Ku-xigeenka Labaad, Mursal Cabdi Aadan. Xasan Sheekh ayaa guddoonka cusub u rajeeyay guul iyo inay si hufan oo xilkasnimo leh u gutaan waajibaadka loo igmaday, isaga oo ku boorriyay inay mudnaanta siiyaan danta guud, wadajirka iyo horumarka Galmudug. Sidoo kale, Madaxweynaha ayaa ku adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay xoojinta wada-shaqeynta hay’adaha dowlad goboleedka iyo horumarinta howlaha Golaha Wakiillada, si loo xaqiijiyo gudashada waajibaadka ka saaran hoggaaminta iyo matalaadda shacabka. Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya ayaa sidoo kale bogaadiyay doorashooyinka ka dhacay deegaannada Galmudug, kuwaas oo uu ku tilmaamay tallaabo muhiim u ah horumarinta hannaanka dimuqraadiyadeed ee dalka iyo xaqiijinta xuquuqda muwaadiniinta ee doorashada hoggaankooda. Doorashada guddoonka cusub ee Golaha Wakiillada Galmudug ayaa imaanaysa iyadoo dowlad goboleedku uu sii wado howlaha la xiriira dhismaha iyo xoojinta hay’adihiisa dowladeed.

items.title: Nabadda Somaliland: Tiirka qaranimadda iyo mustaqbalka bulshada
items.description: NABADDA SOMALILAND: TIIRKA QARANIMADA IYO MUSTAQBALKA BULSHADA Nabaddu waa tiirka ay ku taagan yihiin wada-noolaanshaha, horumarka iyo jiritaanka bulsho kasta. Waa hanti aan lagu qiimayn karin maal iyo magac, balse lagu garto xasilloonida, kalsoonida iyo wanaagga ay dadku wadaagaan. Somaliland waxay soo martay marxalado adag oo bulshada baray qiimaha nabadda. Dadaalladii dib-u-heshiisiinta iyo dhismaha xasilloonida waxaa door muuqda ku lahaa hoggaanka dhaqanka, oo ay weheliyeen waxgaradka, culimada, haweenka iyo qaybaha kale ee bulshada. Suldaannada, ugaasyada, caaqillada iyo odayaasha dhaqanka Somaliland waxay weli bulshada ku dhex leeyihiin masuuliyad muhiim ah. Waa dad laga filayo talo, dhexdhexaadin, isu-soo-dhoweyn iyo ilaalinta xidhiidhka bulshada. Dhaqankeenna waxaa qiimo weyn ku leh garta, garawshiyaha iyo isu-tanaasulka. Marka khilaaf yimaaddo, waxaa muhiim ah in la dhegaysto dhinacyada, xaqa la dhowro, lana raadiyo xal lagu wada qanci karo. Heshiiska wanaagsani ma aha oo keliya in muran la soo afjaro, balse waa in la soo celiyo kalsoonidii iyo wada-noolaanshihii dadka. Hoggaanka dhaqanka Somaliland waxaa maanta looga baahan yahay inuu sii xoojiyo kaalintiisa nabadaynta, ka hortagga khilaafaadka iyo isku xidhka bulshada. Waxaa sidoo kale muhiim ah inuu la shaqeeyo hay’adaha dawladda, isaga oo dhowraya sharciga, caddaaladda iyo xuquuqda muwaadiniinta. Nabaddu ma aha hawl la qabto marka colaad dhacdo oo keliya. Waa masuuliyad joogto ah oo u baahan feejignaan, wada-tashi iyo in la qaboojiyo wax kasta oo keeni kara kala fogaansho bulsho. Hoggaanka dhaqanka waxaa looga fadhiyaa inuu noqdo mid dadka isu keena, talada mideeya, kana shaqeeya danta guud. Odaynimadu waxay qiimo yeelataa marka ay ku dhisan tahay dhexdhexaadnimo, run-sheegid iyo u-turidda bulshada. Somaliland nabaddeedu waa dhaxal ay jiilal badan ka qayb qaateen. Ilaalinteeduna waxay u baahan tahay in hoggaanka dhaqanku sii wado kaalintiisa, bulshada inteeda kalena ay garab istaagto dadaallada lagu xoojinayo wadajirka iyo xasilloonida. Nabaddu waa tiirka qaranimada; hoggaanka dhaqankuna wuxuu leeyahay kaalintiisa ilaalinta tiirkaas. Mohamed Farah Tahar Cilmi-baare Madax-bannaan | Aqoonyahan ku Takhasusay Maamulka iyo Qorshaynta |

items.title: Guddoonka Baarlamaanka Galmudug oo lagu doortay Dhuusamareeb (SAWIRRO)
items.description: Xildhibaanada Baarlamaanka Galmudug ayaa maanta Magaalada Dhuusamareeb ku doortay Gudoomiyaha Baarlamaanka iyo Labadiisa Kuxigeen. Xildhibaan Xuseen Maxamed Nuur (Dhegaweyne) ayaa loo doortay Gudoomiyaha Baarlamaanka Galmudug, ka dib markii uu 79 cod kaga adkaaday Xildhibaan Ismaaciil Cabdi Jimcaale oo helay 8 cod. Xildhibaan Cabdiqaadir Axmed Cali (Quuri) ayaa loo doortay Gudoomiye Kuxigeenka 1aad ee Baarlamaanka Galmudug, kaas oo ku guuleystay 87 cod. Sidoo kale Xildhibaan Mursal Cabdi Aadan (Haaraa) ayay Xildhibaanadu u doorteen jegada Gudoomiye Kuxigeenka 2aad ee Baarlamaanka Galmudug, isagoona xilka ku guuleystay tartan la’aan. Xildhibaan Mursal Cabdi Aadan ayaa helay 87 cod, markii Xildhibaanadu ay qaab gacan taag ah ugu codeeyeen. Guddoonka cusub ee Baarlamaanka Galmudug ayaa isla maanta lagu dhaariyay Xarunta Baarlamaanka ee Dhuusamareeb. Xildhibaanada Baarlamaanka Galmudug oo ka kooban 89 xubnood ayaa lagu wadaa in dhawaan ay doortaan Hoggaamiyaha cusub ee Dowlad Goboleedka Galmudug.

items.title: Waxa laga yaabaa Cabdikariin Axmed Mooge in markale
items.description: WAXA LAGA YAABAA CABDIKARIIN AXMAD MOOGE INAY MARKALE MOWJADDII UU KU YIMID MAAYARNIMADA OO KALE UU KU GAADHO KAALINTA MADAXWEYNAHA. Cabdikariim axmad wuxuu ku yimid maskabkii maayarnimo si cajiiba oo rabbaaniya, Anigoo soo koobaya qoraalkayga si wanaagsan ayuu u shaqeeyay iyadoo dhaliilo uu xukunku wataana ay jireen. Cabdikariim Maroodijeex wax weyn ayuu u qabtay, waa maayarkii ugu waxqabadka badnaa dadkuna badiyaa way jecelyihiin xirfadiisa. Cabdikariim wuxuu ka soo jeedaa qoys halgamaa ah oo qalbiga umadda ku sawiran, aabbihii iyo adeerkii waxay ahaayeen Kacdoonkii suugaanta ee dadka lagu kiciyay kaalin culus qaar kasoo qaatay ilaa 1971kii laga bilaabo. Cabdikariim wuxuu dheeryay siyaasiyiinta tartanka ku jira, waxay isku ayni yihiin jiilka maanta dadku u badanyahay oo ah Technology generation waa aqoonta keli ah ee umadda ka saari karta maskaxdii daashay ee lixdamaadkii , taas oo ah siyaasadda gaboowday (jactaday) ee umadda lagu hago ilaa iminka siyaasiyiinta maanta joogta wuu ka sucmad fiicanyay waanuu ka jaanis badanyay hadduu u qalab uruursado inuu madaxweyne noqdo. MAHADSANID. CABDI BACAW. GUUL ALLE.

items.title: Kuraasta xildhibaannadii ka goostay Waqooyi Bari oo la buuxiyay iyo xiisad taagan
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Kulan ay maanta yeesheen xildhibaannada maamulka Waqooyi Bari ayaa isku beddelay buuq iyo gacan qaad kadib markii qaar ka mid ah mudanayaashu ay ka horyimaadeen habraaca loo maray buuxinta shantii kursi ee ay baneeyeen xubnihii ku biiray Somaliland. Khilaafka ayaa salka ku haya kuraas ay leeyihiin xildhibaanno ka soo jeeda gobolka Sanaag, kuwaas oo ku eedeeyay hoggaanka maamulka in si aan waafaqsanayn habraaca loo buuxiyay boosaskii ay baneeyeen xubnaha Somaliland ku biiray. Xildhibaannada cabashada muujiyay ayaa sheegay in xoog lagula wareegay kuraastooda, iyagoo eeddaas si gaar ah ugu jeediyay madaxweynaha Waqooyi Bari, Cabdiqaadir Axmed Aw Cali (Firdhiye). Dhankiisa, madaxweyne ku-xigeenka maamulka, Cabdirashiid Yuusuf Jibriil (Abwaan) ayaa walaac ka muujiyay xaaladda ka dhex taagan Golaha Wakiillada, isaga oo sheegay in la hareer maray heshiisyadii iyo wadajirka lagu dhisay maamulka. “Waa ayaan-darro weyn waxa Golaha Wakiillada Waqooyi Bari ka socda. Taasi waxay wiiqaysaa wax-wada-lahaanshaha iyo heshiiskii bulsho ee la wada galay. Waxaan eegaynaa waxa ay dhasho,” ayuu Abwaan ku yiri qoraal uu soo dhigay bartiisa Facebook. Dhacdadan ayaa kusoo aadeysa xilli uu sii xoogeysanayo khilaafka u dhexeeya madaxda sare ee Waqooyi Bari, gaar ahaan madaxweynaha iyo ku-xigeenkiisa, kuwaas oo muddooyinkii dambe isku hayay arrimaha maamulka. Labadan mas’uul ayaa haatan la sheegayaa inay ku dhow yihiin inay mooshin xilka iskaga tuuraan, iyadoo khilaafkoodu uu muddo soo jiitamayay. The post Kuraasta xildhibaannadii ka goostay Waqooyi Bari oo la buuxiyay iyo xiisad taagan appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Puntland oo qiil yaab leh u sameysay in lala dagaalamo madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh
items.description: Garoowe (Caasimada Online) – Puntland ayaa ku baaqday in la iska kaashado ka hortagga Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ee uu hoggaamiyo Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, iyadoo ku eedeysay inay waddo hannaan doorasho oo khatar gelin kara midnimada dalka. Baaqan ayaa imanaya xilli uu sii xoogeysanayo khilaafka siyaasadeed ee u dhexeeya Dowladda Federaalka iyo Puntland oo si weyn uga soo horjeedda hannaanka doorashooyinka ee la shaaciyay. Madaxweyne ku-xigeenka Puntland, Ilyaas Cismaan Lugatoor oo hadda ah ku-simaha madaxweynaha ayaa baaqan jeediyay, isagoo si gaar ah ugu boorriyay shacabka reer Muqdisho inay ka horyimaadaan Dowladda Federaalka, ayna la dagaalamaan. Lugatoor ayaa sheegay in la dagaallanka dowladda uu hoggaamiyo Xasan Sheekh laga helayo ajar iyo xasanaad, sida uu hadalka u dhigay. Hadalkan ayaa muujinaya heerka ay gaarsiisan tahay diidmada maamulka Puntland uga soo horjeedo jihada siyaasadeed ee dowladda iyo hannaanka doorasho ee ay waddo. Sidoo kale, Lugatoor ayaa sheegay in haddii Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh uu qaban waayo doorasho heshiis lagu yahay ay Puntland qaadan doonto go’aan u gaar ah oo ku aaddan xaaladda taagan. Mowqifka Puntland ayaa soo baxaya xilli ay sii kordhayaan diidmada iyo doodaha siyaasadeed ee ka dhashay jadwalka doorashooyinka ee la shaaciyay. Guddiga Madaxa-bannaan ee Doorashooyinka Qaranka iyo Soohdimaha ayaa maalmo ka hor ku dhawaaqay jadwalka doorashooyinka baarlamaanka iyo madaxweynaha, tallaabadaas oo uga sii dartay xiisadda siyaasadeed ee taagan, iyadoo si adag uga horyimaadeen mucaaradka. Sida ku cad jadwalka guddiga, doorashada labada Aqal ee Baarlamaanka Federaalka ayaa loo asteeyay 15-ka April 2027, halka doorashada madaxweynaha la qorsheeyay 15-ka May ee isla sanadkaas. Si kastaba, Puntland iyo dhinacyada kale ee ka soo horjeeda hannaankaas ayaa ku doodaya in doorashooyinka dalka lagu saleeyo heshiis siyaasadeed oo ay dhammaan dhinacyada khuseeya ku wada qanacsan yihiin. Khilaafkan ayaa weli ah mid ka mid ah caqabadaha ugu waaweyn ee horyaalla geeddi-socodka siyaasadeed ee Soomaaliya. items.title: Ciidamada taageersan Laftagareen oo go’doon ciidan iyo ciriiri nololeed geliyay Baydhabo
items.description: Ciidamada taabacsan Madaxweynihii hore ee Koonfur Galbeed, Cabdicasiis Xasan Maxamed (Laftagareen) ayaa xaalad ciriiri ah geliyay Magaalada Baydhabo, ka dib markii ay la wareegeen magaalooyinka iyo deegaanada ka baxsan magaaladaasi ee ka tirsan Gobolka Baay. Ciidamadan ayaa wax ka yar toban maalmood kula wareegay dhammaan Degmooyinka Gobolka Baay, marka laga soo tago magaalda xarunta u ah gobolkaasi ee Baydhabo. Ciidamada u daacadda ah Madaxweynihii hore ee Koonfur Galbeed ayaa si buuxda ula wareegay Degmooyinka Diinsoor, Qansaxdheere, Berdaale iyo Buurhakaba iyo sidoo kale deegaanada istiraatiijiga ah ee gobolkaasi amaba hoostaga Baydhabo. Tani ayaa waxay mucaaradka uu Cabdicasiis Laftagareen hoggaamiyo ay siisay inay yeeshaan gacanta sare ee awoodda iyo maamulka gobolka. Shacabka ku dhaqan Baydhabo ayaa kuu sheegaya in ciidamada taageersan Laftagareen ay go’doon iyo xaalad ciriiri ah ay geliyeen magaalada, wax kastana ay u muuqaan inay sii qaaliyoobayaan. Sarkaal ka tirsan Ciidanka Ilaalada Madaxtooyada Koonfur Galbeed oo aan la hadalnay ayaa inoo sheegay in Baydhabo ay sidoo kale wajaheyso go’doon ciidan, bacdamaa waddooyinka laga soo galo ay gacanta ku hayaan ciidamada ka soo horjeeda Dowlad Goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed. Sarkaal kale oo ka tirsan Taliska Qaybta 60aad ee Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka ee fadhigoodu yahay Baydhabo ayaa Universaltv u sheegay in xaaladda aysan sidaan sii ahaan doonin, isla-markaana uu jiro diyaargarow ciidan oo lagu furayo waddooyinka laga soo galo Baydhabo ee haatan laga maamulayo bannaanadeeda. Ciidamada Laftagareen oo aad mooddo inay sii ballaarinayaan awooddooda militari iyo gacan ku haynta degmooyinka ka tirsan Koonfur Galbeed ayaa abuuray cabsi ku aaddan in ay isku fidiyaan Gobolka Bakool. Maamulka Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Aadan Madoobe) oo ka walaacsan in laga la wareego Xudur iyo Waajid ayaa magaalooyinkaasi ka wada abaabul ciidan, oo looga hortagayo weerar ay suurtagal tahay in ay ku qaadaan ciidamada taabacsan Laftagareen.

items.title: Ra’iisulwasaare Xamse oo Wasiir Cusub u Magacaabay Wasaaradda Dekedaha
items.description: Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Xukuumadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Xamsa Cabdi Barre, ayaa Cabdulqaadir Cumar Macalin u magacaabay Wasiirka Wasaaradda Dekedaha iyo Gaadiidka Badda ee dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya. Magacaabistan ayaa lagu saleeyay qodobka 120-aad, farqadihiisa 2-aad iyo 3-aad, ee Dastuurka Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, iyadoo sidoo kale la tixgeliyay taariikh nololeedka, aqoonta iyo khibradda shaqo ee Cabdulqaadir Cumar Macalin. Sida lagu sheegay qoraalka magacaabista, Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamsa Cabdi Barre ayaa sidoo kale tixgeliyay talada Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya ka hor inta uusan soo saarin go’aanka magacaabista wasiirka cusub. Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ayaa wasiirka cusub kula dardaarmay inuu xilkiisa u guto si hufan, masuuliyad leh, isla markaana uu ilaaliyo waajibaadka ka saaran adeegga dowladda iyo shacabka Soomaaliyeed. Wasaaradda Dekedaha iyo Gaadiidka Badda ayaa ka mid ah hay’adaha dowladda ee qaabilsan arrimaha la xiriira dekedaha iyo gaadiidka badda, kuwaas oo door muhiim ah ku leh ganacsiga, isu socodka badeecadaha iyo horumarinta dhaqaalaha dalka.

items.title: Waa kuma Guddoomiyaha Cusub ee Wakiillada Galmudug ?
items.description: Golaha Wakiillada Galmudug ayaa guddoomiye u doortay Xildhibaan Xuseen Maxamed Nuur, ka dib Doorasho ka dhacday magaalada Dhuusamareeb ee Caasimadda Maamulkaas . Xuseen ayaa ka guulaystay Murasharixii la tartamayay, Cismaaciil Cabdi Jaamac, ka dib markii uu helay 79 cod oo kamid 87 cod oo ay xubnaha goluhu dhiibteen. Xuseen Maxamed Nuur, waa siyaasi Soomaaliyeed oo soo qabtay xilal kala duwan oo maamul iyo siyaasadeed, kana soo shaqeeyay hay’ado dowladeed oo heer federaal iyo heer gobol ah. Xuseen Maxamed Nuur ayaa waayihiisa shaqo ka soo bilaabay maamulka adeegyada caafimaadka, isaga oo soo noqday Agaasimaha Guud ee Isbitaalka Digfeer ee magaalada Muqdisho, oo maanta loo yaqaan Isbitaalka Erdogan. Khibraddiisa maamulka ayaa markii dambe u horseedday inuu ka mid noqdo mas’uuliyiinta maamulka Gobolka Banaadir. Bishii Janaayo 2018, waxaa loo magacaabay Guddoomiye-ku-xigeenka Gobolka Banaadir ee dhinaca maamulka iyo maaliyadda, xilkaas oo uu ka qabtay maamulka caasimadda iyo arrimaha maaliyadeed ee gobolka. Markii dambe ayuu u gudbay siyaasadda heer federaal, waxaana doorashadii baarlamaanka ee 3-dii Febraayo 2022 uu ku guuleystay kursiga tirsigiisu yahay HOP051 ee Golaha Shacabka Baarlamaanka Federaalka Soomaaliya. Sannadkan 2026, Xuseen Maxamed Nuur ayaa mar kale ka dhex muuqday siyaasadda, isaga oo u tartamay xilka Guddoomiyaha Golaha Wakiillada Dowlad-goboleedka Galmudug, isagoo ka socday ururka siyaasadeed ee Caddaaladda iyo Wadajirka. Xuseen Maxamed Nuur wuxuu ka mid yahay siyaasiyiinta Soomaaliyeed ee soo maray shaqada maamulka iyo siyaasadda, isaga oo khibrad ka helay adeegyada caafimaadka, maamulka caasimadda iyo matalaadda baarlamaanka.

items.title: SOMALILAND oo jawaabtay kadib markii Itoobiya shaacisay in aysan aqoonsan karin
items.description: Tel Aviv (Caasimada Online) – Somaliland ayaa si adag u diidau digniin uu bixiyay safiirka Itoobiya ee Israel, oo sheegay in aqoonsiga Somaliland uu khatar gelin karo amniga gobolka, isla markaana uu sababi karo in ciidamada Itoobiya laga saaro Soomaaliya. Wakiilka Somaliland ee Israel, Maxamed Xaaji, ayaa sheegay in qiimeynta safiirka Itoobiya ay tahay mid aan sax ahayn, isagoo ku dooday in aqoonsiga Somaliland uu Addis Ababa u horseedi karo faa’iidooyin waaweyn oo dhinacyada amniga, dhaqaalaha iyo istaraatiijiyadda ah. “Waxaan ku qanacsanahay in arrintu ay taa caksigeeda tahay. Itoobiya waxay aqoonsiga Somaliland ka heli kartaa faa’iidooyin istaraatiiji ah, dhaqaale iyo amni oo aad u waaweyn, iyadoo aysan jirin wax khatar amni ah,” ayuu Maxamed Xaaji ku qoray bartiisa X. Jawaabtiisa ayaa timid kaddib markii safiirka Itoobiya ee Israel, Tesfaye Yetayeh Anteneh, uu wareysi uu siiyay telefishinka i24NEWS ku sheegay in aqoonsiga Somaliland uu keeni karo in dowladda Soomaaliya ay dalbato in ciidamada Itoobiya laga saaro dalkeeda, taas oo fursad siin karta kooxda Al-Shabaab. Safiirka ayaa ku dooday in tallaabadaasi ay abuuri karto xaalad amni oo halis ah, taas oo saameyn karta Soomaaliya, Somaliland iyo Itoobiya lafteeda, isagoo ku baaqay inaan lagu degdegin go’aanka aqoonsiga. Hase yeeshee, Maxamed Xaaji ayaa dooddaas ku tilmaamay mid aan tixgelinayn faa’iidooyinka ay Itoobiya ka heli karto xiriir rasmi ah oo ay la yeelato Somaliland. Waxa uu ku eedeeyay dowladda Soomaaliya inay xiriir dhow la sameysaneyso dalal ay Itoobiya ku loollamayaan gobolka, kuwaas oo uu sheegay inay dano istaraatiiji ah ka leeyihiin Soomaaliya, isla markaana ay khatar ku noqon karaan amniga Addis Ababa. Wakiilka ayaa sidoo kale ku dooday in Somaliland ay ku guuleysatay inay ka hortagto in Al-Shabaab iyo kooxaha burcad-badeeddu ay saldhigyo ka sameystaan deegaannada ay maamusho, taas oo uu sheegay inay caddeyn u tahay in Somaliland ay noqon karto saaxiib amni oo lagu kalsoonaan karo. Dhinaca kale, Maxamed Xaaji ayaa su’aal geliyay sababta joogitaanka ciidamada Itoobiya ee Soomaaliya looga dhigayo caqabad hortaagan aqoonsiga Somaliland. “Ciidamada Afrika lagama filan karo inay Soomaaliya sii joogaan weligood,” ayuu yiri, isagoo ku baaqay in laga sii shaqeeyo qorshaha mustaqbalka ee bixitaanka ciidamadaasi. Waxa uu intaas ku daray in aqoonsiga Somaliland uu Itoobiya siin karo saaxiib istaraatiiji ah oo lagu kalsoonaan karo, dardargelin karo koboca dhaqaalaha, isla markaana ballaarin karo saameynteeda gobolka Geeska Afrika iyo Badda Cas. Is-weydaarsigan hadallada ayaa dib u soo nooleeyay doodda ku saabsan mowqifka Itoobiya ee Somaliland, gaar ahaan kaddib markii Israel ay bishii December 2025 si rasmi ah u aqoonsatay Somaliland. Itoobiya ayaa horay Somaliland ula saxiixatay heshiis is-afgarad oo la xiriiray marin-badeed bishii Janaayo 2024. Heshiiskaas ayaa Itoobiya siin lahaa dhul badeed 20km ah, halka Addis Ababa ay aqoonsan laheyd Somaliland. Heshiiska ayaa dhaliyay khilaaf diblomaasiyadeed oo xooggan oo kala dhex galay Soomaaliya iyo Itoobiya. Khilaafkaas ayaa markii dambe lagu qaboojiyay heshiiskii Ankara ee December 2024, kaas oo labada dowladood ay ku xaqiijiyeen ixtiraamka madax-bannaanida iyo midnimada dhuleed ee midba midka kale. Inkastoo safiirka Itoobiya uusan gebi ahaanba meesha ka saarin aqoonsiga Somaliland mustaqbalka, haddana waxa uu caddeeyay in Addis Ababa aysan ku degdegi karin tallaabo saameyn ku yeelan karta iskaashiga amni ee ay la leedahay Soomaaliya. Jawaabtiisa ayaa timid kaddib markii safiirka Itoobiya ee Israel, Tesfaye Yetayeh Anteneh, uu wareysi uu siiyay telefishinka i24NEWS ku sheegay in aqoonsiga Somaliland uu keeni karo in dowladda Soomaaliya ay dalbato in ciidamada Itoobiya laga saaro dalkeeda, taas oo fursad siin karta kooxda Al-Shabaab. Safiirka ayaa ku dooday in tallaabadaasi ay abuuri karto xaalad amni oo halis ah, taas oo saameyn karta Soomaaliya, Somaliland iyo Itoobiya lafteeda, isagoo ku baaqay inaan lagu degdegin go’aanka aqoonsiga. Hase yeeshee, Maxamed Xaaji ayaa dooddaas ku tilmaamay mid aan tixgelinayn faa’iidooyinka ay Itoobiya ka heli karto xiriir rasmi ah oo ay la yeelato Somaliland. Waxa uu ku eedeeyay dowladda Soomaaliya inay xiriir dhow la sameysaneyso dalal ay Itoobiya ku loollamayaan gobolka, kuwaas oo uu sheegay inay dano istaraatiiji ah ka leeyihiin Soomaaliya, isla markaana ay khatar ku noqon karaan amniga Addis Ababa. Wakiilka ayaa sidoo kale ku dooday in Somaliland ay ku guuleysatay inay ka hortagto in Al-Shabaab iyo kooxaha burcad-badeeddu ay saldhigyo ka sameystaan deegaannada ay maamusho, taas oo uu sheegay inay caddeyn u tahay in Somaliland ay noqon karto saaxiib amni oo lagu kalsoonaan karo. Dhinaca kale, Maxamed Xaaji ayaa su’aal geliyay sababta joogitaanka ciidamada Itoobiya ee Soomaaliya looga dhigayo caqabad hortaagan aqoonsiga Somaliland. “Ciidamada Afrika lagama filan karo inay Soomaaliya sii joogaan weligood,” ayuu yiri, isagoo ku baaqay in laga sii shaqeeyo qorshaha mustaqbalka ee bixitaanka ciidamadaasi. Waxa uu intaas ku daray in aqoonsiga Somaliland uu Itoobiya siin karo saaxiib istaraatiiji ah oo lagu kalsoonaan karo, dardargelin karo koboca dhaqaalaha, isla markaana ballaarin karo saameynteeda gobolka Geeska Afrika iyo Badda Cas. Is-weydaarsigan hadallada ayaa dib u soo nooleeyay doodda ku saabsan mowqifka Itoobiya ee Somaliland, gaar ahaan kaddib markii Israel ay bishii December 2025 si rasmi ah u aqoonsatay Somaliland. Itoobiya ayaa horay Somaliland ula saxiixatay heshiis is-afgarad oo la xiriiray marin-badeed bishii Janaayo 2024. Heshiiskaas ayaa Itoobiya siin lahaa dhul badeed 20km ah, halka Addis Ababa ay aqoonsan laheyd Somaliland. Heshiiska ayaa dhaliyay khilaaf diblomaasiyadeed oo xooggan oo kala dhex galay Soomaaliya iyo Itoobiya. Khilaafkaas ayaa markii dambe lagu qaboojiyay heshiiskii Ankara ee December 2024, kaas oo labada dowladood ay ku xaqiijiyeen ixtiraamka madax-bannaanida iyo midnimada dhuleed ee midba midka kale. Inkastoo safiirka Itoobiya uusan gebi ahaanba meesha ka saarin aqoonsiga Somaliland mustaqbalka, haddana waxa uu caddeeyay in Addis Ababa aysan ku degdegi karin tallaabo saameyn ku yeelan karta iskaashiga amni ee ay la leedahay Soomaaliya.
