items.title: The would-be African nation in love with Donald Trump
items.description: Many people in Somaliland are convinced that the United States, under the incoming presidency of Donald Trump, is poised to become the world’s first country to recognise the self-declared republic. The territory declared independence 33 years ago after Somalia descended into civil war – and in many ways has functioned as a de facto nation-state ever since. “Donald is our saviour. He is a wise and practical man. God bless America,” says university student Aisha Ismail, whose voice trembles with delight at the prospect. She is speaking to me from Hargeisa, Somaliland’s capital – a city 850km (530 miles) north of Mogadishu, the seat of Somalia’s government. For those in Mogadishu, Somaliland is an indivisible part of Somalia. “I doubt Donald Trump knows what Somaliland is, never mind where it is,” says Abdi Mohamud, a data analyst in Mogadishu, whose voice starts to shake. “I am spitting fire.” He is so angry because Ms Ismail’s great expectation is not necessarily a pipe dream, at least in the long term. Powerful and influential Republicans are pushing for the same thing, including Congressman Scott Perry who last month introduced a bill proposing formal US recognition for Somaliland . It followed the publication in April 2023 of Project 2025 , a roadmap for the second Trump presidency compiled by the prominent right-wing Heritage Foundation and more than 100 other conservative organisations The document mentions only two African territories in its sub-Saharan Africa section – Somaliland and Djibouti – and proposes “the recognition of Somaliland statehood as a hedge against the US’s deteriorating position in Djibouti”. Getty Images Any move towards recognising Somaliland’s independence would not only contravene Somalia’s sovereignty but also destabilise the region by setting a dangerous precedent” Ali Mohamed Omar Somali state minister for foreign affairs However, the fact that sub-Saharan Africa takes up less than two pages in the 900-plus page plan suggests the continent is very low on the priority list. Also, there is no guarantee the incoming administration will follow the blueprint, some of which Trump has already disavowed. But one thing is clear. The US has already started to change its stance on Somaliland, moving away from its Mogadishu-focused approach, known as the “one-track” Somalia policy. Somalia has cost the US dearly in financial, resource and human terms since the early 1990s when the bodies of 18 American servicemen were dragged through the streets of Mogadishu after US helicopters were shot down by Somali clan fighters. The battle, known as “Black Hawk Down”, was America’s worst in terms of casualties since the Vietnam War. “Any move towards recognising Somaliland’s independence would not only contravene Somalia’s sovereignty but also destabilise the region by setting a dangerous precedent,” says Somali State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ali Mohamed Omar. The African Union and other global powers believe territorial integrity is paramount. Recognising Somaliland could set off a chain reaction with separatists across the world demanding recognition for the territories they claim. Omar also highlighted concerns about a possible repeat of the first Trump administration’s decision to withdraw from Somalia most American troops who have been fighting al-Shabab, regularly described as al-Qaeda’s most successful affiliate. Under Joe Biden’s presidency about 500 US troops have been stationed in Somalia – carrying out special operations and training an elite Somali force, Danab, which means “Lightning” and has proved more effective than the regular Somali army at rooting out al-Shabab. The Americans have an airbase at Baledogle, north-west of Mogadishu, and conduct regular airstrikes against Islamist insurgents. “A withdrawal would create a significant security vacuum, emboldening terrorist groups and threatening the stability of not only Somalia but the broader Horn of Africa,” Omar warned. Getty Images The US has been training members of Somalia’s elite Danab brigade to take on Islamist militants The minister’s remarks are in a similar vein but more measured than Somalia’s response to a deal between Somaliland and Ethiopia whereby recognition would reportedly be granted in exchange for sea access. I received late-night calls from Somalis who said they were unable to sleep over the controversial proposal. Somalia’s then-Environment Minister Aden Ibrahim Aw Hirsi told me at the time: “You are always going on about ‘political bombshells’ in your reporting. “People here are talking about a political earthquake. This is far more serious. It is a tsunami.” Turkey has since mediated an end to the feud but the fact that Somalia recently signed a $600,000 (£492,000) a year deal with top Washington lobbying firm, the BGR Group, suggests it is worried about relations with the incoming Trump administration. The US last month abstained from voting on a UN Security Council resolution to fund the latest incarnation of the African Union intervention force in Somalia. A key architect of Republican Africa thinking, especially when it comes to Somali issues, is Joshua Meservey, who recently moved from the Heritage Foundation to the right-leaning Hudson Institute. “The case for Somaliland in US terms is very compelling,” he argues. “I think the question of recognition will definitely be discussed, although the guiding north star is what is best for US national interests in practical terms.” Senior Africa officials under Trump mark one, including the former Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, Tibor Nagy, and Africa envoy, Peter Pham, are energetic supporters of Somaliland’s independence. Like many American Republicans, Somaliland’s Foreign Minister Abdirahman Dahir Adan sees the relationship in transactional terms. “If the deal is good for us, we will take it. If the US wants a military base here we will give it to them.” Recognition sympathisers argue that Somaliland is located at the site of several converging US interests – economic, military and strategic. Mr Meservey adds that the territory should be “rewarded” for adhering to democratic principles, not relying on foreign aid and having a small government. Its long coastline runs along one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes. Yemen’s Iranian-backed Houthi rebels may have replaced Somali pirates as the main disruptor of traffic in the area but the attacks remain a major threat to global trade and draw the region closer to the war in the Middle East. The scramble for foreign bases along the Horn of Africa’s coast is of concern to the US, which established its largest military facility on the continent in Djibouti in 2002. Russia has its eyes on Port Sudan; the United Arab Emirates (UAE) used Eritrea’s Assab to fight the Houthis and Djibouti is chock-a-block with foreign forces, including the Chinese, who not only have a well-placed military facility but also run the huge port. Turkey’s largest base on foreign soil stretches along Somalia’s coastline just south of Mogadishu. Dealing with a rising China is a top Trump priority. The US has accused the Chinese of interfering with its activities in Djibouti by shining lasers into the eyes of its air force pilots and is keen to move elsewhere. It also wants to disrupt China’s Belt and Road Initiative, which is taking over much of Africa. The Red Sea port of Berbera, whether you see it as part of Somaliland or Somalia, has much to offer as an alternative. China is not there; indeed it is outraged that Taiwan in 2020 established diplomatic relations with the breakaway republic. The UAE, a key US ally, runs the recently expanded port and hopes it will rival Djibouti. During the Biden administration, top American officials, including the chief of US Africa Command (Africom), conducted site visits of Berbera, which has a 4km runway ironically constructed by the Soviet Union during the Cold War. This was later identified by the US as an emergency landing site for space shuttles – interesting given Trump’s ally Elon Musk’s obsession with space. In 2022, the US National Defence Authorisation Act was amended to include Somaliland, enhancing security co-operation and potentially paving the way for stronger diplomatic and economic ties. AFP Donald Trump may be enticed to recognise Somaliland if he sees a good business deal in it Pro-recognition Republicans have presented Somaliland as a good business case, hoping to appeal to Trump’s deal-making approach. Project 2025 used the term “hedge”. A US-based Somaliland diplomat said: “It depends how they sell it to him. They have to make it attractive; they have to seduce him.” Whether he means it or not, bringing up the explosive issue of recognition would likely suit Trump the disruptor. It would certainly bring him attention and he could boast about being first. It would also enrage Somalia, a country he included in his reported 2018 list of “shithole” nations and a place to which he wants to deport undocumented Somalis, failed asylum seekers and criminals. There is already talk in Somaliland that the territory will be used as a “dumping ground” for such people in exchange for US recognition. US academic Ken Menkhaus, who has followed Somali issues for decades, brings much-needed balance to the debate. “It is very likely we will see significant shifts in US policy towards Somaliland and Somalia,” he says. “Mr Trump has a deep suspicion of foreign aid, is sceptical about state-building and is a neo-isolationist.” The Horn of Africa needs to be braced for change. Mary Harper has written two books about Somalia, including Everything You Have Told Me Is True, a look at life under al-Shabab.

items.description: 𝐌𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐜𝐲𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐢 𝐃𝐡𝐮𝐥𝐤𝐚 𝐒𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝: Sooyaal 11 Kun oo sanno ah !! Sida ay ku xuseen Buugga Pastoral Democracy taariikhyahanada waawayn ee Siciid Samatar iyo I.M. Lewis, kelmada ama magaca “Soomaali” maaha mid da’weyn marka laga hadlayo taariikhda qoran oo waxaa qoraal laga heli karo u horaysay qarnigii 15naad. Somaliland oo ah goob facwayn oo taariikh badani ka lunsan tahay magacyadii loo diwaangeliyay waxaa ka mid ah: 𝟏. 𝐃𝐡𝐮𝐥𝐤𝐢𝐢 𝐈𝐥𝐚𝐚𝐡𝐲𝐚𝐝𝐚 (𝐓𝐚 𝐍𝐞𝐭𝐣𝐞𝐫) 𝐢𝐲𝐨 𝐋𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐟 𝐏𝐮𝐧𝐭 (𝐃𝐡𝐮𝐥𝐤𝐢𝐢 𝐔𝐝𝐮𝐠𝐚): 4500 sanno ka hor ayay u yaqaaneen masaaridii hore labbadan magac waxayna ahayd meel ay ka barakaystaan. 𝟐. 𝐌𝐚𝐜𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐢𝐚 (𝐂𝐢𝐦𝐫𝐢 𝐃𝐡𝐞𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐲𝐚𝐚𝐥): 2,550 sanno ka hor ayay magacan u xuseen Giriigu waxaana lagu sheegaa inay ahayd Somaliland, waa dhul ay ku noolaayeen dad hodan ah, qorqoran, dhaadheer oo aad u cimri dheeraa. 𝟑. 𝐌𝐚𝐥𝐚𝐨 (𝐁𝐞𝐫𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐚), 𝐀𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐬 (𝐙𝐞𝐢𝐥𝐚), 𝐌𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐮𝐬 (𝐗𝐢𝐢𝐬), 𝐢𝐲𝐨 𝐀𝐜𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐞 (𝐌𝐚𝐲𝐝𝐡): 1970 sanno ka hor, Giriigu mar kale waxay ku xuseen inay Somaliland ka jireen magaalooyin ganacsiyeed qani ah oo ay ugu mudnaayeen Saylac iyo Berbera. 𝟒. 𝐋𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐟 𝐏𝐨-𝐩𝐚-𝐥𝐢 (𝐁𝐞𝐫𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐚): 1,660 sanno ka hor taariikhyahanka Shiinaha ah ee Tuan Ch’eng-shih wuxuu ku magacaabay Somaliland dhulkii Berberiyiinta, waa markii ugu horaysay ee Shiinuhu Afrika yimaado waana barta ay u aqoonsan yihiin inuu ka bilaabmay xidhiidhka Africa iyo Shiinuhu. 𝟓. 𝐈𝐟𝐚𝐭 𝐒𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐞 / 𝐙𝐞𝐢𝐥𝐚 𝐒𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐞: 800 sanno ka hor 𝟔. 𝐀𝐝𝐚𝐥 𝐒𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐞: 600 sanno ka hor 𝟕. 𝐁𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐬𝐡 𝐒𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝: 1884 – 1960 𝟖. 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐒𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝: 26 June – 1 July 1960 𝟗. 𝐒𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐚: 1960 – 1991 𝟏𝟎. 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜 𝐨𝐟 𝐒𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝: 1991 – hadda Dr Cabdiqani Muse Xasan

𝐌𝐚𝐜𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐢𝐚 (𝐂𝐢𝐦𝐫𝐢 𝐃𝐡𝐞𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐲𝐚𝐚𝐥): 2,550 sanno ka hor ayay magacan u xuseen Giriigu waxaana lagu sheegaa inay ahayd Somaliland, waa dhul ay ku noolaayeen dad hodan ah, qorqoran, dhaadheer oo aad u cimri dheeraa. 𝟑. 𝐌𝐚𝐥𝐚𝐨 (𝐁𝐞𝐫𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐚), 𝐀𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐬 (𝐙𝐞𝐢𝐥𝐚), 𝐌𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐮𝐬 (𝐗𝐢𝐢𝐬), 𝐢𝐲𝐨 𝐀𝐜𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐞 (𝐌𝐚𝐲𝐝𝐡): 1970 sanno ka hor, Giriigu mar kale waxay ku xuseen inay Somaliland ka jireen magaalooyin ganacsiyeed qani ah oo ay ugu mudnaayeen Saylac iyo Berbera. 𝟒. 𝐋𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐟 𝐏𝐨-𝐩𝐚-𝐥𝐢 (𝐁𝐞𝐫𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐚): 1,660 sanno ka hor taariikhyahanka Shiinaha ah ee Tuan Ch’eng-shih wuxuu ku magacaabay Somaliland dhulkii Berberiyiinta, waa markii ugu horaysay ee Shiinuhu Afrika yimaado waana barta ay u aqoonsan yihiin inuu ka bilaabmay xidhiidhka Africa iyo Shiinuhu. 𝟓. 𝐈𝐟𝐚𝐭 𝐒𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐞 / 𝐙𝐞𝐢𝐥𝐚 𝐒𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐞: 800 sanno ka hor 𝟔. 𝐀𝐝𝐚𝐥 𝐒𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐞: 600 sanno ka hor 𝟕. 𝐁𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐬𝐡 𝐒𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝: 1884 – 1960 𝟖. 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐒𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝: 26 June – 1 July 1960 𝟗. 𝐒𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐚: 1960 – 1991 𝟏𝟎. 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜 𝐨𝐟 𝐒𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝: 1991 – hadda Dr Cabdiqani Muse Xasan

items.title: Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka oo Kulan la Qaatay Guddiga Garsoorka iyo Arrimaha Diinta
items.description: Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka ee Baarlamaanka Federaalka Soomaaliya, Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac), ayaa kulan la qaatay Guddiga Garsoorka, Awqaafta iyo Arrimaha Diinta ee Golaha Shacabka, kaas oo diiradda lagu saaray dib-u-eegista iyo casriyeynta Sharciga Ciqaabta Soomaaliya. Kulanka oo uu sidoo kale ka qeybgalay Wasiirka Wasaaradda Caddaaladda iyo Arrimaha Dastuurka, Xasan Macallin Maxamuud, ayaa looga hadlay Hindise-Sharciyeedka Sharciga Ciqaabta Soomaaliya oo horyaalla Golaha Shacabka, iyadoo la doonayo in la waafajiyo isbeddellada bulsho, dhaqaale iyo teknoolojiyadeed ee dalka ka dhacay. Doodaha kulanka ayaa si gaar ah diiradda loogu saaray baahida loo qabo in sharciga ciqaabta lagu daro qodobo ka jawaabaya noocyada cusub ee dembiyada, gaar ahaan kuwa la xiriira teknoolojiyadda iyo nidaamyada macluumaadka, kuwaas oo u baahan hab sharciyeed casri ah oo wax looga qabto. Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka, Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac), ayaa sheegay in casriyeynta Sharciga Ciqaabtu ay muhiim u tahay xoojinta caddaaladda, ilaalinta xuquuqda muwaadiniinta, sugidda amniga iyo dhowrista kala dambeynta bulshada. Waxa uu sidoo kale carrabka ku adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay in Soomaaliya yeelato nidaam sharciyeed la jaanqaadaya baahiyaha bulshada maanta iyo kuwa mustaqbalka, si loo xoojiyo ku dhaqanka sharciga loona helo hannaan caddaaladeed oo wax ka qaban kara caqabadaha cusub ee dalka. Kulankan ayaa qeyb ka ah dadaallada lagu horumarinayo shuruucda dalka, si ay uga jawaabaan isbeddellada socda, una xoojiyaan caddaaladda iyo dowladnimada Soomaaliya.

items.title: GOLAHA WASIIRRADA OO ANSIXIYAY QARAARKA DHAQAN-GELINTA DASTUURKA
items.description: Muqdisho, 13 Oktoobar 2026 — Golaha Wasiirrada Xukuumadda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa ansixiyay qaraarka dhaqan-gelinta Dastuurka, iyaga oo sidoo kale guddi wasiirro ah u saaray diyaarinta hindise-xeerka qeexaya tirada xubnaha Xukuumadda iyo waajibaadkooda. Shir aan caadi ahayn oo caawa uu guddoomiyay Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamsa Cabdi Barre ayaa looga hadlay fulinta Dastuurka, dowlad-dhiska, xoojinta hay’adaha dowladda iyo horumarinta nidaamyada maamulka qaranka. Goluhu wuxuu guddi uu hoggaaminayo Wasiirka Caddaaladda iyo Arrimaha Dastuurka u xilsaaray dardargelinta fulinta Dastuurka iyo diyaarinta hindise-xeerka dhismaha Xukuumadda, kaas oo lagu wado in lagu soo diyaariyo muddo laba bilood ah. Sida lagu sheegay war-saxaafadeedka Xukuumadda, xeerkan ayaa qeexaya tirada xubnaha Xukuumadda iyo waajibaadkooda, waxaana lagu tilmaamay xeer markii ugu horreysay dalka yeelanayo tan iyo 1968-kii. Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamsa Cabdi Barre ayaa sheegay in Dastuurku dhaqan-gal yahay, fulintiisana loo marayo marxalado kala duwan. Waxa uu sidoo kale xusay in Xukuumaddu ku howlan tahay sidii sannadka 2027 dalka looga qaban lahaa doorasho qof iyo cod ah oo heer federaal ah, sida uu dhigayo Dastuurka dalka. Dhanka kale, Wasaaradda Gaadiidka iyo Duulista Hawada ayaa Golaha Wasiirrada u soo bandhigtay warbixin ku saabsan dib u soo celinta nidaamka code-ka Soomaaliya ee IATA, kaas oo loo adeegsado maamulka iyo nidaaminta tikidhada diyaaradaha. Wasaaraddu waxay sheegtay in dib u soo celinta nidaamkan ay Soomaaliya u suuragelinayso inay xoojiso awooddeeda maareynta adeegyada tikidhada duulimaadyada iyo xiriirka nidaamyada safarrada caalamiga ah, taas oo qayb ka ah horumarinta adeegyada duulista rayidka iyo dib u soo celinta xuquuqo muhiim ah oo dalka ka maqnaa.

items.title: Maxkamadda Sare oo go’aan kama dambeys kasoo saartay doorashadii Galmudug
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Maxkamadda Sare ee dalka ayaa si kama dambays ah u ansixisay natiijada doorashadii ku celiska ahayd ee Galmudug, taas oo dhacday 30-kii Sebtembar ee sanadkan 2026, ayna ka qayb-galeen 12 urur oo ku loollamay 89 kursi oo Golaha Wakiillada ah. Maxkamaddu oo qoraal soo saartay ayaa sheegtay in aanay jirin dacwad sharci ah oo laga keenay natiijada doorashada Galmudug, sidaas darteedna ay si rasmi ah u ansixisay natiijada doorashada ku-celiska ahayd ee Golaha Wakiillada Dowlad-goboleedka Galmudug. Sidoo kale, Maxkamadda Sare ayaa amartay in go’aanka ansixinta natiijada doorashada loo gudbiyo Guddiga Madaxa-bannaan ee Doorashooyinka Qaranka iyo Soohdimaha, si loo fuliyo tallaabooyinka xiga ee waafaqsan shuruucda iyo habraacyada doorashooyinka dalka. Natiijada oo horay la shaaciyay ayaa muujineysa in ururka Caddaaladda iyo Midnimadda uu ku guuleystay 1,085 cod iyo hal kursi, halka Madalsan uu helay 4,025 cod iyo laba kursi. Ururka Muwaadiniinta Soomaaliyeed ayaa helay 842 cod iyo hal kursi, halka Dimuqraadiga Soomaaliyeed uu ku guuleystay 2,283 cod iyo hal kursi. Caddaaladda iyo Wadajir ayaa noqday ururka ugu codadka badan, isagoo helay 110,072 cod iyo 67 kursi, halka Dadka Soomaaliyeed uu helay 158 cod, balse uusan wax kursi ah ku guuleysan. Sidoo kale, Karaama ayaa heshay 10,309 cod iyo lix kursi, halka SAAB ay heshay 880 cod iyo hal kursi. Dan Shacab ayaa isna helay 738 cod, balse wax kursi ah ma uusan helin. Ururka Sincad ayaa helay 10,895 cod iyo toddoba kursi, halka Dhallinyarada Talo-Qaran ay heleen 2,043 cod iyo hal kursi. RamaaS ayaa iyaduna heshay 3,044 cod iyo laba kursi. Natiijada guud ayaa muujineysa in 89-ka kursi ee Golaha Wakiillada Galmudug loo kala helay 12-ka urur siyaasadeed, iyadoo Caddaaladda iyo Wadajir ay heleen 67 kursi, Sincadna uu ku xigay toddoba kursi, halka Karaama ay heshay lix kursi. Doorashadan ayaa qayb ka ah hannaanka doorashooyinka qof iyo cod ee Soomaaliya, iyadoo guddigu sheegay in hawlaha doorashooyinku ay ka socdaan meelo kala duwan oo dalka ah. The post Maxkamadda Sare oo go’aan kama dambeys kasoo saartay doorashadii Galmudug appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: The Somali Regional State confirm that Somali troops have entered Ethiopia.
items.description: The Ethiopian Somali Regional State has confirmed for the first time that troops trained by the Federal Government of Somalia have entered Ethiopian territory and are currently undergoing a formal bilateral process. The region’s security chief, Abdulkadir Rashid Duale, stated that the troops recently arrived in Jigjiga after crossing the border between Somalia and Ethiopia. He noted that the troops were deployed in groups and are currently subject to the established procedures and agreements between the two nations. He explained that the troops did not initially cross into Ethiopia under a clearly defined process confirming the purpose of their movement, but efforts are now underway to align the situation with the laws and protocols of both countries. According to him, the matter is being handled by the legal and diplomatic authorities of Somalia and Ethiopia, who are working toward a formal resolution. Duale also stated that verified news and official information regarding the issue would be shared with the public, while warning against the spread of unverified reports that could cause confusion. These troops had recently been stationed within the Somali Regional State but have now been moved to the city of Dire Dawa, according to available information. Reports also indicate that the leaders of Somalia and Ethiopia have discussed the status of these troops, with the possibility that they may be airlifted back to Somalia. These soldiers were among thousands trained this year in the Galgaduud region—troops the government stated were intended to fight the Al-Shabaab group. After their training concluded, hundreds of these soldiers defected to Ethiopia, reportedly taking with them the weapons the government had issued to them upon completion of their training. Somaliland standard

items.title: Xog: Golaha wasiirrada oo caawa leh shir deg-deg ah + Ujeedka
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Golaha Wasiirrada Xukuumadda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa la filayaa in caawa ay yeeshaan shir deg-deg ah, kaas oo uu isugu yeeray Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Soomaaliya, Xamza Cabdi Barre. Sida ay ogaatay Caasimada Online, shirkan ayaa diiradda lagu saari doono xaaladihii ugu dambeeyay ee dalka, gaar ahaan arrimaha amniga iyo dastuurka cusub, maadaama berri wixi ka dambeeyo qorshuhu yahay in la kala saaro xukuumadda iyo baarlamaanka. Xukuumadda Dan-Qaran ayaa la filayaa inay Guddiga Madaxa-bannaan ee Dastuurka ka dalbato waqti dheeraad ah, si loo kala caddeeyo xilalka wasiirka iyo xildhibaanka. Sidoo kale, waxaa suuragal ah in golaha wasiirrada ay qaadaan tallaabooyin la xiriira isbeddal dhanka hoggaanka sare ee laamaha amniga, si wax looga qabto xaaladaha kasoo cusboonaaday caasimada oo maalmahan laga dareemayay dhaq-dhaqaaqyo ciidan. Wararka ayaa intaas kusii daraya in shirka warbixin looga dhageysan doono Maareeyaha Hay’adda Duulista Rayidka Axmed Macalin, taas oo la xiriirta soo dhaweynta khubarro sare oo ka socda hay’adda u qaabilsan adduunka arrimaha duulimaadyada iyo rakaabka ee magaceeda loo soo gaabiyo IATA. kuwaasi oo Muqdisho imaan doona 18,ka bishan. Guddiga Madaxa-bannaan ee Dib-u-eegista iyo Hirgelinta Dastuurka ayaa maalmo ka hor ku dhawaaqay in la dhaqan-gelinayo dastuurka cusub, iyadoo 14-ka bishan loo qabtay wasiirrada sidoo kale xubnaha ka ah baarlamaanka, si loo kala saaro labada xil ee wasiirnimo iyo xildhibaannimo. “Waxaa dhaqangalaya, maalinta 14aad ee bisha Oktoobar 2026, Qodobka 81aad, Faqradda 1aad, xarafka (f) iyo Qodobka 117aad, Faqradda 3(a) ee Dastuurka, oo xeerinaya kala saaridda xildhibaannada iyo Wasiirrada, taas oo ah in wasiirka ah xildhibaan uu luminayo xubinnimada Golaha Wasiirrada. Sidoo kale, xildhibaanku wuxuu luminayaa xildhibaannimada haddii uu aqbalo xil kale oo dawladeed,” ayaa lagu yiri bayaankii u dambeeyay ee guddiga. Soomaaliya ayaa haatan ku jirto marxalad xasaasi ah, iyadoo weli ay taagan tahay xiisad culus oo ka dhalatay wax ka beddelka dastuurka iyo hannaanka doorashooyinka dalka. Sida ay ogaatay Caasimada Online, shirkan ayaa diiradda lagu saari doono xaaladihii ugu dambeeyay ee dalka, gaar ahaan arrimaha amniga iyo dastuurka cusub, maadaama berri wixi ka dambeeyo qorshuhu yahay in la kala saaro xukuumadda iyo baarlamaanka. Xukuumadda Dan-Qaran ayaa la filayaa inay Guddiga Madaxa-bannaan ee Dastuurka ka dalbato waqti dheeraad ah, si loo kala caddeeyo xilalka wasiirka iyo xildhibaanka. Sidoo kale, waxaa suuragal ah in golaha wasiirrada ay qaadaan tallaabooyin la xiriira isbeddal dhanka hoggaanka sare ee laamaha amniga, si wax looga qabto xaaladaha kasoo cusboonaaday caasimada oo maalmahan laga dareemayay dhaq-dhaqaaqyo ciidan. Wararka ayaa intaas kusii daraya in shirka warbixin looga dhageysan doono Maareeyaha Hay’adda Duulista Rayidka Axmed Macalin, taas oo la xiriirta soo dhaweynta khubarro sare oo ka socda hay’adda u qaabilsan adduunka arrimaha duulimaadyada iyo rakaabka ee magaceeda loo soo gaabiyo IATA. kuwaasi oo Muqdisho imaan doona 18,ka bishan. Guddiga Madaxa-bannaan ee Dib-u-eegista iyo Hirgelinta Dastuurka ayaa maalmo ka hor ku dhawaaqay in la dhaqan-gelinayo dastuurka cusub, iyadoo 14-ka bishan loo qabtay wasiirrada sidoo kale xubnaha ka ah baarlamaanka, si loo kala saaro labada xil ee wasiirnimo iyo xildhibaannimo. “Waxaa dhaqangalaya, maalinta 14aad ee bisha Oktoobar 2026, Qodobka 81aad, Faqradda 1aad, xarafka (f) iyo Qodobka 117aad, Faqradda 3(a) ee Dastuurka, oo xeerinaya kala saaridda xildhibaannada iyo Wasiirrada, taas oo ah in wasiirka ah xildhibaan uu luminayo xubinnimada Golaha Wasiirrada. Sidoo kale, xildhibaanku wuxuu luminayaa xildhibaannimada haddii uu aqbalo xil kale oo dawladeed,” ayaa lagu yiri bayaankii u dambeeyay ee guddiga. Soomaaliya ayaa haatan ku jirto marxalad xasaasi ah, iyadoo weli ay taagan tahay xiisad culus oo ka dhalatay wax ka beddelka dastuurka iyo hannaanka doorashooyinka dalka. items.title: Somalia says 260 armed men removed from opposition leaders’ homes
items.description: MOGADISHU – Somalia’s Defence Minister Ahmed Moalim Fiqi said on Tuesday that authorities had removed 260 armed men from opposition leaders’ homes in the capital Mogadishu, accusing them of threatening security. Fiqi said the men were in government custody and would be presented to the media. He alleged that other armed fighters remained in the residences. He accused the United Arab Emirates of arming opposition leaders and said recent talks hosted by the UAE were aimed at destabilising Somalia. He also alleged that forces linked to the regional administrations of Puntland and Jubaland had been brought to Mogadishu and armed inside opposition leaders’ homes. Fiqi rejected reports that the government was preparing a military operation to disarm and arrest opposition leaders, accusing them instead of provoking security agencies. The dispute comes amid mounting tensions between Somalia’s federal government and opposition figures, with residents fearing the standoff could escalate into a wider conflict. items.title: Kooxda Lafta-gareen oo jawaab ka bixisay tallaabada DF
items.description: Nairobi (Caasimada Online) – Kooxda taaabacsan madaxweynihii hore ee Koonfur Galbeed, Cabdicasiis Xasan Maxamed (Lafta-gareen) ayaa jawaab deg-deg ah ka bixisay tallaabada ay maanta qaaday dowladda Soomaaliya oo cunaqabateyn kusoo rogtay shaqsiyaadkaas, kadib markii ay ku eedeysay inay ku lug leeyihiin maalgelinta iyo taageeridda kooxda Al-Shabaab. Guddiga Qaran ee ka-hortagga lacag-dhaqidda iyo la-dagaallanka maalgelinta Argagixisada oo soo saaray war-saxaafadeed ayaa liiska cunaqabataynta maaliyadeed ee Cayiman ku daray shakhsiyaadkan oo haatan dagaal adag kula jiray maamulka Koonfur Galbeed. Xubnaha cunaqabateynta la saaray ayaa kala ah;- 1-Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed (Laftagareen) 2- Hassan Abdulkadir Mohamed 3- Mahad Abdirahman Adan (Shub) 4- Ibrahim Adan Ali (Najah) 5- Hassan Abdi Mohamed (Ugaas Hassan) 6-Abdullahi Ali Watiin 7-Abdifatah Mahad Abdirahman 8-Abdimajid Mowlid Hassan 9-Amiin Mad Daruur 10-Abshir Aden Isak. Intaas kadib waxaa soo jawaabtay, Ugaas Xasan Cabdi Maxamed oo ku magacaaban mas’uulka warfaafinta ee Lafta-gareen, kaas oo kamid ah shaqsiyaadka xayiraadda la saaray, wuxuuna sheegay in argoosi ay u arkaan go’aanka kasoo baxay dowladda Soomaaliya. Ugaas Xasan ayaa sidoo kale tilmaamay in natiijada go’aankan laga arki doono Teendhada Afisyooni oo ah halkii dib loogu soo doortay Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud. “Marka nidaamka maaliyada ee dalka,aargoosi loo isticmaalo, Sharcigii hawada aargoosi loo isticmaalo, ciidanka aargoosi loo isticmaalo, hubkii cunaqabataynta laga qaaday aargoosi loo isticmaalo, E-Visa aargoosi loo isticmaalo. Turkida aargoosi loo isticmaalo. Natiijada ka dhalan karta, waxaa laga dareemi doonaa Teendhada Afisiyooni,” ayuu yiri Ugaas Xasan. Dhinaca kale, Xildhibaan Cabdullahi Aadan kulane oo ka tirsan Golaha Shacabka Soomaaliya oo ka fal-celiyay tallaabada ay qaaday dowladda ayaa kasoo horjeestay, wuxuuna wax laga xumaado ku tilmaamay in siyaasad iyo dano gaar ah loo adeegsado hay’adaha dowladda. “Xaqiiqadii waa ayaan darro in qof kaste oo siyaasad la isku hayaa looga faa’deysto in loo adeegsado Hey’adaha dowladda ee muhiimka u ah qarandhiska. Arrintaan waxay keeneysaa in madaxda maanta joogta ayagana loo adeegsado. Dowladnimadii waxay kusoo aruurtay aargoosi iyo aragti gaabni wadanka sii kala fogeyneysa,” ayuu yiri Cabdullahi Aadan Kulane. Waxaa kale oo uu xildhibaanku sii raaciyay ““Fallaartii Cirka loo ganay, waa taa soo foorartee, nin walboow filo”. Tallaabooyinkan ayaa kusoo aadayo xilli xasaasi ah, isla markaana ay taagan tahay xiisad siyaasadeed oo ka dhalatay hannaanka doorashooyinka iyo wax ka beddelka dastuurka. The post Kooxda Lafta-gareen oo jawaab ka bixisay tallaabada DF appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: MAXKAMADDA SARE OO ANSIXISAY NATIIJADA DOORASHADA KU-CELISKA AH EE GALMUDUG
items.description: Muqdisho, 13 Oktoobar 2026 — Maxkamadda Sare ee Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa maanta si rasmi ah u ansixisay natiijada doorashada ku-celiska ah ee Golaha Wakiillada Dowlad Goboleedka Galmudug, kaddib markii Guddiga Madaxbannaan ee Doorashooyinka Qaranka iyo Soohdimaha uu natiijada u gudbiyay maxkamadda. Guddiga Madaxbannaan ee Doorashooyinka Qaranka iyo Soohdimaha ayaa natiijada doorashada ku-celiska ah u gudbiyay Maxkamadda Sare ee Federaalka, si loo maro hannaanka sharciyeed ee la xiriira ansixinta natiijada doorashada. Maxkamadda Sare ayaa maanta ansixisay natiijada loo soo gudbiyay, taas oo khusaysa doorashada ku-celiska ah ee Golaha Wakiillada Dowlad Goboleedka Galmudug. Tallaabadan ayaa qayb ka ah hannaanka rasmiga ah ee lagu xaqiijinayo natiijooyinka doorashooyinka, iyadoo guddiga doorashooyinka iyo Maxkamadda Sare ay door ku leeyihiin marxaladaha kala duwan ee la xiriira maamulka iyo ansixinta natiijooyinka doorashada.

items.title: Puntland oo gacanta ku soo dhigtay ninkii dadka badan ku laayay Garoowe
items.description: Garoowe (Caasimada Online) – Ciidamada Booliska Puntland oo howlgal gaar ah sameeyay ayaa gacanta kusoo dhigay eedeysane Mowliid Siciid Warsame (Dhakhare) oo loo haysto dad shacab ah oo dhawaan lagu laayay magaalada Garoowe ee xarunta gobolka Nugaal. Warsaxaafadeed kasoo baxay Taliska Booliska Puntland ayaa lagu sheegay in eedeysanaha uu gacanta ku jira la horgeyn doono maxkamad, si looga qaado tallaabo sharciga waafaqsan. Mowliid ayaa si gaar ah loogu eedeeyay dilka saddex qof iyo dhaawac saddex kale oo shacab ah, sida lagu sheegay warka qoraalka ee kasoo baxay Booliska Puntland. “Falka ayaa dhacay 11-kii Oktoobar 2026, agagaarka Suuqa Inji ee Garoowe, waxaana ku dhintay saddex qof, halka saddex kalena ay ku dhaawacmeen,” ayaa lagu yiri qoraalka. Waxaa kale oo lasii raaciyay “Ciidanka Booliska Puntland waxay xaqiijinayaan in eedaysanaha loo gudbin doono hay’adaha sharciga, si kiiska loogu qaado habraacyada sharciga iyo garsoorka dalka”. Eedaysanaha ayaa lagu soo qabtay howlgal ay iska kaashadeen talisyada qaybaha Booliska ee gobollada Nugaal iyo Sool, kaas oo ka dhacay deegaanka Jidhaan, oo u dhow Carooley, halkaas oo ciidamadu ku guuleysteen inay gacanta ku dhigaan. Tallaabadan ayaa si weyn loogu bogaadiyay ciidamada ammaanka ee Puntland maanta ugu dambeyn gacanta kusoo dhigeen eedeysanaha oo baxsad ka ahaa cadaaladda. items.title: Joint Statement on the United Kingdom’s Attribution of Iran’s Involvement in Attempted Terrorist Attack at RAF Fairford
items.description: Joint Statement on the United Kingdom’s Attribution of Iran’s Involvement in Attempted Terrorist Attack at RAF Fairford Office of the Spokesman The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America, the United Kingdom, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, and Sweden. Begin Text. The United States of America, the United Kingdom, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, and Sweden condemn in the strongest terms Iran’s use of violent attacks, including the acts of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities against us and our partners. We recognize the United Kingdom’s attribution of Iran’s involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford on 27 September. The UK has also concluded this event demonstrates the IRGC’s continued willingness to project hostile activity beyond its borders through covert networks and proxy actors. This comes soon after the recent campaign of attacks across Europe targeting Jewish communities, Iranian journalists, and U.S. interests, claimed by Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI). Any attempt by Iran to threaten, silence, intimidate, harass, harm, or coerce people on our territories through proxies or any other means is unacceptable. Anyone who conducts hostile activities on behalf of Iran, or any other state, should know that we will take action to identify, investigate, disrupt, and prosecute these acts. Iran should be in no doubt that we are united and remain committed to safeguarding our sovereignty and strengthening our international coordination, bolstering our national resilience, protecting our communities, and ensuring that those responsible are held to account.

items.title: Ethiopia transfers 220 Somali soldiers to Addis Ababa amid rising tensions
items.description: The soldiers were detained while reportedly on leave in Ethiopia’s Somali Region, raising fresh questions about Mogadishu’s silence and the deteriorating relationship between the two neighbours. JIGJIGA (WDN) — Ethiopia has transferred approximately 220 Somali National Army soldiers to Addis Ababa after detaining them while they were reportedly on leave in Ethiopia’s Somali Regional State, adding to tensions between the two neighbouring countries. The soldiers had been held at Garab Case military camp in Jijiga before Ethiopian military personnel transported them by bus to the capital on Monday. Neither government had publicly provided a detailed explanation of the detention or transfer, according to the available reporting. The troops reportedly belonged to a force whose training President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud attended at Xananbuure, in the Galgaduud region of Galmudug state, in August. Their detention raises questions about why serving Somali military personnel were in Ethiopian territory, the circumstances of their arrest and the purpose of their transfer to Addis Ababa. Ethiopian suspicions over Egyptian links Security officials cited in reports about the incident said Ethiopia suspects that Egypt trained the soldiers and that they were travelling towards areas administered by Jubaland, the federal member state in southern Somalia. These allegations have not been independently verified, and Ethiopian authorities have not publicly presented evidence to substantiate them. The claims are particularly sensitive given the rivalry between Egypt and Ethiopia, which extends beyond their longstanding dispute over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam to competing security interests in the Horn of Africa. Egypt has strengthened its engagement with Somalia, including security cooperation, while Ethiopia has expressed concern about developments that could increase Egyptian military influence near its borders. Against this backdrop, reports that Egyptian-trained Somali troops may have been heading towards Jubaland could intensify Ethiopian suspicions. However, it remains unclear whether the allegations explain the soldiers’ detention. The available information does not establish how they entered Ethiopia, whether their travel was officially authorised or whether Ethiopian authorities believe they violated any laws. Mogadishu’s silence raises concerns The Somali federal government has yet to publicly explain the incident or clarify what steps it is taking to secure the soldiers’ release or return. Its silence leaves unanswered questions about diplomatic contacts with Addis Ababa and the legal status of the detained personnel. The detention of approximately 220 serving soldiers by a neighbouring country is a significant concern for Somalia’s military leadership. Mogadishu faces pressure to establish the facts, confirm the soldiers’ welfare and ensure that their treatment is addressed through appropriate diplomatic and legal channels. It is also unclear whether the soldiers have been formally charged, whether they remain in custody in Addis Ababa or whether the transfer forms part of a broader security investigation. Neither government has publicly clarified these matters in the available reporting. Relations already under strain The incident comes amid deteriorating relations between Mogadishu and Addis Ababa over regional security and competing strategic interests. Ethiopia has reportedly accused President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud of betraying Ethiopia by aligning himself with Egypt and Eritrea, reflecting growing mistrust between the governments. The wider dispute involves sensitive questions of sovereignty, military cooperation and influence across the Horn of Africa. Somalia is seeking to strengthen its security partnerships, while Ethiopia remains concerned about developments in neighbouring territories that it considers relevant to its national security. The soldiers’ detention risks further complicating an already fragile relationship. Without clear explanations and direct diplomatic engagement, the incident could deepen mistrust and undermine cooperation on shared security challenges. The immediate priority is to establish why the soldiers were detained, clarify their legal status and secure a resolution through diplomatic channels . Until Ethiopia and Somalia provide fuller accounts, allegations concerning Egyptian training and the soldiers’ intended destination should remain attributed claims rather than established facts. The episode presents another test for both governments: whether they can contain a sensitive military incident through communication and diplomacy or allow it to become a further source of regional tension. Their detention raises questions about why serving Somali military personnel were in Ethiopian territory, the circumstances of their arrest and the purpose of their transfer to Addis Ababa. Ethiopian suspicions over Egyptian links Security officials cited in reports about the incident said Ethiopia suspects that Egypt trained the soldiers and that they were travelling towards areas administered by Jubaland, the federal member state in southern Somalia. These allegations have not been independently verified, and Ethiopian authorities have not publicly presented evidence to substantiate them. The claims are particularly sensitive given the rivalry between Egypt and Ethiopia, which extends beyond their longstanding dispute over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam to competing security interests in the Horn of Africa. Egypt has strengthened its engagement with Somalia, including security cooperation, while Ethiopia has expressed concern about developments that could increase Egyptian military influence near its borders. Against this backdrop, reports that Egyptian-trained Somali troops may have been heading towards Jubaland could intensify Ethiopian suspicions. However, it remains unclear whether the allegations explain the soldiers’ detention. The available information does not establish how they entered Ethiopia, whether their travel was officially authorised or whether Ethiopian authorities believe they violated any laws. Mogadishu’s silence raises concerns The Somali federal government has yet to publicly explain the incident or clarify what steps it is taking to secure the soldiers’ release or return. Its silence leaves unanswered questions about diplomatic contacts with Addis Ababa and the legal status of the detained personnel. The detention of approximately 220 serving soldiers by a neighbouring country is a significant concern for Somalia’s military leadership. Mogadishu faces pressure to establish the facts, confirm the soldiers’ welfare and ensure that their treatment is addressed through appropriate diplomatic and legal channels. It is also unclear whether the soldiers have been formally charged, whether they remain in custody in Addis Ababa or whether the transfer forms part of a broader security investigation. Neither government has publicly clarified these matters in the available reporting. Relations already under strain The incident comes amid deteriorating relations between Mogadishu and Addis Ababa over regional security and competing strategic interests. Ethiopia has reportedly accused President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud of betraying Ethiopia by aligning himself with Egypt and Eritrea, reflecting growing mistrust between the governments. The wider dispute involves sensitive questions of sovereignty, military cooperation and influence across the Horn of Africa. Somalia is seeking to strengthen its security partnerships, while Ethiopia remains concerned about developments in neighbouring territories that it considers relevant to its national security. The soldiers’ detention risks further complicating an already fragile relationship. Without clear explanations and direct diplomatic engagement, the incident could deepen mistrust and undermine cooperation on shared security challenges. The immediate priority is to establish why the soldiers were detained, clarify their legal status and secure a resolution through diplomatic channels . Until Ethiopia and Somalia provide fuller accounts, allegations concerning Egyptian training and the soldiers’ intended destination should remain attributed claims rather than established facts. The episode presents another test for both governments: whether they can contain a sensitive military incident through communication and diplomacy or allow it to become a further source of regional tension. items.title: Hoggaamiyaha Koonfur Galbeed oo Muqdisho kula kulmay Safiirka Ingiriiska
items.description: Muqdisho, 13 Oktoobar 2026 — Hoggaamiyaha Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed Soomaaliya, Sheekh Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Madoobe), ayaa magaalada Muqdisho kulan kula yeeshay Safiirka Dowladda Ingiriiska u fadhiya Soomaaliya, Charles King, kaas oo looga hadlay xoojinta xiriirka iyo iskaashiga labada dhinac. Kulanka ayaa diiradda lagu saaray iskaashiga dhinacyada nabadda, amniga, dowlad-dhiska iyo horumarinta adeegyada bulshada ee deegaannada Koonfur Galbeed. Sheekh Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Madoobe) ayaa kulanka ku adkeeyey muhiimadda ay leedahay taageerada saaxiibbada caalamiga ah ee ku aaddan dadaallada lagu xaqiijinayo nabadda, xasilloonida iyo horumar waara, isaga oo sidoo kale tilmaamay baahida loo qabo xoojinta hay’adaha dowladda iyo horumarinta adeegyada aasaasiga ah ee bulshada. Kulankan ayaa qayb ka ah dadaallada Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed ay ku xoojinayso xiriirka diblomaasiyadeed iyo iskaashiga ay la leedahay saaxiibbada caalamka, si loo horumariyo nabadda, dib-u-heshiisiinta iyo dowlad-wanaagga deegaannada maamulkaas. Hoggaamiyaha waxaa kulanka ku weheliyey Wasiirka Tamarta, Wasiir Ku-xigeenka Wasaaradda Amniga iyo Agaasimaha Guud ee Madaxtooyada Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed Soomaaliya.

items.title: The Politics of Targeting: Unpacking the Unfounded Obsession with the Somali Diaspora in Western Societies
items.description: By Prof. Askar Abdishakur In contemporary political discourse, the rhetoric of division has found a dangerous new focal point. Across the Atlantic and throughout Europe, populist right-wing factions increasingly isolate specific ethnic and national groups as political scapegoats. Among these, the Somali diaspora has faced a persistent, disproportionate, and unwarranted campaign of stigmatization. Modeled after the polarizing strategies once deployed against high-profile figures like President Barack Obama, this rhetoric seeks to otherize a vibrant, deeply integrated community. To understand this fixation is to confront a glaring paradox: why are a people who exemplify the core tenets of civic integration persistently targeted by political demagogues? A- The Reality of Integration vs. The Myth of the Outsider: For decades, the primary demand placed on migrants by Western societies has been clear: integrate, contribute economically, respect democratic institutions, and become active members of the civic fabric. By every measurable standard, the global Somali diaspora has met and exceeded these expectations. Arriving largely over the past three decades, fleeing a devastating civil conflict, Somalis have woven themselves into the socioeconomic tapestry of Western nations: 1. Civic and Political Leadership: Somali-Americans, Somali-Canadians, and individuals of Somali descent in the United Kingdom, Sweden, Norway, and the Netherlands hold prominent legislative and parliamentary seats, shaping policy from within the halls of power. 2. Public Service and Essential Infrastructure: From physicians, nurses, and support staff within the United Kingdom’s National Health Service (NHS) to professionals running vital public transport networks, Somalis form part of the backbone of essential public services. 3. Economic Enterprise: Across Western metropolitan hubs, thriving Somali-owned businesses, commercial enterprises, and entrepreneurial networks generate jobs, revitalize neighborhoods, and contribute substantially to national tax bases. Given this reality, the political targeting of Somalis defies logical metrics of social cohesion. It begs the question: “What have Somalis done to provoke the ire of these political elements?” The answer lies not in community behavior, but in the tactical utility of xenophobia. Populist playbooks rely on a recognizable “boogeyman” to galvanize base politics, substituting complex socio-economic anxieties with a visible, racialized target. B- Historical Debt and Forgotten Alliances: This modern hostility also reveals a profound historical amnesia. When European democracies faced existential threats during the twentieth century, Somali soldiers did not hesitate to stand alongside them. 1.The First World War: The “Tirailleurs Somalis” (Somali Batallion/ Tirailleurs), recruited from the Horn of Africa, fought valiantly on the Western Front. They were instrumental in harrowing engagements such as the grueling Battle of Verdun and the fierce recapture of Fort Douaumont, one of the most heavily fortified German positions. Their blood was spilled on European soil in defense of liberty. 2. The Second World War: Units like the Somaliland Camel Corps and various regional contingents operated alongside Allied forces in the East African and broader campaigns, enduring severe conditions to break axis blockades and secure strategic territories. To turn around decades later and treat this community, or their descendants, as permanent internal threats is a historical betrayal. It strips away the shared sacrifices that bound Europe and the Horn of Africa during their darkest hours. C- Human Imperfection vs. Manufactured Collective Guilt: To be intellectually honest, no sociologist or community leader denies a fundamental truth of the human condition:  “every single community on Earth possesses its share of fraudsters, slackers, and unsavory characters. Human nature is remarkably consistent across all races, borders, and creeds.” President Donald Trump However, populist rhetoric relies on a dishonest double standard. When an individual from a dominant majority commits a crime, it is treated as an isolated human failure. When an individual from a marginalized group like the Somali community stumbles, it is weaponized as an indictment of an entire ethnicity. Donald Trump’s repeated political attacks, disparaging remarks, and obsessive fixations on prominent Somali-American figures (such as members of the U.S. Congress) are designed to exploit this exact prejudice.  By reducing a rich, resilient culture to crude caricatures, this rhetoric normalizes racism and provides a template that European right-wing extremists eagerly copy to energize their own political fortunes. Conclusion The relentless focus on Somalis by political figures like Donald Trump and their European emulators is not driven by facts, statistics, or genuine civic concerns. It is a calculated distraction, a political tool that feeds on prejudice when rational arguments fail. The Somali diaspora stands as a testament to resilience, successful integration, and historical loyalty. Recognizing this requires looking past the cynical noise of modern demagogues and acknowledging a simple truth: targeting a community that has given so much, integrated so deeply, and achieved so widely exposes the moral bankruptcy of the attackers, not the character of the attacked. Prof. Askar Abdishakur Email: eastafridac@gmail.com The post The Politics of Targeting: Unpacking the Unfounded Obsession with the Somali Diaspora in Western Societies appeared first on WardheerNews .

items.title: DF oo cunaqabatayn kusoo rogtay C/casiis Laftagareen, taliye Shub iyo siyaasiyiin kale
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Federaalka ah ee Soomaaliya ayaa maanta cunaqabatayn maaliyadeed kusoo rogtay madaxweynihii hore ee Koonfur Galbeed, Cabdicasiis Xasan Maxamed (Lafta-gareen) iyo 9 xubnood oo kale oo kamid ah saaxibadiisa ku kala sugan duleedka Baydhaba iyo magaalada Nairobi ee caasimada dalka Kenya. Kooxdan ayaa dowladda Soomaaliya waxa ay ku eedeysay inay ku lug leeyihiin maalgelinta iyo taageeridda Al-Shabaab, kadib weerarradii ay kusoo qaadeenmagaalada Baydhaba, kuwaas oo loo adeegsaday gawaari laga soo buuxiyay walxaha qarxa. Guddiga Qaran ee ka-hortagga lacag-dhaqidda iyo la-dagaallanka maalgelinta Argagixisada oo soo saaray war-saxaafadeed ayaa liiska cunaqabataynta maaliyadeed ee Cayiman ku daray shakhsiyaadkan oo haatan dagaal adag kula jiray maamulka Koonfur Galbeed. Sidoo kale, guddiga ayaa shaaca ka qaaday winay ka go’an xoojinta dadaallada lagu ciribtiraayo maalgelinta argagixisada, laguna adkaynaayo hirgelinta cunaqabataynta maaliyadeed ee cayiman, si loo ilaaliyo amniga iyo xasilloonida dalka. Xubnaha cunaqabateynta la saaray ayaa kala ah;- 1-Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed (Laftagareen) 2- Hassan Abdulkadir Mohamed 3- Mahad Abdirahman Adan (Shub) 4- Ibrahim Adan Ali (Najah) 5- Hassan Abdi Mohamed (Ugaas Hassan) 6-Abdullahi Ali Watiin 7-Abdifatah Mahad Abdirahman 8-Abdimajid Mowlid Hassan 9-Amiin Mad Daruur 10-Abshir Aden Isak. Dhanka kale, Guddiga Qaran ee ka-hortagga lacag-dhaqidda iyo la-dagaallanka maalgelinta Argagixisada ayaa uga digay muwaadiniinta Soomaaliyeed iyo hay’adaha kale inay xiriir la sameeyaan ama la macaamilaan shaqsiyaadkan, waxaana lasoo saaray qodobbada hoose;- 1) Waxaa ka reeban in ay la macaamilaan shaqsiyaadka ku jira liiskan 2) Waxaa waajib ku ah in ay xayiraan hanti kasta ay leeyihiin shaqsiyaadka ku xusan liiskan; 3) Waxaa sidoo kale waajib ku ah in warbixin deg deg ah ee dhaqdhaqaaqyada (transactions) shaqsiyaadkan u diraan Xarunta Warbixinada Maaliyadda, Financial Reporting Center (FRC). “Dhammaan muwaadiniinta Soomaaliyeed waxaa lagu wargelinayaa in ay mamnuuc tahay xiriir kasta oo dhaqaale ama fududayn ah oo loo sameeyo shaqsiyaadka kor ku xusan, iyada oo ciddii jebisa go’aanka Guddiga lala tiigsan doono xeerarka la-dagaallanka argagixisada ee dhaqangalka ah,” ayaa lagu yiri qoraalka kasoo baxay guddiga. The post DF oo cunaqabatayn kusoo rogtay C/casiis Laftagareen, taliye Shub iyo siyaasiyiin kale appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Trump Calls Somalia and Somaliland ‘Totally Different Countries,’ Reviving Debate Over Independence
items.description: The US president’s remarks come as Somaliland intensifies its campaign for international recognition following Israel’s historic decision to recognize the territory in December 2025. U.S. President Donald Trump has described Somalia and Somaliland as “totally different” countries and suggested that Somaliland should immediately change its name, adding a new twist to the politically sensitive question of whether the self-governing territory should become internationally recognized as an independent state. “I call it Somalia land, not Somaliland, because actually it’s a totally different country. Some people like Somaliland. It has nothing to do, you know that, has nothing to do. I said, you got to be kidding. I think they should change the name immediately,” Trump said in remarks referring to the distinction between Somalia and Somaliland. The comments have attracted attention amid a renewed campaign by Somaliland’s leadership to secure U.S. recognition, following Israel’s decision in December 2025 to become the first United Nations member state to formally recognize the territory as independent. However, Trump’s comments should not be interpreted as a formal change in U.S. policy. Washington has continued to support Somalia’s territorial integrity, and the administration has not announced recognition of Somaliland. A separate colonial history Somaliland’s independence claim is rooted in a distinct colonial history. The territory was administered as a British protectorate, while southern Somalia was under Italian administration. British Somaliland became independent on June 26, 1960. Five days later, on July 1, it united with the former Italian-administered territory to establish the Somali Republic. The union was driven partly by pan-Somali nationalism and the desire to unite Somali-speaking populations after colonial rule. However, the political arrangement subsequently became a source of grievance among some northern communities, who argued that they were marginalized within the new state. Following the collapse of President Mohamed Siad Barre’s military government in 1991, Somaliland’s leaders declared the restoration of independence. Since then, the territory has operated with its own government, security forces, currency and institutions, while seeking international recognition. Its supporters argue that the claim is not simply an attempt to create a new state by breaking away from an existing country. Rather, they maintain that Somaliland is seeking recognition of its earlier independence and the failure of the 1960 union to deliver the political settlement they expected. That historical argument is central to Somaliland’s diplomatic campaign, although Somalia rejects separation and maintains that the territory remains part of its sovereign territory. Genocide allegations remain central to the independence argument The legacy of violence under Siad Barre’s government is another major element of Somaliland’s case for independence. During the late 1980s, government forces launched a brutal counterinsurgency campaign against the Somali National Movement, an armed opposition group with a strong base among the Isaaq clan in the north. Human Rights Watch documented widespread killings of civilians, arbitrary detention, torture, the destruction of settlements and livestock, and aerial bombardment of Hargeisa and other northern towns in 1988. The violence drove large numbers of people from their homes, including hundreds of thousands who fled into neighbouring Ethiopia. Somaliland’s advocates describe the campaign as genocide against the Isaaq population and argue that the atrocities destroyed the political foundations of the union. Human Rights Watch’s documentation provides evidence of systematic abuses and mass civilian suffering, although the legal classification of particular crimes must be distinguished from the historical record of those abuses. The events remain deeply significant to Somaliland’s political identity and its argument that renewed integration with Mogadishu cannot simply be assumed. Israel breaks the diplomatic deadlock The international debate changed on December 26, 2025, when Israel formally recognized Somaliland as an independent state. The announcement was welcomed by Somaliland’s President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, widely known as Irro, as a major diplomatic breakthrough. Israel said the relationship would include cooperation in economic development, agriculture and other sectors, while Somaliland expressed interest in joining the Abraham Accords. Israel’s decision, however, prompted strong opposition from Somalia and other regional governments, which argued that recognition undermined Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. The dispute also reached the United Nations Security Council, where officials warned of potential regional consequences. The recognition has not automatically led to broader international acceptance. The United States has not followed Israel, and the African Union’s longstanding emphasis on territorial integrity remains an important obstacle to Somaliland’s campaign. Nevertheless, Israel’s move has demonstrated that recognition is no longer merely a theoretical question. It has become a live diplomatic issue with implications for security, trade and competition around the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. Why Washington and other powers are interested Somaliland’s campaign is increasingly framed around strategic and commercial interests, as well as historical and legal arguments. Its location along the Gulf of Aden, near the Bab el-Mandeb maritime corridor linking the Red Sea with the Indian Ocean, gives it potential importance for shipping security, military logistics and regional trade. Berbera, its principal port, has attracted attention as a possible gateway for investment and as an alternative maritime outlet for parts of the Horn of Africa. Somaliland’s leadership has also promoted access to minerals, infrastructure and other commercial opportunities in its efforts to win international support. In September 2026, Semafor reported that President Irro was offering Washington opportunities involving the port, mineral resources and potentially expanded military access in exchange for recognition. Irro said such arrangements would involve reciprocal benefits, while leaving the possibility of future military access open to negotiation. That offer reflects Somaliland’s effort to make recognition relevant to U.S. strategic priorities. It does not mean Washington has agreed to establish a military base or recognize the territory. The United Arab Emirates has also developed significant commercial interests in Berbera, while Somaliland maintains relations with Taiwan, another relationship that intersects with broader geopolitical competition involving China. Ethiopia, meanwhile, has an important economic interest in gaining reliable access to the sea. Its January 2024 memorandum of understanding with Somaliland, which raised the prospect of maritime access and a possible path toward recognition, triggered a major dispute with Somalia. The two countries subsequently signed the Ankara Declaration in December 2024, committing to pursue arrangements for Ethiopia’s access to the sea under Somalia’s sovereign authority. These interests do not establish that Western governments collectively intend to recognize Somaliland. They do, however, show why the territory’s status has become increasingly connected to the strategic calculations of governments beyond the Horn of Africa. Trump’s position remains uncertain Trump’s latest remarks come amid renewed attention to Somaliland’s recognition campaign. In August 2025, he said his administration was looking into the question, but after Israel’s recognition later that year, he indicated that Washington would not immediately follow suit. On October 12, 2026, Somaliland’s president again appealed directly to Trump, describing him as a leader who could make history by recognizing the territory, according to an interview published by Breitbart News. The combination of Trump’s latest comments and Somaliland’s lobbying illustrates the uncertainty surrounding the U.S. position. His description of the two territories as different countries may be read as an acknowledgment of their distinct political realities, but it does not itself constitute diplomatic recognition. The wider dispute remains a clash between two principles: Somaliland’s argument for self-determination, based on its colonial history, separate institutions and experience of mass violence, and Somalia’s claim to territorial integrity, backed by the prevailing international position. For Somaliland, the immediate challenge is to convert its long-standing de facto autonomy and Israel’s recognition into broader diplomatic acceptance. For Somalia, the priority is to prevent further international recognition from weakening its territorial claims. Trump’s comments have added visibility to that debate, but whether the United States changes its position will depend on a formal policy decision rather than the president’s choice of words.SECO   Etbusinessview.

U.S. President Donald Trump has described Somalia and Somaliland as “totally different” countries and suggested that Somaliland should immediately change its name, adding a new twist to the politically sensitive question of whether the self-governing territory should become internationally recognized as an independent state. “I call it Somalia land, not Somaliland, because actually it’s a totally different country. Some people like Somaliland. It has nothing to do, you know that, has nothing to do. I said, you got to be kidding. I think they should change the name immediately,” Trump said in remarks referring to the distinction between Somalia and Somaliland. The comments have attracted attention amid a renewed campaign by Somaliland’s leadership to secure U.S. recognition, following Israel’s decision in December 2025 to become the first United Nations member state to formally recognize the territory as independent. However, Trump’s comments should not be interpreted as a formal change in U.S. policy. Washington has continued to support Somalia’s territorial integrity, and the administration has not announced recognition of Somaliland. A separate colonial history Somaliland’s independence claim is rooted in a distinct colonial history. The territory was administered as a British protectorate, while southern Somalia was under Italian administration. British Somaliland became independent on June 26, 1960. Five days later, on July 1, it united with the former Italian-administered territory to establish the Somali Republic. The union was driven partly by pan-Somali nationalism and the desire to unite Somali-speaking populations after colonial rule. However, the political arrangement subsequently became a source of grievance among some northern communities, who argued that they were marginalized within the new state. Following the collapse of President Mohamed Siad Barre’s military government in 1991, Somaliland’s leaders declared the restoration of independence. Since then, the territory has operated with its own government, security forces, currency and institutions, while seeking international recognition. Its supporters argue that the claim is not simply an attempt to create a new state by breaking away from an existing country. Rather, they maintain that Somaliland is seeking recognition of its earlier independence and the failure of the 1960 union to deliver the political settlement they expected. That historical argument is central to Somaliland’s diplomatic campaign, although Somalia rejects separation and maintains that the territory remains part of its sovereign territory. Genocide allegations remain central to the independence argument The legacy of violence under Siad Barre’s government is another major element of Somaliland’s case for independence. During the late 1980s, government forces launched a brutal counterinsurgency campaign against the Somali National Movement, an armed opposition group with a strong base among the Isaaq clan in the north. Human Rights Watch documented widespread killings of civilians, arbitrary detention, torture, the destruction of settlements and livestock, and aerial bombardment of Hargeisa and other northern towns in 1988. The violence drove large numbers of people from their homes, including hundreds of thousands who fled into neighbouring Ethiopia. Somaliland’s advocates describe the campaign as genocide against the Isaaq population and argue that the atrocities destroyed the political foundations of the union. Human Rights Watch’s documentation provides evidence of systematic abuses and mass civilian suffering, although the legal classification of particular crimes must be distinguished from the historical record of those abuses. The events remain deeply significant to Somaliland’s political identity and its argument that renewed integration with Mogadishu cannot simply be assumed. Israel breaks the diplomatic deadlock The international debate changed on December 26, 2025, when Israel formally recognized Somaliland as an independent state. The announcement was welcomed by Somaliland’s President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, widely known as Irro, as a major diplomatic breakthrough. Israel said the relationship would include cooperation in economic development, agriculture and other sectors, while Somaliland expressed interest in joining the Abraham Accords. Israel’s decision, however, prompted strong opposition from Somalia and other regional governments, which argued that recognition undermined Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. The dispute also reached the United Nations Security Council, where officials warned of potential regional consequences. The recognition has not automatically led to broader international acceptance. The United States has not followed Israel, and the African Union’s longstanding emphasis on territorial integrity remains an important obstacle to Somaliland’s campaign. Nevertheless, Israel’s move has demonstrated that recognition is no longer merely a theoretical question. It has become a live diplomatic issue with implications for security, trade and competition around the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. Why Washington and other powers are interested Somaliland’s campaign is increasingly framed around strategic and commercial interests, as well as historical and legal arguments. Its location along the Gulf of Aden, near the Bab el-Mandeb maritime corridor linking the Red Sea with the Indian Ocean, gives it potential importance for shipping security, military logistics and regional trade. Berbera, its principal port, has attracted attention as a possible gateway for investment and as an alternative maritime outlet for parts of the Horn of Africa. Somaliland’s leadership has also promoted access to minerals, infrastructure and other commercial opportunities in its efforts to win international support. In September 2026, Semafor reported that President Irro was offering Washington opportunities involving the port, mineral resources and potentially expanded military access in exchange for recognition. Irro said such arrangements would involve reciprocal benefits, while leaving the possibility of future military access open to negotiation. That offer reflects Somaliland’s effort to make recognition relevant to U.S. strategic priorities. It does not mean Washington has agreed to establish a military base or recognize the territory. The United Arab Emirates has also developed significant commercial interests in Berbera, while Somaliland maintains relations with Taiwan, another relationship that intersects with broader geopolitical competition involving China. Ethiopia, meanwhile, has an important economic interest in gaining reliable access to the sea. Its January 2024 memorandum of understanding with Somaliland, which raised the prospect of maritime access and a possible path toward recognition, triggered a major dispute with Somalia. The two countries subsequently signed the Ankara Declaration in December 2024, committing to pursue arrangements for Ethiopia’s access to the sea under Somalia’s sovereign authority. These interests do not establish that Western governments collectively intend to recognize Somaliland. They do, however, show why the territory’s status has become increasingly connected to the strategic calculations of governments beyond the Horn of Africa. Trump’s position remains uncertain Trump’s latest remarks come amid renewed attention to Somaliland’s recognition campaign. In August 2025, he said his administration was looking into the question, but after Israel’s recognition later that year, he indicated that Washington would not immediately follow suit. On October 12, 2026, Somaliland’s president again appealed directly to Trump, describing him as a leader who could make history by recognizing the territory, according to an interview published by Breitbart News. The combination of Trump’s latest comments and Somaliland’s lobbying illustrates the uncertainty surrounding the U.S. position. His description of the two territories as different countries may be read as an acknowledgment of their distinct political realities, but it does not itself constitute diplomatic recognition. The wider dispute remains a clash between two principles: Somaliland’s argument for self-determination, based on its colonial history, separate institutions and experience of mass violence, and Somalia’s claim to territorial integrity, backed by the prevailing international position. For Somaliland, the immediate challenge is to convert its long-standing de facto autonomy and Israel’s recognition into broader diplomatic acceptance. For Somalia, the priority is to prevent further international recognition from weakening its territorial claims. Trump’s comments have added visibility to that debate, but whether the United States changes its position will depend on a formal policy decision rather than the president’s choice of words.SECO   Etbusinessview.

items.title: Trump Says Somaliland and Somalia Are Two Completely Different Countries
items.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. (Somali Report) – US President Donald Trump has said Somaliland and Somalia are two completely different countries, clarifying that his comments about Somalis and problems he says they have caused in the United States were not directed at Somaliland. Trump referred to “Somalia-land,” saying he did not mean Somaliland because he considers it a completely different country from Somalia. He added that some people might misunderstand his use of the term as referring to Somaliland. “I call it Somalia-land, not Somaliland, because Somaliland is a completely different country. Some people like Somaliland, so I don’t mean that. Somaliland and Somalia have nothing to do with each other. I think it would be good if Somaliland changed its name quickly,” Trump said. Somaliland’s presidency welcomed Trump’s remarks, saying they reinforced the territory’s distinct identity and its political differences from Somalia. “The Republic of Somaliland remains committed to pursuing international recognition through principled diplomacy and constructive engagement with the international community,” the presidency said in a statement. The remarks come amid Somaliland’s continued efforts to secure international recognition for its independence. Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, also known as Irro, recently travelled to the United States as part of a diplomatic campaign to strengthen relations with Washington and seek support for recognition. During his visit to Washington, D.C., and other locations, Irro held meetings with American officials and politicians to discuss relations between Somaliland and the United States. Irro has also urged Trump to recognize Somaliland, saying such a decision could open a new chapter in history for the American president. He made the appeal in an interview with Breitbart News published on Monday.

items.title: Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh oo qaabilay safiirrada dalalka Carabta ee Soomaaliya
items.description: Muqdisho — Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, ayaa qaabilay safiirrada dalalka Carabta ee deggan Soomaaliya, kuwaas oo uu kala hadlay xoojinta xiriirka diblomaasiyadeed, iskaashiga labada dhinac iyo horumarinta xiriirka Soomaaliya iyo dalalka Carabta. Kulanka oo ka dhacay Muqdisho ayaa diiradda lagu saaray xaaladihii ugu dambeeyay ee Soomaaliya, sidii loo sii xoojin lahaa xiriirka walaaltinimo ee ka dhexeeya Soomaaliya iyo dalalka Carabta, iyo sidii loo ballaarin lahaa iskaashiga dhinacyada kala duwan ee danaha wadajirka ah. Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ayaa kulanka ku adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay xoojinta xiriirka diblomaasiyadeed iyo ballaarinta fursadaha iskaashi ee Soomaaliya iyo dalalka Carabta, gaar ahaan dhinacyada ay labada dhinac ka leeyihiin danaha wadajirka ah. Sidoo kale, waxaa kulanka lagu muujiyay muhiimadda ay leedahay ilaalinta nabadda iyo xasilloonida gobolka, iyadoo la adkeeyay sida ay lagama maarmaanka u tahay iskaashi wadajir ah oo lagu taageerayo nabadda iyo xasilloonida gobolka. Kulankan ayaa qayb ka ah dadaallada Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ay ku xoojinayso xiriirka ay la leedahay dalalka Carabta iyo horumarinta iskaashiga diblomaasiyadeed ee heer gobol iyo heer caalami.

items.title: Soomaaliya U-17 oo Barbar-Dhac La Gashay Tanzania, Kenya-na Isu Diyaarinaysa
items.description: MUQDISHO (Goobjoog News) — Xulka kubadda cagta Soomaaliya ee da’doodu ka hooseyso 17 sano ayaa barbarro 1–1 ah la galay dhiggiisa Tanzania, kulan ka tirsan tartanka CECAFA ee loogu soo baxayo Koobka Qaramada Afrika ee U-17 sannadka 2027. Soomaaliya ayaa hoggaanka ciyaarta qabatay daqiiqaddii koowaad, kaddib markii Abdikarin Abdulkadir uu dhaliyey goolka furitaanka. Bilowga degdegga ah wuxuu xulka Soomaaliyeed siiyey fursad uu cadaadis ku saaro Tanzania qaybtii hore ee kulanka. Tanzania ayaa ciyaarta barbarreysay daqiiqaddii 24-aad, markii Elick Yusuph uu dhaliyey rigoore. Labada xul ayaa intii ka dambeysay sameeyey isku-dayo kale, balse kulanku wuxuu ku soo dhammaaday min hal gool. Soomaaliya ayaa kulankeeda xiga la ciyaari doonta Kenya 14-ka Oktoobar. Ciyaartaas ayaa muhiim u noqon karta rajada xulka Soomaaliyeed ee u soo bixitaanka wareegga xiga iyo xaqiijinta booska looga qeybgalayo AFCON U-17. Saddexda kooxood ee ugu sarreeya tartanka CECAFA ayaa u gudbaya Koobka Qaramada Afrika ee da’yarta sannadka 2027. Natiijada kulanka Kenya ayaa sidaas darteed noqon karta mid go’aamisa halka Soomaaliya kaga dhammaan doonto tartanka.

items.title: Kenya oo Hawlgallo Ka Dhan Ah Al-Shabaab Ka Billowday Mandheera Iyo Gaarisa
items.description: NAIROBI (Goobjoog News) — Ciidamada ammaanka Kenya ayaa hawlgallo ballaaran ka bilaabay gobollada Mandheera iyo Gaarisa, kaddib markii deegaannadaas ay ku soo bateen qaraxyada iyo weerarrada lala xiriirinayo Al-Shabaab. Booliska, cutubyada la-dagaallanka argagixisada iyo ciidamada kale ee ammaanka ayaa la geeyey goobaha loo arko inay halistu ku badan tahay. Hawlgallada waxaa lagu baarayaa waddooyinka, deegaannada xuduudaha iyo goobaha laga shakisan yahay inay ku dhuumaaleysanayaan xubnaha kooxaha hubeysan. Mustaqbal Media ayaa sheegtay in dhowr qof lagu qabtay hawlgallada, hase yeeshee tirada saxda ah, magacyadooda iyo caddeymaha xiriirinaya Al-Shabaab weli lama shaacin. Hay’adaha ammaanka Kenya ayaa laga sugayaa faahfaahin rasmi ah oo ku saabsan dadka la xiray iyo eedeymaha loo haysto. Hawlgalladan ayaa daba socda qarax 9-kii Oktoobar ka dhacay Gaarisa, kaas oo ay ku dhinteen sarkaalka booliska Stephen Ekirapa iyo darawalkiisa David Rotich. Dhacdadaas ayaa sare u qaadday walaaca laga qabo weerarrada lala beegsado ciidamada iyo gaadiidka isticmaala waddooyinka waqooyi-bari Kenya. Mandheera iyo Gaarisa waxay xuduud dheer la wadaagaan Soomaaliya, waxaana muddo dheer ka jiray dhaqdhaqaaqyo hubeysan iyo weerarro ka gudba xadka. Adkeynta ammaanka waxay saameyn kartaa isu-socodka dadka iyo badeecadaha, sidaas darteedna waxaa muhiim ah in hawlgallada lagu ilaaliyo xuquuqda dadka rayidka ah.

items.title: Soomaaliya Ooo Karantiishay 10 Qof o Ka Soo Laabtay DR Congo
items.description: MUQDISHO (Goobjoog News) — Wasaaradda Caafimaadka Soomaaliya ayaa xarunta daaweynta iyo karantiilka Ebola ee Muqdisho geysay 10 muwaadin Soomaaliyeed oo ka soo laabtay Jamhuuriyadda Dimuqraadiga Congo, kuwaas oo safarkooda soo maray Uganda. Sida lagu sheegay bayaanka Wasaaradda Caafimaadka ee 12-kii Oktoobar, dadka la karantiilay waxaa lagu sameynayaa baaritaanno shaybaar iyo dabagal caafimaad. Waxaa sidoo kale socda raadraaca dadka ay la kulmeen intii ay safarka ku jireen iyo markii ay dalka soo gaareen. Tallaabadan ayaa ka dambeysay walaaca laga qabo faafitaanka Ebola iyo xogtii hore ee ku saabsanayd qof keliya oo looga shakiyey inuu xiriir la yeeshay bukaan qaba cudurka. Karantiilka 10-ka qof wuxuu muujinayaa in dowladda ay ballaarisay tallaabooyinka taxaddarka iyo dabagalka caafimaadka. Ilaa hadda, Wasaaradda Caafimaadku ma xaqiijin in qof ka mid ah dadka la karantiilay laga helay fayraska Ebola. Sidaas darteed, karantiilka iyo baaritaannadu waa tallaabooyin ka-hortag ah, mana aha xaqiijin muujinaysa inuu cudurku Soomaaliya soo gaaray. Natiijooyinka baaritaannada ayaa muhiim u noqon doona go’aaminta tallaabada xigta. Dowladda waxaa sidoo kale laga sugayaa inay bulshada si joogto ah ula wadaagto xogta caafimaadka, si looga hortago warar aan sal lahayn iyo cabsi aan loo baahnayn.

items.title: Boqolaal askari oo ka tirsan milatariga Soomaaliya oo loo qaaday Addis Ababa kadib…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Itoobiya ayaa magaalada Addis Ababa u wareejisay 220 askari oo ka tirsan milatariga Soomaaliya, kuwaas oo ay dhawaan ku qabatay gudaha Dowlad Deegaanka Soomaalida, xilli ay fasax ku joogeen halkaas. Askartan oo muddo lagu hayay xerada Garab Case ee magaalada Jigjiga ayaa la sheegay in shalay lagu qaaday basas ay leeyihiin ciidamada Itoobiya, kuwaas oo u gudbiyay caasimadda dalkaas ee Addis Ababa. Ciidamadan ayaa ka mid ahaa askartii uu Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud bishii August tababarka ugu soo xiray deegaanka Xananbuure ee gobolka Galgaduud oo hoos taga maamulka Galmudug. Ilaa hadda, Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya kama aysan soo saarin war rasmi ah oo ku saabsan qabashada askartan iyo tallaabada Itoobiya ay ugu wareejisay Addis Ababa, iyadoo arrintani ay dhalisay su’aalo ku saabsan xaaladdooda iyo sababta halkaas loogu qaaday. Dhanka kale, saraakiil amni oo ka tirsan dowladda Itoobiya ayaa lagu soo warramayaa inay aaminsan yihiin in ciidamadaas ay tababartay dowladda Masar, isla markaana ay ku sii jeedeen deegaannada maamulka Jubaland. Arrintan ayaa kusoo aadeysa xilli uu xiriirka diblomaasiyadeed ee Soomaaliya iyo Itoobiya wajahayo xiisado, kaddib markii ay labada dowladood isku khilaafeen arrimo la xiriira gobolka iyo isbahaysiyada siyaasadeed ee Geeska Afrika. Xukuumadda Ra’iisul Wasaare Abiy Axmed ayaa dhawaan muujisay caro la xiriirta mowqifka Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ee xiriirka uu la leeyahay Masar iyo Ereteriya. Wararka laga helayo dhinaca Itoobiya ayaa sheegaya in Addis Ababa ay tallaabooyinkaas u aragto kuwo khatar ah oo ka hor imaanaya danaha ay gobolka ka leedahay. Wareejinta askartan ayaa kusoo beegmaysa xilli ay sii xoogeysanayaan loollanka siyaasadeed iyo kan amni ee gobolka. Si kastaba, waxaa weli la sugayaa faahfaahin rasmi ah oo ku saabsan sababta loo qabtay ciidamada, xaaladdooda hadda iyo wada-hadallada labada dowladood ee arrintan la xiriira.
