items.title: Israel’s Somaliland Recognition Opens a New Front in the Horn
items.description: Saudi Arabia Backs Somalia as Rival Gulf Powers Face Off Across the Red Sea Riyadh / Mogadishu (WDN) — Israel’s decision to recognize Somaliland has done more than alter a diplomatic equation in the Horn of Africa. It has opened another front in a widening geopolitical contest stretching from the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden to the wider Horn — where Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are pursuing increasingly different strategic interests. Saudi Arabia has responded by reaffirming its support for Somalia’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, rejecting Israel’s recognition of Somaliland and warning against moves that could undermine Somalia’s territorial integrity. The dispute is no longer simply about Somaliland. It is increasingly about ports, maritime routes, security partnerships and influence along one of the world’s most strategically important waterways. A Recognition That Changed the Equation Israel became the first United Nations member state to formally recognize Somaliland in December 2025, giving the territory a diplomatic breakthrough after decades of seeking international recognition. Somaliland’s location helps explain why the move has attracted such intense attention. The territory lies along the Gulf of Aden, opposite Yemen, while the port of Berbera sits near a major maritime corridor linking the Indian Ocean with the Red Sea. That geography gives the recognition significance far beyond the question of diplomatic status. It immediately raised questions about whether Israel’s move could lead to deeper security cooperation, encourage other countries to follow and increase Somaliland’s importance in the competition over the Red Sea. For Somalia, however, the issue is fundamentally one of sovereignty. Mogadishu maintains that Somaliland remains part of Somalia and that any external recognition of its independence violates Somalia’s territorial integrity. Riyadh Draws the Line Saudi Arabia has aligned itself firmly with Mogadishu on the central issue.Riyadh has reaffirmed Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and joined wider Arab and Islamic diplomatic opposition to Israel’s recognition of Somaliland. The African Union and Organization of Islamic Cooperation have likewise rejected the recognition and reaffirmed Somalia’s territorial integrity. The message is clear: Israel’s decision has changed the diplomatic landscape, but it has not produced broad international acceptance of Somaliland’s independence. For Saudi Arabia, the issue also carries a wider strategic dimension. The Red Sea and Gulf of Aden are vital to international trade and regional security. Any major shift in political or military alignments along those waterways has consequences well beyond Somalia. The UAE Factor The most complicated element is the role of the United Arab Emirates. Abu Dhabi has developed extensive economic and security ties across the Horn of Africa, including a major commercial presence in Somaliland through DP World’s involvement in Berbera. That relationship does not, by itself, establish that the UAE orchestrated Israel’s recognition of Somaliland. But it places the development within a broader Saudi-Emirati competition for influence in the Horn. The two Gulf powers have increasingly pursued different partnerships and strategic interests across Somalia, Sudan and the wider region. Their rivalry has become particularly visible as the Red Sea and Horn of Africa have assumed greater importance in regional security calculations. The result is a complicated equation in which commercial ports, military partnerships and diplomatic alliances increasingly overlap. Mogadishu Strikes Back Somalia responded forcefully, accusing the UAE of undermining its sovereignty and moving against existing arrangements with Abu Dhabi. But the reaction also exposed Somalia’s internal political divisions. Puntland and Jubaland have maintained their own economic and security relationships with the UAE, illustrating the difficulty Mogadishu faces in establishing a single national foreign-policy position across the federal system. That makes the Somaliland issue even more complicated. The dispute is no longer simply about recognition. It is exposing competing foreign-policy interests within Somalia itself. A New Contest Around the Red Sea The strategic calculations of the major players are different. For Saudi Arabia, the stability and security of the Red Sea are vital national and economic interests. For the UAE, longstanding commercial and security relationships give it significant stakes in the Horn. For Israel, Somaliland’s position on the Gulf of Aden offers potential strategic value near one of the world’s most important maritime corridors. For Somalia, the recognition represents a direct challenge to its claim of territorial unity. And for the wider international community, it adds another geopolitical layer to a region already destabilized by conflicts and rivalries involving Somalia, Sudan, Ethiopia and Yemen. The danger is that local disputes become increasingly entangled with the ambitions of outside powers. Ports become strategic assets. Security partnerships acquire political meaning. Commercial investments become instruments of geopolitical influence. And a dispute that began as a Somali territorial question becomes part of a much larger struggle over the future of the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa. What Comes Next? Israel’s recognition has already changed the diplomatic conversation. Saudi Arabia has rejected it. The African Union and OIC have opposed it. Somalia has taken action against the UAE. Meanwhile, the broader Gulf rivalry is becoming increasingly visible across the Horn. The critical question now is whether the recognition remains an isolated diplomatic decision or becomes the beginning of a wider realignment. For Somaliland, the recognition represents a major diplomatic breakthrough. For Somalia, it is a challenge to a core principle of national sovereignty. For Saudi Arabia and the UAE, it is another point of competition in a strategically important region. And for Israel, it may represent the opening of a new strategic relationship on the shores of the Gulf of Aden. The ports are strategic. The sea lanes are vital. The alliances are shifting. And Somaliland has suddenly found itself at the centre of all three. WardheerNews The post Israel’s Somaliland Recognition Opens a New Front in the Horn appeared first on WardheerNews .

items.title: Cornered in the Horn: Ethiopia’s New War Tests Abiy Ahmed’s Grip on Power
items.description: Former Enemies Unite as Tigray Fighting Shatters the Post-Pretoria Order and Opens a New Front Across Ethiopia ADDIS ABABA (WDN) — Eight years after Abiy Ahmed came to power promising political reform, reconciliation and a break with Ethiopia’s old order, his government is confronting an extraordinary reversal: former enemies who once fought one another are now joining forces against the federal government. The formation of the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival has transformed Ethiopia’s security crisis from a collection of separate insurgencies into a potentially coordinated national challenge. The alliance, announced on September 20, brings together seven armed and political movements, including the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), the Amhara Fano National Movement and the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), alongside movements from Afar, Benishangul-Gumuz and the Somali region. Their declared objective is to remove Abiy’s government and establish an inclusive transitional administration. Only a few years ago, such an alliance would have appeared almost unthinkable. During the 2020–2022 Tigray war, Amhara Fano forces fought alongside federal troops against the TPLF. The OLA, meanwhile, has been engaged in its own armed conflict with the federal government. Now, those former adversaries have identified a common opponent in Addis Ababa. And as fighting has erupted again in Tigray, the political alliance is being tested on the battlefield. The Alliance That Changed the Equation The significance of the new coalition lies less in the number of groups involved than in the political geography it represents. The TPLF is rooted in Tigray. Fano is a major armed force in Amhara. The OLA operates primarily in Oromia. Other members have grievances tied to Afar, Benishangul-Gumuz and the Somali regions. Together, they give the alliance a presence across several of Ethiopia’s most politically sensitive areas. The groups remain deeply divided over territory, ethnicity and Ethiopia’s constitutional future. Their competing interests are particularly evident in the dispute over Western Tigray, claimed by both Tigrayan and Amhara actors. But for the moment, they have found common ground in opposition to Abiy’s government. The coalition says it wants to remove the current government, establish an inclusive transitional government, resolve outstanding disputes peacefully and eventually move toward a new political settlement. That creates an unusual political equation: Groups that once fought each other have concluded that their immediate interests are better served by confronting the federal government together. Tigray: The Peace Deal Unravels The immediate battlefield is once again Tigray. The region descended into a devastating war in November 2020 after relations between the TPLF and Abiy’s government collapsed. The conflict ended with the November 2022 Pretoria Agreement, but many of the issues that produced the war were left unresolved. Those unresolved disputes have now returned to the centre of Ethiopian politics. Fighting intensified sharply in September, with federal and Tigrayan forces accusing each other of triggering the renewed conflict. Tigrayan forces moved against federal positions and seized several airports, while Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to Tigray. Fighting also spread toward neighbouring Afar and Amhara. The renewed violence has effectively shattered the fragile political calm created by Pretoria. The question is no longer whether the agreement is under pressure. The question is whether the political order created by the agreement can survive at all. From Former Allies to New Enemies Perhaps the most damaging development for Abiy is what has happened in Amhara. During the Tigray war, Fano forces were among the federal government’s important allies. Their relationship with Addis Ababa later deteriorated dramatically, particularly after the federal government moved to dismantle or integrate regional armed forces. That dispute developed into a major armed conflict in Amhara from 2023 onward. The transformation is striking.The forces that helped Abiy fight the TPLF have now joined the TPLF in opposing Abiy. This does not erase the profound differences between Fano and Tigrayan forces. Nor does it mean that their alliance will necessarily survive once their common confrontation with Addis Ababa is over. But strategically, it creates a new problem for the federal government. A regional force that once helped contain the TPLF is now part of an alliance that seeks to challenge the federal government itself. A War on Multiple Fronts Ethiopia’s security challenge is no longer concentrated in one region. The renewed fighting in Tigray has coincided with continuing instability in Amhara and the long-running insurgency involving the OLA in Oromia. That creates the possibility of simultaneous pressure across several major regions. The federal government therefore faces a difficult military calculation: maintaining sufficient forces in one theatre while preventing deterioration in another. The seizure of airports in Tigray has already demonstrated how quickly the conflict can affect infrastructure and mobility. Communications disruptions have also accompanied the fighting, complicating the flow of information from the region. Federal forces retain substantial military capabilities, including air power and drones. But expanding the conflict across several regions would place additional demands on Ethiopia’s military and security institutions. The result could be a prolonged contest rather than a single decisive confrontation. The Political Cost of a Return to War For Abiy, the challenge is not only military. His rise to power in 2018 was initially associated with political opening, reconciliation and reform. His peace initiative with Eritrea contributed to his receiving the 2019 Nobel Peace Prize. But the Tigray war fundamentally altered that image. The return of large-scale fighting now threatens to reinforce the perception that Ethiopia’s underlying political conflicts were never fully resolved. The government’s national dialogue process was intended to provide a political mechanism for addressing some of those disputes. Yet major armed movements have remained outside or opposed to the process. The new alliance is therefore presenting a competing political proposition: remove the current government, establish a transitional arrangement and reopen the country’s constitutional and political settlement. Whether the alliance can deliver such an outcome is far from established. Its members have competing territorial claims, different political objectives and very different histories. That is its greatest potential weakness. But its existence is already a major political fact. Eritrea and the Regional Dimension Ethiopia’s internal conflict is also becoming increasingly difficult to separate from the wider politics of the Horn of Africa. Relations between Addis Ababa and Eritrea have deteriorated sharply since the Pretoria Agreement. The two governments have exchanged accusations, particularly over the future of Tigray and Ethiopia’s ambitions for access to the Red Sea. The Ethiopian government has also accused Eritrea of supporting armed opposition groups. Eritrea has denied the allegations. The new alliance adds another layer to those regional tensions. The possibility of outside involvement is one reason the conflict is attracting attention well beyond Ethiopia’s borders. Ethiopia’s relations with Sudan have also become increasingly complicated, while its disputes with Somalia and Egypt have added further strategic pressure around the Horn and the Red Sea. A domestic Ethiopian conflict could therefore acquire regional dimensions very quickly. The Alliance’s Greatest Test For all its political drama, the Alliance for Survival faces a fundamental test. Can groups with profoundly different interests maintain cooperation once the immediate objective of confronting Abiy’s government comes under pressure? The alliance itself acknowledges that its members have differences. Tigrayan and Amhara forces, in particular, remain divided over territory and political authority. The coalition says those disputes can be resolved through dialogue. That proposition will be tested if the alliance gains greater military influence. The groups must demonstrate that they can move from shared opposition to shared governance. That is considerably harder. Removing a government is one political objective. Agreeing on what comes afterward is another. Abiy’s Most Difficult Political Moment? Abiy Ahmed remains in control of Addis Ababa and the principal institutions of the federal state. His government retains significant military capabilities and considerable political resources.It would therefore be premature to assume that the new alliance can overthrow the government. But the political landscape has undeniably changed. The most consequential development is not simply that fighting has returned to Tigray. It is that the old alliances have been rearranged. The TPLF is no longer isolated in the way it was at the beginning of the 2020 war. Fano is no longer uniformly aligned with Addis Ababa. The OLA and other regional movements have joined the same political project. That does not guarantee their success. But it creates a challenge that cannot easily be managed through the regional alliances and military interventions that shaped the earlier phase of Abiy’s rule. The Horn of Africa is now watching a potentially dangerous new chapter unfold. A peace agreement that ended one Ethiopian war is coming apart. Former enemies have found a common cause. Fighting has returned to Tigray. And a government once celebrated for reconciliation is confronting an opposition coalition whose reach extends far beyond one region. The central question for Ethiopia is no longer simply whether another war has begun. It is whether the country can find a political settlement before its newest alliance turns a collection of regional conflicts into a single national war. items.title: Nearly 20 Somali Pirates Escape Puntland Custody in Major Security Failure
items.description: Prisoners Captured in SIBU 1 Operation Escape During Transfer to Garowe, Raising Serious Questions Over Security and Custodial Procedures Garowe (WDN) — Nearly 20 suspected Somali pirates reportedly escaped Puntland custody on Thursday night while being transported from Garacad to Garowe, exposing what appears to be a serious breakdown in the security arrangements responsible for guarding high-value maritime prisoners. The prisoners had been captured following the operation to retake the MT SIBU 1, the oil tanker seized by suspected Somali pirates in the Gulf of Aden. According to the report, the convoy was moving inland from Garacad when the prisoners escaped in an area known as Shakaal, in Jariiban district, near the boundary between Nugaal and Mudug regions. One of the prisoners reportedly died and another was wounded during the escape. The incident raises an immediate and troubling question: How were so many heavily guarded piracy suspects allowed to escape while being transported between two major Puntland locations? A Custody Operation That Went Wrong The prisoners were reportedly being transferred from Garacad to Garowe after being taken into custody following the SIBU 1 operation. Among those who escaped were reportedly two suspects recently captured at Garacad, who had allegedly been part of the group that boarded the Turkish vessel Lutuf. The reported escape of such a large number of prisoners during a land transfer points to potentially serious weaknesses in planning, escort arrangements, prisoner restraints, intelligence and command coordination. These are not ordinary detainees. Suspected pirates captured during a major maritime-security operation represent sensitive prisoners whose custody requires disciplined security procedures, particularly during long-distance transportation through remote areas. Yet nearly 20 reportedly escaped from a convoy travelling through Puntland territory. Confusion Over the Number of Prisoners The incident has also exposed conflicting figures surrounding the number of piracy suspects captured in the SIBU 1 operation. Puntland authorities had previously stated that 46 pirates were detained. However, independent reports indicated that only 21 prisoners were brought to Garacad when the detainees were transferred there. The discrepancy raises another question that authorities will need to answer: What happened to the difference between the numbers announced and those actually brought into custody? Without a clear official account, uncertainty over the prisoner count risks creating further confusion surrounding an operation that was initially presented as a significant maritime-security success. Puntland Yet to Explain the Escape Puntland authorities had not, at the time of the report, issued a detailed public explanation of the escape. Conflicting accounts were circulating about what caused the prisoners to break free. That silence is particularly significant because the detainees were reportedly under the responsibility of security forces while being transferred. A serious custodial incident involving this number of prisoners requires more than a confirmation that an escape occurred. The public needs to know how it happened, who was responsible for the prisoners, what security measures were in place, whether weapons were used, and what action has been taken against those responsible for the security breach. From Maritime Victory to Custody Crisis The SIBU 1 operation was initially portrayed as a major success in the fight against piracy. The tanker and its crew were freed after an operation involving the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF) and Iraqi personnel linked to the vessel’s ownership. But the reported prisoner escape has introduced an unexpected second chapter. A successful maritime interception is only part of a counter-piracy operation. Capturing suspects is one task. Keeping them securely in custody is another. If prisoners captured during a high-profile maritime operation can escape in large numbers while being transported under government protection, it raises questions about the professionalism, preparedness and coordination of the forces responsible for their custody. It also risks undermining the credibility of future anti-piracy operations. The Questions Puntland Must Answer The reported escape now places the focus firmly on Puntland’s security authorities. Were the prisoners properly restrained? How many security personnel accompanied the convoy? Were the vehicles appropriate for transporting high-risk prisoners? Was the route assessed for security risks? Did the escort have adequate communications and backup? Were the prisoners being transported according to established custodial procedures? And most importantly: How did a convoy carrying nearly two dozen high-value detainees lose control of almost all of them? These questions cannot be dismissed as a routine security incident.The prisoners had been captured in an operation involving an internationally significant maritime-security case. Their escape could have consequences not only for Puntland but also for Somalia’s wider efforts to demonstrate that piracy suspects can be captured, detained and brought through a credible judicial process. The immediate priority is to recapture those who escaped, establish the exact circumstances surrounding the incident and provide a transparent account of what went wrong. The SIBU 1 operation may have freed the ship — but the escape of its alleged captors has turned a maritime-security success into a serious test of Puntland’s ability to secure the prisoners it captures. items.title: Should Africa Get a United Nations Security Council (UNSC) Seat? Why This Is Not a Good Idea
items.description: By Ahmed Hujale The push to reform the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has reached a fever pitch, with UN Secretary-General António Guterres and global leaders loudly advocating for permanent African representation in the UNSC. Proponents argue that an institution established in 1945 cannot effectively police a 21 st century world while completely omitting a continent of 1.5 billion people from its permanent chambers. A Moral Argument with a Geopolitical Problem While the moral argument for correcting this historical injustice is undeniably strong, the practical execution presents a profound geopolitical paradox. Africa is not a monolith. Unlike current veto-wielding permanent members, which operate under single national governments, Africa is a sprawling tapestry of 54 distinct sovereign nations. Granting a permanent seat to “Africa” assumes a level of political and strategic cohesion that simply does not exist—and forcing it could inadvertently trigger severe diplomatic friction, domestic disputes, and even armed conflict across the continent. Africa Is Not a Single Political Entity To understand the core flaw of an African UNSC seat, one must examine the fundamental nature of the continent’s geopolitics. Unlike existing permanent members (the P5) such as the United States, Russia, or China, which execute unified foreign and internal policies, Africa will never possess a single, Pan-African foreign policy. The African Union (AU) attempts to foster continental unity, but its member states are driven by vastly divergent national interests, economic realities, Colonial legacies, and ideological alliances. A vote cast by an African representative on a crisis in the Middle East, a global trade dispute, or a climate mandate cannot realistically represent the wills of both democratic and autocratic regimes simultaneously. The Problem of Representing 54 Sovereign States When a single seat is expected to speak for 54 disparate voices, the representative must either dilute their stance into meaningless neutrality or choose a side, instantly alienating dozens of African states. If a seat must be given, then it should be given to all 54 African nations otherwise it should not be given to only one nation because that one nation would not be able to fairly and without external influence or interference to represent the interests of all other nations. Governance and Political Stability This issue of representation is further exacerbated by the fragile state of governance across much of the continent. Democracy and the rule of law remain frustratingly lax or volatile in many African countries. Military coups, corruption, unconstitutional extensions of presidential terms, and weak institutional checks and balances mean that a country holding the UNSC seat today could experience a sudden, violent shift in leadership tomorrow. If a military junta takes power in the nation designated to represent Africa on the world’s most powerful security body, the continent’s global representation shrinks to the whims of an illegitimate regime. Also, the lack of standardized, continent-wide adherence to democratic norms makes it impossible to establish a stable, accountable mechanism for managing a permanent UN vote. The Unresolved Legacy of Colonial Borders Beyond internal governance, the continent is still actively haunted by the structural legacy of European imperialism. The artificial borders drawn during the 1884 Berlin Conference ignored ethnic, linguistic, and geographic realities, leaving behind a permanent landscape of border and territorial disputes. From the Horn of Africa to the Great Lakes region, neighboring African countries frequently find themselves in bitter diplomatic or military standoffs over land and resources. Furthermore, the presence of entrenched armed opposition groups, transnational militias, and terrorist factions actively destabilizes multiple governments. Who Would Get the African Seat? If a permanent UNSC seat is introduced into this volatile mix, the selection process itself threatens to become a catalyst for conflict. Which country gets the seat? If economic giants like Nigeria or South Africa are chosen, regional rivals like Egypt, Ethiopia, or Kenya will rightfully argue that their specific sub-regional security threats and interests are being ignored. The scramble for the seat risks reopening historical wounds and worsening existing territorial friction. Another important consideration should be the security environment in which African states operate. Africa currently faces several serious interstate and regional tensions that could complicate the work of any country representing the continent in a major international body. For example, Egypt and Ethiopia remain at odds over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam and the use of Nile waters, with Egypt continuing to demand a binding agreement on the dam’s operation.  Ethiopia and Eritrea have also experienced a sharp deterioration in relations, with Ethiopia accusing Eritrea of military aggression and support for armed groups, while tensions along their border have raised concerns about renewed war.  Ethiopia and Sudan likewise have unresolved tensions, including disputes over their border and allegations connected to Sudan’s ongoing civil war. There are also significant tensions elsewhere on the continent. Morocco and Algeria remain divided over Western Sahara, with diplomatic relations severely strained and their common border closed.  In West Africa, Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger have withdrawn from ECOWAS and established the Alliance of Sahel States (AES. In Central Africa, the conflict involving Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the M23 movement remains a major regional security concern despite ongoing peace efforts. Also, relations between South Africa and Ghana have also experienced diplomatic strain following anti-foreigner violence in South Africa and Ghana’s evacuation of nationals. These circumstances do not mean that countries involved in regional disputes should automatically be excluded from consideration. Rather, they raise an important question about whether a country seeking to represent Africa can act impartially, build consensus among competing states, and avoid allowing bilateral or regional rivalries to influence its responsibilities. So I don’t think there is single African country that has the capacity to impartially and constructively engage with all states on opposing sides of the continent’s or world’s major disputes. A Permanent Seat Could Deepen Regional Rivalries Instead of fostering unity, a permanent African seat could democratize dysfunction. If the designated voting member votes in favor of a UN intervention or sanction that negatively impacts a neighboring rival, that vote will not be seen as a global peacekeeping measure; it will be viewed as an act of regional aggression. In a landscape already fractured by militia violence and border disputes, the immense geopolitical leverage of a UNSC vote could easily transform diplomatic disagreements into proxy wars or direct armed conflicts, as states compete to influence or neutralize the voting power of their neighbor. The Risk of Importing Global Polarization into Africa Ultimately, while the desire to democratize the United Nations is noble, treating a vast and complex continent as a single political entity is a dangerous miscalculation. Africa’s structural diversity, coupled with its colonial scars and governance challenges, means that a singular UNSC seat cannot justly represent the continent. Rather than correcting a historical imbalance, forcing a pan-African seat onto a non-monolithic continent risks importing global polarization directly into Africa’s delicate regional dynamics, turning a tool for global peace into a new engine for continental instability. items.title: Netanyahu oo safar qarsoodi ah ku tegay Imaaraadka, xilli ay taagan tahay fadeexadda…
items.description: Abu Dhabi (Caasimada Online) — Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Israel Benjamin Netanyahu ayaa Axadda maanta ah booqasho aan horay loo shaacin ku tegay dalka Imaaraadka Carabta, halkaas oo uu kula kulmay Madaxweynaha dalkaas Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, sida ay sheegeen warbaahinta Israel. Netanyahu ayaa diyaarad gaar ah ku tegay Abu Dhabi subaxnimadii Axadda, wuxuuna halkaas ku qaatay inta badan maalinta ka hor inta uusan dib ugu laaban Israel, sida ay sheegtay Ynet . Channel 12 ayaa sidoo kale xaqiijisay safarka, iyadoo soo xiganaysa laba ilo-wareed. Xafiiska Netanyahu iyo dowladda Imaaraadka ayaan isla markiiba shaacin kulanka, mana cadda waxa ay labada hoggaamiye si gaar ah uga wada hadleen. Kulankan ayaa imanaya xilli Israel ay ka taagan tahay fadeexad xooggan oo ku saabsan warar sheegaya in Madaxweyne Mohamed bin Zayed uu Netanyahu uga digay qorshe weerar oo Hamas ay diyaarineysay maalmo ka hor weerarkii weynaa ee 7-dii October 2023, balse uu iska indho-tiray. Warbixin ay Haaretz daabacday bishan ayaa sheegtay in MBZ uu Netanyahu si shaqsi ah uga digay in hoggaamiyihii Hamas Yahya Sinwar uu diyaarinayo tallaabo militari oo weyn. Netanyahu ayaa si adag u beeniyay jiritaanka digniintaas, wuxuuna sheegay in diiwaannada xafiiskiisa aysan muujineyn wax wada-hadal ah oo dhex maray isaga iyo madaxweynaha Imaaraadka xilligaas. Wuxuu sidoo kale ku hanjabay inuu dacwad ka gudbinayo Haaretz . Hase yeeshee, ilo Imaaraati ah oo la hadlay warbaahinta Israel ayaa sheegay in digniintu dhacday. The Times of Israel ayaa 8-dii September sheegtay in ilo Imaaraati ah oo xog-ogaal u ahaa wada-hadalka ay xaqiijiyeen in MBZ uu Netanyahu uga digay weerar weyn oo Hamas qorsheyneysay. Muranka ayaa sii xoogeystay toddobaadkii hore markii Channel 12 ay sheegtay in sirdoonka Imaaraadka uu hay’adda amniga gudaha Israel ee Shin Bet bishii September 2023 gaarsiiyay xog ku saabsan suurta-galnimada weerar Hamas ah. Sida ay warbaahintu sheegtay, xogtaas ayaa sababtay in MBZ uu Netanyahu taleefan kula xiriiro si uu u hubiyo in digniintu gaartay madaxda sare ee Israel. Channel 12 waxay xogta ku saleysay saddex ilo sare oo Imaaraati ah oo ay sheegtay inay si toos ah arrinta ula socdeen. Dowladda Imaaraadka si toos ah uma aysan xaqiijin ama beenin wada-hadalka la sheegay. Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda Imaaraadka ayaa horraantii bishan sheegtay in dowladda aysan ka hadlin wararka saxaafadda ee la xiriira wada-hadallada madaxda, balse waxay xustay in labada dal ay leeyihiin xiriir toos ah isla markaana xogaha sirdoonka la is dhaafsado marka loo baahdo. Xiriir amni oo sii xoogeysanaya Booqashada Axadda ayaa sidoo kale ku soo aadeysa xilli xiriirka amni ee Israel iyo Imaaraadka uu aad u xoogeysanayo, gaar ahaan wixii ka dambeeyay dagaalkii dhawaan dhex maray Israel iyo Iran. Ynet ayaa sheegtay in Israel ay xilligii dagaalka si ku-meel-gaar ah Imaaraadka u siisay nidaamka difaaca gantaallada ee Iron Dome, iyadoo sidoo kale dirtay shaqaale Israeli ah oo nidaamkaas maamula. Diblomaasiyiin Imaaraati ah ayaa tallaabadaas ku tilmaamay mid aan la illoobi doonin. Xiriirka labada dal ayaa rasmi noqday sanadkii 2020, markii Imaaraadka iyo Israel ay heshiis ku gaareen inay caadiyeeyaan xiriirkooda, iyadoo Mareykanku dhex-dhexaadiyay heshiisyadii loo bixiyay Abraham Accords. Tan iyo markaas labada dhinac waxay si weyn u ballaariyeen iskaashiga dhinacyada ganacsiga, maalgashiga, tiknoolajiyadda iyo amniga, inkastoo Abu Dhabi ay marar badan si cad uga hor timid siyaasadaha Israel ee Gaza iyo dhulka Falastiiniyiinta. Si kastaba, xiriirka heerka sare ah ayaa sii socday. Wakiillada Imaaraadka ayaa sidoo kale ka mid ahaa diblomaasiyiintii Carabta ee ku haray hoolka Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay intii Netanyahu uu khudbaddiisa jeedinayay toddobaadkii hore, xilli wufuud badan ay hoolka ka baxeen. Safarka Axadda ma aha markii ugu horreysay ee la soo sheego booqasho qarsoodi ah oo Netanyahu uu ku tegay Abu Dhabi. Xafiiskiisa ayaa bishii May sheegay inuu Imaaraadka booqday intii uu socday dagaalkii Iran, hase yeeshee dowladda Abu Dhabi ayaa markaas si cad u beenisay warkaas, iyadoo sheegtay in xiriirkeeda Israel uu yahay mid furan, islamarkaana aysan jirin booqashooyin qarsoodi ah oo aan mas’uuliyiinta Imaaraadku xaqiijin. Booqashada cusub ayaa sidaas darteed kusoo aadeysa xilli xiriirka labada dal dhinaca amniga uu sii xoogeysanayo, balse gudaha Israel ay weli taagan tahay dood culus oo ku saabsan waxa Netanyahu ogaa kahor weerarkii 7-dii October iyo digniinta la sheegay inay uga timid hoggaamiyaha Imaaraadka. Sida ay warbaahintu sheegtay, xogtaas ayaa sababtay in MBZ uu Netanyahu taleefan kula xiriiro si uu u hubiyo in digniintu gaartay madaxda sare ee Israel. Channel 12 waxay xogta ku saleysay saddex ilo sare oo Imaaraati ah oo ay sheegtay inay si toos ah arrinta ula socdeen. Dowladda Imaaraadka si toos ah uma aysan xaqiijin ama beenin wada-hadalka la sheegay. Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda Imaaraadka ayaa horraantii bishan sheegtay in dowladda aysan ka hadlin wararka saxaafadda ee la xiriira wada-hadallada madaxda, balse waxay xustay in labada dal ay leeyihiin xiriir toos ah isla markaana xogaha sirdoonka la is dhaafsado marka loo baahdo. Xiriir amni oo sii xoogeysanaya Booqashada Axadda ayaa sidoo kale ku soo aadeysa xilli xiriirka amni ee Israel iyo Imaaraadka uu aad u xoogeysanayo, gaar ahaan wixii ka dambeeyay dagaalkii dhawaan dhex maray Israel iyo Iran. Ynet ayaa sheegtay in Israel ay xilligii dagaalka si ku-meel-gaar ah Imaaraadka u siisay nidaamka difaaca gantaallada ee Iron Dome, iyadoo sidoo kale dirtay shaqaale Israeli ah oo nidaamkaas maamula. Diblomaasiyiin Imaaraati ah ayaa tallaabadaas ku tilmaamay mid aan la illoobi doonin. Xiriirka labada dal ayaa rasmi noqday sanadkii 2020, markii Imaaraadka iyo Israel ay heshiis ku gaareen inay caadiyeeyaan xiriirkooda, iyadoo Mareykanku dhex-dhexaadiyay heshiisyadii loo bixiyay Abraham Accords. Tan iyo markaas labada dhinac waxay si weyn u ballaariyeen iskaashiga dhinacyada ganacsiga, maalgashiga, tiknoolajiyadda iyo amniga, inkastoo Abu Dhabi ay marar badan si cad uga hor timid siyaasadaha Israel ee Gaza iyo dhulka Falastiiniyiinta. Si kastaba, xiriirka heerka sare ah ayaa sii socday. Wakiillada Imaaraadka ayaa sidoo kale ka mid ahaa diblomaasiyiintii Carabta ee ku haray hoolka Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay intii Netanyahu uu khudbaddiisa jeedinayay toddobaadkii hore, xilli wufuud badan ay hoolka ka baxeen. Safarka Axadda ma aha markii ugu horreysay ee la soo sheego booqasho qarsoodi ah oo Netanyahu uu ku tegay Abu Dhabi. Xafiiskiisa ayaa bishii May sheegay inuu Imaaraadka booqday intii uu socday dagaalkii Iran, hase yeeshee dowladda Abu Dhabi ayaa markaas si cad u beenisay warkaas, iyadoo sheegtay in xiriirkeeda Israel uu yahay mid furan, islamarkaana aysan jirin booqashooyin qarsoodi ah oo aan mas’uuliyiinta Imaaraadku xaqiijin. Booqashada cusub ayaa sidaas darteed kusoo aadeysa xilli xiriirka labada dal dhinaca amniga uu sii xoogeysanayo, balse gudaha Israel ay weli taagan tahay dood culus oo ku saabsan waxa Netanyahu ogaa kahor weerarkii 7-dii October iyo digniinta la sheegay inay uga timid hoggaamiyaha Imaaraadka. items.title: Fiqi oo tallaabo qaaday kadib cadaadiskii uga yimid BF + Sawirro
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga Soomaaliya, Mudane Axmed Macallin Fiqi oo uu wehliyo Taliyaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed, Sarreeye Guuto Ibraahim Maxamed Maxamuud ayaa qaaday tallaabo la xiriirta arrintii Baarlamaanka ee ku aadaneyd cabashadii kasoo yeertay qoysaska iyo agoonta ciidamada Xoogga Dalka. Xildhibaannada Baarlamaanka ayaa maalin kahor si kulul uga hadlay cabasho ku saabsan 6,000 oo askari oo isugu jiro hawlgab, naafo iyo qoysaska askartii dhimatay oo la sheegay in la jaray xuquuqdoodii. Guddiga difaaca ee Golaha Shacabka ayaa sidoo kale soo bandhigay 4 su’aal oo ku geedaamay arrintan, iyaga oo u yeeray wasiirka iyo taliyaha, si ay horyimaadaan golaha, una jawaabaan su’aalahaas muddo 72 saacadood gudahood ah. “Mudane Wasiir, waxaa lagaa sugayaa in aad qoraal ahaan uga soo jawaabto su’aalaha sare ku xusan muddo 72 saacadood gudahood ah. Sidoo kale waxa lagu farayaa in aad hortimaado Guddiga Difaaca adiga iyo Taliyaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, taariikhda hoos ku xusan. Taariikhda: 04/10/2026 Saacadda: 11:00 subaxnimo Goobta: Xafiiska Guddiga Difaaca, Golaha Shacabka, Villa Hargeysa,” ayaa lagu yiri warsaxaafadeedka. Intaas kadib, Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga ayaa maanta kulan is-xaalwareysi ah la qaatay qaar ka mid ah qoysaska iyo carruurta ay ka tageen geesiyaashii Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka ee u shahiiday difaaca dalka, isaga oo ka xog wareystay xaaladdooda nololeed. Sidoo kale wasiir Fiqi ayaa qoysaska u sharraxay qorshaha dowladda ee lagu daryeelayo carruurta shuhadada, iyagoo sheegay in Golaha Wasiirrada ay ansixiyeen Xeer-nidaamiyaha Daryeelka Agoonta Shuhadada XDS, isla markaana la dhisi doono hay’ad u gaar ah maamulka agoonta iyo daryeelkooda. Waxaa kale oo uu qoysaska ku wargeliyey in dhowaan la hirgelin doono dugsi iyo goob caafimaad oo u gaar ah agoonta. Ugu dambeyn wuxuu adkeeyey in naf-hurkii geesiyaashii shahiiday aan la hilmaami doonin, daryeelka qoysaskooda iyo ubadkooduna uu yahay waajib qaran. items.title: Burcadbadeedda oo dil ugu hanjabay Pakistaniyiin lagu qabtay Puntland
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Kooxaha burcadbadeeda Soomaalida ee gacanta ku haya Markabka MT Honour 25, oo sita calanka Palau ayaa dil ugu hanjabay shaqaalaha saaran markabkaas oo ay la socdaan illaa 17 shaqaale ah, oo 10 ka mid ah ay yihiin Pakistani. Ehellada badmaaxiinta oo kasoo muuqday warbaahinta ayaa sheegay inay waayeen xiriirka wiilashooda, xilli ay soo baxayaan walaacyo cusub oo ku saabsan badbaadada shaqaalaha la socda markabka oo 21-kii Abriil lagu qabsaday xeebaha Puntland ee Soomaaliya. Xaaladda shaqaalaha ayaa hadda laga dayrinayaa, waxaana burcadbadeeddu ugu hanjabeen inay dilayaan haddii ciidamada ammaanku isku dayaan inay xoog ku soo furtaan, sida ay ku warrantay Arab News. Sidoo kale, waxaa la helay farriimo iyo sawirro uu soo diray kabtanka markabka oo lagu magacaabo Ashari Samadikun, kuwaas oo muujinaya in shaqaalaha markabka loogu hanjabay hub, isla markaana ay ku jiraan xaalad cabsi iyo wal-wal ah. Dhanka kale, Hay’adda Ansar Burney Trust International, oo xiriir la leh shaqaalaha markabka ayaa sheegtay in budhcad-badeeddu dalbadeen lacag madax furasho ah oo dhan 1.9 milyan oo dollar, si ay u sii daayaan shaqaalaha iyo markabka iyadoo dalabkaas lala wadaagay dowladda Pakistan. Hanjabaadahan ayaa kusoo aaday, xilli Jimcihii ciidamada badda ee maamulka Puntland ay soo badbaadiyeen 20 shaqaale ah oo saarnaa markabka SIBU 1, kaas oo sidoo kale ay horay u afduubteen burcadbadeeddu. Maalmo ka hor wasaaradaha arrimaha dibadda ee dalalka Soomaaliya iyo Pakistan oo yeeshay wada-hadallo khadka taleefoonka ah ayaa ka arrinsaday xaaladda muwaadiniinta Pakistan ee saaran markabka MT Honour 25, iyadoo Pakistan ay Soomaaliya ka dalbatay inay ka caawiso sidii loo soo badbaadin lahaa muwaadiniinteeda. Si kastaba, ha’ahaatee, Bishii April ee lasoo dhaafay ayay ahayd markii ay gacanta burcadbadeeda galeen ilaa seddax markab oo labo ka mid ah oo kala ah Honour 25 oo laga leeyahay dalka Palau iyo Eureka oo laga leeyahay dalka Togo, kuwaas shidaal siday kadibna la qabsaday, waxaana loo jiheeyay dhanka xeebaha Puntland. The post Burcadbadeedda oo dil ugu hanjabay Pakistaniyiin lagu qabtay Puntland appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Afar Wasaaradood, Hal Agaasime Guud: Saameynta Ka Dhalan Karta Wareejinta Joogtada ah ee Mas’uuliyiinta Dowladda
items.description: Muqdisho – Magacaabista Axmed Yuusuf ee Agaasimaha Guud ee Wasaaradda Isgaarsiinta iyo Teknolojiyadda ayaa dhalinaysa dood ku saabsan habka loo maareeyo xilalka sare ee dowladda, gaar ahaan wareejinta masuuliyiinta u kala wareegaya wasaarado leh waajibaadyo iyo shaqooyin kala duwan. Axmed Yuusuf ayaa hore u soo noqday Agaasimaha Guud ee Wasaaradda Dekedaha, Wasaaradda Tamarta iyo Khayraadka Biyaha iyo Wasaaradda Caafimaadka, isaga oo hadda loo magacaabay Agaasimaha Guud ee Wasaaradda Isgaarsiinta iyo Teknolojiyadda. Taas ayaa ka dhigan inuu xilka Agaasimaha Guud ka soo qabtay afar wasaaradood oo kala duwan afartii sano ee lasoo dhaafay ee Xukuumadda Xamze Cabdi Barre. Arrintan ayaa keenaysa su’aalo ku saabsan joogtaynta maamulka, khibradda gaarka ah ee wasaaradaha iyo sida ay wareejinta soo noqnoqota u saameyn karto hufnaanta iyo waxqabadka hay’adaha dowladda. Joogtaynta maamulka iyo qorshayaasha wasaaradaha Agaasimaha Guud waa masuulka ugu sarreeya ee maamulka iyo hawlgalka maalinlaha ah ee wasaaradda, isaga oo door muhiim ah ku leh fulinta qorshayaasha, maaraynta shaqaalaha iyo dabagalka mashaariicda. Marka masuul xilal kala duwan loo wareejiyo, waxaa dhici karta in qorshayaashii hore ay wajahaan dib-u-eegis, halka maamulka cusub uu u baahan karo waqti uu ku fahmo nidaamyada iyo baahiyaha wasaaradda. Haddii wareejinta xilalku ay noqoto mid soo noqnoqota, waxaa dhici karta in mashaariicda muddada dheer qaata ay la kulmaan dib-u-dhac, isla markaana ay adkaato in si joogto ah loola socdo fulinta qorshayaasha. Khibradda guud iyo aqoonta gaarka ah Wasaarad kasta waxay leedahay waajibaad iyo aqoon u gaar ah. Wasaaradda Dekeduhu waxay ku shaqaysaa maamulka dekedaha, Wasaaradda Tamarta iyo Khayraadka Biyuhu waxay diiradda saartaa tamarta iyo biyaha, halka Wasaaradda Caafimaadku ay masuul ka tahay adeegyada caafimaadka. Wasaaradda Isgaarsiinta iyo Teknolojiyaddu waxay iyaduna leedahay hawlo la xiriira isgaarsiinta, adeegyada dijitaalka ah iyo horumarinta teknoolojiyadda. Khibradda maamul ee uu masuulku ka soo kasbaday wasaaradihii hore waxay noqon kartaa mid waxtar leh, balse waxaa muhiim ah in la helo aqoon iyo faham ku filan oo ku saabsan waajibaadka wasaaradda cusub. Isla xisaabtanka iyo qiimeynta waxqabadka Wareejinta joogtada ah ee masuuliyiinta waxay sidoo kale dhalin kartaa su’aalo ku saabsan isla xisaabtanka iyo qiimeynta waxqabadka. Waxaa muhiim ah in la ogaado muddada uu masuulku xil kasta hayay, waxqabadkii uu ka sameeyay wasaaradihii uu soo maray iyo sababaha keenay in loo wareejiyo wasaarado kala duwan. Haddii aan si cad loo qiimeyn waxqabadka masuuliyiinta, waxaa adkaan karta in la ogaado in wareejinta xilalku ay ku salaysan tahay baahida hay’adaha, khibradda masuulka ama arrimo kale oo maamul. Maxaa laga filayaa xilka cusub? Magacaabista Axmed Yuusuf ee Wasaaradda Isgaarsiinta iyo Teknolojiyadda waxay fursad u noqon kartaa inuu ka faa’iideysto waayo-aragnimadii uu ka soo kasbaday wasaaradihii hore. Hase yeeshee, waxaa muhiim ah in maamulka cusub uu yeesho qorshe shaqo oo cad, yoolal la cabbiri karo iyo hannaan lagu qiimeeyo waxqabadka, si loo xaqiijiyo in wasaaraddu gaarto himilooyinkeeda. In hal masuul uu xilka Agaasimaha Guud ka soo qabto afar wasaaradood oo kala duwan waxay dhalinaysaa dood ku saabsan habka loo maareeyo hoggaanka maamulka dowladda iyo joogtaynta shaqada hay’adaha. Khibradda maamulku waa muhiim, balse waxaa sidoo kale muhiim ah in la tixgeliyo aqoonta gaarka ah ee wasaaradaha, muddada xilka, waxqabadka iyo sababaha keenaya wareejinta masuuliyiinta. Su’aasha ugu weyn ayaa ah: Maxaa lagu saleeyay in Axmed Yuusuf afar wasaaradood oo kala duwan loo wareejiyo, maxaase laga filayaa inuu ka qabto Wasaaradda Isgaarsiinta iyo Teknolojiyadda?

Magacaabista Axmed Yuusuf ee Wasaaradda Isgaarsiinta iyo Teknolojiyadda waxay fursad u noqon kartaa inuu ka faa’iideysto waayo-aragnimadii uu ka soo kasbaday wasaaradihii hore. Hase yeeshee, waxaa muhiim ah in maamulka cusub uu yeesho qorshe shaqo oo cad, yoolal la cabbiri karo iyo hannaan lagu qiimeeyo waxqabadka, si loo xaqiijiyo in wasaaraddu gaarto himilooyinkeeda. In hal masuul uu xilka Agaasimaha Guud ka soo qabto afar wasaaradood oo kala duwan waxay dhalinaysaa dood ku saabsan habka loo maareeyo hoggaanka maamulka dowladda iyo joogtaynta shaqada hay’adaha. Khibradda maamulku waa muhiim, balse waxaa sidoo kale muhiim ah in la tixgeliyo aqoonta gaarka ah ee wasaaradaha, muddada xilka, waxqabadka iyo sababaha keenaya wareejinta masuuliyiinta. Su’aasha ugu weyn ayaa ah: Maxaa lagu saleeyay in Axmed Yuusuf afar wasaaradood oo kala duwan loo wareejiyo, maxaase laga filayaa inuu ka qabto Wasaaradda Isgaarsiinta iyo Teknolojiyadda?

items.title: Maxaa kasoo baxay kulankii dhex-maray R/W Xamza iyo guddoomiye Jaamac?
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Ra’iisul wasaaraha Soomaaliya, Mudane Xamza Cabdi Barre ayaa maanta kulan gaar ah la yeeshay guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka, Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac), xilli uu khilaaf xooggan soo kala dhex-galay labada xafiis. Xamza iyo Jaamac ayaa ka wada-hadlay arrimo xasaasi ah oo ku aadan dardargelinta wada-shaqeynta labada xafiis, si loo xaqiijiyo himilooyinka qaranka. Sidoo kale, labada mas’uul ayaa isla soo hadal arrimaha keenay khilaafka, waxayna isla gareen ilaalinta dastuurka, sarreynta sharciga iyo ixtiraamka curfiga maamulka dowladeed, sida uu shaaciyay guddoomiye Jaamac oo qoraal kooan oo saaray kadib kulanka uu la yeeshay Ra’iisul wasaaraha. “Waxaan mahad ballaaran u celinayaa Ra’iisul Wasaaraha XFS, Mudane Xamsa Cabdi Barre, oo maanta iigu yimid booqasho shaqo, taas oo aan ku dardargelinayno wada-shaqeynta labada gole, si loo xaqiijiyo himilooyinka qaranka iyo dowlad-dhis ku salaysan ilaalinta Dastuurka, sarreynta sharciga iyo ixtiraamka curfiga maamulka dowladeed,” ayuu yiri Jaamac. Khilaafka labada xafiis ayaa yimid, kadib markii uu guddoomiyaha Baarlamaanka ku dhiiraday tallaabo ka dhan ah Ra’iisul wasaaraha isagoo qaraar kusoo saaray mooshinkii dhawaan lagu baabi’iyay wareegtadii Ra’iisul wasaare Xamza ee ku aadanaa in xilalka agaasime-waaxeedyada wasaaradaha iyo hay’adaha kale ee dowladda lagu buuxiyo hannaan tartan ah. Arrintan ayaa keentay is-qab-qabsi awoodeed oo ka dhex bilowday guddoonka Baarlamaanka iyo xafiiska Ra’iisul wasaaraha Soomaaliya, taas oo si weyn loo dareemay todobaadkii lasoo dhaafay. Is-haysiga labada xafiis ayaa loo arkaa mid salka ku haya ku tartanka awoodda iyo saamaynta siyaasadda guud ee dalka, maadaama lagu jiro xilli adag oo kala guur ah. items.title: Somalia: Pirates captured in SIBU tanker raid escape Puntland convoy
items.description: MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – Nineteen pirates escaped from a convoy of vehicles transporting them to Puntland’s regional capital on Saturday, a day after being captured in a raid to free the SIBU tanker off Somalia’s northeastern coast, Caasimada Online news website reported on Sunday. The pirates broke free in the Shakaal area near Jariiban as regional security forces moved them by road from the coastal town of Gara’ad toward Garowe, the reports said. One of the men was killed attempting to flee and another was wounded. The remainder got away. The size of the group initially captured remains unclear. Puntland authorities said 46 pirates were taken in the operation to free the SIBU1 tanker. Media reports have put the figure at 21. Two of the men who escaped on Saturday had been captured separately following the earlier release of the Lutuf cargo ship, which was carrying weapons for a Turkish military base in Mogadishu. That vessel was freed after a ransom was paid. Puntland authorities did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Contact us: info@somaliguardian.com

items.title: Riyadii guurka oo isku beddeshay Geeri – Qisada xanuunka badan ee Maryan
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Allaha u naxariistee waxaa maanta magaalada Muqdisho ku geeriyootay Marxuumad Maryan Maxamed Cabdi, oo ahayd gabar da’yar oo rajo weyn ka qabtay nolosha, isla markaana ku jirtay diyaar-garowgii ugu dambeeyay ee arooskeeda. Maryan, oo ahayd gabar ay waalidkeed si weyn ugu tiirsanaayeen ayaa xalay si nabad ah ugu hoyatay gurigeeda, balse saq-dhexe ayay u timid geeridii xaqa ahayd, sida ay sheegeen ehelladeeda. Marxuumadda ayaa maalmaha soo socda ku howlanayd arooskeeda, iyadoo ay maalmo kooban ka harsanaayeen maalintii ay rajaynaysay inay noqoto bilowga nolosheeda cusub, hase yeeshee qorshihii guurka ayaa si lama filaan ah isu beddelay sagootintii ugu dambeysay ee nolosheeda. Juure Sheekh Xuseen, oo ah wiilka ay Marxuumad Maryan qorsheynayeen inay wada aqal-galaan ayaa ka sheekeeyay qisadan xanuunka badan, isagoo sheegay in labada waalid ay isku raaceen guurka, isla markaana ay wax walba u socdeen sidii loo qorsheeyay. Waxaase qaddarta Alle ay noqotay in farxaddii la sugayay ay isu beddesho murugo iyo baroor-diiq, iyadoo geeridu ka soo hormartay maalintii arooskooda. Hoos ka akhriso qoraalka Juure oo dhammaystiran;- Maryam Maxamed Cabdi, marka hore waxaan Alle uga baryayaa inuu u naxariisto, Jannatul Firdowsana ka waraabiyo, qabrigana u waasiciyo oo u iftiimiyo. Toddobaadkan ayaan ku ballansanayn in meherkeennu dhaco. Hooyadeed iyo aabaheed, oo ay kaligeed u ahayd, waxayna ogaayeen inaan is jecel nahay soona doona rabo. Aad ayaan u jeclaa Maryam, waxaana ii muuqatay inay ahayd riyo guur iyo mustaqbal ifaya oo aan wadaagi doonno. Maryam waxay ahayd qof Ahlu-Diin ah. Mar walba waxay igala hadli jirtay inaan Qur’aanka wada xifdinno haddii aan is guursanno, sidoo kalena waxay mar walba igu waanin jirtay Alle ka cabsiga iyo dhowrsanaanta. Shalay galab, anigoo shaqada ka sii baxaya, ayay ii soo qortay fariin qalbigayga weligeed ku sii jiri doonta: “Jacaylkaygiiyow, ma garanayo eray aan ku cabbiro waxa qalbigaygu kuu qabo, sababtoo ah jacaylka aan kuu qabo erayo kama weynaan karo. Waxaad noqotay qof aan qalbigayga ka dhex arko xitaa marka indhahaygu ku waayaan…” Waxay ii sheegtay inay rabto inay noqoto qofka garabkayga istaaga marka aan faraxsanahay iyo marka ay noloshu igu adkaato. Xalay, iyadoo caafimaad qabta, ayay ii sheegtay inay daallan tahay, salaaddana ay rabto inay tukato. Waxay igu tiri: “Berri ayaan wada hadleynaa.” Aniguna waan sii salaamay, anigoo aan marnaba ogeyn in hadalkaas uu noqon doono salaantii ugu dambaysay ee aan is dhaafsanno. Subaxnimadii hore waxaa ii timid fariintii ugu naxdinta badnayd ee aan nolosheyda maqlo. Dumashiday, oo arrinteena ogeyd, ayaa ii soo qortay: “Asc dumashi, horta aad baan uga xumahay inaan arrintan naxdinta leh kuu sheego. Maryan Alle ayaa naga jecladay. Xalay 8-dii ayay neeftu ku qabatay, markii isbitaalka la geeyayna waxay dhaheen naftu way ka baxday. Ilaahay ha u naxariisto. Haddii ay jirto wax aad ka tabanayso, walaal iska cafi.” Innaa lillaahi wa innaa ilayhi raajicuun. Waxa iigu daran ma aha oo keliya inaan waayay qofkii aan jeclaa ee aan rabay inay xaaskayga noqoto. Waxa iigu daran waa inaan arkayo waalidkii ay kaligeed u ahayd, oo maanta la kulmay murugo aan erayo lagu cabbiri karin. Ilaahay qalbigooda ha qaboojiyo, samir iyo iimaanna ha ka siiyo. Riyadii guurku waxay hal habeen isku beddeshay safar geeri ah oo aan dib looga soo noqon. Maryam, Alle ayaa igaaga kaa jeclaaday. Waxaan Alle kaaga baryayaa inuu Jannatul Firdowsa kaa dhigo hoygaaga, qabrigana kuu waasiciyo oo kuu iftiimiyo. Waxaan sidoo kale Alle ka baryayaa inuu nagu kulmiyo Jannadiisa. Jacaylkii aan kuu qabay ma dhammaanayo geeridaada. Xusuustaaduna qalbigayga ayay ku sii noolaan doontaa. Innaa lillaahi wa innaa ilayhi raajicuun. Ilahay qalbiga hano qaboojiyo aniga iyo waaridkii dhalay badal qayr qaba allaha siiyo. items.title: Hamza’s Election Plan Meets Somalia’s Political Reality: No Deal, No Access to Puntland or Jubaland
items.description: Prime Minister Says Voting Will Take Place Wherever Possible — But the Federal Government Still Faces a Political and Territorial Deadlock With Puntland and Jubaland Mogadishu (WDN)- Somalia’s federal government is pressing ahead with its election plans, but Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre’s latest comments have exposed a fundamental problem: Mogadishu is outlining how elections will be conducted in territories where it has yet to secure the political agreement or administrative access required to implement them. Speaking on the Miizaan Podcast produced by Dawan Media, Hamza said elections would be held in areas of Jubaland where circumstances permit. Where direct voting is not possible, he said, electoral authorities would use alternative procedures designed for such circumstances. “The election will take place, wherever it can take place,” the prime minister said. Hamza said the situation in Jubaland differs from that of other federal member states because the federal government does not recognize the current Jubaland administration. Nevertheless, he said Mogadishu wants Jubaland to participate in the national electoral process and that voting would take place wherever security and other conditions allow. He specifically mentioned Jilib, Bu’aale, Hagar, Jamaame and Badhaadhe as areas where direct voting could prove impossible. In such locations, he said, the electoral authorities could apply the procedures established for constituencies where voting cannot physically take place. He referred to the “one electoral district” system as providing election authorities with mechanisms for handling parliamentary seats or constituencies where polling cannot be conducted. Hamza also cited Iraq and Afghanistan as examples of countries where elections have been held despite some areas being inaccessible for voting, with alternative arrangements used to manage those constituencies. But the problem confronting Somalia is not merely logistical. It is political. The Missing Agreement The latest political developments provide little evidence of an agreed national electoral settlement. On September 23, former Puntland presidency minister Mohamed Abdirahman Dhabancad, a member of the Somali Future Council’s technical committee, said that government and opposition representatives had held both leadership-level and technical discussions but had failed to reach agreement on key electoral issues. Former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed similarly said on September 18 that the talks had failed to move forward, although he stopped short of formally declaring them collapsed. Puntland and Jubaland representatives have also previously withdrawn from or rejected rounds of talks when they believed the process was not producing an acceptable electoral framework. In July, both states withdrew from talks in Mogadishu, with reports citing unresolved disagreements over the electoral system and the role of the federal government. That leaves a fundamental question hanging over the government’s election timetable: How can an election be nationally implemented when the principal political actors have not agreed on the rules? Jubaland: A Government Mogadishu Does Not Recognize The dispute is particularly acute in Jubaland. In November 2024, Jubaland suspended relations and cooperation with the Federal Government following a bitter dispute over the regional election process. Reuters reported at the time that the two sides had issued reciprocal arrest warrants and that both governments commanded substantial security forces. That rupture has never been fully resolved. Mogadishu does not recognize the current Jubaland administration, while Kismayo has continued to operate its own political and security institutions. The consequence is straightforward: a federal election cannot simply be announced in Jubaland and assumed to be implementable . Even if Mogadishu declares that voting will occur wherever possible, the practical question remains who will provide security, who will administer polling stations, who will register voters, which authorities will recognize the results and what political agreement will govern the distribution of parliamentary seats. Those are not technical questions alone. They go to the heart of Somalia’s federal political settlement. Puntland: An Even Deeper Divide Puntland presents another major obstacle. Puntland suspended cooperation with the federal government over constitutional, electoral and national-security issues and has maintained its own political and administrative processes outside the federal government’s preferred electoral framework. Its dispute with Mogadishu has since become one of the central fault lines in Somalia’s national political crisis. The reality on the ground is therefore difficult to reconcile with the language of a single nationwide election administered from Mogadishu. The federal government does not exercise ordinary administrative authority across Puntland, and there is no current political agreement giving Mogadishu an accepted operational role in organizing elections there. The same broader problem exists in Jubaland. This does not necessarily mean that elections in those territories are impossible. It means that they cannot realistically be implemented through federal declarations alone. North Eastern State and the Other Regions Hamza also distinguished the newly established Northeastern State from Puntland and Jubaland. He said voter registration and local elections would take place there, arguing that the administration’s leadership and parliament still have valid mandates and that its circumstances therefore differ from regions facing deeper political disputes. The distinction illustrates the larger problem facing the federal electoral project: Somalia is no longer dealing with one uniform political environment. Different federal member states have different political arrangements, levels of cooperation with Mogadishu and relationships with the federal electoral institutions. A national election therefore requires more than an electoral timetable. Speaking on the Miizaan Podcast produced by Dawan Media, Hamza said elections would be held in areas of Jubaland where circumstances permit. Where direct voting is not possible, he said, electoral authorities would use alternative procedures designed for such circumstances. “The election will take place, wherever it can take place,” the prime minister said. Hamza said the situation in Jubaland differs from that of other federal member states because the federal government does not recognize the current Jubaland administration. Nevertheless, he said Mogadishu wants Jubaland to participate in the national electoral process and that voting would take place wherever security and other conditions allow. He specifically mentioned Jilib, Bu’aale, Hagar, Jamaame and Badhaadhe as areas where direct voting could prove impossible. In such locations, he said, the electoral authorities could apply the procedures established for constituencies where voting cannot physically take place. He referred to the “one electoral district” system as providing election authorities with mechanisms for handling parliamentary seats or constituencies where polling cannot be conducted. Hamza also cited Iraq and Afghanistan as examples of countries where elections have been held despite some areas being inaccessible for voting, with alternative arrangements used to manage those constituencies. But the problem confronting Somalia is not merely logistical. It is political. The Missing Agreement The latest political developments provide little evidence of an agreed national electoral settlement. On September 23, former Puntland presidency minister Mohamed Abdirahman Dhabancad, a member of the Somali Future Council’s technical committee, said that government and opposition representatives had held both leadership-level and technical discussions but had failed to reach agreement on key electoral issues. Former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed similarly said on September 18 that the talks had failed to move forward, although he stopped short of formally declaring them collapsed. Puntland and Jubaland representatives have also previously withdrawn from or rejected rounds of talks when they believed the process was not producing an acceptable electoral framework. In July, both states withdrew from talks in Mogadishu, with reports citing unresolved disagreements over the electoral system and the role of the federal government. That leaves a fundamental question hanging over the government’s election timetable: How can an election be nationally implemented when the principal political actors have not agreed on the rules? In November 2024, Jubaland suspended relations and cooperation with the Federal Government following a bitter dispute over the regional election process. Reuters reported at the time that the two sides had issued reciprocal arrest warrants and that both governments commanded substantial security forces. That rupture has never been fully resolved. It means that they cannot realistically be implemented through federal declarations alone. items.title: Who Really Freed SIBU 1? Puntland and Iraqi Tribe Offer Rival Accounts of Tanker Rescue
items.description: Puntland Maritime Police Say Their Forces Recaptured the Hijacked Tanker After a 48-Hour Operation, while an Iraqi Tribe Claims Its Members Helped Free the Vessel GAROWE (WDN) — A dramatic rescue of the hijacked oil tanker MT SIBU 1 off Somalia has triggered competing accounts over who actually carried out the operation, with Puntland authorities crediting their maritime forces while an Iraqi tribe says its members travelled to the region and helped retake the vessel from Somali pirates. The dispute emerged after the Al-Shaghanba tribe of Iraq’s Basra Governorate claimed that around 40 of its members participated in an operation to recover the tanker, which it said was owned by an Iraqi businessman from the tribe. At almost the same time, Puntland authorities announced that the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF) had successfully freed SIBU 1 and its 20-member crew in a counter-piracy operation off the coast of Mudug. Reuters independently reported Puntland’s claim, quoting Mohamed Jama, a PMPF commander, as saying that the operation had been conducted by Puntland forces over two days and that the ship had been freed. The competing accounts have turned what was initially reported as a successful anti-piracy operation into a more intriguing question: Who actually led the operation that freed the tanker? Puntland’s Account: A Two-Day Maritime Operation According to Puntland authorities, the tanker was recovered by the PMPF after being tracked toward the Somali coast. The vessel had been seized on August 20 by armed men while sailing in the Gulf of Aden, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). It was subsequently taken toward Somali waters. Puntland officials said their maritime forces conducted an operation lasting approximately 48 hours off the coast of Mudug. Initial reports from Puntland said 15 suspected pirates were captured, one was killed and four were wounded, while a Puntland officer was also injured. A subsequent PMPF statement gave a higher figure, saying that 41 suspected pirates were detained, with one killed and five wounded. Puntland also said the tanker, its cargo and all 20 crew members were safe. The crew reportedly included 16 Indians, two Syrians, one Iraqi and one Sudanese national. Reuters reported the rescue as a Puntland maritime-police operation, providing the strongest independent confirmation currently available for Puntland’s version of events. The Iraqi Version The Al-Shaghanba tribe has presented a different account. Sheikh Ali Al-Shaghanbi told Iraqi media that approximately 40 members of the tribe, recruited from Abu Al-Khasib district and the village of Jikour near Basra, mobilized after learning that a tanker belonging to a member of the tribe had been seized. According to the sheikh, the group coordinated with contacts outside Iraq to locate and recover the vessel. Iraqi reports said the tribal members eventually confronted the alleged pirates and helped retake the tanker and free its crew. Al-Shaghanbi said seven alleged pirates were captured while others escaped. Some Iraqi reports have described a firefight lasting several hours. The tribe has also claimed that its operation was conducted after communication and coordination with the Somali government. That claim, however, has not been independently established. The Numbers Raise Questions The competing accounts contain significant differences. The Iraqi tribal account speaks of approximately 40 tribesmen and seven captured pirates. Puntland’s later account refers to 41 suspected pirates detained, alongside one death and five wounded. The two versions also differ over the nature and leadership of the operation. Puntland says its maritime police conducted the counter-piracy operation. The Iraqi tribe says its members travelled to the area and participated directly in recovering the vessel. Somali maritime-security sources cited by Horseed Media have suggested that personnel working on behalf of the tanker-owning company may also have assisted Puntland forces. But available images and videos have not established who led the boarding operation or precisely how the different parties may have interacted. What Is Established — and What Is Not Several elements of the incident are now relatively clear. SIBU 1 was hijacked on August 20 in the Gulf of Aden and subsequently taken toward Somali waters. Puntland says its maritime forces recovered the tanker off Mudug after a two-day operation. The 20 crew members were reported safe. What remains unclear is the exact role played by the Iraqi tribal group. The Al-Shaghanba claim has been reported by several Iraqi outlets, and videos purporting to show the confrontation have circulated online. But the precise location of the alleged tribal operation, the identity of those involved, the command structure and the relationship between the Iraqi group and Puntland forces have not been independently established. That distinction matters. A successful maritime recovery involving a regional security force, a foreign tribal group and personnel linked to the vessel’s ownership would be highly unusual. A Remarkable Maritime Intervention The Iraqi account, if ultimately confirmed in full, would add an extraordinary dimension to the incident. It would mean that members of a Basra-based tribe travelled across international waters to help recover a vessel allegedly owned by one of their members after it was seized by pirates. But the Puntland account is equally significant. The PMPF has long presented itself as one of Somalia’s principal regional forces responsible for combating piracy along Puntland’s extensive coastline. Its claim that it tracked and intercepted SIBU 1 after the vessel was brought toward Mudug places the rescue squarely within its counter-piracy operations. The competing narratives therefore go beyond a dispute over credit. They raise questions about who exercised operational control, who authorized the intervention and how foreign nationals could participate in an armed maritime operation inside Somali waters. The Evidence Gap For now, the safest conclusion is that SIBU 1 was recovered and its crew freed, but the full story of how the operation was conducted remains unresolved. Puntland has provided an official account supported by statements from its maritime police and independent reporting by Reuters. The Al-Shaghanba tribe has provided its own account, claiming direct involvement. Neither account, however, fully explains the other’s reported presence. The videos and photographs circulating online may eventually help establish what happened, but they do not by themselves determine who planned, commanded or executed the operation. The tanker is free. The crew is safe. Suspected pirates are in custody. But the battle over who deserves credit for the rescue has only just begun. Until the competing accounts are independently reconciled, the SIBU 1 rescue remains a story with two versions — and one crucial unanswered question: Who actually took back the ship? items.title: Oromo Leaders and Abiy Hold High-Stakes Talks as Ethiopia Faces New Political Storm
items.description: ADDIS ABABA (WDN) — In a striking development as Ethiopia faces renewed fighting and the emergence of a broad anti-government alliance, senior Oromo political figures have reportedly held talks with Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali over the country’s political future, national unity and the growing security crisis. The discussions reportedly focused on what has gone wrong in Ethiopia, the deepening political divisions and possible ways to strengthen the country’s unity in the face of mounting internal and external pressures. What makes the meeting particularly significant is not simply who attended, but who was brought together. Oromo political figures from both government-aligned and opposition backgrounds reportedly participated in discussions about the country’s future, suggesting an attempt to create a common Oromo political position at a moment when Ethiopia’s political landscape is undergoing another dramatic transformation. The meeting comes just days after seven Ethiopian armed and political movements announced the formation of the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, a coalition that includes the Tigray People’s Liberation Front, Amhara Fano, the Oromo Liberation Army and other regional movements. The alliance says it seeks to remove the current federal government and establish an inclusive transitional administration. The ONLF Question Dominates the Conversation One of the most sensitive issues reportedly raised during the meeting was the involvement of the Ogaden National Liberation Front (ONLF) in the new alliance. According to the account presented by participants, Oromo leaders questioned why the federal government had failed to deal with the ONLF in a manner they believed reflected the organisation’s historical status and its decades-long armed struggle. PM Abiy and Oromo opposition leaders The argument reportedly put forward was that the federal government had made a serious political mistake in its handling of the organisation and had treated it in a manner that fell short of the political weight it had accumulated after decades of conflict. The issue has become particularly sensitive because ONLF’s participation in the new alliance is itself disputed. The faction led by Abdirahman Mohamed Sheikh Mahdi has said it is part of the new coalition, while another ONLF leadership faction has publicly rejected the alliance and said its name was used without authorisation. That internal split makes the ONLF question even more politically complicated for Addis Ababa. An Unusual Oromo Political Gathering The most striking element of the reported discussions is that Oromo political figures from different political camps reportedly engaged with one another as Oromos, rather than simply as representatives of competing parties. Among those reportedly designated to pursue discussions with ONLF and its chairman Abdirahman Mohamed Mahdi are several prominent Oromo political figures: Professor Merera Gudina, chairman of the Oromo Federalist Congress (OFC); Daud Ibsa, chairman of the Oromo Liberation Front (OLF); Aba Dula Gemeda, former president of Oromia; Muktar Kedir, former president of Oromia; Juneydi Sado, former president of Oromia; Jawar Mohammed, prominent Oromo political activist and commentator; and other Oromo figures whose names were not immediately available. The reported decision to establish such a group suggests that the discussions went beyond a routine political consultation. The proposed committee would be tasked with engaging ONLF and exploring whether a political channel can be established with the organisation and the faction led by Abdirahman Mohamed Mahdi. A New Political Reality The timing is impossible to ignore. For years, Ethiopia’s political crises have largely been managed through separate negotiations with individual regions, parties and armed movements. The emergence of the new Alliance for Survival has changed that equation by bringing together movements from several parts of Ethiopia, including groups that were once bitter enemies. The Oromo dimension is particularly important. The Oromo are Ethiopia’s largest ethnic community, and Oromo politics has long been central to the country’s struggle over federalism, political representation and the distribution of power. The reported meeting therefore raises a larger question: Can Oromo political forces find enough common ground to influence the direction of Ethiopia’s next political settlement? That question has become more urgent as the country confronts renewed conflict in Tigray, continuing instability in Amhara and armed conflict in parts of Oromia. From Confrontation to Dialogue? The reported discussions appear to reflect an effort to explore political solutions before Ethiopia’s multiple conflicts become even more deeply interconnected. The proposed engagement with ONLF could be particularly significant if it produces a political channel with the Mahdi-led faction. But the internal split within ONLF means that any such effort would face an immediate challenge over who legitimately represents the organisation. One faction has reaffirmed the 2018 peace agreement with Addis Ababa and rejected armed alliances, while the Mahdi-led faction has asserted that it authorised participation in the new coalition. The Oromo leaders’ reported initiative therefore comes at a moment when Ethiopia’s political map is becoming increasingly fragmented. A Critical Moment for Ethiopia The broader political significance of the meeting may ultimately lie in the decision to bring together Oromo figures from different political backgrounds. Government supporters and opposition figures rarely find themselves on the same side of the political table. Yet Ethiopia’s rapidly changing security environment may be forcing political actors to reconsider old divisions. The immediate challenge is whether dialogue can produce concrete political arrangements before armed confrontation overwhelms the possibility of compromise. For Abiy Ahmed, the reported discussions offer a potential political avenue at a moment when his government faces a newly coordinated armed opposition. For Oromo political leaders, they offer an opportunity to articulate a broader position on Ethiopia’s future. For ONLF, the competing claims over its representation could determine whether it becomes part of a new national political settlement or remains divided between competing political paths. And for Ethiopia as a whole, the stakes are enormous. A country already facing renewed war is now witnessing something equally consequential: political figures from different Oromo camps attempting to speak across their divisions while former enemies assemble on the battlefield. The question now is whether Ethiopia’s political leaders can achieve at the negotiating table what armed groups have so far failed to achieve on the battlefield: a framework for sharing power without breaking the country apart. items.title: DFS oo mushaarka u fasaxday in ka badan 2,500 askari oo ku sugan Waqooyi Bari
items.description: Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya (DFS) ayaa xalay markii ugu horreysay mushaarkooda u fasaxday in ka badan 2,500 oo askari oo ku sugan maamulka Waqooyi Bari. Warbixinta ayaa sidoo kale sheegaysa in ku dhowaad 200 oo sarkaal loo dalacsiiyay maamulka Waqooyi Bari, gaar ahaan saraakiisha qaybta 26-aad oo la qorsheeyay in laga aasaaso maamulkaas. Tallaabooyinkan ayaa imanaya xilli ay socdaan qorshayaal la xiriira dhismaha iyo habaynta ciidamada maamulka Waqooyi Bari, iyadoo fasaxa mushaharka iyo dalacsiinta saraakiishu ay qayb ka yihiin isbeddellada lagu sameynayo qaab-dhismeedka ciidamada. Ilaa hadda ma jiro faahfaahin dheeraad ah oo laga bixiyay sababta rasmiga ah ee tallaabooyinkan iyo qorshaha guud ee qaybta 26-aad.

items.title: Ciidamada Dowladda oo Kaaraan ku Qabtay Gaari Siday Hub
items.description: Muqdisho – Ciidamada ammaanka dowladda Soomaaliya ayaa degmada Kaaraan ee magaalada Muqdisho ku qabtay gaari nooca Toyota Qooqan ah oo la sheegay inuu siday hub iyo rasaas badan. Gaariga ayaa la sheegay in ciidamada ammaanku ay markii hore ka shakiyeen, kaddibna ay istaajiyeen, iyagoo baaritaan ku sameeyay. Baaritaanka kaddib, waxaa la sheegay in gaariga laga helay 30 qori oo AK-47 ah iyo 10 qori oo nooca BKM-ka loo yaqaan Dabo-jeex ah. Wararka laga helayo dadka deegaanka ayaa sheegaya in gaariga iyo hubka lagu qabtay loo qaaday Madaxtooyada Soomaaliya, kaddib markii uu la wareegay Maslax oo ah taliyaha ciidamada Madaxtooyada. Warar kale ayaa sheegaya in hubka la qabtay uu leeyahay mas’uul ka tirsan dowladda Soomaaliya oo aan magaciisa la shaacin, iyadoo la sheegay in aan la doonayn in xogtiisa loo dusiyo warbaahinta. Dhanka kale, waxaa la sheegay in baaritaanno lagu bilaabay wadihii gaariga si loo ogaado halka uu hubka ka keenay iyo halka uu u waday. Gaariga ayaa lagu qabtay isgoyska Jiiro-Wacbuudhan ee degmada Kaaraan, halkaas oo muddo saacado ah uu xirnaa. Isgoyska ayaa markii dambe dib loo furay, iyadoo gaadiidka iyo dadweynuhu ay dib u isticmaali karaan waddada. Ilaa hadda ma jiro war rasmi ah oo ka soo baxay hay’adaha ammaanka dowladda oo faahfaahin dheeraad ah ka bixinaya dhacdadan iyo cidda iska leh hubka la qabtay.
