items.title: Four Years Too Late: Somalia Suddenly Discovers Meritocracy
items.description: By Ahmed A. Yusuf Four years after taking office, and with its mandate drawing to a close, the Federal Government of Somalia has suddenly discovered the virtues of meritocrac y . Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre has ordered federal ministries and government agencies to begin filling senior civil-service positions through open competition, with appointments supposedly based on competence, education, experience, leadership and performance. The first phase of the exercise is scheduled to begin on September 20 and will focus on departmental directors. The process is then expected to extend to director-general positions across government institutions. The announcement would ordinarily be welcomed as a long-overdue step toward building a professional state. But the timing is impossible to ignore. Why did a government that had four years to institutionalize merit-based recruitment wait until the closing stages of its mandate to announce that qualified Somalis should finally have an equal opportunity to compete for government jobs? That is the question many citizens are likely to ask. A functioning civil service cannot be built by issuing reform directives when a government’s term is nearly over. Meritocracy is supposed to be the operating principle of government—not an election-season promise. The extraordinary timing Prime Minister Hamza says the government has spent the past four years establishing the legal and institutional foundations for public-sector reform, including laws, policies, regulations and organizational structures governing government institutions and civil servants. He has now instructed the Civil Service Commission to oversee an open competitive process and ensure that qualified civil servants receive equal opportunities to compete for vacant positions. There is nothing controversial about that principle. What is controversial is the apparent gap between what the government is now promising and what critics say has characterized appointments during its tenure. The Hassan Sheikh Mohamud administration has faced persistent criticism over allegations of nepotism, political patronage, clan-based considerations and the concentration of important government positions among politically connected individuals. Such allegations should be assessed against actual appointment records rather than political rhetoric. But if the government genuinely intends to introduce a merit-based system, it should have little difficulty demonstrating how senior appointments were made over the preceding four years. That is where the public deserves transparency. Where was meritocracy before? The question is particularly uncomfortable because the principle being announced today is not a new constitutional invention. Somalia has been struggling for decades to establish a professional, politically neutral and competent public administration. Competitive recruitment is among the most basic requirements of such a system. Yet critics argue that under the current administration, access to senior state positions has too often been influenced by political relationships, family connections and clan considerations. The allegations extend beyond civilian ministries. The same questions have been raised about senior positions within the security and military establishment, where professionalism and competence should be even less negotiable. If family members and political allies of those in power are perceived to occupy influential positions throughout government and the security sector, then simply announcing an open competition for departmental directors at the end of the government’s mandate will inevitably invite skepticism. The public is entitled to ask whether this is genuine institutional reform—or an attempt to rewrite the government’s record before it leaves office. The corruption contradiction The announcement also comes at an extraordinary moment for Somalia’s international reputation. According to Transparency International’s 2025 Corruption Perceptions Index, Somalia scored just 9 out of 100, placing it among the countries with the lowest scores globally for perceived public-sector corruption. The index measures perceptions of public-sector corruption based on assessments by experts and businesspeople. Against that backdrop, the government cannot reasonably expect the public to be satisfied with declarations alone. A country struggling at the bottom of global corruption rankings needs institutions that are visibly transparent, independently accountable and resistant to political interference. It needs recruitment systems in which a highly qualified Somali with no political connections can compete on equal terms with someone who has access to the corridors of power. It needs a security establishment where promotion is determined by professional achievement rather than political loyalty or family connections. And it needs appointments that can survive public scrutiny. The family-and-patronage question Perhaps the most sensitive issue is whether the government is prepared to apply the same standards to its own political establishment. If meritocracy is now the principle, then it should apply universally. The public should be able to examine the qualifications and appointment processes of senior officials. It should be possible to determine whether relatives and close associates of senior political figures have received government positions, and under what procedures. If those appointments were made through transparent, competitive and lawful procedures, the government should have no reason to fear scrutiny. If they were not, the government should explain why. That is the essence of institutional accountability. A civil service is not a political reward system The danger of politicized recruitment goes far beyond individual appointments. When government jobs become rewards for political loyalty, institutions gradually lose their independence. Qualified professionals become discouraged. Competent officials may find themselves competing against people whose principal qualification is proximity to power. Eventually, the state itself suffers. The consequences are visible in weak institutions, poor service delivery, corruption, declining public confidence and an administrative culture in which personal connections can become more valuable than professional qualifications. Somalia cannot build a modern state on that foundation. The Prime Minister’s real test Prime Minister Hamza’s directive therefore creates an opportunity—but also a test. If the government is serious about meritocracy, it should publish the vacancies, qualifications, selection criteria and competitive procedures. It should make the process independently verifiable and ensure that unsuccessful candidates have appropriate avenues for appeal. Most importantly, the government should demonstrate that the rules apply equally to the politically powerful and the politically powerless. The public should not have to take another government promise on faith. After four years in office, citizens have every right to ask: Where was this merit-based system when the government first took power? Why is it being introduced now? How many senior positions were filled through genuine open competition during the past four years? How many appointments involved political, family or clan considerations? And perhaps the most important question of all: Will the same standards now being promised apply to the people closest to the centres of power? Somalia needs evidence, not slogans There is nothing wrong with a government deciding to professionalize its civil service. On the contrary, Somalia desperately needs a competent, accountable and politically neutral public administration. But after four years, the announcement inevitably raises eyebrows. A government cannot spend most of its mandate operating under one set of political realities and then, as its term approaches its end, present the introduction of competitive recruitment as though it were the beginning of a new era. The Somali public is more sophisticated than that. It understands the difference between reform announced and reform implemented. It understands that meritocracy cannot exist alongside unchecked patronage. And it understands that a professional government is measured not by the speeches of its leaders but by the transparency of its institutions. If the Hassan administration truly wants to leave behind a professional civil service, it has an opportunity to prove it. But after four years, the burden of proof is no longer on the public to believe the promise. It is on the government to demonstrate that the promise is real. Somalia has heard enough declarations about reform. Now it needs receipts. Ahmed A. items.title: Khaire Accuses Hassan Sheikh Government of Failure as Somalia’s Humanitarian Crisis Deepens
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN) — Millions of Somalis are facing hunger, displacement and a deepening humanitarian emergency while Somalia remains trapped in a political crisis over a presidency whose original constitutional mandate has expired. That contradiction has become the centerpiece of a blistering attack by former Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire, who says President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s government has spent too much political energy defending its hold on power and too little demonstrating that it can protect citizens facing one of the country’s most serious humanitarian crises. Khaire, a senior figure in the opposition Future Council, argues that Somalia’s leadership should be mobilizing around drought, food insecurity, displacement and the collapse of essential services rather than remaining consumed by constitutional disputes, electoral arrangements and political confrontation. His criticism comes as the United Nations estimates that 4.8 million people will need humanitarian assistance in Somalia in 2026, amid drought, conflict, displacement and severe humanitarian funding constraints. “4.8 million Somalis are today facing humanitarian hardship, and it is unfortunate that a government whose mandate has expired has no vision, plan or national agenda for rescuing these Somali people who urgently need assistance and relief,” Khaire said. The statement is more than another opposition attack on Villa Somalia. It captures the increasingly difficult question facing President Hassan Sheikh: what does political legitimacy mean when millions of citizens are struggling to survive while the country’s political institutions remain locked in dispute? Somalia’s political crisis has continued long after the expiration of the president’s original mandate, while constitutional amendments and electoral disagreements have produced competing interpretations of how the country should proceed. The resulting uncertainty has consumed much of the national political debate, even as humanitarian needs have continued to rise. A Government Consumed by Political Survival Khaire’s broader criticism is that Somalia’s humanitarian emergency has unfolded alongside a political crisis that has consumed much of the Federal Government’s attention. President Hassan Sheikh’s continued stay in office after the expiration of his original mandate has become one of the central disputes in Somali politics. Reuters reported in June that the president’s decision to remain in power after his mandate expired had contributed to violent clashes in Mogadishu between government forces and militias aligned with opposition politicians. The political dispute has also been complicated by constitutional amendments approved by Parliament in March that could delay elections and potentially extend the president’s tenure by one year. The changes were contested by opposition figures and constitutional experts, while the government defended its electoral and constitutional agenda. For Khaire, the consequence is a government increasingly preoccupied with political confrontation at precisely the moment when Somalia needs an administration focused on drought relief, food security, displacement, healthcare and economic recovery. That criticism is not limited to political rhetoric. The humanitarian system itself has warned that its capacity is shrinking as funding falls. The UN’s 2026 humanitarian plan sought $852 million to provide life-saving assistance, but humanitarian partners warned that funding shortages were already forcing reductions in operations at a time when needs remained extremely high. Four Years of Hassan Sheikh: Khaire’s Broader Indictment Khaire went beyond the immediate humanitarian crisis, accusing President Hassan Sheikh’s four years in office of being marked by what he described as lack of vision, poor planning, weak governance and corruption. He further accused the administration of political favoritism, misuse of national assets, displacement of vulnerable communities and failure to provide a coherent national development agenda. Those are political allegations made by an opposition leader, rather than independently established findings. The Federal Government has rejected similar criticisms and maintains that its political, constitutional and security programs are intended to strengthen Somalia’s state institutions. But Khaire’s argument goes to a larger question: what has the Hassan Sheikh presidency delivered after more than four years in power? The government can point to institutional reforms, constitutional changes, security operations and international partnerships. Its critics, however, argue that these initiatives have been overshadowed by political polarization, disputes with Federal Member States and an unresolved electoral crisis. The humanitarian situation provides another measure of the government’s performance. UN agencies have warned that drought, conflict, displacement and inadequate funding are combining to weaken livelihoods and essential services. UNICEF estimates that about 4.8 million people, including 3 million children, require humanitarian assistance in 2026, while nearly 1.85 million children under five are projected to suffer from wasting. The health system is also under severe pressure. UNICEF has warned that hundreds of health and nutrition facilities have already closed or are at risk of closure because of funding shortages. Reuters reported in August that 205 facilities had already shut down, while another 618 faced possible closure. These figures make the political debate more consequential. A government facing such an emergency cannot afford to treat humanitarian policy as a secondary issue. The Cost of Political Paralysis Khaire’s central accusation is therefore less about one failed policy than about priorities. While political leaders argue over constitutional authority and electoral arrangements, millions of Somalis are dealing with hunger, displacement, disease and the loss of livelihoods. The danger is that political paralysis becomes a multiplier of humanitarian suffering. A divided political leadership finds it harder to mobilize resources. A contested government struggles to build broad political consensus. Federal disputes complicate coordination with regional authorities. International partners become increasingly cautious about committing resources when political institutions are themselves disputed. Meanwhile, ordinary Somalis continue to bear the consequences. The United Nations has warned that the humanitarian response is operating at a critical moment, with reduced funding and diminished humanitarian presence even as needs remain high. For Khaire, that is evidence of a deeper failure of political leadership. His accusation is essentially that the government has spent too much political capital defending its position and too little demonstrating that it can provide a credible national response to the problems facing ordinary citizens. A Presidency Under Increasing Scrutiny Khaire’s intervention adds another layer to the growing political pressure surrounding President Hassan Sheikh. The president’s supporters argue that Somalia needs institutional reform, direct elections and stronger federal institutions. His opponents counter that constitutional and electoral changes cannot provide legitimacy if they are pursued without broad political consensus. The humanitarian crisis now adds another test. Can the government demonstrate that it can manage the country’s political transition while simultaneously responding effectively to drought, hunger, displacement and the collapse of essential services? That question matters because humanitarian emergencies eventually become political crises themselves. When families lose livestock, homes, access to water and livelihoods, desperation increases. When health facilities close, preventable illness becomes more dangerous. When young people see little economic future, migration and recruitment by armed groups can become more attractive. Somalia therefore cannot separate political stability from humanitarian security. The country’s ability to respond to drought and hunger is itself a measure of state capacity. The Question of Leadership Khaire’s attack ultimately returns Somalia to the question at the center of its political crisis: what should a government whose political legitimacy is disputed be doing with the authority it still exercises? For the opposition, the priority should be an agreed political transition, accompanied by an urgent national effort to protect vulnerable Somalis. For the government, the argument is different. It maintains that constitutional and institutional reforms are necessary to establish a more durable political system and that its electoral agenda is intended to move Somalia toward direct democratic participation. The disagreement will not be resolved through competing speeches. It will increasingly be judged by outcomes: whether the government can protect citizens from hunger, maintain essential health and nutrition services, reduce displacement, mobilize resources despite falling humanitarian funding, and resolve the political dispute that has left Somalia without a broadly accepted electoral settlement. For millions of Somalis facing hunger and displacement, the political argument in Mogadishu may seem distant. What matters to them is whether water arrives, whether food is available, whether children receive treatment and whether their families can survive another failed season. That is ultimately the harshest test of government performance. A government can defend its political legitimacy in Parliament and at international conferences, but legitimacy is also measured by what happens to citizens when they are most vulnerable. For Somalia’s millions in need, that test is already underway. items.title: CIRRO: Garoonka Berbera waxaan ugu magac darayaa Trump
items.description: Washington (Caasimada Online) — Madaxweynaha maamulka Somaliland, Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdullaahi Cirro ayaa soo jeediyay in garoonka diyaaradaha Berbera loogu magac daro Madaxweynaha Mareykanka Donald Trump, xilli uu Washington ka wado dadaal xooggan oo uu ku raadinayo aqoonsi Mareykan ah. Cirro ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in Trump lagu soo dhoweyn karo inuu dhismo Trump Tower ka hirgeliyo Hargeysa, isaga oo isku dayaya inuu maamulka Mareykanka tuso waxa Somaliland diyaar u tahay inay bixiso haddii xiriirka labada dhinac sare loo qaado. Hadalladan ayuu Cirro ku sheegay wareysi uu magaalada Washington ku siiyay warbaahinta Semafor , xilli uu booqasho ku joogo Mareykanka, isla markaana uu kulamo la leeyahay mas’uuliyiin iyo xubno ka tirsan Congress-ka. Waxa uu sheegay in hadafka ugu weyn uu yahay sidii Somaliland uga heli lahayd Mareykanka aqoonsi, balse dhinacyadu sidoo kale ka wada shaqeyn karaan ganacsi, maalgashi iyo iskaashi amni inta arrinta aqoonsiga laga gaarayo go’aan. Cirro ayaa sheegay in Somaliland ay Mareykanka u soo bandhigi karto dekedda Berbera, kheyraadka dabiiciga ah iyo xarumo kale oo istiraatiiji ah. “Waxba bilaash kuma bixinayno,” ayuu yiri Cirro, isaga oo tilmaamay in heshiis kasta uu ku xirnaan doono waxa dhinaca kale lagu beddelanayo. Saldhig militari Cirro ayaa sheegay inuusan meesha ka saarayn in mustaqbalka Mareykanka, Israel ama dalal kale ay helaan marin militari oo ballaaran ama heshiis saldhig. Arrintaas ayuu ku tilmaamay mid “wada-xaajood” ku xiran. “Meesha kama saarayo,” ayuu yiri, isagoo sheegay in heshiis kasta uu ku xirnaan doono waxa Somaliland beddelkeeda ka hesho, oo ay ka mid noqon karaan taageero amni iyo xoojinta ciidamadeeda. Berbera ayaa ku taalla meel muhiim ah oo ku dhow marin-biyoodka Bab al-Mandab, oo isku xira Badda Cas iyo Badweynta Hindiya, waxaana muhiimaddeeda sare u qaaday khataraha amni iyo weerarrada sanadihii dambe ka dhacay marin-biyoodka Badda Cas. Mareykanka ayaa hore xiriir dhinaca ammaanka iyo tababarka ah ula lahaa Somaliland, balse ma laha saldhig militari oo halkaas ku yaalla, sida ay sheegtay Semafor . Israel ayaa bishii Diseembar 2025 noqotay dalkii ugu horreeyay ee xubin ka ah Qaramada Midoobay ee si rasmi ah u aqoonsada Somaliland, tallaabadaas oo dowladda Soomaaliya si adag u diidday, kuna tilmaantay xadgudub ka dhan ah madax-bannaanida iyo midnimada dalka. Midowga Afrika iyo dalal kale ayaa sidoo kale taageeray midnimada Soomaaliya. Tan iyo markaas, maamulka Somaliland ayaa sare u qaaday dadaalkiisa uu ku doonayo in dalal kale ay raacaan Israel, waxaana Cirro uu Mareykanka ku tilmaamay bartilmaameedka ugu muhiimsan ee ololahaas. Waxa uu xusay dekedda iyo aagga ganacsiga xorta ah ee Berbera, xeeb dhererkeedu gaarayo qiyaastii 850 kiiloomitir, kalluumeysiga, iyo shidaal, gaas iyo macdano uu sheegay inay jiri karaan. Cirro ayaa sheegay in markii uu noqday guddoomiyaha baarlamaanka sanadkii 2005 miisaaniyadda Somaliland ay ka yareyd $50 milyan, halka hadda ay gaartay qiyaastii $500 milyan sanadkii. Waxa uu sheegay in Somaliland ay toban sano gudahood noqon karto meel “aad u hodan ah” haddii la horumariyo dhaqaalaha badda iyo kheyraadka kale. Cirro ayaa xitaa saadaaliyay in miisaaniyadda sanadlaha ah mustaqbalka gaari karto $3 bilyan ilaa $4 bilyan haddii kheyraadkaas la horumariyo. Somaliland ayaa muddo dheer ku doodi jirtay arrimo taariikhi ah iyo kuwo siyaasadeed marka ay raadineyso aqoonsi, balse hadallada Cirro waxay muujinayaan in maamulkiisu hadda diiradda saarayo waxa uu si toos ah ugu beddeli karo aqoonsigaas. Waxa uu Washington u bandhigayaa marin istiraatiiji ah, deked, kheyraad dabiici ah iyo maalgashi suurtagal ah. Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa gebi ahaanba diiddan mowqifkaas, waxayna Somaliland u aragtaa qeyb ka mid ah Soomaaliya. Muqdisho waxay sidoo kale u aragtaa Berbera, xeebaha iyo kheyraadka ku jira dhulkaas inay qeyb ka yihiin dhulka iyo hantida Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya. Taasi waxay ka dhigeysaa dalabyada Cirro kuwo caqabado siyaasadeed iyo mid sharci ah wajahaya ka hor inta aysan dowlad ama shirkad shisheeye gelin heshiis weyn. items.title: Warbixin kooban oo madaxweyne Cirro ka biciyay socdaalkiisa
items.description: Intii aan ku sugnaa Washington, D.C., waxaan kulamo muhiim ah la yeeshay khubaro iyo masuuliyiin sare oo ka tirsan Atlantic Council iyo Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD). Kulamadan waxa aan kaga wada hadalnay danaha istiraatiijiga ah ee Somaliland iyo Maraykanka, amniga Badda Cas iyo Gacanka Cadmeed, xasilloonida Geeska Afrika, ilaalinta marin-biyoodyada muhiimka u ah ganacsiga caalamiga ah, iyo sidii loo dhisi lahaa iskaashi qoto dheer oo waara oo dhex mara labada dal. Waxaan si gaar ah u adkeeyey in Somaliland muddo ka badan saddex iyo soddon sannadood ay dhisaysay dawladnimo ku salaysan rabitaanka shacabka, dimuqraadiyad, doorashooyin xor ah iyo kala-guur siyaasadeed oo nabdoon. Waayo-aragnimadeennu waxay caddeyn u tahay in dimuqraadiyadda, dawladnimada iyo xasilloonidu ay yihiin tiirar isku xidhan oo muhiim u ah nabadda iyo horumarka gobolka. Waxaan sidoo kale iftiimiyey muhiimadda istiraatiijiga ah ee Somaliland iyo Dekedda Berbera, oo ku taalla mid ka mid ah marin-biyoodyada ugu muhiimsan dunida. Somaliland waxay diyaar u tahay inay Maraykanka iyo saaxiibbadiisa kala shaqayso amniga badda, xasilloonida gobolka, ganacsiga iyo maalgashiga. Somaliland maanta waxay Washington la wadaagaysaa farriin cad: waxaan nahay dal dimuqraadi ah, xasilloon oo leh hay’ado shaqaynaya, kuna yaalla goob istiraatiiji ah; waxaanan diyaar u nahay iskaashi ku dhisan kalsooni, dano wadaag iyo mas’uuliyad wadajir ah.

items.title: DF oo war kasoo saartay xaaladda markabka M/V JACUAR
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Wasaaradda Dekedaha iyo Gaadiidka Badda ee Soomaaliya ayaa faahfaahin ka bixisay xaaladda markabka xamuulka ah ee M/V JACUAR (IMO 9181821), kaas oo ay sheegtay inuu caariyay kaddib markii ay cilad biyo-gal ah ka dhacday qayb ka mid ah markabka gudihiisa. Wasaaradda ayaa sheegtay in markabka uu watay calanka Saint Kitts and Nevis, isla markaana uu ka soo shiraacday Nacala Port ee Mozambique, isagoo ku sii jeeday Adabiya Port ee dalka Masar. Sida lagu sheegay war-saxaafadeedka wasaaradda, markabka ayaa siday qiyaastii 7,007.73 tan oo badeeco ah, waxaana saarnaa 18 shaqaale ah oo kasoo kala jeeda dalalka Hindiya, Suuriya iyo Masar. Wasaaradda Dekedaha iyo Gaadiidka Badda ayaa sheegtay inay si dhow ula socoto xaaladda markabka, iyadoo kaashanaysa hay’adaha kale ee ay khusayso. Wasaaraddu waxay sidoo kale sheegtay inay waddo gurmad iyo isku-duwidda hawlaha samatabixinta, iyadoo mudnaanta la siinayo badbaadada shaqaalaha saaran markabka iyo in si habsami leh loo maareeyo xaaladda. Wasaaradda ayaa intaas ku dartay inay bulshada iyo dhammaan dhinacyada ay khusayso la wadaagi doonto wixii war ah ee kasoo kordha xaaladda markabka. Bayaanka wasaaradda ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli ay hay’adaha dowladda Soomaaliya si dhow ula socdaan xaaladda markabka iyo hawlaha gurmadka ee socda. items.title: AJC was honored to meet with Somaliland President
items.description: AJC was honored to meet with Somaliland President (@PresidencySL_) Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, Foreign Minister Abdirahman Dahir Adan, Minister of Defense Mohamed Yusuf Ali Ahmed, Speaker of Parliament Yasin Haji Mohamoud, and other senior Somaliland leaders to discuss developments in the Horn of Africa, regional security, the democratic country’s strategic importance, and Somaliland’s growing relationship with Israel. The discussion also explored the significance of Israel being the first UN member state to officially recognize Somaliland as an independent and sovereign state, as well as opportunities for deeper cooperation between Somaliland and Israel. AJC’s Center for a New Middle East is committed to building trusted partnerships with leaders around the world and fostering dialogue on the issues shaping Israel, the Middle East, and beyond. AJC

items.title: Madaxweyne Firdhiye oo booqday Xarunta Taliska Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka
items.description: Madaxweynaha Maamulka Waqooyi Bari, Cabdiqaadir Axmed Aw-Cali (Firdhiye) ayaa Khamiistan booqday Xarunta Taliska Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka ee Magaalada Muqdisho. Taliyaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, General Ibraahim Maxamed Maxamuud ayaa taliska ku soo dhaweeyay Madaxweynaha Waqooyi Bari, sida uu Taliyuhu ku sheegay war qoraal ah. Taliyaha ayaa tilmaamay in ay ka wada hadleen xaaladda guud ee amniga dalka, gaar ahaan buu yiri xoojinta amniga iyo nabadgelyada deegaanada Waqooyi Bari Somaliya. “Waxaan sidoo kale ka wada hadalnay, sidii loo laba jibaari lahaa dadaalada lagu xaqiijinayo amniga, xasilloonida iyo badqabka shacabka iyo sidii loo sii xoojin lahaa wada-shaqaynta Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, hay’adaha amniga iyo maamulka deegaanka.” Ayuu Taliyaha ku sheegay warka. Taliyaha oo warkan ku daabacay bartiisa xiriirka bulshada ayaa intaasi ku daray “Waxaan adkeynay muhiimadda ay leedahay iskaashi iyo isku-duubni lagu xaqiijinayo nabadda iyo amniga guud ee dalka.” Taliyaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka ayaa waxaa kulanka ku wehlinayay Taliyaha Ciidanka Badda, Admiral Cabdiwahaab Cabdullaahi Cumar, Taliyaha Taliska Taakuleynta ee Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, General Maxamed Maxamuud Xasan (Garabey) iyo Taliyaha Taliska Tababarada iyo Doctrine-ka ee Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, General Axmed Ciise Axmed.

items.title: Iiraan oo Trump iyo Netanyahu ku xirtay furitaanka Hormuz
items.description: Tehran (Caasimada Online) – Iiraan ayaa sheegtay inaysan dib u furi doonin Marinka Hormuz ilaa Madaxweynaha Mareykanka Donald Trump iyo Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Israa’iil Benjamin Netanyahu xilalka laga qaado Mohammad Baqer Zolqadr oo ah la-taliyaha siyaasadeed ee Hoggaamiyaha Jamhuuriyadda Islaamiga ah ee Iiraan ayaa sheegay in go’aanka Tehran uu qayb ka yahay jawaabta ay ka bixinayso dagaalka iyo weerarrada ay sheegtay in loo geystay dalkeeda. Zolqadr ayaa tilmaamay in Iiraan ay sii wadi doonto iska-caabbinta Mareykanka iyo Israa’iil, isagoo xiritaanka Marin-biyoodka Hormuz oo ah mid kamid ah marinnada ugu muhiimsan ee maraakiibta shidaalka ee dunida uu ku tilmaamay waxa uu ugu yeeray “marxaladda koowaad ee aargoosiga shacabka Iiraan”. Hadallada mas’uulkan ka tirsan dowladda Iiraan ayaa xoojinaya muhiimadda istiraatiijiga ah ee uu leeyahay Marin-biyoodka Hormuz, kaas oo isku xira Gacanka Faaris iyo Gacanka Cumaan, isla markaana ah marin ay maraan tiro badan oo maraakiib ah oo qaada shidaalka iyo gaaska dabiiciga ah. Xiisadda ka taagan marinka ayaa si gaar ah walaac ugu abuurtay suuqyada tamarta, maadaama carqalad ku timaadda isu-socodka maraakiibta halkaas ay saameyn ku yeelan karto dhoofinta shidaalka ee dalalka Khaliijka iyo silsiladaha sahayda tamarta ee caalamka. Zolqadr ayaa sidoo kale xusay dadkii lagu dilay weerarradii ka dhacay Minab iyo Lamerd iyo xubno ka tirsan ciidamada milatariga Iiraan oo la dilay, isagoo sheegay in Tehran ay doonayso inay uga aargoosato. Hadalladan ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli Hormuz uu noqday meel si weyn diiradda loogu hayo marka laga hadlayo xiisadda u dhexeysa Iiraan, Mareykanka iyo Israa’iil, iyadoo dhaq-dhaqaaq kasta oo militari ama amni oo halkaas ka dhaca uu saameyn ku yeelan karo maraakiibta ganacsiga. Iiraan ayaa muddo dheer awood u lahayd inay saameyn ku yeelato isu-socodka maraakiibta ee marinkan, waxaana Hormuz loo arkaa marin muhiim u ah dhaqaalaha caalamka, maadaama dalal badan oo dhoofiya shidaalka ay isticmaalaan si ay wax-soo-saarkooda ugu gaarsiiyaan suuqyada caalamka. Haddii xaaladda marinku sii adkaato, saameynta ugu weyn waxay noqon kartaa mid dhaqaale iyo amni, gaar ahaan dhinaca maraakiibta ganacsiga, qiimaha tamarta iyo waddamada ku tiirsan shidaalka kasoo baxa gobolka. Si kastaba, hadalka Zolqadr waa mowqif uu sheegay mas’uul Iiraani ah, mana cadda in shuruuddani ay tahay go’aan rasmi ah oo ay si wadajir ah u qaateen dhammaan hay’adaha go’aan-qaadashada Iiraan. Xiisadda Hormuz ayaa sidaas darteed weli ah mid si dhow loola socdo, iyadoo indhaha caalamku ku wajahan yihiin tallaabooyinka ay qaadi doonaan Iiraan, Mareykanka iyo Israa’iil iyo waxa ay xaaladdu ka beddeli karto isu-socodka maraakiibta iyo suuqyada tamarta. items.title: Soomaaliya oo si rasmi ah ula wareegtay mas’uuliyadda…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Maanta waa maalin taariikhi ah oo Soomaaliya ay si rasmi ah u soo afjartay marxalad dheer oo ku saabsan ilaalinta iyo horumarinta xuquuqul insaanka, iyadoo si buuxda ula wareegtay mas’uuliyadda qaran ee xuquuqul insaanka. Tani waxay ka dhigan tahay in si rasmi ah loo soo gabagabeeyey hawshii Xafiiska Xuquuqul Insaanka Qaramada Midoobay ee Soomaaliya, oo hoos imaan jiray UNTMIS. Geeddi-socodkan taariikhiga ah ayaa ka soo bilowday Muqdisho, isagoo soo maray dadaallo iyo wada-hadallo heer caalami ah oo ka dhacay Geneva iyo New York, kuwaas oo ay hormuud u ahayd Wasiir Amb. Khadiija Maxamed Al-Makhzoumi, oo ay garab taagnaayeen hawl-wadeennada kala duwan ee wasaaradda, sida ay sheegtay Wasaaradda Qoyska iyo Horumarinta Xuquuqul Insaanka. Dadaalka wadajirka ah ee hay’adaha dowladda iyo khubarada Soomaaliyeed wuxuu horseeday in la gaaro himilo qaran oo muddo dheer laga shaqeynayay, taas oo ah in Soomaaliya ay si buuxda u yeelato lahaanshaha iyo hoggaaminta ajandaha xuquuqul insaanka ee dalkeeda. “Guushan waxay ka dhalatay qorsheyn joogto ah, go’aan siyaasadeed, wada-hadal miro-dhal ah iyo dadaal qaran oo aan kala go’ lahayn,” ayay sheegtay Wasaaradda Qoyska iyo Horumarinta Xuquuqul Insaanka. Sidoo kale, waxaa saldhig u ahaa go’aannada Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya, horumarradii Soomaaliya ka gaartay Golaha Xuquuqul Insaanka Qaramada Midoobay iyo xoojinta Guddiga Madaxa-bannaan ee Xuquuqul Insaanka Qaranka Soomaaliya. Shirweynihii Qaran ee Xuquuqul Insaanka ee Maarso 2025 ayaa sidoo kale door muhiim ah ka qaatay dhismaha aragti qaran oo ku salaysan hannaan ay Soomaaliya iyadu leedahay, hoggaamiso, kana mas’uul tahay. Xiritaanka Xafiiska Xuquuqul Insaanka Qaramada Midoobay ee Soomaaliya ma aha dhammaadka ilaalinta xuquuqul insaanka, balse waa bilowga marxalad cusub, sida ay sheegtay wasaaradda. “Waa marxalad ay hay’adaha Soomaaliyeed si toos ah u qaadanayaan mas’uuliyadda ilaalinta, horumarinta iyo u doodista xuquuqul insaanka muwaadiniinta Soomaaliyeed.” Soomaaliya waxay maanta muujisay in hay’adaha qaranku ay gaareen heer ay si madax-bannaan ugu hoggaamin karaan ajandaha xuquuqul insaanka, iyadoo iskaashiga iyo taageerada caalamiga ah loo adeegsanayo xoojinta awoodda qaranka, halkii ay beddeli lahaayeen mas’uuliyadda hay’adaha Soomaaliyeed. “Geeddigii dheeraa maanta wuxuu gaaray guul. Soomaaliya waxay si buuxda ula wareegtay mas’uuliyadda xuquuqul insaankeeda. Bog taariikhi ah ayaa xirmay, cutub cusubna waa furmay: cutub ay Soomaaliya iyadu leedahay, iyadu hoggaaminayso, iyaduna ka mas’uul tahay.” Si kastaba, Soomaaliya ayaa maanta furaysa albaab cusub oo ku dhisan lahaanshaha qaran, hay’ado awood leh, isla-xisaabtan, sharciyad iyo ilaalinta xuquuqda muwaadiniinta. Mas’uuliyadda cusub ayaa u baahan dadaal joogto ah, hoggaan adag iyo in hay’adaha Soomaaliyeed ay si buuxda u gutaan waajibaadka dastuuriga ah, qaran iyo kuwa caalamiga ah ee xuquuqul insaanka. items.title: Somaliland president faces backlash after tense Washington interview
items.description: WASHINGTON (Somaliguardian) — Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi Irro arrived in Washington with a familiar message: his administration wants the United States to recognise Somaliland and sees the territory’s strategic position on the Gulf of Aden as an opportunity for a deeper American partnership. The visit offered an unusually prominent platform for that argument. On September 14, Mr Irro appeared at the Hudson Institute for a discussion titled Somaliland as a Strategic Partner in the Horn of Africa , followed by a fireside conversation with Hudson senior fellow Joshua Meservey. The event examined Somaliland’s potential role as an economic and security partner for the United States. But portions of the discussion soon attracted attention for a different reason. Clips circulating online focused on moments in which Mr Irro laughed, hesitated or gave brief answers to questions concerning Somaliland’s mineral resources and regional security. The resulting criticism has raised a broader question: can Somaliland translate its strategic advantages into a sufficiently clear case for why Washington should change its longstanding position on the territory’s status? A minerals question becomes a political moment One of the most widely discussed exchanges concerned critical minerals. Asked about resources Somaliland could potentially offer American companies, Mr Irro replied: “I’m not a geologist.” He then laughed and added: “I don’t know… maybe everything.” The exchange was brief, but the subject was not. Critical minerals have become an increasingly important component of international competition over supply chains, advanced manufacturing and national security. For Somaliland, mineral resources form part of a broader economic proposition that Hargeisa is putting before potential foreign partners. Yet there is a significant difference between geological potential and commercially established deposits. A more detailed discussion could have addressed what Somaliland has already identified, what remains to be explored and what investment opportunities could realistically be developed. Instead, the answer became one of the most circulated moments from the Washington event. That is particularly notable because Mr Irro has subsequently presented a much more expansive economic proposition to the United States. In an interview with Semafor, he said Somaliland could offer American investors access to its facilities and mineral resources, while leaving open the possibility of expanded military access. “We are not giving anything for free,” Mr Irro told the publication. His argument was that economic and strategic cooperation should produce reciprocal benefits. That represents an important evolution in Somaliland’s diplomatic pitch. The campaign is no longer based only on the territory’s historical claim to independence. It is increasingly framed around what Somaliland can offer Washington. From recognition to strategic partnership The central issue remains recognition. Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991 after the collapse of the Somali state and years of conflict. It has since maintained its own government, security institutions and currency, while Somalia continues to regard the territory as part of its sovereign territory. The historical argument is complicated by Somaliland’s brief independence in 1960. The former British Somaliland became independent on June 26 that year and joined the former Italian-administered territory of Somalia on July 1 to form the Somali Republic. The union later became deeply troubled, particularly during the rule of President Mohamed Siad Barre. After years of repression and conflict, Somaliland declared that it was restoring its independence in 1991. Its government argues that decades of separate political administration justify international recognition. Somalia rejects that position and continues to defend the country’s territorial integrity. Those competing claims form the backdrop to virtually every diplomatic conversation about Somaliland. At the Hudson Institute, Mr Irro attempted to distinguish Somaliland’s practical political reality from its formal international status. “Practically [Somaliland] is not part of Somalia,” he said. He also described Somaliland as theoretically part of Somalia. The distinction reflects the central paradox of Somaliland’s position: it functions as a separate political entity but remains largely outside the international system of sovereign states. For Washington, therefore, recognition would represent more than an acknowledgement of conditions on the ground. It would constitute a significant change in diplomatic policy. The Sudan exchange Another moment attracting attention involved Sudan. The question gave Mr Irro an opportunity to discuss the wider regional security environment and Somaliland’s relationship with conflicts across the Horn of Africa. Instead, he described Sudan as too far away before the discussion moved on. The exchange drew criticism because geography is one of Somaliland’s principal arguments for greater international attention. Somaliland lies along the Gulf of Aden, close to the maritime route leading towards the Bab el-Mandeb, the narrow passage connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden. That location places the territory near one of the world’s most strategically sensitive maritime corridors. For Washington, the significance is potentially practical. Berbera could offer logistical and commercial opportunities for a country seeking stronger relationships across the Horn of Africa and the wider Red Sea region. For Hargeisa, the geography is therefore not simply a geographic fact. It is part of the diplomatic argument. Berbera at the centre of Somaliland’s offer Berbera has become the clearest expression of that strategy. The port gives Somaliland access to major maritime routes and has become an important component of the territory’s ambitions to develop trade and foreign investment. Mr Irro is now linking that economic proposition directly to his campaign for recognition. Semafor reported that he is offering US investors access to Somaliland’s port and mineral resources while signalling that future military access could also be negotiated. That does not amount to an announcement of a new American military base. Rather, Mr Irro has indicated that Somaliland is prepared to discuss expanded access if the arrangement produces sufficient benefits for the territory. The distinction is important. The proposal is not simply about where the United States might operate. It is about whether Somaliland can persuade Washington that a closer relationship would serve American economic and security interests while also advancing Somaliland’s quest for recognition. Israel has changed the equation The diplomatic landscape shifted significantly in December 2025, when Israel became the first UN member state to formally recognise Somaliland as an independent and sovereign state. The decision was announced by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on December 26, with both sides signing a declaration of mutual recognition. Israel said it intended to cooperate with Somaliland in areas including agriculture, health, technology and economic development. Somalia condemned the move as a violation of its sovereignty. The African Union also rejected the recognition and reaffirmed its support for Somalia’s territorial integrity. For Somaliland, however, the Israeli decision represented a diplomatic breakthrough. For the first time since its 1991 declaration of independence, a UN member state had formally recognised its sovereignty. That gave Hargeisa something it had previously lacked: a concrete example that international recognition was no longer purely theoretical. But Israel’s decision did not automatically change US policy. Washington has not followed Israel in recognising Somaliland. That leaves Somaliland facing a more difficult diplomatic task: converting the Israeli breakthrough into wider international support without assuming that other governments will reach the same conclusion. Why Washington matters most Mr Irro’s current strategy appears increasingly designed around that challenge. His message to American policymakers is that Somaliland can provide more than a historical argument. It can offer access to a strategically positioned port. It can open opportunities for American investment. It can potentially contribute to regional security. And it can serve as a partner at a time when instability around the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden has increased the strategic value of locations along those waterways. Semafor reported that Mr Irro described the United States as the “big fish” Somaliland wants to pursue and argued that earlier recognition would be preferable. That approach reflects a more transactional diplomatic pitch. Rather than asking Washington simply to recognise Somaliland because of its history or political development, Hargeisa is asking what a formal relationship could deliver for the United States. That proposition, however, creates another set of questions. What precisely would Washington gain? How significant are Somaliland’s proven natural resources? What would expanded military access actually involve? How would recognition affect US relations with Somalia? And would the strategic benefits outweigh the diplomatic consequences? Even Somaliland’s supporters see a messaging problem The criticism following the Hudson event has not come exclusively from opponents of Somaliland’s independence claim. Cameron Hudson, a former US intelligence official who has worked extensively on African affairs, criticised Mr Irro’s performance on social media. Other observers also questioned whether the president had made the most of the opportunity. More significantly, Joshua Meservey himself subsequently said Somaliland had failed to make a consistent case for why recognition was necessary. His comments followed the Hudson Institute discussion he had moderated with Mr Irro. That assessment is particularly notable because Meservey has previously argued publicly that Washington should give Somaliland’s case serious consideration. His criticism therefore points to a question of diplomatic effectiveness rather than simply disagreement over Somaliland’s desired outcome. The challenge for Hargeisa is not merely obtaining attention in Washington. It is making the argument in terms that American policymakers can connect directly to US interests. The wider dispute remains unresolved Somaliland’s campaign ultimately rests on several interconnected claims. It argues that decades of separate administration have produced a political reality distinct from Somalia. It points to its location beside the Gulf of Aden and near the Bab el-Mandeb. It highlights Berbera as a potential commercial and strategic hub. It offers investment opportunities in infrastructure and natural resources. And it argues that recognition would formalise an existing political reality rather than create a new one. Somalia sees the matter differently. Mogadishu regards Somaliland’s territory, coastline, ports and natural resources as part of Somalia and rejects unilateral recognition of the territory by foreign states. That disagreement gives the US decision a regional dimension. Recognition would not take place in isolation from Somalia’s objections or from the broader African concern over territorial integrity. Israel’s decision has already demonstrated how consequential the issue can become. A campaign entering a new phase The Hudson Institute appearance was therefore more than an awkward Washington interview. It exposed the central challenge facing Somaliland’s recognition campaign at a moment when the stakes have increased. Israel has broken the previous pattern by recognising Somaliland. Berbera has become increasingly important to Hargeisa’s economic and strategic messaging. The United States is being offered a wider menu of investment and security cooperation. And Somaliland’s leadership is now attempting to persuade Washington that recognition would be useful not only to Somaliland but also to American interests. That is a considerably more demanding argument than simply asking the world to acknowledge Somaliland’s separate political existence. For President Irro, the task ahead is to connect history, geography, economics and security into a single, concrete proposition for Washington. The question is no longer simply whether Somaliland wants recognition. It is whether the case can be made clearly enough — and with enough demonstrable strategic value — for the United States to consider changing its policy. Contact us: info@somaliguardian.com

Those competing claims form the backdrop to virtually every diplomatic conversation about Somaliland. At the Hudson Institute, Mr Irro attempted to distinguish Somaliland’s practical political reality from its formal international status. “Practically [Somaliland] is not part of Somalia,” he said. He also described Somaliland as theoretically part of Somalia. The distinction reflects the central paradox of Somaliland’s position: it functions as a separate political entity but remains largely outside the international system of sovereign states. For Washington, therefore, recognition would represent more than an acknowledgement of conditions on the ground. It would constitute a significant change in diplomatic policy. The Sudan exchange Another moment attracting attention involved Sudan. The question gave Mr Irro an opportunity to discuss the wider regional security environment and Somaliland’s relationship with conflicts across the Horn of Africa. Instead, he described Sudan as too far away before the discussion moved on. The exchange drew criticism because geography is one of Somaliland’s principal arguments for greater international attention. Somaliland lies along the Gulf of Aden, close to the maritime route leading towards the Bab el-Mandeb, the narrow passage connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden. That location places the territory near one of the world’s most strategically sensitive maritime corridors. For Washington, the significance is potentially practical. Berbera could offer logistical and commercial opportunities for a country seeking stronger relationships across the Horn of Africa and the wider Red Sea region. For Hargeisa, the geography is therefore not simply a geographic fact. It is part of the diplomatic argument. Berbera at the centre of Somaliland’s offer Berbera has become the clearest expression of that strategy. The port gives Somaliland access to major maritime routes and has become an important component of the territory’s ambitions to develop trade and foreign investment. Mr Irro is now linking that economic proposition directly to his campaign for recognition. Semafor reported that he is offering US investors access to Somaliland’s port and mineral resources while signalling that future military access could also be negotiated. That does not amount to an announcement of a new American military base. Rather, Mr Irro has indicated that Somaliland is prepared to discuss expanded access if the arrangement produces sufficient benefits for the territory. The distinction is important. The proposal is not simply about where the United States might operate. It is about whether Somaliland can persuade Washington that a closer relationship would serve American economic and security interests while also advancing Somaliland’s quest for recognition. Israel has changed the equation The diplomatic landscape shifted significantly in December 2025, when Israel became the first UN member state to formally recognise Somaliland as an independent and sovereign state. The decision was announced by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on December 26, with both sides signing a declaration of mutual recognition. Israel said it intended to cooperate with Somaliland in areas including agriculture, health, technology and economic development. Somalia condemned the move as a violation of its sovereignty. The African Union also rejected the recognition and reaffirmed its support for Somalia’s territorial integrity. For Somaliland, however, the Israeli decision represented a diplomatic breakthrough. For the first time since its 1991 declaration of independence, a UN member state had formally recognised its sovereignty. That gave Hargeisa something it had previously lacked: a concrete example that international recognition was no longer purely theoretical. But Israel’s decision did not automatically change US policy. Washington has not followed Israel in recognising Somaliland. That leaves Somaliland facing a more difficult diplomatic task: converting the Israeli breakthrough into wider international support without assuming that other governments will reach the same conclusion. Why Washington matters most Mr Irro’s current strategy appears increasingly designed around that challenge. His message to American policymakers is that Somaliland can provide more than a historical argument. It can offer access to a strategically positioned port. It can open opportunities for American investment. It can potentially contribute to regional security. And it can serve as a partner at a time when instability around the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden has increased the strategic value of locations along those waterways. Semafor reported that Mr Irro described the United States as the “big fish” Somaliland wants to pursue and argued that earlier recognition would be preferable. That approach reflects a more transactional diplomatic pitch. Rather than asking Washington simply to recognise Somaliland because of its history or political development, Hargeisa is asking what a formal relationship could deliver for the United States. That proposition, however, creates another set of questions. What precisely would Washington gain? How significant are Somaliland’s proven natural resources? What would expanded military access actually involve? How would recognition affect US relations with Somalia? And would the strategic benefits outweigh the diplomatic consequences? Even Somaliland’s supporters see a messaging problem The criticism following the Hudson event has not come exclusively from opponents of Somaliland’s independence claim. Cameron Hudson, a former US intelligence official who has worked extensively on African affairs, criticised Mr Irro’s performance on social media. Other observers also questioned whether the president had made the most of the opportunity. More significantly, Joshua Meservey himself subsequently said Somaliland had failed to make a consistent case for why recognition was necessary. His comments followed the Hudson Institute discussion he had moderated with Mr Irro. That assessment is particularly notable because Meservey has previously argued publicly that Washington should give Somaliland’s case serious consideration. His criticism therefore points to a question of diplomatic effectiveness rather than simply disagreement over Somaliland’s desired outcome. The challenge for Hargeisa is not merely obtaining attention in Washington. It is making the argument in terms that American policymakers can connect directly to US interests. The wider dispute remains unresolved Somaliland’s campaign ultimately rests on several interconnected claims. It argues that decades of separate administration have produced a political reality distinct from Somalia. It points to its location beside the Gulf of Aden and near the Bab el-Mandeb. It highlights Berbera as a potential commercial and strategic hub. It offers investment opportunities in infrastructure and natural resources. And it argues that recognition would formalise an existing political reality rather than create a new one. Somalia sees the matter differently. Mogadishu regards Somaliland’s territory, coastline, ports and natural resources as part of Somalia and rejects unilateral recognition of the territory by foreign states. That disagreement gives the US decision a regional dimension. Recognition would not take place in isolation from Somalia’s objections or from the broader African concern over territorial integrity. Israel’s decision has already demonstrated how consequential the issue can become. A campaign entering a new phase The Hudson Institute appearance was therefore more than an awkward Washington interview. It exposed the central challenge facing Somaliland’s recognition campaign at a moment when the stakes have increased. Israel has broken the previous pattern by recognising Somaliland. Berbera has become increasingly important to Hargeisa’s economic and strategic messaging. The United States is being offered a wider menu of investment and security cooperation. And Somaliland’s leadership is now attempting to persuade Washington that recognition would be useful not only to Somaliland but also to American interests. That is a considerably more demanding argument than simply asking the world to acknowledge Somaliland’s separate political existence. For President Irro, the task ahead is to connect history, geography, economics and security into a single, concrete proposition for Washington. The question is no longer simply whether Somaliland wants recognition. It is whether the case can be made clearly enough — and with enough demonstrable strategic value — for the United States to consider changing its policy. Contact us: info@somaliguardian.com

items.title: WAR DEG DEG AH: Markab Xamuul ah oo kusoo caariyay Xeebaha Soomaaliya
items.description: Muqdisho, 17 Sebteembar 2026: Wasaaradda Dekedaha iyo Gaadiidka Badda ee Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa xaqiijisay in markabka xamuulka qaada ee M/V JACUAR (IMO 9181821) uu ku caariyay xeebaha Soomaaliya, kaddib markii ay biyo galeen qeyb ka mid ah markabka. Markabka oo watay calanka Saint Kitts and Nevis ayaa ka soo baxay Dekedda Nacala ee dalka Mozambique, isagoo ku sii jeeday Dekedda Adabiya ee dalka Masar. Markabka ayaa siday ku dhowaad 7,007.73 tan oo xamuul ah. Waxaa markabka saarnaa 18 shaqaale ah, kuwaas oo u kala dhashay Hindiya, Suuriya iyo Masar. Wasaaradda Dekedaha iyo Gaadiidka Badda ayaa sheegtay inay si dhow ula socoto xaaladda markabka, iyadoo la kaashanaysa hay’adaha ay khusayso, isla markaana la isku dubbaridayo howlaha gurmadka iyo samatabbixinta si loo xaqiijiyo badbaadada shaqaalaha markabka. Wasaaraddu waxay sheegtay inay sii wadi doonto wargelinta shacabka iyo dhinacyada ay khusayso, iyadoo la bixin doono xog cusub marka xaaladdu isbeddesho.

items.title: Soomaaliya oo soo gebagabeysay hawshii Xafiiska Xuquuqul Insaanka Qaramada Midoobay
items.description: Muqdisho, Soomaaliya — 17 Sebteembar 2026: Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa maanta si rasmi ah u soo gabagabeysay hawshii Xafiiska Arrimaha Xuquuqul Insaanka Qaramada Midoobay ee Soomaaliya, kaas oo hoos imaanayay UNTMIS/HRPG, iyadoo mas’uuliyadda arrimaha Xuquuqul Insaanka si buuxda loogu wareejiyay hay’adaha qaranka. Geeddi-socodka ayaa soo maray wada-hadallo iyo diyaar-garow heer qaran iyo heer caalami ah, oo ay ka mid ahaayeen kulamo ka dhacay Muqdisho, Geneva iyo New York. Waxaa hoggaaminayay Wasiirka Wasaaradda Qoyska iyo Horumarinta Xuquuqul Insaanka XFS, Amb. Khadiija Maxamed Al-Makhzoumi, iyadoo ay ka qeyb qaateen maamulka Wasaaradda, agaasimeyaal, la-taliyeyaal, khubaro iyo shaqaale Soomaaliyeed. Tallaabadan ayaa qeyb ka ah dadaallada lagu xoojinayo lahaanshaha iyo hoggaaminta qaranka ee ajandaha Xuquuqul Insaanka, iyadoo Soomaaliya ay sii xoojinayso hay’adaha u xilsaaran ilaalinta iyo horumarinta xuquuqda muwaadiniinta. Dowladdu waxay sheegtay in geeddi-socodka ay saldhig u ahaayeen horumarrada Soomaaliya ka sameysay dhinaca Xuquuqul Insaanka, go’aannada dowladda iyo xoojinta Guddiga Madaxa-bannaan ee Xuquuqul Insaanka Qaranka Soomaaliya. Shirweynihii Qaran ee Xuquuqul Insaanka ee Maarso 2025 ayaa sidoo kale lagu tilmaamay inuu door ka qaatay dhismaha aragti qaran oo ku wajahan ilaalinta Xuquuqda Aadanaha. Xiritaanka xafiiska Qaramada Midoobay looma arko dhammaadka taageerada iyo shaqada Xuquuqul Insaanka, balse wuxuu calaamad u yahay marxalad cusub oo hay’adaha Soomaaliyeed ay si toos ah ugu qaadanayaan masuuliyadda ilaalinta, horumarinta iyo u doodista xuquuqda muwaadiniinta. Marxaladdan cusub waxay Soomaaliya ka doonaysaa xoojinta hay’adaha, isla-xisaabtanka, ku dhaqanka sharciga iyo gudashada waajibaadka dastuuriga ah iyo kuwa caalamiga ah ee la xiriira Xuquuqul Insaanka. Soomaaliya waxay maanta soo gabagabeysay cutub, waxayna furtay mid cusub—cutub ay hay’adaha qaranku leeyihiin, hoggaaminayaan, kana mas’uul yihiin ilaalinta Xuquuqda Aadanaha.

items.title: Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh oo u baxaya safar dibadda ah
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ayaa lagu wadaa inuu maalmaha soo socda gaaro magaalada New York ee dalka Mareykanka, si uu uga qayb-galo shirka Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay. Madaxweynaha ayaa kamid noqon doona madaxda dalalka xubnaha ka ah Qaramada Midoobay ee ka qayb-galaya kulamada iyo doodaha guud ee shirka, iyadoo sidoo kale la filayo inuu khudbad ka jeediyo madasha golaha guud. Ajendaha khudbadda Xasan Sheekh ayaa la filayaa inuu uga hadlo xaaladda Soomaaliya, isagoo soo bandhigi doona arrimaha la xiriira amniga, siyaasadda iyo geeddi-socodka dowlad-dhiska dalka. Waxaa sidoo kale la filayaa in Madaxweynaha uu ka hadlo horumarka ay Dowladda Federaalka sheegtay inay ka samaysay dhinacyada kala duwan iyo tallaabooyinka ay qaaday muddadii u dambeysay. Inta uu ku sugan yahay New York, Xasan Sheekh ayaa fursad u heli doona inuu kulamo la yeesho madaxda iyo mas’uuliyiinta dalalka kale ee shirka ka qayb-galaya iyo saraakiisha hay’adaha caalamiga ah. Kulamada Madaxweynaha ayaa lagu wadaa in looga hadlo xoojinta xiriirka Soomaaliya iyo beesha caalamka, iskaashiga dhinacyada kala duwan iyo taageerada caalamiga ah ee Dowladda Federaalka. Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay ayaa sanad kasta magaalada New York ku martigeliya madaxda iyo wakiillada dalalka xubnaha ka ah ururka, kuwaas oo kaga hadla arrimaha caalamiga ah iyo xaaladaha dalalkooda. Wafdiga Soomaaliya ee shirka ka qayb-galaya ayaa la filayaa inuu ka koobnaado xubno ka tirsan Dowladda Federaalka oo ay kamid yihiin wasiirro iyo xildhibaanno, kuwaas oo Madaxweynaha ku wehlin doona safarkiisa New York. The post Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh oo u baxaya safar dibadda ah appeared first on Caasimada Online .

Golaha Wasiirada Koonfur Galbeed oo ka shiray amniga, fatahaadaha iyo adeegyada bulshada
items.description: Baydhabo, 17 Sebtembar 2026: Hoggaamiyaha Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed, Sheekh Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Madoobe), ayaa maanta shir-guddoomiyey kulanka Golaha Wasiirada Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed, kaas oo looga hadlay xaaladda amniga, maamulka, fatahaadaha iyo horumarinta adeegyada bulshada. Golaha Wasiirada ayaa si gaar ah uga hadlay xoojinta amniga deegaannada Koonfur Galbeed iyo sidii loo sii adkeyn lahaa wada-shaqeynta hay’adaha amniga iyo maamulka, si loo xaqiijiyo nabadgelyada shacabka. Sidoo kale, kulanka waxaa lagu soo qaaday u diyaar-garowga fatahaadaha iyo saameynta El Niño, iyadoo la qiimeeyey qorshayaasha loogu talagalay ka hortagga iyo yareynta saameynta fatahaadaha iyo xaaladaha cimilada, gaar ahaan deegaannada ay bulshada ugu nugushahay. Golaha ayaa sidoo kale ka dooday maamul-daadejinta iyo dardargelinta adeegyada dowladda, iyadoo xoogga la saaray sidii adeegyada aasaasiga ah loogu dhoweyn lahaa shacabka, loona xoojin lahaa hufnaanta iyo isla-xisaabtanka hay’adaha dowladda. Ugu dambeyn, Hoggaamiyaha Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed Sheekh Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Madoobe) ayaa Golaha Wasiirada kula dardaarmay in la xoojiyo wada-shaqeynta hay’adaha dowladda, lana dardar-geliyo qorshayaasha wax looga qabanayo baahiyaha shacabka iyo horumarinta adeegyada dowladda.

items.title: Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka oo shir-guddoomiyey kulanka 7-aad ee Guddiga Joogtada
items.description: Muqdisho, 17 Sebtembar 2026: Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka ee Baarlamaanka Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac), ayaa maanta shir-guddoomiyey kulanka toddobaadlaha ah ee 7-aad ee Guddiga Joogtada ah ee Golaha Shacabka, kaas oo lagu qabtay Xarunta Guddoonka iyo Guddiyada ee Villa Hargeysa. Guddoomiyaha ayaa kulanka furitaankiisa ku bogaadiyey xubnaha Guddiga Joogtada ah dadaallada ay ku bixinayaan gudashada waajibaadkooda iyo dardargelinta howlaha sharci-dejinta. Kulanka ayaa sidoo kale lagu dhageystay warbixin uu soo jeediyey Xoghayaha Guud ee Golaha Shacabka, Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdulle (Jaabiri), taas oo ku saabsanayd Hindise Sharciyeedyada horyaalla guddiyada Golaha, marxaladaha ay marayaan, waqtiga la qorsheeyey in loo gudbiyo fadhiyada guud iyo caqabadaha u baahan in wax laga qabto. Xubnaha Guddiga Joogtada ayaa intii uu kulanku socday dejiyey ajandaha iyo jadwalka kulamada guud ee Golaha Shacabka ee toddobaadka soo socda, iyagoo sidoo kale ansixiyey hadal-qoraalkii kulankii 6-aad ee Guddiga Joogtada ah. Ugu dambeyn, Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka ayaa kulanka soo xiray, isagoo xubnaha guddiga ku adkeeyey inay sii xoojiyaan dadaallada ku aaddan gudashada waajibaadkooda dastuuriga ah, dardargelinta howlaha sharci-dejinta iyo in shaqada Golaha Shacabka loo fuliyo si hufan oo waafaqsan qorshayaasha shaqo.

Xubnaha Guddiga Joogtada ayaa intii uu kulanku socday dejiyey ajandaha iyo jadwalka kulamada guud ee Golaha Shacabka ee toddobaadka soo socda, iyagoo sidoo kale ansixiyey hadal-qoraalkii kulankii 6-aad ee Guddiga Joogtada ah. Ugu dambeyn, Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka ayaa kulanka soo xiray, isagoo xubnaha guddiga ku adkeeyey inay sii xoojiyaan dadaallada ku aaddan gudashada waajibaadkooda dastuuriga ah, dardargelinta howlaha sharci-dejinta iyo in shaqada Golaha Shacabka loo fuliyo si hufan oo waafaqsan qorshayaasha shaqo.

items.title: Safaaradda Mareykanka oo ka digtay khataro ka jira Doolo Zone ee Itoobiya
items.description: Safaaradda Mareykanka ee Addis Ababa ayaa soo saartay digniin amni oo ku saabsan Doolo Zone (Dollo Zone) ee ka tirsan Deegaanka Soomaalida Itoobiya, iyadoo sheegtay inay heshay xog ku saabsan khataro suurtagal ah oo loo geysan karo ajaanibta, oo ay ku jiraan muwaadiniinta Mareykanka. Safaaradda ayaa sheegtay in khatarta sii kordheysa awgeed, shaqaalaha dowladda Mareykanka aan loo oggolaan doonin inay u safraan Doolo Zone, haddii aysan helin oggolaansho gaar ah. Sidoo kale, muwaadiniinta Mareykanka ayaa lagula taliyay inaysan u safrin Doolo Zone, halka dadka ku sugan ama qorsheynaya inay tagaan deegaanka lagu boorriyay inay feejignaadaan, kana fogaadaan goobaha ay dadku ku badan yihiin iyo xaaladaha keeni kara khatar amni. Digniintan ayaa kusoo beegmeysa iyadoo Mareykanku weli Itoobiya ku qiimeynayo Heerka 3-aad ee safarka – “Reconsider Travel”, sababo la xiriira qalalaase, dambiyo, afduub, argagixiso, miinooyin dhulka lagu aasay iyo carqalado dhanka isgaarsiinta ah. Digniinta Mareykanka waxay si gaar ah u xustay Doolo Zone, taas oo ka mid ah deegaannada Soomaalida Itoobiya, iyadoo aan si faahfaahsan loo shaacin nooca khatarta ama cidda ka dambeysa hanjabaadaha la sheegay.

items.title: Xukuumadda Soomaaliya 𝐨𝐨 𝐤𝐮 𝐝𝐡𝐚𝐰𝐚𝐚𝐪d𝐚𝐲 𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐠𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐚 𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐚𝐚𝐧𝐤𝐚 𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐤𝐚 𝐟𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐧 𝐞𝐞 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐪𝐚𝐚𝐥𝐚𝐡𝐚 𝐝𝐨𝐰𝐥𝐚𝐝𝐝a
items.description: Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Xukuumadda Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Mudane Xamsa Cabdi Barre, Isaga oo ka duulaya Dastuurka Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya Qodobka 161aad farqadda (1), Sharciga Shaqaalaha Rayid ah qodobkiisa 7aad, iyo dhammaan xeerarka, shuruucda iyo qaraarada la xiriira Shaqaalaha Rayidka ah ee Dowladdda Federaalka ah, ayuu faray dhammaan Wasiirrada iyo Mas’uuliyiinta kale ee dowladda in si buuxda oo aan dib-u-dhac lahayn loo hirgeliyo hannaanka shaqaalaysiinta iyo magacaabista ku salaysan kartida iyo mudnaanta. Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Xukuumadda Mudane Xamsa, faray Guddiga Shaqaalaha Rayidka Dowladda in 20-Sebteembar la bilaabo wajiga 1aad ee dib-u-habaynta Agaasime Waaxeedyada maadama ay laf-dhabar u yihiin maamulka hey’adaha dowladda ayna door muuqda ka qaataan hoggaaminta, hirgalinta siyaasadda, fulinta qorsheyaasha iyo joogtaynta shaqada hey’adaha. Marka la hirgaliyo wajiga 1-aad waxaa dib-u-habayn lagu samayn doona Agaasimayaasha Guud ee hey’adaha dowladda iyada oo lagu salaynayo karti, aqoon, khibrad, hoggaamin iyo waxqabad, si loo dhiso hoggaan maamul oo xirfad leh isla-xisaabtan leh oo ka shaqeeya natiijooyin muuqda. Mudane Xamsa, ayaa sheegay in ujeeddada laga leeyahay nidaamkan ay tahay in Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ay yeelato hoggaan maamul oo xirfad leh, joogto ah, awoodda in uu hirgaliyo siyaasadda dowladda una beddelo natiijooyin muuqda oo ay markhaati ka noqdaan shacabka Soomaaliyeed. Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamsa, ayaa xusay in Afartii sano ee la soo dhaafay, Xukuumadda DanQaran ay qaaday tallaabooyin muhiim ah oo lagu xoojinayo dhismaha, maamulka iyo tayada hay’adaha dowladda, iyada oo ujeeddadu tahay in la helo hay’ado dowladeed oo leh saldhig sharci iyo maamul adag iyo Shaqaale Rayid ah oo leh aqoon, karti iyo karaan ku filan gudashada waajibaadka saaran. “Waxaan dhidibka u taagnay tiirar sharci iyo kuwa hay’adaha ee lagama maarmaanka u ah dib-u-habaynta iyo horumarinta shaqaalaha rayidka ah, Waxa aan ansixinnay sharciyo, siyaasado, xeerar iyo qaab-dhismeedyo muhiim ah oo hagaya maamulka hay’adaha iyo shaqaalaha dowladda”. Ayuu yiri Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamsa Cabdi Barre. Ugu Dambayn: Ra’iisul Wasaaraha, ayaa faray dhammaan Wasaaradaha iyo Hey’adaha Dowladda In si buuxda loo hirgeliyo qaab-dhismeedyada hay’adaha ee la ansixiyey, iyada oo xilalka Agaasime Waaxeedyada lagu buuxinayo hannaan tartan furan, dhammaan shaqaalaha u qalma ee ku jira adeegga rayidka ah la siiyo fursad loo siman yahay oo ay ugu tartamaan xilalkaas, iyo In wixii xil ama jago bannaan ah ee shaqaalaha dowladda ah lagu buuxiyo hannaan tartan furan oo waafaqsan shuruucda iyo xeerarka dowladda.

items.title: U.S. Airstrike Targets Al-Shabaab Weapons Depot in Puntland’s Al-Madow Mountains
items.description: Garowe (WDN) — The United States has carried out an airstrike targeting an Al-Shabaab weapons and ammunition depot in Puntland’s Al-Madow Mountains, Puntland authorities said Thursday, as counterterrorism operations against militant networks continue in northern Somalia. In a statement dated 17 September 2026, the Puntland Government said the strike targeted a site known as Markad, in the Golis mountain range, which it described as a storage facility used by Al-Shabaab to stockpile weapons, ammunition and other military supplies. The operation was conducted in coordination with Puntland government security institutions, according to the statement. “The Puntland Government and the United States Government have confirmed the success of a counterterrorism operation conducted in the Golis Mountains of the Al-Madow area,” the statement said. Puntland said the targeted facility served as a logistical base supporting Al-Shabaab’s operations and its ability to plan and carry out attacks. The Al-Madow and wider Golis mountain ranges are strategically significant because their rugged terrain provides armed groups with remote locations that can be difficult for ground forces to access. Puntland security forces have conducted sustained operations in the broader area as part of efforts to prevent extremist groups from establishing permanent footholds. The latest strike forms part of continuing counterterrorism cooperation between Puntland and the United States. Puntland said the objective is to disrupt Al-Shabaab’s logistical networks, restrict its ability to store and move military supplies, and deny the group locations from which it can organize attacks. “The targeting of locations and facilities used by the group to support its operations is intended to place pressure on and disrupt its ability to plan and carry out attacks,” the statement said. Puntland and the United States reaffirmed their commitment to continued efforts aimed at weakening Al-Shabaab and preventing the group from establishing safe locations in northern Somalia. The Puntland statement did not provide information on casualties, the extent of damage caused by the strike, or whether senior Al-Shabaab figures were present at the targeted facility. Those details could not be independently verified. WardheerNews The post U.S. Airstrike Targets Al-Shabaab Weapons Depot in Puntland’s Al-Madow Mountains appeared first on WardheerNews .

items.title: Somali National Killed in Armed Attack in Kenya’s Migori County
items.description: MIGORI, Kenya (WDN) — A Somali national identified as Abdi Jama has reportedly been killed in an armed attack in Lolgorian, a village in Kenya’s Migori County, according to local reports. The attackers reportedly stormed the house where Abdi was staying while he was asleep and opened fire, striking him in several parts of his body. Reports further allege that the attackers mutilated his body after the shooting. The circumstances surrounding the killing remain unclear, and the details have not been independently verified. Local authorities and security agencies are expected to investigate the incident and provide further information about the identity of the attackers and their possible motive. Migori County, particularly areas involved in gold mining, has attracted a growing Somali business community in recent years. Somali traders and investors are involved in the gold trade and related commercial activities, while employing local Kenyan workers in various parts of the sector. The latest killing has therefore raised concerns within the Somali community, particularly because several Somali nationals have reportedly been killed in Lolgorian and surrounding areas in recent months under different circumstances. Sources said Abdi Jama’s body was expected to be transported to Isebania, a town near the Kenya-Tanzania border, where relatives and members of the Somali community were preparing for his burial. The reported killing has renewed calls for greater attention to the security of Somali traders and residents operating in Kenya’s gold-producing areas, where criminal networks, commercial disputes and other security risks have previously been reported. Further details are expected as Kenyan police authorities and local residents establish the circumstances surrounding the attack. items.title: Xuutiyiinta oo shuruud ku xiray in maraakiibta Mareykanka ay si xor ah ku maraan Bab El-Mandeb
items.description: Ururka Xuutiyiinta Yemen ayaa ogolaaday in maraakiibta Mareykanka ay si nabdoon ku maraan marin biyoodka Bab El-Mandeb, haddii Washington ay ka fogaato inay si toos ah ugu lug yeelato dagaalka uu Sacuudiga hoggaamiyo ee kala dhexeeya Dowladda Yemen ee caalamka uu aqoonsan yahay. Telefishinka Al Jazeera ayaa ku waramay in labada dhinac ay heshiiskan gaareen, ka dib wada hadalo qarsoodi ah oo daba-yaaqadii isbuuca ay ku yeesheen Magaalada Muscat, oo Saldanada Cumaan ay garwadeen ka ahayd. Warbaahinta Mareykanka ayaa sheegtay in Xuutiyiinta ay ogolaadeen in maraakiibta wata Calanka Mareykanka ama xiriirka la leh Mareykanka ay si xor ah ugu gooshaan Badda Cas iyo Marinka Bab El-Mandeb, iyadoo shuruud looga dhigayo in Washington aysan si toos ah ugu lug yeelan dhanka militariga ee dagaalka uu Sacuudiga hoggaaminayo ee ka socda Yemen. Waxaa jira warar sheegaya in Mareykanka uu Xuutiyiinta ka dalbaday inaanan sidoo kale la beegsan maraakiibta laga leeyahay amaba xiriirka la leh Dekedaha Israel, balse ay Xuutiyiinta ku adkeysteen inay ixtiraamayaan heshiiskii xabad joojinta ay labada dhinac gaareen 6-dii bishii May ee sanadkii 2025. Saraakiisha Xuutiyiinta ayaa laga soo xigtay in is fahamka Washington uusan ku saleysnayn badbaadinta Israel ama joojinta hawlgalada ka dhanka ah danaha Israel, taas oo la macno ah in hawlgalada ay taageerada ugu muujinayaan shacabka Falastiin ee ka dhanka ah amniga iyo danaha Israel ee gobolka ay sii socon karaan. Xuutiyiinta ayaa Sabtidii sheegay in dhammaan maraakiibta ganacsiga caalamiga ah oo dhan ay adeegsan karaan biyaha Badda Cas iyo Bab El-Mandeb, marka laga reebo kuwa laga leeyahay Sacuudiga. Xafiiska Siyaasadda Xuutiyiinta ayaa Axaddii Israel ku eedeeyay inay sii waddo dilalka iyo xadgudubyada ay ku sameynayso heshiiskii xabad joojinta Gaza ee la dhaqangeliyay 10-kii bishii October ee sanadkii hore. Xafiiska oo warsaxaafadeed soo saaray ayaa ku baaqay in laga hortago xadgudubyada joogtada ah ee Israel iyo in la sii wado taageerada caalamiga ah ee qaddiyadda qaranimada Falastiin. Xoogaga Xuutiyiinta oo toddobaadkii hore la wareegay deegaanada xeebaha dalkaasi Yemen ee ku teedsan Badda Cas iyo Bab El-Mandeb ayaa soo cusbooneysiin kara weeraradii ay ku hayeen maraakiibta lala xiriiriyo Dekedaha Israel, iyagoo adkeynaya in la ilaaliyo xabad joojinta Gaza.

items.title: Cirro oo ku ceeboobay wareysi lagula yeeshay Washington
items.description: Washington (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha maamulka Somaliland, Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi (Cirro), ayaa ku ceeboobay wareysi lagula yeeshay magaalada Washington, kaddib markii jawaabo uu ka bixiyay macdanta, dagaalka Suudaan iyo sababta Mareykanka looga doonayo inuu aqoonsado Somaliland ay dood ka dhaliyeen baraha bulshada iyo qaar ka mid ah falanqeeyayaasha Mareykanka. Wareysiga ayaa ka dhacay machadka Hudson Institute 14-kii September, xilli Cirro uu booqasho ku joogo Mareykanka, isaga oo olole ugu jira sidii maamulka Somaliland uu Washington uga heli lahaa aqoonsi. Hudson Institute ayaa kulanka ku tilmaamay mid looga hadlayay doorka Somaliland ee Geeska Afrika iyo muhiimaddeeda istaraatiijiyadeed. Warbaahinta Middle East Eye ayaa sheegtay in qaabka uu Cirro uga jawaabay qaar ka mid ah su’aalaha uu dhaliyay dhaleeceyn, gaar ahaan xilli Somaliland ay isku dayeyso inay Mareykanka ka dhaadhiciso inay leedahay muhiimad dhinacyada amniga, dekedaha iyo khayraadka dabiiciga ah. Mid ka mid ah su’aalaha sida weyn loo hadal hayo ayaa ku saabsaneyd macdanta muhiimka ah ee Somaliland ay sheegato in ay u soo bandhigi karto Mareykanka. Markii la weydiiyay nooca macdantaas, Cirro ayaa qoslay, isagoo sheegay inuusan ahayn khabiir cilmiga dhulka ah. “Ma garanayo… malaha wax walba,” ayuu yiri. Jawaabta ayaa timid xilli Cirro uu wareysi kale oo uu siiyay warbaahinta Semafor ku sheegay in Somaliland ay Mareykanka u soo bandhigi karto dekedo, macdan iyo suurta-galnimada wada-xaajood ku saabsan marin ama adeegyo militari, iyadoo beddelkeeda dooneysa xiriir dhow iyo aqoonsi. Semafor ayaa sidoo kale sheegtay in Cirro uu Washington u sheegay in “wax bilaash ah” aan la bixineyn. Hase yeeshee, tani ma ahayn markii ugu horreysay ee Cirro uu ka hadlo macdanta Somaliland. Bishii February, wuxuu Reuters u sheegay in deegaanku leeyahay macdan, shidaal iyo gaas, isagoo si gaar ah u xusay sheegashada ku saabsan kaydka lithium-ka. Su’aal kale oo dood dhalisay ayaa ku saabsaneyd dagaalka Suudaan. Markii wax laga weydiiyay colaaddaas, Cirro wuxuu sheegay in Suudaan ay “aad uga fog tahay” Somaliland, isagoo masaafadeeda tusaale ahaan ula barbar dhigay Venezuela. Ninka wareysiga qaaday ayaa markaas ku jawaabay in Suudaan aysan sidaas uga fogeyn, ka hor inta uusan u gudbin su’aal kale. Dagaalka Suudaan ayaa tan iyo 2023 u dhexeeya ciidamada dowladda iyo xoogagga Rapid Support Forces (RSF), waxaana colaadda ku lug leh dano iyo loollan goboleed oo ballaaran. Imaaraadka Carabta ayaa lagu eedeeyay inuu taageero RSF, balse Abu Dhabi ayaa beenisay eedeymahaas. Cameron Hudson, oo hore uga tirsanaa hay’adaha dowladda Mareykanka kana faallooda arrimaha Afrika, ayaa si adag u dhaleeceeyay muuqaalka Cirro ee kulanka, isaga oo qoraal uu soo dhigay X ku tilmaamay hoggaamiye ay ku adkaatay inuu gudbiyo farriintii uu Washington ula yimid. Hudson ayaa xitaa adeegsaday ereyga “African Biden” isagoo ku sifeynaya sida uu u arkay wareysiga, ulana jeeday sida madaxweynihii hore ee Mareykanka uu hadalkii uu dhibbanaa inta uusan xukunka ka degan, kadib markii ay da’da ka daba timid. Dood kale ayaa dhalatay markii Cirro la weydiiyay sababta Mareykanku u aqoonsan lahaa Somaliland. “Ficil ahaan Somaliland kama mid aha Soomaaliya,” ayuu yiri, ka hor inta uusan raacin: “Mabda’a ahaan Somaliland waxay ka mid tahay Soomaaliya.” Somaliland waxay sheegatay inay Soomaaliya inteeda kale ka go’day sanadkii 1991-kii, balse dowladda federaalka Soomaaliya waxay u aragtaa qayb ka mid ah dhulkeeda, waana mowqif ay taageeraan Midowga Afrika iyo dalal badan oo caalamka ah. Israel ayaa 26-kii December 2025 noqotay dalkii ugu horreeyay ee xubin ka ah Qaramada Midoobay ee si rasmi ah u aqoonsada Somaliland, tallaabadaas oo dowladda Soomaaliya si xooggan u cambaareysay, kuna tilmaantay mid ka dhan ah madax-bannaanideeda iyo midnimada dhuleed. Tan iyo markaas, Somaliland waxay sare u qaaday dadaallada ay ugu jirto inay hesho aqoonsiyo kale, iyadoo Mareykanka u aragta bartilmaameedka ugu muhiimsan. Cirro ayaa warbaahinta Semafor u sheegay in Somaliland ay Washington u soo bandhigi karto dekedda Berbera, khayraad dabiici ah iyo iskaashi dhinaca amniga ah, halka Mareykanka laga doonayo xiriir siyaasadeed oo ka ballaaran kan hadda jira.
