items.fullContent: By Isha Qarsoon On the night of September 9, 2026, drones struck a tugboat named TEDY near Odesa, Ukraine . The vessel was hit again as it tried to reach Constanta. Two Azerbaijani crew members were killed and two suffered burns. Its ten-person crew included Azerbaijani, Turkish, German and Ukrainian nationals. Mert Marine Corporation, a Turkish company, owned the tug. TEDY sailed under the Somali flag. No Somali was aboard. [1] Ukraine’s government blamed Russia and described the attack as part of a wider campaign against civilian shipping. Russia’s Defence Ministry said it had struck two cargo vessels and a tugboat near Odesa, alleging that the ships were carrying military supplies. It did not identify TEDY, and the connection between its statement and the attack has not been independently confirmed. Azerbaijan did not attribute responsibility. The competing accounts do not change the point. A Turkish-owned vessel with an entirely foreign crew carried Somali nationality into a European war. The attack does not prove that the registry was inappropriate. A ship under any flag can be attacked in a war. Also, a ship crew does not have to include nationals of the flag it is sailing under. The attack exposes, however, the scale of the risk Somalia accepted: within months of reviving its ship registry, Somali nationality appeared on a foreign-owned ship with a foreign crew operating in a European conflict. Somalia acquired the flag state’s legal duties and reputational exposure without acquiring control of the voyage. The Turkish ownership was not incidental: Turkish interests already run Somalia’s main port and airport, train and help command its military, hold rights to its offshore oil and fish stocks, and now operate the very registry that flagged TEDY in the first place. TEDY is the trigger for examining what happens when that system is abused. What a flag of convenience is The term flag of convenience entered common use in the 1950s. American owners had used Panama between the two world wars to avoid domestic taxes, labour rules and crewing requirements. Liberia opened its international registry in 1948, and Honduras later joined the historical group known as PanLibHon. A flag of convenience generally describes a vessel registered in a country other than the country of its beneficial ownership or commercial control, often to reduce costs or avoid stricter regulation. A 1970 British government inquiry identified six common features of flag of convenience: foreign ownership or control, easy registration and withdrawal, low taxation, a registry maintained mainly for fee income rather than national shipping needs, unrestricted foreign crews, and limited capacity or willingness to enforce shipping rules.[3] These are descriptive indicators, not a binding legal test. Somalia’s new registry displays several of those features. On March 30, 2026, Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur, then minister of ports and marine transport, signed a memorandum with Somali Ship Register Limited, represented by Turkish national Cagdas Oykun Saltas. On April 2, 2026, the government announced GUNEY as the first vessel admitted under the revived flag. It was foreign-owned or controlled, had just left the Honduran flag, and was registered while in Turkey.[2] The memorandum was signed on March 30, 2026, and Guney entered the register three days later, on April 2. That interval is too short for an owner unfamiliar with a newly created registry to locate it, complete a flag change out of Honduras, and clear administrative review. It indicates the vessel’s move to the Somali flag was arranged before the memorandum was signed, not decided afterward, which means the registry and its first customer were not two separate developments but one planned transaction presented as two. The September attack revealed that TEDY, another Turkish-owned vessel, was flying the Somali flag.[1] The public record establishes that Somalia opened its nationality to foreign shipping through a foreign private operator before publishing how that operator would be supervised. Private administration is not automatically disreputable. Liberia and the Marshall Islands show that an overseas administrator can coexist with effective state regulation. Somalia’s problem is the political setting. The registry entered a relationship in which Turkey and Turkish-linked bodies already occupy Somalia’s airport, port, military and maritime security, petroleum, fisheries licensing and prospective minerals.[8] In that setting, abuse cannot be treated as a remote possibility to be considered after the first scandal. It is the working risk that should govern the registry. The burden belongs on the government to prove that Somali officials can refuse, suspend and deregister a ship against Turkish commercial or political pressure. The duties stay with Somalia Article 91 of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea requires a genuine link between a ship and the state whose flag it flies. Article 94 requires the flag state to exercise effective jurisdiction and control over administrative, technical and social matters. Those duties include maintaining a register, enforcing safety and crewing standards, and investigating serious casualties.[4] A private registrar may process applications, collect fees and arrange surveys. It cannot take Somalia’s international responsibility with it. UNCLOS’s genuine-link rule offers less protection than its wording suggests. In M/V Saiga, the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea held that the absence of an effective link does not, by itself, allow another state to refuse recognition of a vessel’s nationality. Coastal and port states retain enforcement powers under other rules, but they cannot erase the Somali flag simply because Somalia fails to control the ship. UNCLOS therefore leaves the main burden where Somalia placed it: on Somalia. What abuse would cost Somalia The first cost is damage to the flag’s reputation. A poorly maintained vessel may be detained because of its own deficiencies. The Paris Memorandum of Understanding on Port State Control coordinates inspections of foreign ships entering participating European and North Atlantic ports. It classifies flags according to their inspection and detention records over a rolling three-year period. A flag enters the white, grey or black list only after at least thirty inspections. Once that threshold is met, repeated deficiencies and detentions can push the flag into a worse category and subject other vessels flying it to greater scrutiny.[5] Reputable owners then face higher inspection, insurance and chartering costs merely for carrying the same flag. The fastest customers to leave are often the ones Somalia should want to keep. The second cost is loss of control over who claims Somali nationality. The International Maritime Organization has documented fraudulent registrations and unauthorized use of flags, including several African flags targeted by vessels seeking a permissive or unverifiable identity.[6] A new international registry with opaque records is attractive to operators fleeing another flag, concealing ownership, manipulating vessel identities or avoiding scrutiny. If Somalia cannot publish and verify its register in real time, foreign authorities and commercial databases will struggle to distinguish a valid Somali ship from a fraudulent one. Both damage the same name. The third cost is sanctions exposure. The US Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control administers sanctions in support of United States foreign policy and national security. A Somali flag provides no immunity when a vessel, owner, manager, or service provider is subject to a US sanctions program. OFAC has warned that helping a blocked carrier reflag its vessels may constitute providing services to a blocked person and may itself support designation.[7] Misconduct by one vessel would not automatically subject Somalia or its registry to sanctions. It could nevertheless associate the Somali flag with weak screening, increase scrutiny of other vessels flying it, and discourage reputable owners from using the registry. The remaining costs are practical and political. Unsafe ships injure crews. Uninsured ships leave pollution and wreck-removal claims behind. Deceptive ships switch off tracking, falsify cargo papers or move sanctioned oil and weapons. Ships trading near wars pull the flag state into disputes it did not create. Each event demands records, investigation, cooperation and enforcement from Mogadishu. If the Somali government cannot or will not act against a vessel admitted by a Turkish operator, Somalia carries the liability while foreign owners and managers keep the commercial benefit. The control question The registry memorandum has not been published. The public therefore cannot see who has final authority over admission, beneficial-ownership checks, sanctions screening, surveyors, casualty investigations, suspension, deregistration, data and audits. Even if there is no public evidence that Ankara formally directs Somali Ship Register Limited, formal instructions are not the only measure of control. When a government already depends on the same foreign partner across its principal gateways, security and resources, the registrar’s independence cannot simply be presumed. Nur, who signed the registry memorandum and invited international owners to use the flag, later became Speaker of the House of the People. The issue is larger than one official. Somalia has built a structure in which the state must police ships brought to it through a relationship it may be politically unable to challenge. That conflict is exactly how a flag of convenience becomes dangerous: enforcement against a ship can also become a confrontation with the power behind the registry. Conclusion TEDY is a warning of potential misconduct. It shows how quickly Somalia’s legal identity can travel far beyond Somali commerce, territory or control. The next case may involve sanctions evasion, pollution, crew abuse, false registration or a voyage that serves a foreign war. By the time that case arrives, the cost will already carry Somalia’s name. The government licensed use of its flag through a Turkish-run company inside a relationship already marked by extreme dependence. Before more ships are admitted, Somalia should publish the memorandum and the live register, keep final registration and deregistration authority in accountable Somali hands, require independent ownership and sanctions screening, audit the operator, and fund the investigations and enforcement required by UNCLOS. Without those safeguards, Somalia will collect registration fees while assuming legal, diplomatic and reputational risks it cannot control. That is the harm an abused flag of convenience can do. items.title: The Battle for Marib Could Echo Across the Red Sea and Horn of Africa
items.description: Adan, Yemen (WDN) — Marib is a strategically and geopolitically important city in Yemen and a key part of the conflict-affected Red Sea region; if Marib were to fall, the consequences could extend well beyond Yemen’s borders, with wider implications for regional security and stability A Houthi breakthrough in this strategic oil- and gas-producing region could send a new shockwave across the Red Sea, placing Djibouti, Eritrea and Somalia directly in the path of a rapidly changing security threat. What begins as a battle for one Yemeni governorate could ultimately become a battle over the security of an entire maritime region. Marib is far more than another battlefield in Yemen’s seemingly endless war. The governorate remains one of the most important strongholds of Yemen’s internationally recognized government and contains significant oil and natural-gas resources. Whoever controls Marib gains territory, economic resources, military depth and considerable political leverage. That is precisely why the battle for Marib matters beyond Yemen. The Houthis already control Yemen’s capital, Sana’a, as well as large parts of the country’s north and west. A major Houthi advance into Marib would strengthen their position considerably, potentially giving them greater access to resources while consolidating their control over much of northern Yemen. But the strategic consequences would not necessarily stop at Yemen’s borders. Yemen sits across the water from the Horn of Africa, separated from Djibouti, Eritrea and Somalia by some of the world’s most strategically important maritime routes. As the military balance inside Yemen changes, so too can the security calculations surrounding the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. The connection begins with geography. From Marib, a strengthened Houthi movement could consolidate its military position across northern Yemen and maintain greater pressure toward the country’s western coastline. Along that coastline lies the Red Sea, and beyond it the narrow maritime passage of Bab el-Mandeb, the gateway connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and the wider Indian Ocean. Marib therefore does not need to be physically close to Bab el-Mandeb to matter to its security. What matters is what control of Marib could do to the overall military balance inside Yemen. The stronger the Houthis become, the greater their potential ability to influence developments along Yemen’s western coast. And the more militarized that coastline becomes, the greater the pressure on one of the world’s most important shipping corridors. That is where the concerns of neighboring African countries become particularly acute. For Djibouti, Yemen is not a distant conflict. The two countries sit almost face-to-face across the Red Sea. Djibouti has built much of its economy around ports, shipping and logistics and hosts military facilities belonging to several international powers. Its prosperity and strategic importance depend heavily on the security of the surrounding maritime environment. A worsening conflict in Yemen could therefore impose new security costs on Djibouti, from increased maritime surveillance to greater protection of ports and commercial vessels. Eritrea faces a different but equally important exposure. Its long Red Sea coastline places it directly within the broader strategic environment created by the conflict in Yemen. Greater military activity along Yemen’s western coast could increase concerns about weapons trafficking, maritime crime and the security of commercial shipping. For Asmara, what happens across the water can quickly become a matter of national security. Then there is Somalia. Somalia’s coastline stretches along the Gulf of Aden, directly connecting the country to the maritime consequences of instability in Yemen. Somali ports and coastal communities depend on secure waters, while the country’s strategic position makes it an unavoidable part of any discussion about the security of the Gulf of Aden. A prolonged escalation in Yemen could create opportunities for piracy networks, arms traffickers and other criminal groups to exploit resulting security gaps. It could also increase pressure on Somalia to strengthen maritime surveillance and protect shipping routes along its extensive coastline. The consequences could therefore move in both directions: instability in Yemen affecting the Horn of Africa, while insecurity in the Horn could in turn complicate efforts to secure the maritime corridor. There is also a larger geopolitical dimension. The struggle for Marib remains intertwined with the broader rivalry between Saudi Arabia and Iran. Saudi Arabia has supported Yemen’s internationally recognized government, while the Houthis maintain close ties with Tehran. A significant shift in Marib could consequently be interpreted not merely as a local military development but as another change in the regional balance of power. That is why the fighting deserves attention in capitals far beyond Sana’a. The central concern is not that a Houthi advance in Marib would automatically produce a regional war. It is that every significant change in Yemen’s military balance introduces new strategic calculations around the Red Sea. For Djibouti, the question is how to protect a vital maritime and logistics hub. For Eritrea, it is how to protect its Red Sea coastline amid increasing regional militarization. For Somalia, it is how to secure the Gulf of Aden and prevent renewed opportunities for piracy, trafficking and other maritime threats. And for the international community, it is how to keep one of the world’s most important commercial waterways from becoming another front in a widening regional conflict. The battle for Marib is therefore about much more than who controls an oil- and gas-producing governorate. It is about what happens to Yemen’s overall balance of power—and what that balance means for the waters separating Yemen from Africa. Marib may be hundreds of kilometers from Bab el-Mandeb, but a major shift there could eventually be felt in Djibouti, Eritrea and Somalia. The battlefield is in Yemen. The strategic consequences could reach across the Red Sea. WardheerNews The post The Battle for Marib Could Echo Across the Red Sea and Horn of Africa appeared first on WardheerNews .

items.title: Baidoa War Deepens as Former South West President Laftagareen Accuses Hassan Sheikh, Aden Madoobe and Turkey of Targeting the Region
items.description: Baidoa (WDN) — Somalia’s political crisis has increasingly taken on the character of an armed confrontation in and around Baidoa, with forces aligned with former South West State President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen accusing the Federal Government of using national security forces and Turkish military support to consolidate control over the regional capital. The latest accusations came from Ugaas Hassan Mohamed, spokesperson for Laftagareen-aligned forces, who launched a strong attack on President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, South West State President Aden Mohamed Nur (Aden Madoobe) and Turkey over their roles in the unfolding conflict. Ugaas Hassan accused the Federal Government and the current South West State leadership of treating communities that support Laftagareen as adversaries, alleging that military operations and reported airstrikes have increasingly affected communities around Baidoa. He also claimed that authorities were pressuring residents to support Turkey and alleged that President Hassan Sheikh intends to expand the Turkish military presence in Baidoa, including the use of F-16 aircraft and drones. The allegations have not been independently verified, and neither the Federal Government nor Turkey has publicly confirmed the specific claims concerning air operations against civilian areas. The dispute itself, however, reflects a much deeper struggle over the political future of South West State. Laftagareen lost control of the South West presidency following the political and military developments that brought Aden Madoobe to power. Since then, Laftagareen has remained a powerful opposition figure, with his supporters rejecting the legitimacy of the current regional administration and resisting what they describe as federal interference in South West State affairs. The confrontation has therefore evolved beyond a conventional dispute between rival politicians. It has become a struggle between the Federal Government and its allies in Baidoa on one side, and Laftagareen’s political and armed supporters on the other. For residents caught in the middle, the distinction between political rivalry and military confrontation has become increasingly difficult to ignore. Growing Allegations Over Turkish Military Support The most controversial element of the conflict is the alleged role of Turkey. Laftagareen’s supporters accuse Ankara of providing military assistance to federal and South West forces operating against them, including alleged air support. Turkish involvement has become particularly contentious because Ankara has traditionally presented its security partnership with Somalia as support for national institutions and the fight against Al-Shabaab. If foreign military capabilities are perceived by local communities as being used in an internal political confrontation, the consequences could extend well beyond Baidoa. It could deepen resentment toward both the Federal Government and Turkey while making an already complicated political settlement considerably more difficult. “We Will Resist” Ugaas Hassan said forces aligned with Laftagareen would continue resisting what he described as an externally supported military campaign. “As long as our South West Darawiish forces remain capable and ready to confront the forces that have invaded our territory—with Aden Madoobe and Hassan Sheikh leading them and Turkey providing air support—we will, God willing, drive them out,” he said. He also described Turkey as a company allegedly “hired” by President Hassan Sheikh and warned residents of South West State against what he characterized as Ankara’s growing involvement. The comments demonstrate how sharply the political narrative has shifted. A dispute that initially centered on regional leadership and federal authority has increasingly become intertwined with military power and foreign security assistance. Civilians Caught in the Middle For ordinary residents around Baidoa, the political arguments between Mogadishu, the Aden Madoobe administration and Laftagareen’s camp are increasingly being experienced through insecurity, displacement and disruption to daily life. The central question is no longer simply who has the stronger political claim to South West State. It is whether the dispute can be resolved politically before the confrontation causes further damage to civilians and institutions. For the Federal Government, the challenge is to demonstrate that its military presence is directed toward legitimate national security objectives rather than political consolidation. For Laftagareen and his supporters, the challenge is to translate their opposition into a credible political strategy capable of competing for legitimacy without further destabilizing the region. Until that happens, Baidoa is likely to remain at the center of one of Somalia’s most dangerous political confrontations—one in which the struggle for regional power increasingly carries consequences far beyond the political arena. items.title: Somaliland’s president puts everything on the table for Trump
items.description: Somaliland’s president is putting almost everything on the table in his campaign to win US recognition for the breakaway territory of Somalia, offering US investors access to a strategically located port and mineral resources while leaving open the possibility of expanded military access.ĺ “We are not giving anything for free,” Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi “Irro” said in an interview with Semafor in Washington. “We have to offer something. And we expect the other partner [to have] the same or equal opportunities.” Recognition is the prize, but economic cooperation, trade and investment can proceed in parallel. Somaliland can offer “our facilities and our minerals,” he said. The US already has a military relationship with Somaliland, including training and security cooperation, but no military base there. The head of US Africa Command visited Hargeisa and Berbera last year as Washington continued to assess the territory’s strategic importance. Irro is signaling that the relationship could go further. Military access for the US, Israel or other countries, he said, “is a negotiation.” “I will not rule out,” he said of a future base agreement, arguing that any deal would depend on what Somaliland receives in return, including greater security and support for its forces. Israel’s recognition in December changed the diplomatic equation on Somaliland’s status. It gave the breakaway territory its first recognition from a UN member state and, more importantly, demonstrated that the decades-old consensus against recognizing the territory could be broken. Irro is now trying to turn that breakthrough into momentum. He is spending this week in Washington pressing his case at the White House and on Capitol Hill before heading to New York, where he hopes to meet other world leaders during the UN General Assembly and make the case for recognition. The US is the next prize. Irro described America as the “big fish” Somaliland wants to pursue. “The earlier, the better is always better,” he said. His appeal is also tailored to Trump. Somaliland could name Berbera’s airport after him, Irro suggested, or welcome him to build a Trump Tower in Hargeisa. The message underneath the flattery is more consequential since Somaliland is no longer simply making a historical or moral case for recognition. Irro is trying to show Washington what recognition could buy. Room for Disagreement Somalia sees the proposition very differently. Mogadishu rejects Somaliland’s claim to sovereignty and considers Berbera, its coastline and its resources part of Somalia. That makes Irro’s offer of strategic and commercial access politically contested before any foreign government or company accepts it. Israel’s recognition has sharpened that dispute, turning Somaliland’s push for wider recognition into a more consequential challenge to Somalia’s territorial claims. Know More Geography is central to Irro’s proposition. Berbera sits on the Gulf of Aden, close to the Bab el-Mandeb, the narrow maritime gateway between the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean. As conflict and disruption have put renewed pressure on the region’s sea lanes, Somaliland sees an opportunity to turn its location into diplomatic leverage. Diego Garcia, the US military facility in the central Indian Ocean, lies thousands of kilometers away from the Red Sea theater. Berbera offers a far closer location for logistics, resupply or other military operations around the Gulf of Aden and Bab el-Mandab, even if it would not simply replace the much larger US presence on Diego Garcia. Irro argued that American officials understand that strategic case. “They know that,” he said, pointing to US training and security cooperation already taking place in Somaliland. His offer is deliberately open-ended. Somaliland is not announcing a new US base; it is signaling that greater access could be negotiated. “We are not giving anything for free,” Irro said, returning to the transactional logic behind his recognition campaign. Step Back Irro is also trying to sell Somaliland as an economic opportunity rather than simply a strategic outpost. He points to Berbera’s port and free zone, an 850-kilometer coastline, fisheries and potentially significant oil, gas and mineral resources. Somaliland’s government budget has risen from less than $50 million when he became parliament speaker in 2005 to about $500 million today, he said. The ambition is considerably bigger. Irro said Somaliland could be “very rich” within a decade and claimed its budget could eventually reach $3 billion-$4 billion a year if its marine economy and other resources are developed. Recognition, in his view, would help unlock that potential by making it easier for US and other international investors to treat Somaliland as a conventional investment destination rather than an unrecognized territory. The View From China Irro’s push for US recognition does not mean he wants Somaliland locked into a single geopolitical camp. Taiwan’s representative office will remain in Hargeisa despite Beijing’s opposition. “We have decided Taiwan to remain,” Irro said, noting that Taiwan was already present when he took office. China is still welcome to invest. “If China is coming without condition, we will welcome China,” he said. Chinese companies already operate in Somaliland, he added. The line Irro draws is political saying no foreign power will decide Somaliland’s diplomatic relationships. “Nobody can dictate to us,” he said. SEMAFOR

items.title: Soomaaliya oo si adag u cambaareysay weerar diyaaradeed oo la isku dayay in lagu qaado Makkah
items.description: Muqdisho, 16 Sebtembar 2026 — Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa si adag u cambaareysay isku day weerar loo adeegsaday diyaarad aan duuliye lahayn (drone), kaas oo lagu beegsaday magaalada barakeysan ee Makkah Al-Mukarramah ee Boqortooyada Sacuudiga. Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah ee Soomaaliya ayaa sheegtay in Ciidamada Difaaca Cirka ee Boqortooyada Sacuudiga ay ku guuleysteen inay dhexda u galaan oo ay qabtaan diyaaraddii aan duuliyaha lahayn ka hor inta aysan gaarin magaalada Makkah. Soomaaliya ayaa sidoo kale cambaareysay weerarradii dhowaan lagu qaaday goobaha rayidka ah ee gudaha Boqortooyada Sacuudiga. War-saxaafadeedka Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda ayaa lagu sheegay in Soomaaliya ay muujineyso garab istaag buuxa oo ay la garab taagan tahay Boqortooyada Sacuudiga, iyadoo xaqiijisay xaqa Boqortooyada ay u leedahay inay ilaaliso dhulkeeda, dadkeeda iyo goobaha barakeysan ee Islaamka.

items.title: Baidoa’s Pro-Türkiye Rally Raises Questions as Ankara’s Image in Somalia Comes Under Strain
items.description: Baidoa (WDN) — Three days after reports of alleged Turkish airstrikes around Baidoa—and less than two weeks after anti-Türkiye protests erupted elsewhere in Somalia—a crowd gathered in the city on Tuesday, September 15, waving Turkish flags and praising Ankara. The timing could hardly be more striking. Hundreds of people gathered at Dr. Ayuub Stadium, carrying Turkish and Somali flags and expressing support for the longstanding relationship between Somalia and Türkiye. Organizers described the event as a demonstration of gratitude for Turkish assistance in security, development and humanitarian affairs. But the rally took place against a dramatically changed political backdrop. On September 12, reports emerged of alleged Turkish airstrikes around Baidoa, including claims of casualties and damage. The reports have not been independently verified, and neither Türkiye nor the Federal Government has publicly confirmed responsibility. The demonstration also came less than two weeks after the September 3–4 Doolow incident, when Jubaland officials accused Turkish aircraft of striking the residence of former Somali security commander General Mahad Abdirahman “Taliye Shub.” The allegations triggered protests in several parts of Somalia, including demonstrations in which Turkish flags were reportedly burned. The Federal Government disputed elements of the account, while Türkiye has not publicly acknowledged responsibility for the alleged strike. Critics question whether Tuesday’s gathering represented spontaneous public enthusiasm or a politically organized effort to demonstrate that Ankara still enjoys popular support. Some political opponents allege that former Speaker Sheikh Aden Mohamed Nur “Aden Madoobe” and political allies associated with the current South West administration helped organize or finance the rally. The allegation is politically significant because Turkish military assistance has become increasingly entangled with the confrontation surrounding Baidoa and the forces aligned with the Federal Government. There is, however, no independent evidence publicly establishing that Aden Madoobe personally financed the demonstration. The claim should therefore be treated as an allegation rather than an established fact. A Relationship Under Pressure For years, Türkiye enjoyed an unusually positive image in Somalia. Erdoğan’s visits, Turkish humanitarian assistance, infrastructure projects, scholarships, health services and military cooperation helped establish Ankara as one of Somalia’s most prominent international partners. The Turkish flag was widely associated with friendship and solidarity. That image is now under pressure. Protests and flag-burning incidents reported in recent weeks suggest that Türkiye’s military role has become increasingly controversial among sections of the Somali public. The dispute is no longer simply about development assistance or diplomatic relations. It is increasingly about whether Ankara has become involved in Somalia’s internal political and security conflicts. That distinction matters. Türkiye has trained Somali forces, provided military equipment and developed an extensive defense relationship with the Federal Government. Turkish armed drones have also been associated with Somalia’s counterterrorism campaign. But when Turkish aircraft or drones are alleged to have been used in operations connected to domestic political confrontations, the perception of Ankara’s role changes. A security partnership can quickly become a political liability if communities begin to associate it with controversial military operations. Why Baidoa Is Different Baidoa is at the center of that controversy. The city has become a major arena in the confrontation between the Federal Government and forces associated with former South West President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen. As a result, Turkish military involvement in or around the region is being interpreted through an increasingly political lens. For Federal Government supporters, Ankara remains a strategic partner helping rebuild Somalia’s security institutions and combat Al-Shabaab. For opponents, the same military relationship has become evidence of foreign involvement in Somalia’s internal political struggle. The September 15 rally therefore carries significance beyond the crowd gathered at the stadium. Its timing raises questions about whether the demonstration was intended, at least in part, to counter the growing backlash against Türkiye and reinforce the image of a continuing Somalia–Türkiye partnership. The Bigger Question for Ankara A single demonstration cannot determine public opinion across Somalia. Nor can photographs of people waving Turkish flags erase the anger expressed in other parts of the country. The more consequential question is whether Türkiye can maintain its longstanding relationship with Somalia while avoiding the perception that it has become aligned with one side of the country’s increasingly polarized political landscape. That challenge is particularly acute because Türkiye’s influence in Somalia has been built on two pillars: development and security. The first created goodwill. The second now risks becoming the source of controversy. For Ankara, the distinction between supporting Somalia’s national security institutions and becoming involved in Somalia’s internal political disputes will therefore be increasingly important. For Mogadishu, the issue is equally sensitive. Foreign military assistance may strengthen the government’s capabilities, but if that assistance becomes identified with one faction in a domestic confrontation, it can deepen political divisions rather than resolve them. And for ordinary Somalis, the contrast is increasingly difficult to miss. In Baidoa, Turkish flags were raised on September 15. Elsewhere, they were burned. That is not simply a contradiction between two demonstrations. It is evidence of a relationship undergoing a profound political test. The Somalia–Türkiye friendship that once appeared almost unquestionable is now being debated in the streets—and its future may depend less on official speeches than on how Somalis perceive Ankara’s actions on the ground. items.title: Dhuumaha shidaalka Sacuudiga oo qaarkood waxyeello la gaarsiiyay
items.description: Riyadh (Caasimada Online) – Laba xarumood oo ku yaalla dhuumaha shidaalka ee isku xira bariga iyo galbeedka Sacuudiga ayaa waxyeello kasoo gaartay weerar toddobaadkii hore lagu qaaday, sida ay sheegtay Reuters oo soo xigatay ilo-wareedyo ka tirsan dhinacyada shidaalka iyo amniga. Dhuumahaasi oo dhererkoodu ku dhow yahay 1,200 oo kilomitir ayaa mara guud ahaan Jasiiradda Carabta, waxaana maamusha shirkadda Sacuudiga ee Aramco. Dhuumahan ayaa muhiimad gaar ah u leh dhoofinta iyo gaadiidka shidaalka Sacuudiga, maadaama ay shidaalka ka gudbiyaan bariga dalka, oo ah halka ugu weyn ee wax-soo-saarka, una gudbiyaan dhanka galbeed, si looga fogaado in maraakiibtu maraan Marinka Hormuz. Saddex ilo-wareed oo Reuters la hadashay ayaa sheegay in labada xarumood ay waxyeello kasoo gaartay weerarka, inkastoo aan si rasmi ah loo shaacin heerka uu gaarsiisan yahay khasaaraha soo gaaray kaabayaasha. Mas’uuliyiin Sacuudi ah ayaa horey u sheegay in shaqada dhuumaha si ku-meel-gaar ah loo hakiyay Jimcihii, kadib markii weerar loo adeegsaday diyaarad aan duuliye lahayn laga soo qaaday dhulka Ciraaq. Hakinta shaqada dhuumaha ayaa kusoo aadeysa xilli kaabayaasha shidaalka ee gobolka ay wajahayaan khataro amni oo sii kordhaya, gaar ahaan iyadoo ay socdaan xiisado saameynaya maraakiibta iyo isu-socodka shidaalka ee gobolka. Dhuumaha isku xira bariga iyo galbeedka Sacuudiga ayaa ah marin istiraatiiji ah oo dalka u saamaxaya inuu qayb ka mid ah shidaalkiisa u gudbiyo xeebaha Badda Cas, taas oo muhiim u ah yareynta ku-tiirsanaanta marinnada maraakiibta ee dhinaca Gacanka. Dhanka kale, Aramco iyo xafiiska warbaahinta dowladda Sacuudiga ayaan weli ka jawaabin codsi lagu weydiiyay baaxadda khasaaraha iyo muddada ay qaadan karto dayactirka xarumaha waxyeelloobay. Weerarkan ayaa kusoo aadaya xilli milatariga Sacuudiga uu la tacaalayo weerarro ay fulinayaan diyaarado aan duuliye lahayn oo ay Xuutiyiintu soo direen, iyadoo xiisadda u dhexeysa labada dhinac ay kasii dareyso. items.title: Beesha Xawaadle oo go’aanno culus soo saartay iyo dhismaha HirShabelle cusub
items.description: Beledweyne (Caasimada Online) – Beesha Xawaadle ayaa si cad uga hortimid doorashada la qorsheeyay in laga qabto maamulka HirShabelle, iyadoo dalbatay in la hakiyo doorashooyinka iyo tallaabooyinka la xiriira dhismaha maamulka HirShabelle. Go’aankan ayaa kasoo baxay kulan maalmo ka socday magaalada Beledweyne, kaas oo ay isugu yimaadeen waxgarad iyo siyaasiyiin ka tirsan beesha, waxaana diiradda lagu saaray xaaladda siyaasadeed ee Hiiraan iyo qaabka loo wajahayo dhismaha maamulka. War-murtiyeedka kasoo baxay kulanka ayaa lagu sheegay in aan la aqbali karin hannaan siyaasadeed oo laga hirgeliyo Hiiraan iyadoo aan heshiis laga gaarin, isla markaana aan la helin oggolaanshaha iyo ka qayb-galka bulshada deegaanka. Xoghayihii hore ee maamulka gobolka Banaadir, Xiirey Axmed Rooble oo war-murtiyeedka la wadaagay warbaahinta ayaa sheegay in beesha Xawaadle aysan taageerayn hannaan siyaasadeed oo laga sameeyo gobolka haddii aysan qayb ka ahayn bulshada reer Hiiraan. Beesha ayaa sidoo kale ku baaqday in dhismaha HirShabelle saddexaad lagu saleeyo hannaan loo dhan yahay, kaas oo dhinacyada kala duwan ay ku wada qanacsan yihiin, laguna xaqiijinayo caddaalad, matalaad iyo awood-qaybsi. “Waa in la joojiyo dhammaan doorashooyinka iyo habraacyada aan ku dhisnayn heshiiska iyo oggolaanshaha bulshada,” ayaa lagu yiri mid ka mid ah qodobada war-murtiyeedka. Waxgaradka Xawaadle ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in tabashooyinka reer Hiiraan loo baahan yahay in si dhab ah loo qaado, iyadoo xalkeedana lagu raadinayo wada-tashi iyo is-afgarad siyaasadeed, halkii la sii wadi lahaa tallaabooyin ay bulshadu ka biyo diidan tahay. War-murtiyeedka ayaa intaas ku daray in maamulka HirShabelle ee ka howlgala Hiiraan uu tixgeliyo go’aannada kasoo baxay waxgaradka, isla markaana uu isu diyaariyo geeddi-socod cusub oo lagu dhisayo maamul loo dhan yahay. Sidoo kale, beesha ayaa digniin ka bixisay wax kasta oo qalalaase ama gacan-ka-hadal ah oo ka dhasha doorasho aan heshiis lagu ahayn, iyadoo sheegtay in mas’uuliyadda wixii arrintaas kasoo baxa ay qaadi doonaan guddiga doorashooyinka. Ugu dambeyn, Xawaadle ayaa ku adkaysatay in aan la dhisi karin HirShabelle waarta iyadoo la iska indha tirayo tabashooyinka iyo rabitaanka bulshada reer Hiiraan, waxayna beesha ku baaqday in la dedejiyo hannaan cusub oo lagu dhisayo maamul ka duwan kan hadda jira. items.title: Sacuudi Carabiya oo Digniin ‘Khad Cas’ ah ka Bixisay Kadib Markii Drone Xuutiyiintu Leeyihiin Lagu Soo Riday Meel u Dhow Maka
items.description: Maka (WDN) — Sacuudi Carabiya ayaa ku dhawaaqday in amniga labada goobood ee ugu barakada badan Islaamka iyo amniga xujeydu ay yihiin “khad cas”, kadib markii ciidamada difaaca cirka Sacuudigu maalintii Salaasada burburiyeen diyaarad aan duuliye lahayn oo ay sheegeen inay Xuutiyiintu leeyihiin. Arintaas oo ka dhacday koonfurta magaalada Maka ka hor inta aysan gelin hawada xaddidan ee magaalada barakaysan. Afhayeenka isbahaysiga milatari ee Sacuudigu hoggaamiyo, Turki al-Malki, ayaa sheegay aroornimadii Arbacada in Sacuudi Carabiya ay qaadi doonto tallaabooyin lagama maarmaan ah oo lagaga hortegayo laguna joojinayo weerarro kale oo noocan ah. “Amniga labada goobood ee barakaysan ee Islaamka iyo badqabka xujeydu waa khad cas,” ayuu yiri al-Malki, isaga oo uga digay Xuutiyiinta in isbahaysigu qaadi doono tallaabooyin looga hortagayo khatar kasta oo soo wajahda goobahaas. Maka, oo ay ku yaallaan goobaha ugu barakada badan Muslimiinta adduunka, ayaa ah magaalada ugu barakada badan Islaamka, sidoo kalena waa xarunta xajka sannadlaha ah ee ay malaayiin Muslimiin ahi sannad kasta u soo xajiyaan. Xajkuna waa mid ka mid ah shanta tiir ee Islaamka. Sacuudiga: Tani Waa Isku Daygii Labaad ee Lagu Beegsanayo Makka Al-Malki wuxuu sheegay in dhacdadan ay tahay isku daygii labaad ee Xuutiyiintu ay ku doonayaan inay beegsadaan magaaalada Maka, isaga oo tusaalle u soo qaatay gantaal ballistic ah oo isbahaysiga Sacuudigu hoggaamiyo sheegay in Xuutiyiintu ku rideen dhanka Makka bishii Luulyo 2017. Hase yeeshee, Xuutiyiintu waxay si adag u diideen eeddaas. Afhayeenka kooxda, Hazem al-Assad, ayaa Arbacadii qoraal uu ku daabacay barta X-  ku sheegay in sheegashada ah in Maka la beegsaday ay tahay “been duugowday” oo hore loo adeegsaday, isaga oo intaas ku daray in aanay cidna mar dambe ku qancinayn. Ururka Iskaashiga Islaamka oo Cambaareeyay Weerarka Ururka Iskaashiga Islaamka (OIC) ayaa cambaareeyay waxa uu ku tilmaamay weerar “foosha xun” oo lagu qaaday magaalada barakaysan ee Makka, isaga oo mas’uuliyadda weerarka dusha ka saaray Xuutiyiinta. Ururka oo ay xubno ka yihiin 57 dal oo Muslimiin u badan ayaa sidoo kale cambaareeyay waxa uu ku tilmaamay “gardarrada joogtada ah” ee ka dhanka ah Boqortooyada Sacuudi Carabiya. Cambaareynta OIC ayaa kusoo beegmaysa xilli gobolka Bariga Dhexe uu wajahayo xiisado militari oo sii kordhaya, iyadoo weerarrada kooxaha xiriirka la leh Iran ay Sacuudi Carabiya si isa soo taraysa ugu riixayaan gudaha dagaalka gobolka. Sacuudi Carabiya oo Soo Saartay Digniino Amni Sacuudi Carabiya ayaa Salaasadii soo saartay digniino amni oo laga bixiyay qaybo ka mid ah dalka, oo ay ku jirto Makka iyo magaalooyin kale, kadib toddobaad ay jireen weerarro isdaba joog ah oo ay qaadeen kooxo xiriir la leh Iran. Weerarradaasi ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli Xuutiyiintu ay sheegteen inay qabsadeen qaybo ka mid ah xeebaha Badda Cas ee Yemen, oo ay ku yaallaan jasiirado istiraatiiji ah oo dhinaca Bab al-Mandab ka eegaya. Bab al-Mandab waa mid ka mid ah marin-biyoodka ugu muhiimsan dunida ee maraakiibtu isticmaalaan, waxaana muhiimad gaar ah u leh ganacsiga caalamiga ah iyo dhoofinta shidaalka ee gobolka. Xuutiyiintu waxay sidoo kale toddobaadkan ku dhawaaqeen dhowr weerar oo waaweyn oo ay ku qaadeen gudaha Sacuudi Carabiya. Waxaa ka mid ahaa weerar ay Isniintii sheegeen inay ku qaadeen saldhig diyaaradeed, iyaga oo ku andacooday inuu ahaa aargoosi ay kaga jawaabayeen duqeymo cirka ah oo lagu qaaday Yemen. Maraykanka oo Digniin Safar Soo Saaray Safaaradda Maraykanka ee Sacuudi Carabiya ayaa kadib digniinaha amni soo saartay tallo ku aaddan in muwaadiniinta Maraykanku “dib uga fiirsadaan safarrada” ay ku tagayaan Sacuudi Carabiya. Digniinta ayaa lagu sheegay in ay jiraan khataro la xiriira weerarro ay Iran u adeegsan karto diyaaraddaha aan duuliyaha lahayn iyo gantaallada, khataraha ku wajahan danaha Maraykanka, iska horimaadyo hubaysan, argagixisanimo, xannibaad safar iyo xeerarka maxalliga ah ee la xiriira isticmaalka baraha bulshada. Safaaradda ayaa sidoo kale muwaadiniinta Maraykanka uga digtay inay u safraan xuduudda Yemen, iyadoo sabab uga dhigtay khatar argagixisanimo. Xiisadda oo Saameynaysa Badda Cas iyo Dhoofinta Shidaalka Xuutiyiinta ayaa sheegtay inay gacanta ku dhigeen qaybo ka mid ah xeebaha Yemen ee Badda Cas, taas oo siinaysa kooxda meel istiraatiiji ah oo ay kaga dhowaan karto Bab al-Mandab. Haddii xaaladdu sii xumaato, waxay saameyn ku yeelan kartaa isu-socodka maraakiibta ganacsiga iyo dhoofinta shidaalka ee Sacuudi Carabiya, gaar ahaan kuwa loo weeciyo waddooyin kale si looga fogaado marin-biyoodka Hormuz. Xuutiyiintu waxay toddobaadkan kordhiyeen hanjabaadaha iyo weerarrada ay ku sheegayaan inay ku qaadayaan Sacuudi Carabiya, iyagoo ku andacoonaya inay uga jawaabayaan duqeymaha cirka ah ee ka socda Yemen. Sacuudi Carabiya, dhankeeda, waxay sheegtay in difaaca dhulkeeda, goobaha barakaysan iyo amaanka dadka rayidka ah ay yihiin mudnaanta koowaad. Dhacdada drone-ka ee ku dhow Makka ayaa sidaas darteed kusoo beegmaysa xilli Bariga Dhexe uu wajahayo xaalad amni oo sii cakirmaysa, iyadoo dagaallada iyo iska horimaadyadu ay si isa soo taraysa ugu fidayaan xuduudaha dalalka gobolka. Sacuudi Carabiya waxay hadda si cad u sheegtay in Makka iyo goobaha kale ee barakaysan aysan ahayn meel loo dulqaadan doono weerar kasta—iyadoo dhacdadan cusub ay kordhinayso walaaca laga qabo in dagaalka gobolka uu gaaro meelaha ugu xasaasisan ee dunida Islaamka. items.title: Saudi Arabia warns of ‘red line’ after Houthi drone intercepted close to holy city of Mecca
items.description: Mecca – (WDN) – The Iran-aligned militant group rejected the suggestion it had targeted Mecca, while the Organization of Islamic Cooperation condemned the attack. Saudi Arabia’s air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ⁠Houthi drone south of Mecca on Tuesday before it entered prohibited airspace over the holy city, according to a ⁠spokesperson for the ⁠Saudi-led ​military coalition which is fighting the Iran-aligned group in Yemen . The security of Islam’s two holiest sites and of pilgrims was a “red line”, ⁠coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said early on Wednesday, adding that the coalition would take necessary deterrent measures against the ⁠Houthis. Mecca, home to shrines sacred to Muslims worldwide, is Islam’s holiest ​city and the focal point ‌of the annual ‌hajj pilgrimage, one of the five pillars of Islam, which millions of Muslims ‌undertake each year. Malki described the incident as the second Houthi attempt to target Mecca, after what the coalition said was a ballistic missile launch in July 2017. A Houthi official rejected the claim on Wednesday, with spokesperson Hazem al-Assad writing on X: “The claims about targeting Mecca are a worn-out lie that has been used before and no longer fools anyone.” The Organization of Islamic Cooperation condemned what they called a “heinous” attack on Islam’s holy city, blaming the Houthis. The group – which is made up of 57 Muslim-majority countries decried the “ongoing aggression against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia .” Saudi Arabia issued security alerts across parts of the country on Tuesday, including in Mecca and other ‌cities, following a week of attacks by Iran-aligned fighters that have drawn the kingdom deeper into the Middle East ​war. The US embassy issued an advisory to “reconsider travel” to Saudi Arabia after the alerts in Mecca and other areas amid Houthi attacks. The advisory warns of the “risk of Iranian drone and missile targeting of American interests, armed conflict, terrorism, exit bans and local laws regarding social media activity,” adding “Do Not Travel to the Yemen border due to threat of terrorism.” The Houthis have seized control of parts of ⁠Yemen’s Red Sea coast overlooking the Bab al-Mandab, one of the ​world’s most important ​shipping straits, threatening Saudi oil ​exports rerouted from the strait of Hormuz. The group has ​announced several major ‌attacks on ​Saudi Arabia over ​the past week, including strikes on an airbase on Monday that it said were retaliation for airstrikes on Yemen. A Houthi official rejected the claim on Wednesday, with spokesperson Hazem al-Assad writing on X: “The claims about targeting Mecca are a worn-out lie that has been used before and no longer fools anyone.” The Organization of Islamic Cooperation condemned what they called a “heinous” attack on Islam’s holy city, blaming the Houthis. The group – which is made up of 57 Muslim-majority countries decried the “ongoing aggression against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia .” Saudi Arabia issued security alerts across parts of the country on Tuesday, including in Mecca and other ‌cities, following a week of attacks by Iran-aligned fighters that have drawn the kingdom deeper into the Middle East ​war. The US embassy issued an advisory to “reconsider travel” to Saudi Arabia after the alerts in Mecca and other areas amid Houthi attacks. The advisory warns of the “risk of Iranian drone and missile targeting of American interests, armed conflict, terrorism, exit bans and local laws regarding social media activity,” adding “Do Not Travel to the Yemen border due to threat of terrorism.” The Houthis have seized control of parts of ⁠Yemen’s Red Sea coast overlooking the Bab al-Mandab, one of the ​world’s most important ​shipping straits, threatening Saudi oil ​exports rerouted from the strait of Hormuz. The group has ​announced several major ‌attacks on ​Saudi Arabia over ​the past week, including strikes on an airbase on Monday that it said were retaliation for airstrikes on Yemen. items.title: Puntland Orders Occupants to Vacate Government Land and Buildings
items.description: Galkayo (WDN) — The Puntland Government has ordered people occupying government-owned land and buildings to vacate the properties and make alternative housing arrangements, as the administration moves to reclaim and protect public assets intended for government institutions and essential public services. Puntland Minister of Public Works, Transport and Housing Farah Awad made the announcement on Wednesday in Galkayo, saying the government had completed a comprehensive inventory of vacant government land and public buildings across Puntland. According to the minister, the properties have been formally surveyed and their locations recorded using GPS technology, creating a centralized record of government-owned assets and their exact locations. Farah said the government would soon present the inventory to the Puntland Cabinet, which is expected to review the properties and establish a legal framework governing their protection, management and future use. The minister stressed that government land and buildings are public assets, not private property, and are reserved for institutions that provide services to citizens. He warned that individuals would not be permitted to occupy, settle on or otherwise appropriate government-owned land without legal authorization. The move is expected to form part of a broader effort by the Puntland administration to strengthen the management of public property, prevent illegal occupation and ensure that government institutions have adequate land and facilities from which to deliver essential services. Nevertheless, any government claim over public assets should be pursued through proper legal and institutional procedures, particularly amid continuing concerns over the illegal appropriation and transfer of public land in Mogadishu during President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s administration. In many parts of Puntland, government-owned properties have historically faced pressure from informal settlement, private occupation and competing claims of ownership. Such disputes can make it difficult for the government to expand schools, hospitals, administrative offices, security facilities and other public infrastructure. By documenting government properties through a formal inventory and GPS mapping, the administration appears to be seeking to establish a clearer record of public ownership and reduce future disputes. Minister Farah urged those currently occupying government-owned land and buildings to vacate the properties promptly and make alternative arrangements for accommodation, stressing that the government would not accept further unauthorized settlement on public land. The issue is likely to be particularly important in rapidly growing cities such as Galkayo, Garowe and Bosaso, where demand for land is increasing while government institutions require additional space to expand public services. The minister’s announcement also places greater emphasis on the principle that government property ultimately belongs to the public and should be preserved for public purposes. Once the inventory is presented to the Cabinet and the proposed regulations are adopted, Puntland will face the more difficult task of enforcing the new framework fairly and transparently. For the administration, however, the message is clear: government land and buildings are public assets intended to serve the public, and unauthorized occupation will no longer be treated as an acceptable use of state property. items.title: Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga Soomaaliya oo ka qaybgalay Madasha 13-aad ee Beijing Xiangshan
items.description: Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga Xukuumadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Mudane Axmed Macallin Fiqi, iyo wafdi uu hoggaaminayo ayaa maanta ka qaybgalay munaasabadda furitaanka Madasha 13-aad ee Beijing Xiangshan, oo ka socota magaalada Beijing ee Jamhuuriyadda Dadka Shiinaha. Madashan oo socota 15–17 Sebtembar 2026 waxaa ka qaybgalaya madaxda iyo saraakiisha difaaca, khubaro iyo wakiillo ka socda ku dhowaad 100 dal iyo hay’ado caalami ah. Hal-ku-dhigga madasha sanadkan waa “Dhisidda Is-afgarad ku saabsan Xasilloonida iyo Wadajir u Horumarinta Maamulka Amniga.” Ajandayaasha madasha waxaa ka mid ah xasilloonida istiraatiijiyadeed, amniga caalamiga ah, xal u helidda colaadaha gobollada, amniga Aasiya iyo Baasifigga, amniga badaha, iyo khataraha ka dhasha adeegsiga teknoolojiyadda cusub iyo sirdoonka macmalka ah ee dhinaca milatariga. Sidoo kale, waxaa madasha barbar socda Madasha 4-aad ee Nabadda iyo Amniga Shiinaha iyo Afrika, taas oo diiradda lagu saarayo arrimaha nabadda iyo amniga qaaradda Afrika.

items.title: Guddiga Doorashooyinka iyo Wasaaradda Haweenka oo ka wada hadlay qoondada haweenka
items.description: Guddiga Madax-Bannaan ee Doorashooyinka Qaranka iyo Soohdimaha ayaa maanta xarunta dhexe ee Guddiga kulan kula yeeshay Wasiirka Wasaaradda Haweenka iyo Arrimaha Qoyska, Marwo Khadiija Al-Makhsuumi, iyo masuuliyiin sare oo ay hoggaaminaysay. Kulanka ayaa diiradda lagu saaray ka-qaybgalka haweenka ee doorashooyinka, gaar ahaan ilaalinta qoondada haweenka ee 30%, iyo sidii loo xaqiijin lahaa ka-qaybgalka dadka baahiyaha gaarka ah qaba ee geeddi-socodka doorashooyinka. Kulankan oo daba socday wada-tashiyo hore, ayaa labada dhinac waxay dib ugu qiimeeyeen horumarka laga sameeyay ilaalinta qoondada haweenka iyo ka-qaybgalka dadka baahiyaha gaarka ah qaba, iyadoo sidoo kale laga wada hadlay tallaabooyinka lagu sii xoojin karo arrimahaasi. Ugu dambeyn, labada dhinac ayaa isku raacay in la xoojiyo wada-shaqeynta Guddiga iyo Wasaaradda, iyadoo la dhisayo guddi heer farsamo ah oo u xilsaaran isku-dubbaridka iyo ka wada shaqeynta arrimaha ay labada dhinac iska kaashan karaan, si loo sii xoojiyo horumarka laga gaaray ka-qaybgalka haweenka iyo dadka baahiyaha gaarka ah qaba ee doorashooyinka.

items.title: Somalia: Al-Shabaab ‘stronger than ever’ despite billions spent on AU missions
items.description: MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – In July, the U.S. Mission to the African Union announced that it would be cutting support for the United Nations Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS). This unit provides logistical support, food rations, fuel, and medical supplies for the African Union peacekeeping mission in Somalia. The cut, which takes effect on Dec. 31, marks the end of U.S. support for the peacekeeping mission, known as the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission. After two decades of military intervention in the anarchic war-torn Horn of Africa nation – intervention overwhelmingly paid for by the U.S. government – the al Qaeda-affiliated Islamist group al-Shabab is arguably stronger than ever. Analysts who spoke with Foreign Policy said the decision by the Trump administration to cut support for UNSOS and the African Union peacekeeping mission is partly due to this questionable result. “Despite the savior rhetoric of the past two decades, the international community has neither developed a strategy to defeat al-Shabaab,” wrote Abukar Arman, a political analyst and former Somali diplomat to the United States, in an email. “Nor have they ever executed anything in a coordinated way.” In March 2007, African Union (AU) peacekeepers from Uganda were deployed to the Somali capital, Mogadishu, to prop up a fragile transitional government battling armed Islamist rebels – most notably, al-Shabab. In the years that have followed, the AU peacekeeping force has managed to push al-Shabab out of major cities and urban areas across south-central Somalia, including Mogadishu. But despite these successes, the militant group still dominates most of rural south and central Somalia. In these areas, it has morphed from a guerilla movement into something akin to a shadow state. Since 2007, the United States has provided an estimated $3.6 billion to sustain consecutive African Union peacekeeping missions in Somalia, which includes nearly $2 billion sent through U.N. support offices and close to $1.6 billion in bilateral assistance to African countries contributing troops to Somalia, according to a recent U.S. congressional research assessment from July. But “the international community has focused on propping up a mission, while al-Shabab has focused on building a state,” according to Jethro Norman, a senior researcher with the Danish Institute for International Studies. Al-Shabab has formed a parallel government in the areas that it rules, with its own judiciary courts and tax system. Within this system, al-Shabab can raise somewhere between $100 million and $150 million a year from taxation, Norman said, while the Somali government’s own tax revenue runs at a little more than $250 million, most of it from Mogadishu port customs and donor transfers. “You have an insurgency that funds itself and a government that does not,” Norman said. With its revenue, al-Shabab has prioritized providing services to civilians. One result has been the near-total eradication of drugs and crime in areas that al-Shabab governs. Since the insurgency’s inception, its leaders have understood the importance of securing grassroots legitimacy while also adroitly navigating Somalia’s often-complex clan-based society. They have garnered support from local communities, especially in rural areas, while the Somali government has been ranked the country’s most corrupt government since 2006, according to Transparency International. Even in government-controlled areas such as Mogadishu, civilians flock to the sharia courts run by al-Shabab. Norman said that for many members of Somalia’s political class, defeating al-Shabab was not obviously in their interest. Regional leaders’ cooperation with the campaign “was shallow even at its high points,” he said, because they worried that a government victory against al-Shabab would confer a legitimacy needed to remove them from office. The presence of foreign forces on Somali soil has been controversial throughout history. The AU deployment was predated by an Ethiopian military intervention in December 2006. This intervention saw thousands of Ethiopian troops invade Somalia, eventually operating under the cover of U.S. drones. The George W. Bush administration aimed to overthrow the Islamic Courts Union (ICU), a coalition of sharia courts that had seized power in Somalia and which marked the first instance in the post-9/11 era of political Islam gaining a foothold on the African continent. Members of the current AU peacekeeping force, and the two against al-Shabab that preceded it, have been implicated in allegations of widespread human rights abuses and atrocities ranging from extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, massacres of civilians, and even using rape as a weapon of war. These allegations span decades, and without any justice or accountability, the public has turned against the AU peacekeepers. The Somali government, too, is seen as turning a blind eye. A textbook example was the 2024 Bulo-Mareer killings, in which African Union peacekeeping troops from Uganda brutally decapitated two local farmers in the agricultural town of Bulo-Mareer. The deaths sparked protests in the town, and local residents called on AU troops to leave. Al-Shabab responded by releasing a statement condemning the attack and vowing retaliation and vengeance for the killing of the civilians; the federal government has not yet addressed the situation two years on. Al-Shabab, meanwhile, is viewed by many Somalis as defending the country from foreign subjugation and occupation, and it follows in a nationalist tradition of armed religious resistance to foreign encroachment from colonial times. The group uses that history to incentivize young men to take up arms and join the insurgency. But it’s not just nostalgia tied to the 19th century that Al-Shabab utilizes, but also the more recent memory of the “global war on terror.” “Before December 2006, al-Shabab was a small and radical component of the Islamic Courts Union,” Norman said. Then the Ethiopian intervention came, with U.S. diplomatic and intelligence backing, followed by the American airstrikes. “Al-Shabab expanded by presenting itself as the resistance, and many who joined appear to have been moved by Ethiopian conduct rather than by commitment to al Qaeda’s broader ideological project,” he said. Another burning issue is that al-Shabab has retaken nearly all the territory that it lost in a 2022-2023 Somali army campaign. During a 2025 counter-offensive, insurgents came as close as 45 kilometers to the Somali capital, Mogadishu. Their blitzkrieg-style offensive forced one of Mogadishu’s key allies, Turkey, to deploy 500 extra troops to Somalia, including drone operators. That al-Shabab has since recovered that ground underscores that after two decades of combat and consecutive interventions, the group remains a factor and a potent threat. Following the U.S. announcement of ending support for the AU peacekeeping mission in Somalia, troops have begun the process of withdrawing. Burhakaba, located in the Bay region of Somalia, was the first town to see a troop withdrawal. It has been encircled and isolated by al-Shabab since 2014. Many more towns are expected to go through similar phases of withdrawal before the Trump administration’s Dec. 31 deadline. The uncertainty is made worse by the fact that there is no one other nation that can fill the United States’ void. Turkey can only provide air support, and it doesn’t have the capacity to replace the AU peacekeepers. Al-Shabab will wait patiently until the last foreign boots leave Somali soil, said Arman, the political analyst. A recent summit held by countries currently contributing troops to the African Union peacekeeping mission in Somalia saw several governments request an 18 month to 24 month extension – signaling uncertainty around whether Somali forces will be ready to take responsibility for the country’s security when the AU troops leave. “The one thing Al-Shabaab does well is filling vacuums when they present themselves,” Arman wrote. Contact us: info@somaliguardian.com

items.title: United States Welcomes Djibouti’s Signing of the Artemis Accords
items.description: United States Welcomes Djibouti’s Signing of the Artemis Accords Office of the Spokesman September 14, 2026 The Department of State congratulates the Republic of Djibouti on joining the Artemis Accords. Djibouti is the 72nd country to sign the Accords to date, pledging its commitment to the peaceful exploration of space. Djibouti’s Ambassador to the United States Mohamed Siad Douale signed the Accords on behalf of the Republic of Djibouti on September 14, 2026. NASA Deputy Administrator Matthew Anderson and State Department Assistant Secretary for African Affairs Frank Garcia witnessed and celebrated the signing at a ceremony at the Mary W. Jackson NASA Headquarters in Washington, D.C. items.title: Shirkii golaha Wasiirrada Somaliland iyo wixii lagaga hadlay
items.description: Fadhigii 75-aad ee Shirka Golaha Wasiirrada JSL oo uu Shir-guddoominayey Madaxweyne ku-xigeenka Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland ahna ku-simaha Madaxweynaha, Mudane Maxamed Cali Aw Cabdi ayaa maanta ka qabsoomay Qasriga Madaxtooyada Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland. Qodobbada lagaga wada hadlay Fadhiga 75-aad waxa ka mid ahaa: 𝟏. 𝐗𝐚𝐚𝐥𝐚𝐝𝐝𝐚 𝐆𝐮𝐮𝐝 𝐞𝐞 𝐀𝐦𝐧𝐢𝐠𝐚 𝐃𝐚𝐥𝐤𝐚: Wasiirka Arrimaha Gudaha iyo Amniga Qaranka JSL, Mudane Cabdalle Maxamed Carab, ayaa Golaha uga xog-warramay xaaladda amniga iyo xasilloonida dalka, isaga oo adkeeyey in sugidda amniga dalku uu yahay aasaaska xasilloonida, Qarannimada iyo horumarka Somaliland. Wasiirku waxa uu xaqiijiyey in guud ahaan xaaladda amni ee dalku ay wanaagsan tahay, isla markaana Hay’adaha Amniga Qaranku ay si buuxda ugu diyaarsan yihiin ilaalinta nabadda, kala dambaynta iyo midnimada qaranka, iyada oo la sii xoojinayo wada-shaqaynta Hay’adaha Qaranka ee amniga iyo feejignaanta bulshada JSL. 𝟐. 𝐐𝐚𝐛𝐲𝐨-𝐪𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐚𝐥𝐤𝐚 𝐗𝐞𝐞𝐫𝐤𝐚 𝐂𝐢𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐤𝐚 𝐀𝐬𝐥𝐮𝐮𝐛𝐭𝐚 𝐉𝐒𝐋: Wasiirka Wasaaradda Caddaalada JSL, Mudane Yoonis Axmed Yoonis iyo ku-xigeenka Garyaqaanka Guud, ahna ku-simaha, Mudane Garyaqaan Mubaarig Maxamuud Cabdi (Fallaag) ayaa Golaha faahfaahin ka siiyey muhimadda iyo ujeeddada Xeerka Ciidanka Asluubta JSL. Wasiirka Caddaaladda JSL waxa uu xusay in Wasaaraddu ay dhammaystirtay Xeerkan oo ah Xeer muhiim u ah Qaranka, Ciidanka Asluubtuna uu muddo dheer baahi weyn u qabay, maadaama uu yahay Xeer uu waajibiyey Dastuurka JSL qodobkiisa 124-aad. Wasiirku waxa uu iftiimiyey ujeeddada Xeerka, taasoo ah maamulka Ciidanka Asluubta, qeexitaanka qaab-dhismeedka, awoodaha, waajibaadkooda, masuuliyadaha, xuquuqaha, hannaanka dallacaadaha iyo anshax marinta xubnaha Ciidanka Asluubta. Wasiirku waxa uu Golaha ka codsaday in ay soo darsaan Qabyo-qoraalka Xeerka Ciidanka Asluubta JSL, taladoodana ku biiriyaan. 𝟑. 𝐑𝐨𝐨𝐛𝐚𝐛𝐤𝐚 𝐄𝐥 𝐍𝐢ň𝐨, 𝐬𝐚𝐚𝐦𝐚𝐲𝐧𝐭𝐚 𝐚𝐲 𝐤𝐮 𝐲𝐞𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐧 𝐤𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐚𝐧 𝐒𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝, 𝐢𝐲𝐨 𝐝𝐢𝐲𝐚𝐚𝐫-𝐠𝐚𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐠𝐚 𝐥𝐨𝐨𝐠𝐚 𝐛𝐚𝐚𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐲𝐚𝐡𝐚𝐲 𝐇𝐚𝐲’𝐚𝐝𝐚𝐡𝐚 𝐃𝐚𝐰𝐥𝐚𝐝𝐝𝐚 𝐞𝐞 𝐚𝐲 𝐤𝐡𝐮𝐬𝐚𝐲𝐬𝐨: Golaha Wasiirrada Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland ayaa ka arrinsaday roobabka la saadaalinayo ee ka dhasha saamaynta El Niño (dhacdo cimilo), iyo khataraha ay xaaladdaasi ku yeelan karto dalka, gaar ahaan deegaanka, xoolaha, beeraha iyo bulshada nugul. Wasiirka Deegaanka iyo Isbeddelka Cimilada, Mudane Cabdilaahi Cismaan (Geeljire) iyo Wasiirka Horumarinta Beeraha, Mudane Aadan Geedi Qayaad ayaa Golaha ka hor jeediyey warbixinno ku saabsan saamaynta El Niño, xaaladda cimilada iyo diyaar-garowga looga baahan yahay Hay’adaha ay khusayso, si loo yareeyo khataraha fatahaadaha, daadadka iyo waxyeellada ka dhalan karta roobabka xooggan. Dawladda Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland waxa ay bulshada ugu baaqaysaa feejignaan, diyaar-garow iyo wada-shaqayn, iyada oo hay’adaha ay khusayso lagu dhiirrigelinayo in ay qaadaan tallaabooyinka lagama maarmaanka ah ee lagula tacaalayo xaaladdan iyada ah. 𝟒. 𝐃𝐨𝐨𝐝𝐝𝐚 𝐆𝐨𝐥𝐚𝐡𝐚: 𝐒𝐚𝐚𝐦𝐚𝐲𝐧𝐭𝐚 𝐚𝐦𝐧𝐢, 𝐝𝐡𝐚𝐪𝐚𝐚𝐥𝐞 𝐢𝐲𝐨 𝐠𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐜𝐬𝐢 𝐞𝐞 𝐱𝐚𝐚𝐥𝐚𝐝𝐝𝐚 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐤𝐚 𝐁𝐚𝐛 𝐞𝐥-𝐌𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐛 𝐚𝐲 𝐤𝐮 𝐲𝐞𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐧 𝐤𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐨 𝐒𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝 Golaha Wasiirrada Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland ayaa maanta ka dooday saamaynta amni, dhaqaale iyo ganacsi ee xaaladda marinka Bab el-Mandeb iyo colaadaha Bariga Dhexe ayvku yeelan karaan Somaliland, gaar ahaan dhinacyada amniga badda, isu-socodka ganacsiga, dekedaha, iyo dhaqaalaha dalka. Goluhu waxa uu isla qaatay muhiimadda ay leedahay diyaar-garow Qaran, isku-duwidda Hay’adaha Dawladda ee ay khusayso iyo Qorshe midaysan oo lagula tacaalayo waxyeellada ka dhalan karta isbeddellada amni iyo dhaqaale ee gobolka, iyada oo la ilaalinayo xasilloonida, amniga iyo danaha mudnaanta u leh Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland.

items.title: R/W Xamza oo caddeeyey arrin la xiriirta dhaqaalaha DF ay siiso dowlad-goboleedyada
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Xukuumadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Xamza Cabdi Barre ayaa sheegay in Dowladda Federaalku aysan siyaasadeyn taageerada dhaqaale ee ay siiso dowlad-goboleedyada. Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ayaa shaaciyay in sanadkii 2025 uu ahaa sannadkii ay dhaqaalaha ugu badnaa la siiyay maamullada dalka, xilli dowlad-goboleedyada qaar uu khilaaf xooggan kala dhexeeyo dowladda dhexe. “Dowladdu ma aysan siyaasadeyn, mana siyaasadeyn doonto taageerada dhaqaale ee ay siiso dowlad-goboleedyada. Sanadka 2025 wuxuu ahaa sanadkii dhaqaalaha ugu badan la siiyey dowlad-goboleedyada,” ayuu yiri Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamza. Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ayaa hadalkan ka sheegay munaasabad lagu soo bandhigayay Warbixinta Dhaqaalaha Soomaaliya ee 2025, taas oo ay soo diyaarisay Wasaaradda Maaliyadda Xukuumadda Federaalka Soomaaliya. Warbixinta ayaa lagu soo bandhigay xaaladda guud ee dhaqaalaha dalka, horumarka la sameeyay intii lagu jiray 2025 iyo dib-u-habaynta hannaanka maaliyadda qaranka, iyadoo sidoo kale lagu soo qaaday isbeddellada ku yimid taageeradii dhaqaale ee Soomaaliya ka heli jirtay dibadda. Xamza Cabdi Barre ayaa sheegay in inkastoo ay jireen caqabado dhaqaale oo gudaha iyo dibadda ah, haddana adkaysiga shacabka Soomaaliyeed iyo dadaallada hay’adaha dowladda ay door ka qaateen sii socoshada kobaca dhaqaalaha dalka. Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ayaa Wasaaradda Maaliyadda ku bogaadiyey dadaallada ay ku bixisay horumarinta hannaanka maaliyadda qaranka, gaar ahaan kordhinta dakhliga gudaha iyo xoojinta daah-furnaanta iyo isla-xisaabtanka. Waxa uu sidoo kale tilmaamay muhiimadda ay leedahay in la sii wado dib-u-habaynta dhaqaalaha, lana hagaajiyo maamulka iyo maaraynta dhaqaalaha dalka, si loo xoojiyo awoodda dowladda ee dhinaca maaliyadda. Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamza ayaa sheegay in loo baahan yahay in la abuuro jawi ku habboon maalgashiga gudaha iyo kan dibadda, iyadoo la xoojinayo shuruucda iyo siyaasadaha hagaya dhaqaalaha iyo maalgashiga Soomaaliya. Hadalka Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ayaa ku soo beegmaya xilli Dowladda Federaalku ay waddo dib-u-habayn lagu xoojinayo dakhliga gudaha iyo nidaamka maaliyadda qaranka, iyadoo sidoo kale xoogga la saarayo sidii dhaqaalaha dalka looga dhigi lahaa mid si weyn ugu tiirsan ilaha gudaha. The post R/W Xamza oo caddeeyey arrin la xiriirta dhaqaalaha DF ay siiso dowlad-goboleedyada appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Announcement of New Visa Restriction Policy Targeting Foreign Nationals Involved in Race-Based Discrimination
items.description: Announcement of New Visa Restriction Policy Targeting Foreign Nationals Involved in Race-Based Discrimination and Incitement of Imminent Violence, as well as Uncompensated Land Seizures in South Africa Press Statement Marco Rubio, Secretary of State As stated in President Trump’s Executive Order (EO) 14204, “Addressing Egregious Actions of the Republic of South Africa,” the United States remains gravely concerned about racially motivated crime and government-sponsored discrimination occurring against the Afrikaners and other minority populations in South Africa, including race-based discriminatory legislation, threats of land expropriation without compensation, and incitement of racial violence through dehumanizing chants and slogans. The South African government has not adequately addressed the previously laid out concerns and so today, I am announcing a new visa restriction policy under Section 212(a)(3)(C) of the Immigration and Nationality Act targeting foreign nationals who are responsible for, or complicit in, the enactment or implementation of laws or policies that enable uncompensated land seizures, race-based discrimination, and/or the incitement of imminent violence against members of minority ethnic or racial groups in South Africa. The United States will not allow such behavior to go unchecked. These actions directly undermine peace, economic stability, and the rule of law, and they are incompatible with the pillars of America’s foreign policy. We once again strongly urge the South African government to quickly address these egregious actions. This visa restriction policy is pursuant to Section 212(a)(3)(C) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, which authorizes the Secretary of State to render inadmissible any alien whose entry into the United States “would have potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences for the United States.” Certain family members may also be covered by these restrictions.

items.title: China Warns Somaliland Over Support for Taiwan
items.description: MOGADISHU— China has warned Somaliland of “serious consequences” following President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, widely known as Irro, expressing support for Taiwan’s status as an independent country. The Chinese Embassy in Mogadishu said Beijing firmly opposes Somaliland’s position, reiterating that it regards Taiwan as part of China and Somaliland as part of Somalia. In a statement, the embassy accused Somaliland of violating the “One-China” principle and challenging China’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. “We firmly oppose this move,” the embassy said, urging Somaliland officials to recognize Beijing’s position on the Taiwan issue. It warned that what it described as crossing the “red line” on Taiwan could result in serious consequences. China’s ambassador to Somalia also reaffirmed Beijing’s support for Somalia’s territorial integrity, describing Somaliland as an inseparable part of Somali territory. The ambassador said China supports the Federal Government of Somalia and opposes actions aimed at dividing the country. The latest statements reflect Beijing’s continued opposition to Somaliland’s international efforts for recognition and its growing concern over ties between Somaliland and Taiwan. China has consistently maintained that Taiwan is part of its territory and has opposed any form of formal recognition of Taiwanese independence. items.title: Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya iyo Midowga Afrika oo Muqdisho ku soo gabagabeeyay kulamo ku saabsan la-dagaallanka argagixisada
items.description: Muqdisho, Soomaaliya – 16 Sebtembar 2026: La-taliyaha Amniga Qaranka ayaa maanta magaalada Muqdisho ku soo gabagabeeyay kulamo iyo wada-tashiyo muddo laba maalmood ah u dhexeeyay hay’adaha Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya iyo Xarunta La-dagaallanka Argagixisada ee Midowga Afrika. Kulanka gabagabada ah ayaa lagu qiimeeyay qodobadii looga hadlay kulamadii iyo wada-tashiyadii labada maalmood ee lasoo dhaafay, kuwaas oo diiradda lagu saaray xoojinta iskaashiga dhinacyada amniga iyo la-dagaallanka argagixisada. Wafdiga Xarunta La-dagaallanka Argagixisada ee Midowga Afrika ayaa uga mahadceliyay Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya, gaar ahaan Xafiiska Amniga Qaranka, soo dhaweynta iyo fududeynta kulamadii ay la yeesheen hay’adaha kala duwan ee dowladda. Sidoo kale, wafdiga ayaa bogaadiyay horumarka ay Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ka sameysay dadaallada la-dagaallanka argagixisada, iyagoo tilmaamay muhiimadda ay leedahay in la sii xoojiyo wada-shaqeynta iyo iskaashiga amni ee Soomaaliya iyo Midowga Afrika. Kulamadan ayaa qeyb ka ah dadaallada lagu xoojinayo iskaashiga hay’adaha Soomaaliya iyo kuwa Midowga Afrika, gaar ahaan dhinacyada amniga, la-dagaallanka argagixisada iyo is-dhaafsiga khibradaha.

items.title: Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamsa oo bogaadiyey horumarka iyo isbeddelka Dhaqaale ee la sameeyey
items.description: Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Xukuumadda Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Mudane Xamsa Cabdi Barre, ayaa ka qeyb galay munaasabad lagu soo bandhigayay Warbixinta Dhaqaalaha Soomaaliya ee sanadka 2025, oo ay soo diyaarisay Wasaaradda Maaliyadda Xukuumadda Federaalka Soomaaliya. Warbixinta ayaa lagu soo bandhigay xaaladda guud ee dhaqaalaha dalka, horumarka la sameeyay sanadkii 2025, dib-u-habaynta hannaanka maaliyadda Qaranka iyo isbeddellada ku yimid taageeradii dhaqaale ee dibadda ka imaan jirtay. Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ayaa sheegay in, inkastoo ay jireen caqabado dhaqaale oo gudaha iyo dibadda ah, haddana adkaysiga shacabka Soomaaliyeed iyo dadaalka hay’adaha Dowladda ay door muhiim ah ka qaateen sii socoshada kobaca dhaqaalaha dalka. Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamsa ayaa ku bogaadiyey Wasaaradda Maaliyadda dadaalka ay ku bixisay horumarinta hannaanka maaliyadda Qaranka, gaar ahaan kordhinta dakhliga gudaha, xoojinta daah-furnaanta, isla-xisaabtanka, iyo hagaajinta maamulka iyo maaraynta dhaqaalaha dalka. “Dowladdu ma aysan siyaasadeyn, mana siyaasadeyn doonto taageerada dhaqaale ee ay siiso Dowlad-goboleedyada. Sanadka 2025 wuxuu ahaa sanadkii dhaqaalaha ugu badan la siiyey Dowlad-goboleedyada,” ayuu yiri Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamsa Cabdi Barre. Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ayaa sidoo kale xusay muhiimadda ay leedahay in la sii ambaqaado dib-u-habaynta dhaqaalaha, lana abuuro jawi ku habboon maalgashi gudaha iyo mid dibadeed, iyada oo la xoojinayo shuruucda iyo siyaasadaha hagaya dhaqaalaha iyo maalgashiga.

items.title: Mursal ciise oo Taagan Albaabka Baarlamaanka Sweden
items.description: Mursal Isa oo ka tirsan xisbiga Miljöpartiet (MP) ayaa wajahaya fursad uu ku noqon karo xildhibaan ka tirsan Baarlamaanka Sweden, kaddib markii xisbigiisu dib u helay hal kursi oo ka tirsan gobolka Dalarna. Mursal Isa oo ka soo jeeda magaalada Borlänge ayaa ku jira kaalinta koowaad ee liiska musharraxiinta xisbiga, taas oo ka dhigaysa qofka hadda ugu dhow kursiga. Hase yeeshee, natiijada kama dambaysta ah waxaa go’aamin kara codadka qofka ee doorashada, iyadoo musharraxa labaad ee liiska, Maj Ardesjö oo ka soo jeeda Falun, ay sidoo kale leedahay fursad ay kaga horreyso. Isa ayaa sheegay in xaaladdu ay tahay mid aan weli la hubin, isla markaana uu sugayo natiijada codadka qofka. Miljöpartiet ayaa doorashadan ka sameeyay horumar guud ahaan Dalarna. Xisbiga ayaa dib ugu soo laabtay golaha gobolka, kaddib markii uu ka maqnaa tan iyo doorashadii 2022, waxaana sidoo kale uu kuraas ka helay golayaasha degmooyinka Avesta, Mora iyo Säter. Mursal Isa ayaa sheegay in arrimaha tamarta iyo fahamka sii kordhaya ee bulshada ee ku saabsan isbeddelka tamarta ay ka mid yihiin arrimaha uu aaminsan yahay inay gacan ka geysteen kororka taageerada xisbiga.
