items.title: From Somali Refugee to Labour Candidate: Sagal Abdi-Wali’s Remarkable Journey to Parliament
items.description: London (WDN) — In a remarkable story of resilience, opportunity and public service, the British Labour Party has selected Sagal Abdi-Wali, a Somali woman who arrived in Britain as a refugee as a child, as its candidate for the forthcoming by-election in Holborn and St Pancras. The by-election is scheduled for October 8, following the resignation of former Prime Minister Keir Starmer as the constituency’s Member of Parliament on September 1. Starmer had represented the seat since 2015. Sagal’s selection represents a remarkable milestone—not only in her personal journey, but also in the story of a Somali refugee who has risen through local public service to become a leading political figure in the very community that welcomed her family decades ago. She has lived in Camden for nearly 35 years and currently serves as Leader of Camden Council. First elected as a councillor in 2022, she became council leader in May 2026, making history as the first Black woman to hold the position. From Refugee to Community Leader Sagal’s family fled Somalia when she was a child and arrived in Britain as refugees in the early 1990s. Camden became their new home, providing the family with safety, shelter and an opportunity to rebuild their lives. “This place welcomed my family as refugees and gave us hope when we needed it most,” Sagal said. Those words now carry particular significance. The young refugee who once arrived seeking safety could soon return to the same community as its prospective representative in the British Parliament. Before entering elected politics, Sagal spent years working in community and charitable organizations and was involved in school governance. She also previously led the Labour Party organization in Holborn and St Pancras, building a long-standing relationship with the constituency. Her political career has therefore grown from years of community engagement rather than a sudden entry into public life. A Historic Opportunity If elected on October 8, Sagal would represent in Parliament the same Camden community that helped give her family a new beginning after they fled Somalia. Her story offers a powerful illustration of what political inclusion and opportunity can mean for refugee families. It is also a reminder that migration can produce not only people seeking refuge, but future community leaders, public servants and elected representatives. Sagal’s candidacy has already attracted political attention, including controversy over her background after Reform UK figure Zia Yusuf referred on social media to her being born in Somalia. But the central political contest will ultimately be decided by voters in Holborn and St Pancras. The Green Party is expected to mount a strong challenge for the seat, making the by-election a competitive contest. For the Somali community in Britain, however, Sagal’s candidacy carries a significance that extends beyond one constituency. A Somali refugee child arrived in Britain seeking safety. Three decades later, she is seeking a seat in the Parliament of the country that gave her family a new home. If voters elect her, Sagal Abdi-Wali’s journey from refugee to council leader—and potentially to Member of Parliament—will stand as a remarkable story of resilience, integration and public service. items.title: When Clan Becomes a Death Sentence: Somalia Must End Collective Punishment
items.description: By Abdisalam Ali Farah (Biligsey ) A person who grows up in a society where government, police and courts function properly would struggle to understand how an innocent man could be killed because two clans fought somewhere else. Yet in parts of Somalia where state authority remains weak, a person’s clan identity can still become a death sentence. Two Victims, One Dangerous Pattern The recent killings of Ahmed Shire Hussein, a Somali National Army soldier near Ceel Baraf in Middle Shabelle, and Ahmed Yusuf Haamey, a respected businessman and community elder in Gaalkayo, illustrate the human cost of collective revenge. Ahmed Shire was reportedly travelling toward Hiiraan while on leave when armed men intercepted him and two other soldiers. The other two were reportedly released, while Ahmed was killed. A video reportedly shows him pleading for his life and explaining that he was ill and travelling to see his family. Local reports have linked the killing to clan revenge, although the motive and responsibility remain unverified. Days earlier, Ahmed Yusuf Haamey was reportedly shot dead in Gaalkayo while on his way to evening prayers. Local reports have also linked his killing to clan revenge, although authorities have not confirmed the motive. The circumstances of both killings raise the same disturbing question: How can a person become a target for something he did not do? The answer lies in the dangerous logic of collective punishment—when an individual is targeted not because of his own actions, but because of his identity or association with a particular community. I remember living in Gaalkayo in the late 1990s, when clan disputes could quickly turn ordinary citizens into potential targets. When killings occurred, respected members of the affected communities—including doctors, engineers, intellectuals, businessmen and traditional elders—were sometimes placed under protection in hotels while elders negotiated settlements. They had committed no crime. Their only vulnerability was their association with the community involved in the conflict. That experience demonstrated a basic truth that remains relevant today: a clan is not an individual, and one person’s actions cannot make another person guilty. When justice gives way to revenge, the question changes from “Who committed the crime?” to “Who can we kill from the other clan?” That is not justice. It is collective punishment. The Most Dangerous Form of Revenge The practice becomes even more destructive when respected members of a community are deliberately targeted because their deaths are expected to cause greater pain. A doctor, engineer, teacher, businessman, intellectual, elder or community leader may have nothing to do with the original dispute. Yet his status can make him a more valuable target for those seeking retaliation. The objective is no longer accountability. It is intimidation, humiliation and revenge. The killing of Ahmed Yusuf Haamey is particularly painful because he was reportedly a respected businessman and community figure who was on his way to pray when he was attacked. He never reached the mosque. The reported killing of Ahmed Shire Hussein is equally disturbing. Although he was a soldier, reports indicate that he was travelling on leave and away from his military duties when he was intercepted. Whatever investigations ultimately establish, neither death should become justification for another. One innocent death cannot justify another. Islam Rejects Collective Guilt For Somali society, there is also a powerful religious principle that should guide the response to this problem: “No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.” The principle is straightforward. If one man commits murder, his brother is not the murderer. His neighbor is not the murderer. His clan member is not the murderer. The perpetrator must answer for his own actions. This principle should be central to Somalia’s efforts to rebuild justice, social cohesion and the rule of law. A Responsibility for Scholars and Elders Somali religious scholars have demonstrated that they can influence deeply rooted social practices. Their campaigns against harmful traditions, including female genital mutilation, have helped change public attitudes. They now face another important responsibility. They should speak with the same clarity against the killing of war-ma-qabto—people who have nothing to do with the dispute for which they are being punished. Traditional elders have an equally important role. The constructive elements of xeer—mediation, compensation, reconciliation and dialogue—should be strengthened. But traditional authority must never become a justification for killing innocent people. Elders should make one principle unmistakable: If you know who committed the crime, pursue the perpetrator. Do not manufacture another victim. The State Must Restore Individual Protection Ultimately, the long-term solution requires a functioning state. Where police cannot protect citizens, courts cannot reliably prosecute criminals and government authority does not extend effectively into communities, people naturally fall back on clan protection. That is how collective punishment survives. Somalia’s state-building challenge is therefore not simply about ministries, elections and security forces. It is also about restoring something much more basic: the individual’s right to live without being punished for somebody else’s actions. The government must investigate the killings of Ahmed Shire Hussein and Ahmed Yusuf Haamey and bring those responsible to justice. Neither case should be allowed to trigger another cycle of revenge. The same responsibility falls on traditional elders, religious scholars and community leaders. They must reject the logic that says: “Someone from our clan was killed, therefore someone from their clan must die.” That logic has no place in a society trying to rebuild a state. From Collective Revenge to Individual Justice Somalia cannot permanently escape clan violence while collective guilt remains socially acceptable. The question must change. Not: “Who should we kill from Clan X?” But: “Who committed the crime?” That is the difference between revenge and justice. The deaths in Middle Shabelle and Gaalkayo should not become merely two more names added to Somalia’s long list of victims. They should be a warning that the country cannot build lasting peace while innocent people remain vulnerable to crimes committed by others. Let the perpetrator answer for the crime. Let the innocent live. That is not only the foundation of the rule of law. It is the foundation of a society worthy of peace. items.title: Israel Backs Ethiopia’s Bid for Red Sea Access, Raising New Regional Questions
items.description: ADDIS ABABA (WDN) — Israel has publicly backed Ethiopia’s long-running efforts to secure direct access to the Red Sea, marking a significant diplomatic development in a dispute that could reshape political and security dynamics across the Horn of Africa. Israel’s ambassador to Ethiopia, Avraham Neguise, said support for Ethiopia’s pursuit of maritime access was part of Israel’s official policy. He argued that Ethiopia’s access to the sea was not only an economic issue but also a matter of regional security, given the strategic importance of the Red Sea and its surrounding waterways. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, speaking during celebrations marking the country’s New Year, said Ethiopia’s campaign to secure maritime access had received international support, an apparent reference to Israel’s position. Ethiopia has sought reliable access to the sea for years, particularly since becoming landlocked following Eritrea’s independence in 1993. But the latest Israeli endorsement raises questions about where Addis Ababa may ultimately seek that access. It remains unclear whether Ethiopia’s long-term options will involve Somalia, Somaliland, Djibouti or Eritrea, and no new agreement determining a specific route has been confirmed. The issue is particularly sensitive for Somalia, which has strongly opposed arrangements it believes could undermine its sovereignty and territorial integrity. Israel’s intervention therefore comes at a delicate moment for the region, as competition over the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden and strategically located ports continues to intensify. The question now facing the Horn of Africa is not simply whether Ethiopia will secure maritime access, but where that access will be established and whether it can be achieved through agreements that respect the sovereignty and interests of neighboring states. This version keeps the story short while making the Israeli endorsement, Ethiopia’s response and the unresolved regional implications the central news points. items.title: Somaliland Opposition Condemns Cirro’s Gaza Troop Proposal as Political Backlash Grows
items.description: Washington (WDN) — Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi (Cirro) has triggered a political backlash after saying Somaliland could deploy up to 2,000 troops to Gaza if formally requested by the United States and Israel. Cirro made the remarks Wednesday in Washington while attending the MEAD conference, saying Somaliland was not volunteering to send forces to Gaza but would be prepared to contribute troops if Washington and Israel formally requested it. “If we are asked, we can provide them,” Cirro said, according to reports. “We are not putting ourselves forward, but if I am asked, I am ready.” The proposal has drawn strong criticism from Somaliland’s opposition parties, with several political groups condemning the idea and questioning the wisdom of involving Somaliland’s military in an international force for Gaza. Among the parties opposing the proposal is the Kaah Party, which has joined the broader political criticism of the government’s position. The opposition argues that Somaliland should not commit its soldiers to a foreign military mission without a clear national consensus, particularly one involving the highly sensitive Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Opposition Challenges the Government The backlash highlights a growing divide within Somaliland over the direction of President Cirro’s foreign and security policy. Opposition parties have questioned whether the government has the political mandate to make such a far-reaching military commitment, arguing that the deployment of Somaliland troops abroad would require careful public debate and broad political consultation. For critics, the issue is not simply whether Somaliland has soldiers available. It is why Somaliland should send them to Gaza, under whose command they would operate, what their mandate would be, and what political and security consequences Somaliland could face as a result. The criticism is particularly significant because Cirro’s proposal comes at a sensitive moment in Somaliland’s expanding relationship with Israel. A New Chapter in Somaliland-Israel Relations Somaliland has taken several steps to deepen its relationship with Israel. The government reportedly opened a diplomatic mission in Jerusalem in June, following Cirro’s official visit to Israel. Those moves have generated considerable debate within Somaliland and across the wider Somali political landscape. The relationship became even more consequential following Israel’s reported recognition of Somaliland in December 2025, a development that Somaliland has viewed as an important diplomatic breakthrough in its long campaign for international recognition. Cirro’s Gaza proposal could therefore be interpreted by critics as another step toward closer strategic alignment with Israel and the United States. The government, however, appears to view closer international partnerships as an opportunity to enhance Somaliland’s diplomatic position and increase its strategic relevance. The proposed international force for Gaza is expected to involve as many as 20,000 troops, according to reports. Uganda has reportedly agreed to contribute approximately 1,200 personnel, while Morocco has pledged up to 500. Albania, Kazakhstan and Kosovo have also reportedly expressed willingness to contribute troops to the U.S.-led force. The proposed mission would reportedly focus on maintaining security, supporting the training of Palestinian police forces, facilitating humanitarian assistance and preventing Hamas from rebuilding its military capabilities. For Somaliland, participation would represent a significant departure from its traditional security role. Its military has primarily focused on territorial security and maintaining control within Somaliland. Deploying thousands of troops to Gaza would place Somaliland’s forces in an international operation involving one of the world’s most politically sensitive conflicts. A Risky Political Calculation That is why opposition parties are demanding greater scrutiny. Sending troops abroad could expose Somaliland to political, diplomatic and security risks that extend far beyond the immediate mission. It could also deepen divisions inside Somaliland at a time when the government is already attempting to manage competing domestic political interests and strengthen its international position. The question facing Cirro is therefore larger than whether Somaliland can provide 2,000 soldiers. It is whether Somaliland’s national interest is served by becoming a military participant in the Gaza conflict—and whether such a decision can be made without broad political consensus. For the opposition, the answer appears to be no. Their condemnation suggests that the proposal has opened a new domestic political front for Cirro, turning what may have been intended as a gesture of international cooperation into a contentious debate over Somaliland’s foreign policy, military commitments and relationship with Israel. The issue is no longer simply whether Somaliland is willing to send troops to Gaza. It is whether the Somaliland government can convince its own political opposition—and its public—that such a deployment serves Somaliland’s interests. items.title: Sawirro: Xasan Sheekh oo madaxtooyadda ku qaabilay Xoghayaha guud ee…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ayaa Qasriga Madaxtooyada Qaranka ku qaabilay Xoghayaha Guud ee Raabidada Caalamka Islaamka ahna Guddoomiyaha Hay’adda Culimada Muslimiinta, Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulkarim Al-Issa. Kulanka labada dhinac ayaa looga hadlay xoojinta xiriirka iyo iskaashiga Soomaaliya iyo Raabidada Caalamka Islaamka, iyadoo si gaar ah diiradda loo saaray arrimaha khuseeya bulshada iyo horumarinta fahamka saxda ah ee Diinta Islaamka. Madaxweynaha iyo Xoghayaha Guud ayaa sidoo kale ka wada-hadlay dadaallada lagu xoojinayo nabadda, wadajirka iyo wada noolaanshaha bulshada iyo sidii loo horumarin lahaa doorka hay’adaha diinta ee arrimaha bulshada. Qodobada kulanka lagu soo qaaday waxaa kamid ahaa ka hortagga iyo la-dagaallanka fikirka xagjirka ah, iyadoo la adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay in la helo wacyigelin iyo faham diini ah oo sax ah. Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ayaa uga mahadceliyay Raabidada Caalamka Islaamka mowqifkeeda ku aaddan taageerada midnimada iyo madax-bannaanida Soomaaliya, iyo sidoo kale doorka ay ka qaadato horumarinta bulshada Soomaaliyeed. Madaxweynaha ayaa adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay in la sii xoojiyo iskaashiga dhinacyada dowladda iyo hay’adaha diinta, si wax looga qabto caqabadaha la xiriira fikirka xagjirka ah iyo marin-habaabinta dhalinyarada. Kulanka ayaa kusoo dhammaaday is-afgarad ku aaddan sii xoojinta xiriirka iyo iskaashiga Soomaaliya iyo Raabidada Caalamka Islaamka, gaar ahaan dhinacyada nabadda, wacyigelinta bulshada iyo ka hortagga fikradaha xagjirka ah. items.title: Xuutiyiinta oo gaaray Perim, qabsadayna Dhubab
items.description: Xoogagga Xuutiyiinta Yemen ayaa gaaray jasiiradda istaraatiijiga ah ee Perim, oo sidoo kale loo yaqaan Mayun, kuna taalla marin-biyoodka Bab al-Mandab. Afar ilo oo ka tirsan dowladda Yemen ayaa arrintan u xaqiijiyey Reuters⁠ Laba ilo oo kale oo ka tirsan dowladda Yemen ayaa sheegay in Xuutiyiintu la wareegeen magaalada xeebta ah ee Dhubab, kaddib markii ciidamada dowladda ay halkaas ka baxeen. Dhubab iyo Perim ayaa ku yaalla meel istaraatiiji ah oo u dhow halka ay Badda Cas kaga biirto Gacanka Cadmeed. Horumarkan ayaa xoojinaya joogitaanka Xuutiyiinta ee xeebta galbeed ee Yemen, kaddib markii ay hore ula wareegeen magaalada dekedda leh ee Mocha. Warbixintii hore waxay sheegashada ku saabsan Mayun ku tilmaantay mid aan si madax-bannaan loo xaqiijin, balse Reuters ayaa hadda heshay xaqiijin ka timid ilo badan. Ciidamada dowladda Yemen ee Sacuudigu taageero ayaa sheegay inay diyaarinayaan weerar rogaal-celis ah oo lagu soo ceshanayo deegaannadii laga baxay. Faahfaahin rasmi ah lagama bixin waqtiga uu weerarku bilaabanayo, ciidamada ka qaybgelaya iyo taageerada militari ee ay heli doonaan. Perim waxay dhexda kaga taallaa Bab al-Mandab, waana goob muhiim u ah la socodka maraakiibta isaga kala goosha Badda Cas iyo Gacanka Cadmeed. Si kastaba, gaaritaanka jasiiradda iyo qabsashada Dhubab macnaheedu ma aha in Xuutiyiintu si buuxda ula wareegeen marin-biyoodka, mana aysan soo bandhigin caddeyn muujinaysa inay xakameynayaan dhammaan isu-socodkiisa. Isbeddelkan cusub wuxuu sare u qaadayaa khatarta ku wajahan maraakiibta caalamiga ah iyo dalalka ku teedsan Gacanka Cadmeed, oo Soomaaliya ay ku jirto. Dagaal ka qarxa Bab al-Mandab wuxuu saameyn ku yeelan karaa ganacsiga, qiimaha shidaalka iyo ammaanka xeebaha gobolka.

items.title: Muqdisho: 40 Arday oo Lagu Maamuusay Cilmi-Baaris Lagu Daabacay Joornaallo Caalami ah
items.description: MUQDISHO (Goobjoog News) — Afartan arday oo Soomaaliyeed ayaa shalay oo Khamiis ahayd lagu maamuusay Madashii koowaad ee Cilmi-baarista iyo Hal-abuurka Soomaaliyeed, kaddib markii qoraallo cilmi-baaris ah oo ay ka diyaariyeen xaaladda dalka lagu daabacay joornaallo caalami ah oo la aqoonsan yahay. Munaasabaddan oo ka dhacday xarunta Jaamacadda Ummadda Soomaaliyeed ee magaalada Muqdisho, ayaa waxaa soo qabanqaabiyay xarunta Benaadir Research, Consultancy and Evaluation Center, waxaana ka qaybgalay bahda waxbarashada oo ay ku jiraan mas’uuliyiin ka socday Wasaaradda Waxbarashada, hoggaanka jaamacadaha, cilmi-baarayaal sar-sare, iyo ardayda wax ka barata dalka. Qabanqaabiyeyaasha madasha ayaa sheegay in qorshahani uu yahay mid sannadle ah oo lagu dhiirrigelinayo da’yarta aqoonta ku foogan, si kor loogu qaado tayada cilmi-baarista dalka iyo doorka ay ardaydu ku leeyihiin xallinta caqabadaha horyaalla bulshada Soomaaliyeed. Inkastoo madashu ahayd mid muhiimad weyn leh, haddana warbixinta laguma xusin magacyada 40-ka arday ee la abaalmariyay, noocyada joornaallada caalamiga ah ee lagu daabacay qoraalladooda, iyo hab-raacii loo maray qiimeynta tayada cilmi-baaristooda.

items.title: Breakaway Somaliland opens door to Israeli military presence
items.description: Washington (Somalia Today) — The leader of Somalia’s breakaway Somaliland region has said he would welcome a future Israeli military presence on the territory, arguing that closer security cooperation could provide protection and strengthen deterrence. “There is no Israeli security presence in Somaliland yet, but perhaps there will be one in the future,” Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi Irro told Yedioth Ahronoth during a visit to Washington. “We will cooperate with any friendly country, and we need security partners, including Israel,” he said. “If Israel is present, it will provide deterrence. We need protection. I do not rule out Israel or the United States establishing a presence here.” Irro said the possibility had not yet been formally discussed with Israel, despite reports cited by Yedioth Ahronoth that Israeli security officials had already visited Somaliland. His remarks go further than previous statements by Somaliland officials, who had acknowledged growing military cooperation with Israel while denying that talks were under way over establishing an Israeli base. Security ties expand Somaliland Defence Minister Mohamed Yusuf Ali told Reuters in June that Israel was providing training to police and military personnel in the breakaway region, but dismissed reports of negotiations over a military base as rumours. “There is no Israeli military presence or military bases in Somaliland,” Ali said at the time. Irro had also told Reuters earlier this year that Somaliland wanted to develop military cooperation with Israel, but said the two sides had not discussed establishing Israeli bases. Relations have expanded rapidly since Israel formally recognised Somaliland on December 26, 2025, becoming the first UN member state to do so. Somalia rejected the decision as a violation of its sovereignty and territorial integrity, while the African Union reaffirmed its position that Somaliland remains part of Somalia. Irro led a delegation to Israel in June as the two sides sought deeper cooperation in security, technology, agriculture and investment. He told Yedioth Ahronoth that Somaliland has about 25,000 soldiers and a coastguard of roughly 1,500 personnel, but said the region could benefit from additional military technology and training. “We have enough military strength to defend ourselves,” he said, “but perhaps we need technology and training.” Red Sea tensions Irro’s comments come as tensions increase across the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, with Iran-aligned Houthi forces expanding their presence towards the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Houthi forces captured Yemen’s Red Sea port city of Mocha on Thursday and advanced towards the Hanish Islands, strengthening their position near the narrow waterway separating Yemen from the Horn of Africa. The Bab al-Mandab connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and forms a critical maritime route for ships travelling between Europe and Asia. Somaliland lies directly across the Gulf of Aden from Yemen, while its port and airfield at Berbera have increasingly featured in discussions about possible Western and Israeli security operations in the region. Irro said, however, that Somaliland currently had no direct confrontation with the Houthis. “We have been neighbours with Yemen and the Houthis for thousands of years, and as a country we currently have no direct conflict with them,” he told Yedioth Ahronoth . The possibility of an Israeli military presence has drawn particular scrutiny because of Somaliland’s proximity to Yemen and the Bab al-Mandab. Somalia has repeatedly rejected foreign agreements involving Somaliland without the federal government’s approval, maintaining that the breakaway region remains part of Somali territory. Gaza troop offer Irro also told Yedioth Ahronoth that Somaliland would be prepared to contribute up to 2,000 soldiers to a planned international force expected to support security arrangements and demilitarisation in Gaza. The remarks follow his separate statement this week that the breakaway region was not volunteering troops but would respond positively if formally asked to contribute. Irro also rejected suggestions that closer relations with Israel included plans for Somaliland to receive Palestinians from Gaza, saying the issue was not relevant to the region. He said Israel’s recognition had opened opportunities for cooperation in security, trade and the economy, while acknowledging that the new relationship had also created political risks. “There are no free lunches,” Irro said. “We created enemies for ourselves because of the recognition, including Somalia and countries outside Africa that provide Somalia with weapons and intervene on the side of our rivals.” Irro accused foreign governments of providing Somalia with weapons and other military support, citing Turkish aircraft, and claimed Somali officials had threatened to invade Somaliland following Israel’s recognition. Yedioth Ahronoth reported the claims as part of its interview. Somalia Today could not independently verify them. Turkey is one of Somalia’s closest defence partners and operates a major military training facility in Mogadishu. items.fullContent: Washington (Somalia Today) — The leader of Somalia’s breakaway Somaliland region has said he would welcome a future Israeli military presence on the territory, arguing that closer security cooperation could provide protection and strengthen deterrence. “There is no Israeli security presence in Somaliland yet, but perhaps there will be one in the future,” Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi Irro told Yedioth Ahronoth during a visit to Washington. “We will cooperate with any friendly country, and we need security partners, including Israel,” he said. “If Israel is present, it will provide deterrence. We need protection. I do not rule out Israel or the United States establishing a presence here.” Irro said the possibility had not yet been formally discussed with Israel, despite reports cited by Yedioth Ahronoth that Israeli security officials had already visited Somaliland. His remarks go further than previous statements by Somaliland officials, who had acknowledged growing military cooperation with Israel while denying that talks were under way over establishing an Israeli base. Security ties expand Somaliland Defence Minister Mohamed Yusuf Ali told Reuters in June that Israel was providing training to police and military personnel in the breakaway region, but dismissed reports of negotiations over a military base as rumours. “There is no Israeli military presence or military bases in Somaliland,” Ali said at the time. Irro had also told Reuters earlier this year that Somaliland wanted to develop military cooperation with Israel, but said the two sides had not discussed establishing Israeli bases. Relations have expanded rapidly since Israel formally recognised Somaliland on December 26, 2025, becoming the first UN member state to do so. Somalia rejected the decision as a violation of its sovereignty and territorial integrity, while the African Union reaffirmed its position that Somaliland remains part of Somalia. Irro led a delegation to Israel in June as the two sides sought deeper cooperation in security, technology, agriculture and investment. He told Yedioth Ahronoth that Somaliland has about 25,000 soldiers and a coastguard of roughly 1,500 personnel, but said the region could benefit from additional military technology and training. “We have enough military strength to defend ourselves,” he said, “but perhaps we need technology and training.” Red Sea tensions Irro’s comments come as tensions increase across the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, with Iran-aligned Houthi forces expanding their presence towards the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Houthi forces captured Yemen’s Red Sea port city of Mocha on Thursday and advanced towards the Hanish Islands, strengthening their position near the narrow waterway separating Yemen from the Horn of Africa. The Bab al-Mandab connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and forms a critical maritime route for ships travelling between Europe and Asia. Somaliland lies directly across the Gulf of Aden from Yemen, while its port and airfield at Berbera have increasingly featured in discussions about possible Western and Israeli security operations in the region. Irro said, however, that Somaliland currently had no direct confrontation with the Houthis. “We have been neighbours with Yemen and the Houthis for thousands of years, and as a country we currently have no direct conflict with them,” he told Yedioth Ahronoth . The possibility of an Israeli military presence has drawn particular scrutiny because of Somaliland’s proximity to Yemen and the Bab al-Mandab. Somalia has repeatedly rejected foreign agreements involving Somaliland without the federal government’s approval, maintaining that the breakaway region remains part of Somali territory. Gaza troop offer Irro also told Yedioth Ahronoth that Somaliland would be prepared to contribute up to 2,000 soldiers to a planned international force expected to support security arrangements and demilitarisation in Gaza. The remarks follow his separate statement this week that the breakaway region was not volunteering troops but would respond positively if formally asked to contribute. Irro also rejected suggestions that closer relations with Israel included plans for Somaliland to receive Palestinians from Gaza, saying the issue was not relevant to the region. He said Israel’s recognition had opened opportunities for cooperation in security, trade and the economy, while acknowledging that the new relationship had also created political risks. “There are no free lunches,” Irro said. “We created enemies for ourselves because of the recognition, including Somalia and countries outside Africa that provide Somalia with weapons and intervene on the side of our rivals.” Irro accused foreign governments of providing Somalia with weapons and other military support, citing Turkish aircraft, and claimed Somali officials had threatened to invade Somaliland following Israel’s recognition. Yedioth Ahronoth reported the claims as part of its interview. Somalia Today could not independently verify them. Turkey is one of Somalia’s closest defence partners and operates a major military training facility in Mogadishu. items.title: Israel backs Ethiopia’s Red Sea access push amid tensions
items.description: Addis Ababa (Somalia Today) — Israel has publicly backed Ethiopia’s push for access to the Red Sea, with its ambassador in Addis Ababa describing support for the effort as official Israeli policy and arguing that a stronger Ethiopian role could contribute to regional security. “Israel is behind Ethiopia in this effort. This is clear Israeli policy,” Ambassador Avraham Neguise told the state-run Ethiopian News Agency in an interview published on Thursday. Neguise said Israel viewed Ethiopia’s maritime ambitions as part of a wider question of economic and security stability around the Red Sea, rather than an issue affecting Addis Ababa alone. “Empowering and strengthening Ethiopia and creating stability in the Red Sea is the interest of all, not only for Ethiopia,” he said. The comments amount to unusually explicit Israeli support for a strategic objective that Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has increasingly placed at the centre of Ethiopia’s regional policy. Ethiopia has sought more reliable access to the sea to support its growing economy and international trade, while also arguing for a greater security role in the Red Sea. Neguise said access would help Ethiopia strengthen its economy, safeguard its sovereignty and contribute to regional security. He did not identify a particular port or say whether Israel supported commercial access, an Ethiopian naval facility or another arrangement. That question remains politically sensitive because possible routes to the sea involve neighbouring states and, in Somalia’s case, a continuing dispute over sovereignty. Security argument Neguise placed particular emphasis on security, saying threats along the Red Sea affect international trade far beyond the Horn of Africa. “If the Red Sea will not be stable and there are terrorists attacking, it is not only the Horn of Africa, it’s not only the Middle East, the whole world economy will suffer,” he said. The Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb Strait form one of the world’s most important shipping corridors, linking the Indian Ocean and Gulf of Aden with the Suez Canal and Mediterranean. Security concerns around the route have intensified amid attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis , which have disrupted commercial shipping and forced some vessels onto longer routes around southern Africa. Neguise said Israel was ready to share its experience in counter-terrorism and tackling security threats, arguing that security and economic development were closely connected. He described Ethiopia as strategically important to the Horn of Africa and said greater maritime access could contribute to cooperation and stability across the region. “Ethiopia’s return to the Red Sea will be positive,” he said, citing the country’s involvement in peacekeeping and its stated commitment to regional stability. The ambassador also pointed to terrorism and piracy as threats whose effects extend beyond countries bordering the Red Sea to the Middle East, Europe and the wider global economy. Unresolved route Ethiopia became landlocked after Eritrea gained independence in 1993 and remains heavily dependent on Djibouti for access to international markets. More than 95 per cent of Ethiopia’s import-export trade by volume passes through the Addis Ababa-Djibouti corridor, according to the World Bank . Addis Ababa’s search for alternative access sparked a major regional dispute in January 2024 when it signed a memorandum of understanding with Somalia’s breakaway Somaliland region. The arrangement envisaged Ethiopian access to about 20 kilometres of coastline and a possible naval facility. Somaliland linked the agreement to eventual Ethiopian recognition of its independence, while Somalia rejected it as a violation of its sovereignty and territorial integrity. The dispute eased after Abiy and Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud reached the Türkiye-mediated Ankara Declaration in December 2024. The declaration allows the two sides to pursue arrangements that provide Ethiopia with reliable sea access under Somalia’s sovereign authority. Ethiopia and Somalia have not publicly announced a final agreement on a port or route. Israel’s position carries added significance because it formally recognised Somaliland as an independent state in December 2025, becoming the first country to do so. Somalia rejected the move. Israel and Somaliland have since deepened relations, with Somaliland opening an embassy in Jerusalem. Neguise did not say whether Israel linked its support for Ethiopia’s maritime ambitions to Somaliland or any particular route. Egypt and Eritrea have meanwhile opposed efforts by landlocked countries to claim a security role in the Red Sea, arguing that responsibility for the waterway should remain with its coastal states. items.title: Daawo: Dabageed oo shaaciyay in Xasan Sheekh uga baxay heshiis hoose oo uu la galay
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweyne ku-xigeenka dowlad-goboleedka HirShabelle, Yuusuf Axmed Hagar (Dabageed) ayaa Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ku eedeeyay inuu uga baxay ballan siyaasadeed oo uu la galay. Dabageed oo sheegay in Madaxweynaha ay hore ugu heshiiyeen, uguna ballanqaaday inuu hoggaanka HirShabelle isaga siiyo ayaa sheegay in Xasan Sheekh uu hadda waxba kama jiraan kasoo qaaday ballankaas. Dabageed ayaa sheegay in xalay kulan albaabadu u xirnaayeen oo uu la yeeshay Xasan Sheekh uu ku wargeliyay in kursigii HirShabelle aan loo hayn, sidaas darteedna uu tanaasulo. “Madaxweynaha shalay markuu isoo wacay, waxaa u qabay laba qodob midkood: Madaxweynihii ayaa ku siinayaa ee reer HirShabelle ku hoggaami oo shaqadii la wareeg, ama inuu leeyahay waxaan ku ballannay waa shaqeyn waayay, oo nin kale oo Xawaadle ah oo ilma adeer tihiin ayaa kursigii la siiyay ee la shaqee ninkaas, sidaas ayuu ku dhihi islahaa hadduu adiga ku siin waayo,” ayuu yiri. Dabageed ayaa sheegay in Madaxweynuhu uu si cad ugu sheegay in xilka maamulka HirShabelle uu u wado Cali Guudlaawe, oo mar kale isku soo taagaya hoggaanka maamulka. “Madaxweynihii xalay waxaan kala kulmay wax uu nin fiyow oo ehel iyo mas’uul ah oo Madaxweyne Soomaaliyeed uu dhihi karo aanan u qabin. Ballankii reer abtigay waa ka baxay ee kursiga iiga doon, oo iga nabad doonee ayuu igu dhahay,” ayuu yiri Dabageed. Waxa uu intaas kusii daray: “Intee geyni baa dhahay haddaan kasoo helo oo doono. Cali Guudlaawe ayaa siin buu yiri. Madaxweynaha uma badin ee waxaan dhahay arrintaas kama nabad dooneyn karo, nin hadda iga dambeeya oo ka nabaddooneyn kara inuu jiro ilama aha. Raalli ahow, wax aan ka filanayay oo reer abtiga ka sugayeen ma aha, oo xaqoodi ma aha.” Inkastoo weli uusan jirin war rasmi ah oo kasoo baxay Villa Soomaaliya oo si cad u xaqiijinaya in heshiis kama dambeys ah laga gaaray musharraxa Madaxweynaha HirShabelle ama in Guudlaawe loo go’aamiyay inuu mar kale hoggaamiyo maamulka, haddana waxaa isa soo taraya wararka sheegay in Xasan uu kaarka JSP siinayo Guudlaawe, si mar kale loogu dhiso hoggaanka maamulka. Hoos ka daawo muuqaalka The post Daawo: Dabageed oo shaaciyay in Xasan Sheekh uga baxay heshiis hoose oo uu la galay appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Taliska ciidanka xoogga oo qaaday tallaabo la xiriirta dhacdadii Ceelbaraf
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Taliska Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliya ayaa sheegay inuu baaritaan ku hayo dilka askari ka tirsanaa ciidanka, kaas oo lagu dilay deegaanka Calaag ee degmada Ceelbaraf ee gobolka Shabeellaha Dhexe. Taliska ayaa sheegay in marxuum Axmed Shire Xuseen xiliga la dilay uu fasax uga maqnaa shaqada ciidanka. War-saxaafadeed kasoo baxay taliska ayaa sidoo kale lagu sheegay in baaritaanno ku aaddan dhacdada ay haatan socdaan, si loo xaqiijiyo faah-faahinta dilka iyo cid kasta oo ku lug lahayd. Taliska ciidanka xoogga ayaa sheegay in la qaadi doono tallaabooyin waafaqsan sharciga, marka la helo natiijada baaritaanka iyo cidda mas’uulka ka ahayd falka. Sidoo kale, Taliska ayaa tacsi u diray qoyska, ehelada iyo bahda ciidanka ee uu ka baxay marxuum Axmed Shire Xuseen. “Askarta Soomaaliyeed ay mudan yihiin in la dhowro noloshooda, sharaftooda iyo xuquuqdooda,” ayuu yiri taliska. Taliska ayaa adkeeyay in ciidanka xoogga uu yahay ciidan qaran oo u adeegaya dhammaan shacabka Soomaaliyeed, isla markaana ay muhiim tahay in la dhowro sharciga iyo xuquuqda askarta. Dilka askariga ayaa caro ka abuuray bulshada Soomaaliyeed, iyadoo falka lagu tilmaamay mid bahalnimo ah, waxaana lagu baaqay in caddaaladda la horkeeno cid kasta oo lagu helo inay ka dambeysay dilka. Axmed Shire ayaa maleeshiyaad hubeysan ay kala dageen mooto uu la socday, xilli uu kusii jeeday gobolka Hiiraan, kadibna ay sidaas ku toogteen. Ka hor inta aan la dilin askariga, maleeshiyaadka hubeysan oo u abaabulnaa hab beeleed ayaa muuqaal ka duubay marxuumka, iyadoo ehelladiisu ay sheegeen in jirkiisa uu googo’ay kadib markii jir-dil xooggan loo gaystay, taasoo sababtay in si dhib badan lagu aaso. Waa markii labaad oo dhacdo noocaan oo kale ah ay ka dhaceyso aagga Ceelbaraf, waxayna ay ahayd dhammaadkii bishii December ee 2024-kii markii sidaan oo kale aano qabiil darteed halkaas loogu dilay 7 askari oo ka tirsanaa Ciidamada Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed, kana yimid dhanka furimaha hore. Askartaas oo fasax kasoo qaatay goobihii ay ka howl-galeen, kuna sii jeeday ehelladooda, ayaa waxaa gaari kala degay maleeshiyaad beeleed, kuwaas oo indhaha ka xiray, muuqaalna ka duubay, kadibna toogasho ku fuliyay. items.title: Xog: Gantaallada Xuutiyiinta iyo masaafooyinka ay gaari karaan
items.description: Sanca (Caasimada Online) – Xuutiyiinta Yemen ayaa muddooyinkii dambe soo bandhigay awood ciidan oo sii kordheysa, iyadoo kooxdii markii hore ahayd mid kooban ay hadda haysato hub iyo gantaallo kala duwan oo gaari kara masaafooyin fog. Awoodda Xuutiyiinta ayaa si gaar ah loo dareemay sannadihii lasoo dhaafay, kaddib markii ay bilaabeen inay adeegsadaan gantaallo iyo hub kale oo ay ku bartilmaameedsadaan goobo kala duwan. Hubka ay haystaan waxaa qeyb ka ah gantaallo ay soo saareen ama ay ka heleen dalal ay xiriir la leeyihiin, gaar ahaan Iran. Waxaa ka mid ah gantaallada ay adeegsadaan Scud Soviet B1C, kaas oo lagu qiyaaso inuu gaari karo masaafo dhan 300 kiiloomitir. Sidoo kale waxaa jira Hwasong-5 oo laga sameeyay Waqooyiga Kuuriya, kaas oo isna gaaraya ku dhowaad 300 kiiloomitir. Xuutiyiinta ayaa sidoo kale haysta Hwasong-6, oo la sheegay inuu gaari karo ilaa 600 kiiloomitir, halka Scarab Soviet 21 uu leeyahay masaafo lagu qiyaasay 70 kiiloomitir. Gantaalka Earthquake-3, oo lagu farsameeyo Iran, ayaa isna lagu sheegay inuu gaari karo qiyaastii 250 kiiloomitir. Waxaa kale oo liiska hubka Xuutiyiinta lagu xusay Qaher-1, oo asal ahaan kasoo jeeda nidaamyadii Midowgii Soofiyeeti, waxaana lagu qiyaasaa inuu gaaro masaafo dhan 250 kiiloomitir. Sidoo kale waxaa jira gantaalka C802, oo ah hub Shiine ah, kaas oo lagu sheegay inuu gaari karo masaafo u dhexeysa 120 iyo 180 kiiloomitir. Dhanka awoodda badda, Xuutiyiinta ayaa lagu xusay gantaallo ay kamid yihiin Mandab-1, oo lagu sheegay inuu yahay gantaal Shiine ah oo gaari kara 40 kiiloomitir, iyo Mandab-2, oo la xiriira Iran, kaas oo lagu qiyaasay inuu gaaro 250 kiiloomitir. Sidoo kale waxaa liiska ku jira Shaale, oo lagu sheegay inuu yahay gantaal laga sameeyo Iran, isla markaana gaara 180 kiiloomitir, iyo Rubies Soviet, oo masaafo ahaan lagu qiyaasay 80 kiiloomitir. Gantaallo kale oo loo aaneynayo hubka Xuutiyiinta waxaa kamid ah Quddus, oo lagu sheegay inuu Iran farsamayso, isla markaana gaari kara ilaa 800 kiiloomitir, iyo Duufaan, oo isna lala xiriiriyo Iran, iyadoo lagu qiyaasay inuu gaaro 450 kiiloomitir. Waxaa sidoo kale jira Fiyuus, oo lagu sheegay inuu gaaro 140 kiiloomitir, halka gantaalka loogu yeero Badda Cas la sheegay inuu kasoo jeedo Iran, balse aan si cad loo ogeyn masaafada uu gaari karo. Kala duwanaanshaha gantaalladan ayaa siinaya Xuutiyiinta awood ay ku gaaraan bartilmaameedyo ku yaalla masaafooyin kala duwan, iyadoo qaar kamid ah hubkan loogu talagalay weerarrada dhulka, halka kuwo kalena loo adeegsado bartilmaameedyada badda. Awooddan milatari ayaa Xuutiyiinta ka dhigtay koox saameyn weyn ku leh amniga gobolka, gaar ahaan marin-biyoodka Badda Cas iyo Bab al-Mandab, halkaas oo dhaqdhaqaaqyada milatari iyo weerarrada maraakiibta ay walaac ka abuureen. Si kastaba, xogta ku saabsan qaar kamid ah gantaallada iyo halka ay ka yimaadeen ayaa ah mid ay ilo kala duwan si kala duwan u sheegaan. items.title: Retroactive pensions and the long-term financial burden on Local Governments
items.description: Retroactive pensions and the long-term financial burden on Local Governments If there were one mayor and one assistant for each of the 23 degmo doorasho in each of three terms, the basic number of beneficiaries would be: 23 areas × 3 terms × 2 people = 138 That is 138 people receiving pension benefits. Who decided 3 term Mayors and deputy mayors qualify for the pension and on what bases. For instance Burao changed Mayors this term three times then do they all deserve pension. Can Government avoid to pay such huge some yearly. Doesn’t this issue seem like a joke, although Xildhiban Cudhay said this filthy idea passed all levels but Somaliland should have clear legislation explaining: Who is eligible for a pension…. How many years of service are required…. Pension benefits should be earned through transparent rules. My two cent worth of advice to the government is a person should not automatically receive a pension merely because the title attached to the person’s position was “mayor.” The essence or the real meaning of a pension is financial security after retirement which is either for a long service or according to age.   Ahmed Saeed ahmsaeed@hotmail.com
